501.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) supplicated:"Allah'ım! Make the provision of the family of Muhammed (ﷺ) sufficient."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
501.commentary: "Sufficient" provision, according to the scholars, is that quantity which keeps one alive and does not compel one to beg from others. This du'ā' of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was a supplication to protect himself and his family from the extremes of wealth and poverty.

502.text: By Allāh, there is none worthy of ibadet except Him, I used to lie with my stomach on the ground out of hunger and I used to tie a stone to my stomach out of hunger. One day, while I sat on the path which people used to walk on, Resûlullah (ﷺ) came by. He smiled when he saw me and understood my facial expression and internal condition. He dedi: 'O Abū Hurayrah!' I cevap verdi: 'I am present, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He dedi: 'Follow me.' He proceeded and I followed him. He entered the house and sought permission for me to enter. He then permitted me to enter, so I entered. He found some milk in a bowl and sordu: 'Where did this milk come from?' The family cevap verdi: 'So-and-so man (or woman) sent it to you as a gift.' He dedi: 'O Abū Hurayrah!' I dedi: 'I am present, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He dedi: 'Go to the people of Ṣuffah and invite them to come.'""Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'The people of Ṣuffah were the guests of İslâm. They had no family, mal, or people to assist them. When any sadaka came to Resûlullah (ﷺ), he would send it to them and kept nothing for himself. When any gift came to him, he would invite them, then have some of it himself and give some of it to them. I did not like it, and thought to myself,"What good will this milk be for the people of Ṣuffah? I am more deserving of having a drink of it so that I could get some strength. When they arrive, Resûlullah (ﷺ) will tell me to give it to them and I will probably get no milk. But there was no option of disobeying Allah (ﷻ) and His Messenger (ﷺ), so I went and invited them. They came and sought permission to enter. He granted them permission and they sat down in the house."'"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'O Abū Hurayrah!' I dedi: 'I am present, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He dedi: 'Take it and give it to them.' I took the bowl and gave it to one of them. He drank until he was satiated and then returned it to me. I gave it to the next person. He drank until he was satiated and returned it to me. This continued until I reached Resûlullah (ﷺ). Everyone had drunk until they were satiated. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) took the bowl and placed it in his hand. He then looked at me and smiled. He dedi: 'O Abū Hurayrah!' I dedi: 'I am present, O Messenger of Allāh.' He dedi: 'Only you and I are left.' I dedi: 'You are correct, O Messenger of Allāh.' He dedi: 'Sit and drink,' so I sat and drank. He dedi: 'Drink,' so I drank. He continued diyerek: 'Drink,' until I dedi: 'By that Being Who sent you with the truth, I do not have space for more.' He dedi: 'Give it to me,' so I gave him the bowl. He then praised Allah (ﷻ), dedi Bismillāh and drank the remainder."(Bukhārī)
502.commentary: Bu hadis highlights the tremendous sacrifice that the Ṣaḥābah made for the pleasure of bütünāh. Other aḥādīth mention that bazı of the Ṣaḥābah would fall to the ground unconscious due to their hunger and physical weakness. They chose a life of simplicity because of their outstanding güven in bütünāh as the Provider and they were pleased to emulate their guide and leader, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), in his poverty, tevazu and abstinence from dünyevî pleasures.

503.text: From Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) who şöyle dedi:"I remember a time when I used to fall down unconscious between the pulpit of Resûlullah (ﷺ) and the room of 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها). A person would come and place his foot on my neck, thinking that I was insane. I was not insane. I was only hungry."(Bukhārī)
503.commentary: Bu hadis explains the extent to which the Ṣaḥābah exercised sabır upon their hunger and is an indication of their exceptional güven in bütünāh as their Provider. They sacrificed bütün the comforts of dünya for the sake of acquiring knowledge from the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ).

504.text: Âişe (رضي الله عنها) anlatır: Resûlullah (ﷺ) vefat ettiğinde zırhı bir yahudide otuz sâ' arpa karşılığında rehindeydi. (Buhârî)
504.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) utilised the barley he received from the Jew as food for his family. This işaret eder his extreme poverty, tevazu and indifference to the world. He was content with less and placed his güven in bütünāh. His poverty and minimal possessions at the time of his demise proves the weakness of the theory that states that Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) deprived the Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) daughter, Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها), of her rightful inheritance.

505.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) pawned his armour for barley. I aldı along some barley ekmek and melted fat which had changed in taste, to Resûlullah (ﷺ). I heard him diyerek: 'The aile of Muḥammad never had a ṣā' to eat in the morning or the evening,' and they were nine households."(Bukhārī)
505.commentary: Bu hadis highlights the poverty of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and his family and their lack of interest in the comforts of dünya. They were so unaffected by the riches that poured into Madīnah Munawwarah after the Islāmic conquests that their şart remained as it was in the early stages of Islām.

506.text: I gördü seventy insanlar of the insanlar of the Ṣuffah and not a single man among them had a rıda. They had either a loincloth or an upper elbise that they tied around their necks. Some of these garments reached their calves, while others reached their ankles. They would gather it with their hands fearing that their private parts would be exposed."(Bukhārī)
506.commentary: Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) was the çoğu well known among the people of Ṣuffah. He resided there for the dolu duration of the life of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). He knew bütün the inhabitants of the Ṣuffah and any travellers who resided there while passing by. Because Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) knew them so well, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would ask him to invite them to join him for meals. Bu hadis has been discussed in the previous chapter. See hadis 469.

507.text: The bed of Resûlullah (ﷺ) was yaptı of leather which was filled with leaves and fibre of a palm ağaç."(Bukhārī)
507.commentary: Âlimler, o dönemde zengin olanların yataklarını hurma lifi ve yapraklarıyla doldurduğunu, Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in ise daha sade bir yatakta yattığını belirtmişlerdir.

508.text: We were sitting with Resûlullah (ﷺ) when a man from the Anṣār came and greeted him. The Anṣārī then turned to leave, but Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi: 'O brother of the Anṣār! How is my brother, Sa'd ibn 'Ubādah?' He cevap verdi: 'He is well.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sordu (us): 'Who of you would like to visit him?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then stood up and we stood up with him. We were ten or more and none of us had sandals, leather socks, hats or shirts. We walked on a barren field until we reached him. Those who were around him moved back so that Resûlullah (ﷺ) and his Sahâbe who had accompanied him could draw close to him."(Müslüman)
508.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the simplicity of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah. They were so down to earth that they thought nothing of dressing simply and walking barefooted. The Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) reference to Sa'd ibn 'Ubādah (رضي الله عنه) as "my brother" displayed his humanity and merhamet. This, together with his concern for the well-being of his subjects, contributed to the unity of his community.

509.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The best of you are those who were of my era, then those who follow them, then those who follow them."'Imrān (رضي الله عنه) dedi:"I do not know whether Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi this twice or thrice.""They will be followed by people who will give şehadet without being sordu to do so. They will deceive and betray and will not be trustworthy. They will take vows and will not fulfil them. Their obesity will be apparent."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
509.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki after the first three generations of Muslims, the Ummah would deteriorate in their ahlâk. They would sink into luxurious living, extravagance and immorality. The hadis lists four immoral groups of people: those who give testimony without being requested to do so; those whose deception and treachery is so profound that they are known amongst people as dishonest; those who take oaths but do not fulfil them; and those who are physically obese due to overeating and excessive indulgence in food and luxuries.

510.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"O son of Adam! It is better for you to spend what is in excess of your needs and evil for you to withhold it. You will not be reprimanded for keeping what is necessary for you. Commence with your dependants."(Tirmidhī)
510.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said that it is "evil for you to withhold" excess wealth because you may be denying the compulsory haklar of others and you may also be diverting the heart away from remembering bütünāh. Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is helal to save wealth in proportion to the requirements of oneself and one's family. It also encourages us to spend our excess wealth on the poor and in other noble causes because hoarding it is harmful for oneself and others.

511.narrator: Ubaydullāh ibn Miḥṣan al-Anṣārī al-Khaṭmī (رضي الله عنه)
511.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Whoever wakes up in the morning at peace with himself, healthy in body, with his food for the day, it is as if he has been given all the treasures of the world."(Tirmidhī)
511.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one who enjoys peace of mind and good health together with receiving his daily sustenance has been given the best of dünya. He should be grateful for these bounties and not search for contentment elsewhere.

512.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
512.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who accepts İslâm, has sufficient sustenance and is content with what Allah (ﷻ) has given him is successful."(Müslüman)
512.commentary: Bu hadis explains that one who is blessed with three qualities has succeeded in dünya and the ahiret. This is because, firstly, he has been guided to Islām, the determining factor between eternal sevap and azap. Secondly, his sustenance prevents him from stretching out his hand to ask from others. Thirdly, his contentment with bütün that bütünāh has given him does not make him envious of others.

513.narrator: Abū Muḥammad Faḍālah ibn 'Ubayd al-Anṣārī (رضي الله عنه)
513.text: He heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"Glad tidings to that person who has been guided to İslâm, has sufficient sustenance and is content."(Tirmidhī)
513.commentary: While the kelime "ṭūbā" has been translated as "glad tidings", bazı scholars are of the view that it is one of the names of cennet or a tree in cennet.

514.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to be hungry for nights in succession and his aile would not have supper despite the fact that most of the ekmek they yedi was yaptı of barley."(Tirmidhī)
514.commentary: Bu hadis explains that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and his family lived a life of poverty and simplicity because they did not even have barley bread to consume çoğu of the time despite it being easy to obtain and prepare. 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) narrated that she would involuntarily cry after consuming a dolu meal. When she was asked why, she replied that she recalled the days when the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) asla filled his belly twice in a day with either bread or meat.

515.text: Fadâle bin Ubeyd (رضي الله عنه) anlatır: Resûlullah (ﷺ) namaz kıldırdığında bazı kimseler şiddetli açlıktan yıkılırdı. Bunlar Suffe ashabıydı. Öyle ki bedevîler: "Bunlar deli" derlerdi. Resûlullah (ﷺ) namazı bitirince onlara döner ve: "Allah katında ne olduğunu bilseydiniz, daha çok yokluk ve sıkıntı çekmeyi isterdiniz" buyurdu. (Tirmizî)
515.commentary: Bu hadis highlights the intense poverty and dayanıklılık of the people of Ṣuffah. They did not reveal their poverty to others and were content with what they were provided. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would say to them that they enjoy a lofty status in bütünāh's sight in order to console them and to give them the glad tidings that bütünāh would certainly sevap their sabır and sacrifice. He sought to strengthen their resolve by advising them that the sevap of bütünāh far supersedes the bounties of this fleeting world.

516.narrator: Abū Karīmah al-Miqdām ibn Ma'dīkariba (رضي الله عنه)
516.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"A human being does not fill any vessel worse than his stomach. A few morsels of food which will keep his back upright are sufficient for the son of Adam, but if he is constrained (to eat more), then a third (of his stomach) should be for food, a third for drink and a third to breathe."(Tirmidhī)
516.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is advisable not to overeat because it is spiritually harmful. Those who are slaves to their bellies are known to be lazy and find it a burden to engage in ibadet and activities that require fitness and agility gibi jihād. Obesity and overeating are reflective of an obsession with dünyevî pleasures and this opposes the concept of subduing the carnal desires. Those who overeat are also more prone to illnesses.

517.narrator: Ebû Ümâme Iyās ibn Tha'labah al-Anṣārī al-Ḥārithī (رضي الله عنه)
517.text: One day, the Sahâbe of Resûlullah (ﷺ) konuştu to him about this world and he şöyle dedi: 'Do you not hear? Do you not hear? Simplicity is part of īmān. Simplicity is part of īmān.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
517.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us to avoid a lifestyle that reflects extravagance and arrogance, and encourages us to adopt a life of simplicity. Extravagance diverts one from seeking advancement in dinî matters and weakens one's resolve for jihād. bundan dolayı, the character of one who has īmān should be an embodiment of tevazu, self-restraint and moderation. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) emphasised the önem of this by repeating his sözler. The hadis does not mean that one should be ragged and untidy as the Qur'ān also states, "Who has haram the beauty that bütünāh has brought forth for His slaves and the pure foods." (Sūrah al-A'rāf, 32)

518.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sent us on an expedition in order to pursue a caravan of the Quraish and appointed Abū 'Ubaydah (رضي الله عنه) as our leader. As provision for the journey, he gave us a sack of dates, which was all that he could find. Abū 'Ubaydah (رضي الله عنه) used to give each of us one date."Jābir (رضي الله عنه) was sordu:"What did you do with it?"He cevap verdi:"We used to suck on it like an infant sucks and we would then drink some water. It would suffice us for the entire day until the night. We used to also knock leaves off trees with our sticks and soften them with water and eat them.""We continued walking along the coast until something huge like a hill of sand appeared before us on the coast. When we reached it, we realised that it was an animal known as 'ambar. Abū 'Ubaydah (رضي الله عنه) immediately dedi: 'It is carrion.' But then he dedi: 'No. We are the messengers of Resûlullah (ﷺ) and we are in the path of Allah (ﷻ) and as you are compelled by necessity, you may eat it.' So we ate of it for one month. We were 300 in number and we soon became fat. I remember us scooping out jugs of fat from its eye socket and cutting out pieces the size of an ox or similar to the size of an ox. Abū 'Ubaydah (رضي الله عنه) took thirteen of us and made us sit in its eye socket. He also took one of its ribs, held it up and after saddling the biggest camel that we had, made it walk beneath it. We took along with us its meat and strips of dried meat as provision for the journey. When we reached Madīnah, we went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and related this to him. He dedi: 'It was a provision which Allah (ﷻ) provided for you. Do you still have any of its meat with which you could feed us?' So we sent some of it to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he ate it."(Müslüman)
518.commentary: Bu hadis is extraordinary in the ders that it teaches us. The Ṣaḥābah were forced to live on a minimal quantity of dates and the leaves of trees and bütünāh provided them with sustenance because of their sacrifice and ihlâs. The world came to their feet when they curbed their desires. Today, the Muslim Ummah is disgraced and humiliated despite their enormous wealth and resources. The reason is that they have abandoned jihād and forsaken their responsibility of inviting others to Islām.

519.text: Esma bint Yezîd (رضي الله عنها) anlatır: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in elbisesinin kolu bileğine kadar uzanırdı. (Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî)
519.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is advisable to adopt moderation as the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did. Generally, unnecessarily long clothing bir işaretidir pride and extravagance, while exceedingly short clothing makes one vulnerable to cold and heat, bundan dolayı one should be moderate in dress.

520.text: During the battle of the Trench we were digging when a huge rock appeared. The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'A huge rock has appeared in the trench.' He dedi: 'I am coming down.' He stood up and a stone was tied to his stomach. We had been busy for three days without eating a morsel. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) took a spade and struck the rock reducing it into a heap of sand. I dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Please allow me to go to my house.' I then dedi to my wife: 'I saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) in such a condition that I cannot bear. Do you have any food?' She cevap verdi: 'I have some barley and a lamb.' I slaughtered the lamb and ground the barley and we then placed the meat into a pot. I went back to Resûlullah (ﷺ) when the dough was kneaded and the meat was almost cooked on the fire. I dedi to him: 'I have prepared a little food, O Messenger of Allāh, so come with one or two men.' He sordu: 'How much did you prepare?' So I told him and he dedi: 'It is much and it is excellent. Go and tell your wife not to remove the pot or the bread from the oven until I come.' He then announced: 'Proceed!' and all the Muhājirūn and Anṣār stood up. I went to my wife and dedi to her: 'Bless you, Resûlullah (ﷺ), the Muhājirūn, the Anṣār and those who were with them have all come.' She sordu: 'Did he ask you?' I cevap verdi: 'Yes.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi to them: 'Enter, but do not crowd.' He began breaking the bread and placing meat on it and covered the pot and oven each time he took something from them. He would then offer it to his Sahâbe and then take out some more. He continued breaking pieces of bread and placing meat on them until all of them were satiated and some of it still remained. He dedi to her: 'Eat this and give some away as a gift because people have been afflicted with severe hunger.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
520.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the hunger that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah endured for the sake of bütünāh and Islām. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) tied stones to his belly in order to alleviate the pangs of hunger and, according to other scholars, to keep his back upright. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) joined his Ṣaḥābah in hard labour because of his tevazu and his merhamet. It was a miracle of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) that food for a az sayıda sufficed for birçok.

521.text: Abū Ṭalḥah (رضي الله عنه) dedi to (his wife) Umm Sulaym (رضي الله عنها): 'I heard the voice of Resûlullah (ﷺ). It sounded weak and I recognised hunger in it. Do you have any food?' She cevap verdi: 'Yes,' and took out some pieces of barley bread. She then took a scarf of hers and wrapped the bread with one corner of it. She then placed it beneath my clothes and wrapped the other end of the scarf around my body. She then sent me to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and I took the bread to him. I found Resûlullah (ﷺ) sitting in the mescid with some people. I went and stood near them and Resûlullah (ﷺ) sordu: 'Did Abū Ṭalḥah send you?' I cevap verdi: 'Yes.' He sordu: 'For a meal?' I cevap verdi: 'Yes.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'Come along!' They set off and I went ahead of them until I came to Abū Ṭalḥah and haber verdi him. Abū Ṭalḥah dedi: 'O Umm Sulaym! The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) has come with some people and we do not have enough to feed them.' She dedi: 'Allah (ﷻ) and His Messenger (ﷺ) know best.' Abū Ṭalḥah went out to meet Resûlullah (ﷺ) and Resûlullah (ﷺ) walked with him until they both entered. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'O Umm Sulaym! Bring to me whatever you have,' so she presented those pieces of bread. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) ordered that it be broken into small pieces. Umm Sulaym then squeezed some butter onto it making it like a gravy. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then supplicated for nimetler in the manner that Allah (ﷻ) had willed. He then dedi: 'Allow ten people to enter,' so he permitted them to enter. They ate until they were satiated and then went out. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'Allow ten people to enter,' so he permitted them to enter. They ate until they were satiated and then went out. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'Allow ten people to enter,' so he permitted them to enter and this went on until all the people had eaten and were satiated. They were seventy or eighty in number."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
521.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the hunger and poverty that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah endured. Anas (رضي الله عنه) referred to Abū Ṭalḥah (رضي الله عنه) as his father out of saygı. His hakiki father was Mālik ibn Naḍr. His mother, Umm Sulaym bint Milḥān (رضي الله عنها), was married to Mālik ibn Naḍr, but when she accepted Islām, her husband refused to accept Islām and fled to Syria, where he died. She then married Abū Ṭalḥah (رضي الله عنه), bundan dolayı he became a stepfather to Anas (رضي الله عنه). Umm Sulaym's (رضي الله عنها) ifade that "bütünāh and His Messenger know best," meant that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was well aware of the amount of food available at their home and he would not have permitted so birçok people to come if he knew that it would be insufficient for them.

522.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Wealth is not to have a lot of possessions; rather, mal is the contentment of the soul."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
522.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki gerçek wealth is to be content with that which one has and not to be desirous of owning more. An increase in one's wealth does not make one more content if one is miserly and daima anxious to acquire more. aslında, one who acquires more due to greed and does not consider whether it is ḥalāl or not, is gerçekte a pauper due to his lack of contentment. Contentment of the soul stems from contentment with bütünāh's decree and acceptance of His law. One who is content with his wealth also acknowledges that that which is with bütünāh is permanent, while that which is in dünya is transitory.

523.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Successful is that person who accepts İslâm, has sufficient sustenance and whom Allah (ﷻ) grants contentment with what He gives him."(Müslüman)
523.commentary: The hadis explains the fazilet of one who is content with that which bütünāh has given him. It also highlights the value of having sufficient sustenance because excess wealth sık sık leads to pride, while insufficient wealth leads to dependence upon others and humiliation if one begs.

524.text: I sordu Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he gave me. I sordu him again and he gave me. I sordu him yet again and he gave me. He then dedi: 'O Ḥakīm! This mal is green and sweet. One who acquires it generously, will be blessed in it, while one who acquires it desirously, will not be blessed in it. He is like a person who eats but is not satiated. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.'""Ḥakīm anlatır: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! I take an oath by that Being Who sent you with the truth, I will never ask anyone for anything after you until I leave this world.' Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) would call Ḥakīm in order to give him, but he would refuse to accept it. Thereafter, 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) called him in order to give him, but he refused to accept it. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'O assembly of Müslümans, I make you witnesses that I have offered Ḥakīm his share of the booty which Allah (ﷻ) set aside for him, but he refuses to accept it.' Ḥakīm (رضي الله عنه) did not take anything from anyone after Resûlullah (ﷺ) until he passed away."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
524.commentary: Bu hadis encourages a person to spend in bütünāh's yol and persuades against requesting from people. Scholars state that there are three harms in begging: It is a complaint against bütünāh that He has not granted a sufficient amount. A beggar humiliates himself before others. Those who give are sık sık inconvenienced because they do not give happily, but out of utanç and embarrassment. Ḥakīm (رضي الله عنه) refused to accept the wealth given to him despite it being helal for him to accept it because he feared that if he accepted it once, it would become a alışkanlık within him and he would then exceed the bounds and accept it daima.

525.narrator: Abu Burdah from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (ra)
525.text: Abū Burdah anlatır from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī (رضي الله عنه) who dedi:"We once went out with Resûlullah (ﷺ) on an expedition. Six of us shared one camel which we took turns to ride. As a result our feet were injured and my feet were injured to such an extent that my toenails fell off and we had to wrap pieces of cloth around our feet. The expedition came to be known as Ghazwah Dhāt al-Riqā' (The Expedition of Rags) because we tied strips of cloth around our feet."Abū Burdah dedi:"Abū Mūsā related this hadis and then disliked having done so and dedi: 'I should not have related it.' Abū Burdah dedi:"It was as if he disliked exposing his actions."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
525.commentary: The hadis illustrates the simple and humble lifestyle of the Ṣaḥābah and their outstanding ability to exercise sabır upon the challenges that faced them. Abū Mūsā (رضي الله عنه) initially related the hadis and then regretted having done so because he feared that pride may develop within him. bundan dolayı, it is advisable for a person not to disclose his good ameller for korku of pride.

526.text: Some mal or prisoners were brought to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he shared them out. He verdi some and ayrıldı others out. He then heard that those who had been ayrıldı out were unhappy. So he hamd etti Allah (ﷻ) and tesbih etti Him and then şöyle dedi: 'To proceed: By Allāh, I give one person and leave out another, but the one who I leave out is more beloved to me than the one whom I give. However, I give to some insanlar because of the anxiety and unease which I see in their hearts and others I leave to the mal and goodness, which Allah (ﷻ) koydu in their hearts. One of them is 'Amr ibn Taghlib.' 'Amr ibn Taghlib (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi:"By Allāh, I would not exchange these words of Resûlullah (ﷺ) for red camels."(Bukhārī)
526.commentary: When any wealth would arrive in Madīnah Munawwarah, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would distribute it among the poor. He would bilhassa give those who were new Muslims, those whose iman was zayıf and those who were prone to begging. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not give bazı of the Ṣaḥābah because he knew that they were content with what bütünāh had given them and did not ask from others. Wealth and possessions are not a reflection of the honour and salih amel of an individual.

527.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin by spending on your family (before others). The best sadaka is that which leaves the giver with sufficient. Allah (ﷻ) makes a person self-sufficient who desires to abstain from begging; and Allah (ﷻ) grants independence to a person who desires independence."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
527.commentary: Bu hadis has been comprehensively discussed in a previous chapter. See hadis 296. bununla birlikte, with reference to this chapter, it bize öğretir ki one should not spend in charity to such an extent that oneself and one's family are left to beg from others. It also encourages us to develop güven in bütünāh and exercise sabır, instead of requesting for assistance from others. başka bir deyişle, one should strive to be content and independent.

528.narrator: Mu'āwiyah ibn Abū Sufyān (رضي الله عنهما)
528.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not be persistent in asking. By Allāh, a person who asks me for something and his asking makes me give him, but I dislike doing so, will not be blessed in what I give him."(Müslüman)
528.commentary: Bu hadis discourages us from being persistent when requesting help from others because one who is forced to give is overpowered by feelings of resentment and bitterness. The hadis bize öğretir ki charity, which is given with a joyous heart, has tremendous blessings. Imām Ghazālī (رحمه الله) stated that asking from others would only be helal when three şartlar are fulfilled: The one who asks should maintain his self-haysiyet and saygı. One should not be persistent when asking. The one whose assistance is sought should not be inconvenienced.

529.narrator: Abū 'Abd al-Raḥmān 'Auf ibn Mālik al-Ashja'ī (رضي الله عنه)
529.text: We were sitting with Resûlullah (ﷺ) and there were nine, eight or seven of us. He sordu: 'Are you not going to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allāh?' whereas we had just recently pledged allegiance to him [at 'Aqabah]. We cevap verdi: 'We have already pledged allegiance to you, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He sordu: 'Are you not going to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allāh?' So we extended our hands and dedi: 'We have pledged allegiance to you, O Messenger of Allāh. On what basis should we pledge allegiance to you?' He dedi: 'That you ibadet Allāh and not ascribe any partners with Him, offer the five namazs and obey.' He then dedi something softly: 'And that you do not ask anything from people.' I later saw one of those people. He had dropped his whip and he did not ask anyone to pick it up for him."(Müslüman)
529.commentary: In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) instructed the Ṣaḥābah not to ask for wealth from others because independence contributes towards noble character, sabır and self-saygı. The Ṣaḥābah, bununla birlikte, interpreted his instruction in a more genel sense and abstained from asking anything from others. The narrator provided the example of an insignificant object like a whip to indicate that in matters of greater önem they would also not ask others for assistance. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said the last portion of the pledge quietly because it was not a genel pledge, but limited to a az sayıda Ṣaḥābah only.

530.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If any of you continues begging from people, he will meet Allah (ﷻ) without any flesh on his face."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
530.commentary: Bu hadis demektir ki a person who asks of others unnecessarily will be brought on the day of Qiyāmah in a state of disgrace and humiliation - he will have no face before bütünāh. It could also be interpreted literally to mean that such a person will have no flesh on his face as a azap for turning his face to others. This is based on other aḥādīth that state that azap will be meted out to that limb of a person's body with which he had sinned.

531.text: While Resûlullah (ﷺ) was on the pulpit speaking about sadaka and abstaining from begging, he dedi:"The upper-hand is better than the lower-hand. The upper-hand is the hand that spends and the lower-hand is the hand that begs."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
531.commentary: Benzer ifadeli bir hadis önceki bölümlerde geçmiştir. Bkz. hadis 296 ve 527.

532.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who begs from people merely to acquire more mal is asking for a hot coal. So he may ask for less or more."(Müslüman)
532.commentary: Dilenen kişi "bir kor parçası istemiş olur" yani bu yolla elde ettiği her şey ahirette onun için bir azap sebebi olacaktır.

533.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Begging is an injurious act by which a person peels his face, except in a case where he asks from the ruler or when he has no choice."(Tirmidhī)
533.commentary: Requesting for financial assistance from the ruler of an Islāmic state would be helal because he is obliged to serve his subjects and assist them from the public treasury in the form of zakāh, if there is a genuine need. Similarly, a person who is in a crisis and has nothing to see to his basic needs will be permitted to ask the help of others. This applies in cases where bütün of one's possessions were destroyed in a natural disaster, one is unable to work and earn a living due to ill-health, or one is exceptionally poor.

534.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who is afflicted with fakirlik and presents his needs to people, will not be relieved of his fakirlik. One who presents his needs to Allah (ﷻ), then Allah (ﷻ) will grant him sustenance sooner or later."(Abū Dāwūd)
534.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to seek bütünāh's help and focus towards Him at times of difficulty because He will undoubtedly assist. It bize öğretir ki it is irrational to direct our attention to people, who are powerless and helpless and thereby forget bütünāh, who is bütün-Powerful and able to fulfil the needs of bütün His creation without any deficiency resulting in His treasures. The hadis may also mean that a person who asks from people for little things will soon do so for major things, causing him to overlook bütünāh altogether. Such a person will remain a beggar for life because he has not recognised bütünāh, the Supreme Provider.

535.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Is there anyone who will guarantee me that he will not ask anything from people and I will in turn guarantee him Cennet?"I dedi:"I."Thaubān (رضي الله عنه) then never sordu anyone for anything. (Abū Dāwūd)
535.commentary: Bu hadise dayanarak âlimler, insanlardan istemeyen kimsenin, bu talebini kabul edilmeyen bir duaya dönüştürmesi halinde mükâfatlandırılacağını belirtmişlerdir.

536.narrator: Abū Bishr Qabīṣah ibn al-Mukhāriq (رضي الله عنه)
536.text: I assumed responsibility for a debt in order to make peace between two parties. I came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) to ask him for assistance in settling it. He dedi: 'Wait until we receive sadaka and we will give you from it.' He then dedi: 'O Qabīṣah! Begging is only permissible for three types of people: One who assumes responsibility for a debt in order to reconcile between disputing parties. For him begging is permissible until he acquires an amount sufficient to settle the debt, after which he should desist. One who is afflicted by a calamity that destroys his mal. For him begging is permissible until he acquires sufficient sustenance. One who is afflicted by fakirlik which three intelligent people from his community attest to by diyerek: 'So-and-so has been afflicted by fakirlik.' For him begging is permissible until he acquires sufficient sustenance. All other forms of begging, O Qabīṣah, are forbidden and whoever engages in them consumes forbidden mal.'"(Müslüman)
536.commentary: Bu hadis clearly spells out that begging is only helal in three situations and is prohibited in bütün others. The first is when a person assumes responsibility for a debt in order to settle a dispute. In this noble act, the person pays from his own wealth. It is helal for him to beg until he settles the debt. The second is when a natural calamity destroys a person's wealth and possessions and he is left with nothing. It is helal for him to beg until he is able to meet his basic needs. The third is when a person is exceptionally poor and this is teyit edilen to by three intelligent people. It is helal for him to beg until he meets his basic needs.

537.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A poor person is not one who can be turned away by a date or two, or a morsel or two; rather, a poor person is one who does not have enough for himself, but does not disclose it so that sadaka could be given to him, nor does he go around begging from people."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
537.commentary: The hadis bize öğretir ki a truly poor person, who is worthy of being assisted, is one who has the qualities of self-honour and sabır and does not go around begging.

538.narrator: Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar from his father (ra)
538.text: Sālim ibn 'Abdillāh ibn 'Umar anlatır from his father 'Abdullāh ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما) who dedi:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to give me a gift and I would say: 'Give it to someone who is more in need of it than I am.' He would say: 'Take it. When any such mal comes to you without you hankering after it nor asking for it, then you should take it and include it as part of your mal. If you then so choose, you may eat of it or you may give it in sadaka. But whatever does not come to you, do not hanker after it.' Sālim anlatır:"'Abdullāh (رضي الله عنه) would therefore not ask anyone for anything, nor would he refuse anything that was given to him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
538.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is helal for a person to accept wealth yani given to him without him desiring it or asking for it. He should, bununla birlikte, ensure that it is from a ḥalāl source and it is not given as a bribe. It is also not helal to accept anything from such a ruler whose major portion of wealth is ḥarām, or who does not give those who are deserving of it.

539.narrator: Abū 'Abdillāh al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwām (رضي الله عنه)
539.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"It is better for one of you to take his ropes and go to a mountain and to then bring back a bundle of firewood on his back and sell it so that Allah (ﷻ) thereby saves his face from disgrace, than begging from people who may give him or refuse."(Bukhārī)
539.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is far superior to earn a living through hard work than to go around requesting for assistance from people. Islām greatly stresses upon the haysiyet and honour of a insanî being and protects these values by encouraging a lifestyle of self-sufficiency.

540.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"It is better for one of you to load a bundle of firewood on his back than to beg from someone who may give him or refuse."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
540.commentary: Bu hadis reinforces the önem of earning a living through hard work rather than begging from others.

541.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Dāwūd (عليه السلام) would not eat anything except what he earned with his own hands."(Bukhārī)
541.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to emulate the example of the Messengers (عليهم السلام), who lived on what they earned with their own hands. Dāwūd (عليه السلام), despite being a powerful ruler and having everything at his disposal, used to manufacture armour and sell it. The Qur'ān states that bütünāh (ﷻ) had made iron soft for him.

542.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Zakarīyyā (عليه السلام) was a carpenter."(Müslüman)
542.commentary: Bu hadis highlights the goodness of earning a living by engaging in a craft. Engaging in manual labour or occupying oneself in a craft in order to earn a living should asla be regarded as a defect or weakness because the Messengers also earned a living in this şekil. Other aḥādīth teach us that bütün the Messengers looked after sheep. Ādam (عليه السلام) did farming, Nūḥ (عليه السلام) was a carpenter, Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) and Mūsā (عليه السلام) sold sheep and Sulaimān (عليه السلام) sold fish.

543.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"No person has ever eaten any better food than that which he eats as a result of working with his own hands. The Messenger of Allāh, Dāwūd (عليه السلام), used to eat from the earnings of his own hands."(Bukhārī)
543.commentary: Earning a living by utilising a skill or craft does not contradict tawakkul (tevekkül upon bütünāh). aslında, it is the essence of tawakkul when one utilises the means and acknowledges the One who has created and provided those means, şöyle ki bütünāh (ﷻ).

544.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Envy is not lawful except with regard to two people: a person whom Allah (ﷻ) has granted mal and he spends it in the path of truth; and a person whom Allah (ﷻ) granted wisdom and he gives judgments by it and teaches it."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
544.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is meritorious to desire the good that others have been blessed with. Such a desire is synonymous to competing in iyilikler and has been praised in the Qur'ān. "Spending it in the yol of truth," işaret eder a person spending his wealth in noble causes which please bütünāh (ﷻ) gibi for the fayda of family, relatives, orphans, widows, etc. "bütünāh (ﷻ) granting hikmet," işaret eder bütünāh (ﷻ) blessing a person with knowledge and the anlayış of dinî matters.

545.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sordu:"Which of you loves the mal of his heirs more than his own mal?"The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) cevap verdi:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! All of us love our own mal more."He dedi:"A person'in mal is that which he sends forward and the mal of his heirs is that which he leaves behind."(Bukhārī)
545.commentary: In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) posed a question to the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) in order to draw their attention to a vitally important teaching. Man gathers and hoards wealth thinking that it belongs to him, but gerçekte it is passed on to his heirs after his death, bundan dolayı it is not truly his own. Only that wealth, which a person spends in charity or personally faydalar from by yol of food and clothing, is gerçekte his own. bu nedenle, the hadis encourages a person to spend in noble causes so that he may reap the sevap of this in the ahiret.

546.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Safeguard yourselves from cehennem ateşi even if it is by giving half a date (in sadaka)."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
546.commentary: Bu hadis, az da olsa sadaka vermeyi teşvik eder çünkü az sadaka bile kişiyi cehennem ateşinden koruyabilir ve büyük bir sevaptır.

547.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was never sordu for anything to which he cevap verdi: 'No.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
547.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) asla ignored a person who requested him for financial assistance. If he had wealth at his disposal, he would immediately give it. If he did not, he would bazen vaad to give later when wealth came to him, or he would take a loan in order to assist the person asking.

548.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Two angels descend (from the heavens) every morning and one of them says: 'O Allāh, replace for the one who spends,' and the other says: 'O Allāh, destroy the one who withholds.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
548.commentary: Bu hadis passed in a previous chapter. See hadis 295. It encourages us to spend in noble causes and it bize öğretir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) will replenish such spending with a better substitute in dünya or the ahiret.

549.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) dedi: 'Ey Âdemoğlu! Spend, you will be spent on.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
549.commentary: Bu hadis al-Qudsī bize öğretir ki one who spends for the sake of bütünāh (ﷻ) will be granted a substitute in dünya for his spending and he will be handsomely rewarded in the ahiret.

550.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
550.text: A man sordu Resûlullah (ﷺ):"What are the best of actions in İslâm?"He cevap verdi:"To give food and to extend the salām to those you know and those you do not know."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
550.commentary: Bu hadis, insanları doyurmayı ve selamlaşmayı teşvik eder çünkü bu davranışlar sevgiyi artırır ve toplumu kaynaştırır.

551.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
551.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There are forty good qualities, the highest of which is to loan one'in goat to another person. If any person practises upon any of these qualities hoping for their sevap and affirming what has been promised for doing them, Allah (ﷻ) will admit him into Cennet on account of it."(Bukhārī)
551.commentary: Bu hadis has been discussed previously. See hadis 138. Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) stated that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not stipulate the forty good qualities so that a person would engage in her form of good, without thinking it to be insignificant.

552.narrator: Ebû Ümâme Ṣudayy ibn 'Ajlān (رضي الله عنه)
552.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Ey Âdemoğlu! To spend your excess mal is better for you and to withhold it is harmful to you. You will not be reprimanded for keeping back what you need. Begin by spending on your dependents. The upper-hand is better than the lower-hand."(Müslüman)
552.commentary: A hadis with benzer wording passed in a previous chapter. See hadis 527. It encourages us to spend in noble causes and discourages us from begging. It emphasises that withholding wealth is harmful because one will be held accountable for doing so and it will be of no fayda when one requires it çoğu.

553.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was never sordu anything in the name of İslâm without giving it. A man came to him and he gave him sheep that would have filled the space between two mountains. He returned to his people and dedi: 'O my people! Embrace İslâm, for Muhammed (ﷺ) gives like a person who does not korku fakirlik.' Even if a person would embrace İslâm for material motives only, İslâm would soon become more beloved to him than this world and what is in it."(Müslüman)
553.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the generosity of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), who sık sık gave people in order to ssık sık their hearts and would asla ignore a request for assistance. Bilāl (رضي الله عنه) mentioned that if a poorly dressed Muslim came to him, he (ﷺ) would instruct Bilāl (رضي الله عنه) to obtain a loan with which he could purchase a cloak to clothe him and he would also feed him.

554.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) distributed some mal and I dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Others are more deserving of it than these people.' He dedi: 'They gave me two alternatives: they could have either sordu me in a very crude manner or they could have labelled me as a miser and I am not a miser.'"(Müslüman)
554.commentary: In this hadis, 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) requested the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) for an açıklama why he gave booty to bazı people and not to others. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained that the Bedouins requested him for assistance in a very uncouth şekil because of the weakness of their iman and if he did not give them, they would have labelled him as a miser. He preferred to give them based on the wise assumption that they would then be inclined to Islām.

555.text: While he was travelling with Resûlullah (ﷺ) on his return from Ḥunayn, the Bedouins latched onto to him. They began soliciting something from him to such an extent that they forced him back against a thorny ağaç which pulled off his rıda. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) stopped and şöyle dedi: 'Give me back my rıda. If I had as many camels as the number of these trees, I would have certainly distributed them among you and you would not have found me to be a miser, a liar or a coward.'"(Bukhārī)
555.commentary: From this hadis, we learn of the Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) merhamet, goodwill and forbearance in the face of aggression and impolite behaviour. Miserliness, dishonesty and cowardice are undesirable qualities. It is helal for a person to enumerate his good qualities at a time of need and out of korku that those who are uneducated may get a yanlış impression of him, if he does not do so.

556.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Charity does not diminish mal in any way, pardoning another causes Allah (ﷻ) to increase one'in honour and Allāh elevates a person who humbles himself for Allāh'in (ﷻ) pleasure."(Müslüman)
556.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to adopt three noble qualities: giving in charity, forgiving others and being humble. Even though charity means to part with one's wealth for the pleasure of bütünāh (ﷻ), it does not decrease a person's wealth because bütünāh (ﷻ) places blessings therein and grants him a substitute in dünya, ayrıca to the rewards he will receive in the ahiret.

557.narrator: Abū Kabshah Sa'd al-Anmārī (رضي الله عنه)
557.text: He heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"There are three things on which I take an oath and I am telling you something, so remember it. The mal of a person does not diminish because of sadaka. No person is treated unjustly and exercises sabır thereupon without Allah (ﷻ) increasing him in honour. No person opens the door of begging without Allah (ﷻ) opening for him the door of fakirlik,"or words to this effect."I am telling you something, so remember it. He dedi:"This world consists of four types of people: a person whom Allah (ﷻ) blessed with mal and knowledge and he fears his Sustainer with regard to it, he maintains ties of kinship with it and he acknowledges Allāh'in (ﷻ) right over it. Such a person enjoys the most superior position. Then there is a person whom Allah (ﷻ) blessed with knowledge but not with mal. He is truthful in his intention and says, 'If I had mal, I would have done as so-and-so did.' He is considered according to his intention, so the sevap of both of them is the same. Then there is a person whom Allah (ﷻ) blessed with mal but not with knowledge. He acts rashly with his mal, without knowledge. He does not korku his Sustainer with regard to it, he does not maintain ties of kinship with it and he does not acknowledge Allāh'in (ﷻ) right over it. Such a person is in the worst of positions. Then there is a person whom Allah (ﷻ) neither blessed with mal nor knowledge and he says: 'If I had mal, I would have done as so-and-so did.' He is considered according to his intention and the günah of both of them is the same."(Tirmidhī)
557.commentary: Bu hadis discusses four types of individuals: 1. One who is blessed with wealth and knowledge. He expresses his gratitude for this and fulfils the haklar of his wealth by spending on his family, giving zakāh and ṣadaqah. He en hayırlısıdır people. 2. One who is blessed with knowledge but owns nothing of dünya. On account of his knowledge he makes an niyet to spend in the yol of bütünāh (ﷻ) if he is ever blessed with wealth. He receives the same sevap as the first person because of his noble niyet. 3. One who is blessed with wealth but has no knowledge. He squanders his wealth in futile ventures and does not give in zakāh or spend on the poor. He is the worst of people. 4. One who neither has wealth nor knowledge. Due to his foolishness he makes an niyet to squander his wealth if he is ever blessed with it. He will be dealt with in the same yol as the third person because of his evil niyet.

558.text: They slaughtered a koyun and Resûlullah (ﷺ) sordu:"How much of it is ayrıldı?"She cevap verdi:"The only portion ayrıldı of it is its shoulder."He (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"All of it is ayrıldı except its shoulder."(Tirmidhī)
558.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to spend in ṣadaqah. 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) mentioned that they slaughtered a sheep and distributed bütün of it in ṣadaqah except its shoulder. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) then explained to them that, while the shoulder portion was with them it would not fayda them in the şekil that the rest of what they had spent in ṣadaqah would, as the latter was a perpetual form of sevap for them in the ahiret.

559.narrator: Asmā' bint Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (رضي الله عنهما)
559.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Do not withhold mal or it will be withheld from you.'"Another narration has:"Spend, or give out, or give away. Do not withhold by counting your mal or Allah (ﷻ) will withhold His treasures from you. Do not withhold mal or Allāh will withhold it from you."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
559.commentary: The emir not to count wealth demektir ki one should not hoard one's wealth by being engrossed in counting it, or else bütünāh (ﷻ) will similarly grant wealth in limited measure. It could also mean that one should not be miserly in giving a beggar, or else bütünāh (ﷻ) will also sevap a person in limited measure.

560.text: He heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"The similitude of a miser and a charitable person is like that of two men wearing a steel armour from their upper chests to their collar bones. When the charitable person gives in sadaka, his armour stretches over his body until it covers his nails and erases his footsteps. When the miser intends to give in sadaka, every link of the armour remains firmly in its place. He tries to loosen it but it does not become loose."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
560.commentary: Bu hadis excellently explains the difference between a charitable person and a miser by using the example of a soldier in armour. The armour of the first person expands over his bütün body allowing him to move freely against the enemy without korku. The second person's armour remains confined to his chest, exposing the rest of his body to the enemy whilst his hands are shackled to his neck. The example bize öğretir ki a charitable person is comfortable and pleased to spend, while a miser is annoyed and reluctant to do so.

561.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who gives in sadaka, equal to a date, from lawful earnings - and Allah (ﷻ) only accepts that which is lawful - Allah (ﷻ) accepts it with His right hand and then increases it for the giver just as one of you brings up his foal, until (that single date) grows as large as a mountain."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
561.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to spend from wealth yani earned from lawful sources. bütünāh (ﷻ) accepts such ṣadaqah and multiplies the giver's sevap manifold in the ahiret. The Qur'ān states: "Who will give bütünāh a handsome loan, so that He may grant him a manifold increase in it." When a foal is nurtured in the doğru şekil, it grows into a powerful horse, similarly ṣadaqah yani given in the doğru şekil, grows and multiples in sevap.

562.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A man was walking in a desert land when he heard a voice from a cloud diyerek: 'Go and irrigate the orchard of so-and-so person.' So the cloud moved and poured out its water onto a rocky ground, and a water channel then gathered all the water. The man followed the water and found a man standing in his orchard, guiding the water with his spade. So he sordu him: 'O kul of Allāh! What is your name?' He cevap verdi, 'I am so-and-so,' and he gave the same name which the person had heard from the cloud. The man then sordu him: 'O kul of Allāh! Why did you ask me my name?' The man cevap verdi: 'I heard a voice from a cloud from which this water came down, diyerek:"Irrigate the orchard of so-and-so,"and your name was mentioned. What do you do in your orchard?' The man cevap verdi: 'Now that you have sordu, (I can tell you that) I estimate the produce of this land and I give one third of it in sadaka. I and my family eat from one third of it and I re-invest one third of it back into the orchard.'"(Müslüman)
562.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us the fazilet of spending in ṣadaqah. bütünāh (ﷻ) assisted the owner of the orchard by causing rain to fall in his orchard because he spent on the poor and destitute and bütünāh (ﷻ) loves those who spend in His yol. Scholars say that a person should earmark a portion of his income for ṣadaqah in advance because Shaiṭān sık sık persuades a person not to spend in charity, if he does not do so on a scheduled basis.

563.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Abstain from oppression because oppression will be a cause of intense darkness on the day of Kıyamet. Abstain from greed because it destroyed those before you. It prompted them to shed blood and to consider as lawful all that was made unlawful to them."(Müslüman)
563.commentary: Bu hadis has been discussed in a previous chapter. See hadis 203. The hadis demektir ki an oppressor will be engulfed in darkness on the day of Qiyāmah. He will not be guided on the yol of salvation on that day, while the believers will have the light of guidance on bütün sides. Greed and miserliness are responsible for initiating a host of other günahlar. They generate enmity between people and cause them to break ties of kinship and unity.

564.text: A man came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"I am suffering (due to hunger)."So Resûlullah (ﷺ) sent someone to one of his wives, but she cevap verdi:"By the One who sent you with the truth, I have nothing but water."Then he sent to another wife, who dedi the same thing, until all of them had dedi:"By the One who sent you with the truth, I have nothing but water."The Prophet (ﷺ) then dedi:"Who will host this person tonight?"A man from the Anṣār dedi:"I, O Messenger of Allāh."He then took him to his home and dedi to his wife:"Honour the guest of Resûlullah (ﷺ)."In another narration, he dedi to his wife:"Do you have anything?"She cevap verdi:"No, only my children'in food."He dedi:"Distract them with something and when they want their supper, put them to sleep. When our guest enters, extinguish the lamp and show him that we are eating."So they sat down and the guest ate, while they spent the night hungry. When morning came, he went to Peygamber (ﷺ), who dedi:"Allāh was amazed by what you and your wife did for your guest tonight."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
564.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the exemplary generosity and selflessness of the Anṣār. Despite having only enough food for their children, this couple gave preference to their guest over themselves. Their amel was so pleasing to bütünāh (ﷻ) that He was amazed by their hospitality. The verse "They give preference to others over themselves even though they are themselves in need" was revealed concerning this incident.

565.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Food for two is sufficient for three and food for three is sufficient for four."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) A narration of Müslüman from Jābir (رضي الله عنه) states that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"Food for one is sufficient for two, food for two is sufficient for four and food for four is sufficient for eight."
565.commentary: Bu hadis discusses the fazilet of eating in a group. Eating together creates merhamet between Muslims and the resulting communal spirit draws ilâhî blessings which makes a limited quantity of food sufficient for bütün those who partake of it. This teaching also subdues and overpowers the carnal self, which encourages man to hoard things for himself.

566.text: We were once on a journey with Resûlullah (ﷺ) when a man on a camel arrived and began looking to his right and left. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'Whoever has an extra conveyance should give it to someone who has no conveyance and whoever has extra provisions should give them to someone who has no provisions.' He mentioned various types of mal to the extent that we felt that none of us had any right to anything in excess of our basic needs."(Müslüman)
566.commentary: Bu hadis stresses upon the need for Muslims to assist her biri other as a collective entity. The wealthy should assist the poor, the güçlü should assist the zayıf and those with means should assist those who do not have means. Special attention should also be given to those travellers who are stranded and do not have food and means to continue their journey.

567.text: A woman brought a woven shawl to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and şöyle dedi: 'I wove it with my own hands so that you could wear it.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) accepted it from her as he was in need of it. Later on, he geldi to us wearing it as a loincloth and someone şöyle dedi: 'This shawl is so beautiful. Give it to me to wear.' He (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'Yes.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then oturdu down in the assembly. After some time he döndü ev, folded it and gönderdi it to him. The insanlar şöyle dedi to him: 'Your action was not appropriate. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) giydi it out of need and you sordu him for it knowing that he never refuses a request!' The man cevap verdi: 'By Allāh, I did not ask him for it in order to wear it. I sordu him for it so that it could be my burial shroud.' Sahl (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi:"And it was indeed his burial shroud."(Bukhārī)
567.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the generosity and noble character of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). It is helal to derive fayda from the relics of the pious. Exchanging gifts creates mutual sevgi and unity. One should not refuse a gift without a geçerli reason. It is meritorious to continuously ponder over death.

568.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"It was the habit of the Ash'arites that when their provisions on an expedition were depleted or when their families in Madīnah ran short of food, they would gather whatever they had in one cloth and then distribute it equally in each person'in utensil. They are from me and I am from them."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
568.commentary: Bu hadis explains one of the noble practises of the Ash'arī tribe. During times of need, they would gather bütün their possessions and then distribute it equally between themselves so that those who had more would share with those who had less. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) praised this quality saying that they were benzer in davranış and ibadet to him.

569.text: A drink was brought to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he drank some of it. On his right was a young boy and on his left were old people. So he dedi to the young boy: 'Do you grant me permission to give it to them?' The young boy cevap verdi: 'No. By Allāh, I will not give preference to anyone regarding my share from you,' so Resûlullah (ﷺ) placed it in his hand."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
569.commentary: The young boy in this incident was 'Abdullāh ibn 'Abbās (رضي الله عنهما). He did not permit the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) to give preference to the older people because he was eager to fayda from the blessings of the leftover drink of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). This was an indication of his intelligence and sahih judgment. The fact that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not merely ignore the young boy, but respectfully asked him to relinquish his doğru in favour of the older people, işaret eder the Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) exceptional sense of adalet.

570.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"While Ayyūb (عليه السلام) was having a bath in the nude, locusts of gold began falling onto him and he began gathering them in his clothes. Allah (ﷻ) called out to him: 'O Ayyūb! Did I not make you independent of these things that you see?' He cevap verdi: 'Yes, by Your honour, but I can never be independent of Your nimetler.'"(Bukhārī)
570.commentary: In this hadis, Ayyūb (عليه السلام) explained that he did not gather the golden locusts out of sevgi and greed for wealth, but because he wanted to fayda from the blessings of bütünāh (ﷻ) that were being showered upon him. It bize öğretir ki we may acquire wealth if we utilise it correctly and fayda others thereby. One who is wealthy should also express gratitude that bütünāh (ﷻ) has made him independent of others.

571.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Envy is not lawful except with regard to two people: a person whom Allah (ﷻ) has granted mal and he spends it in the path of truth; and a person whom Allah (ﷻ) granted wisdom and he gives judgments by it and teaches it."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
571.commentary: Bu hadis daha önceki bir bölümde ele alınmıştır. Bkz. hadis 544.

572.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Envy is not lawful except with regard to two people: a person whom Allah (ﷻ) has given the Kur'an and he upholds it day and night; and a person whom Allah (ﷻ) has given mal and he spends it day and night."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
572.commentary: Bu hadis mentions the fazilet of a wealthy person who is also generous. It also states the önem of adhering to the Qur'ān at bütün times. The sözler of the hadis encourage us to recite the Qur'ān, teach its sözler, understand its anlam, ponder over its message, issue verdicts by its laws and practise upon its teachings.

573.text: The poor Muhājirūn came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"The wealthy people have appropriated high ranks and eternal bounties."He sordu:"How is that?"They dedi:"They perform namaz as we perform namaz and they fast as we fast, but they give sadaka and we do not give sadaka and they free slaves and we do not free slaves."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"Should I not teach you something by which you can reach those who went ahead of you and outshine those who will come after you, and none will be better than you except one who does the same as you do?"They cevap verdi:"Please do, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!"He dedi:"You should glorify Allāh (i.e. say subḥānallāh), praise Allāh (i.e. say alḥamdulillāh) and express the greatness of Allāh (i.e. say Allāhu akbar) thirty-three times each after every namaz."These poor Muhājirūn then returned to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"Our wealthy brothers heard of what we were doing and they did the same."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"That is the bounty of Allāh which He gives to whoever He wills."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
573.commentary: In this hadis, we learn of the poor Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) complaining to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) that they matched the wealthy Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) in bodily forms of ibadet, but that the latter excelled in monetary forms of ibadet due to their wealth. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained to them that reciting subḥānallāh, alḥamdulillāh and bütünāhu akbar thirty-three times her biri after her Farḍ Ṣalāh equals the sevap of spending in ṣadaqah and freeing slaves.

574.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) aldı hold of my shoulders and şöyle dedi: 'Live in this world as if you are a yabancı or one who is travelling on a path.' Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما) used to say: 'In the evening, do not expect to see the morning and in the morning, do not expect to see the evening. Prepare for your illness while you are healthy and prepare for your death while you are living.'"(Bukhārī)
574.commentary: Bu hadis has been discussed previously. See hadis 471. It explains that man is gerçekte a stranger in dünya. The initial abode of his ancestors, Ādam and Ḥawwā (عليهما السلام), was cennet and he will return to cennet through the rahmet of bütünāh (ﷻ). başka bir deyişle, man's life in dünya is like that of a traveller who is far from his home. tıpkı... gibi a traveller carries very little belongings on a trip, man should not attach too much önem to the goods and luxuries of dünya. The sözler of Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما) teach us that we should be prepared for death at bütün times. We should not procrastinate regarding tövbe and doing iyilikler because death may overtake us at any time.

575.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"It is not correct for a Müslüman who has anything to bequeath to spend two nights without having a written will in his possession."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) This is the wording of Bukhārī. A narration of Müslüman has:"To spend three nights."Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما) dedi:"Not a single night has passed since I heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek this, without my having my will with me."
575.commentary: Bu hadis teaches that a believer should have his bequests written down. Scholars explain that to do so is Mustaḥab (advisable). bununla birlikte, concerning the haklar of others, gibi debts and trusts in one's possession, it is compulsory to have these written down so that it does not result in oppression and injustice after a person's death. While the hadis states "two nights," scholars have stated that it işaret eder a short period of time. başka bir deyişle, one should not delay in drawing up a will.

576.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) drew some lines and şöyle dedi: 'This is man and this is his death. He is occupied in his aspirations when suddenly the closest line (i.e. death) comes upon him.'"(Bukhārī)
576.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki man is inclined towards developing aspirations and hopes for the future, bununla birlikte death reaches him before these are realised. A person should, bu nedenle, prepare for the ahiret and not be deceived by life's aspirations.

577.text: On one occasion, Resûlullah (ﷺ) drew a square and then drew a line through the middle of it which extended beyond it. He then drew small lines from the side within up to the middle line. He then şöyle dedi,"This (middle line) represents man, and these (four sides of the square) which encircle him - or by which he is encircled - represent his life-span. The line that extends beyond the square represents his hopes and these small lines represent afflictions. If one of these misses him, the next one will get him, and if this one misses him, the next one will get him."(Bukhārī)
577.commentary: In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) perfectly explained the reality of life. Man is engulfed by his death; bununla birlikte, his aspirations encourage him to live as if he will asla die. He is continuously faced with events and occurrences that are linked with death gibi illness, old age, weakness and accidents, but he chooses to remain oblivious of his eventual fate. By means of this illustration, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained the need to abstain from long-drawn ambitions in life and to rather do iyilikler and prepare for life after death.

578.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Hasten with good deeds before seven things overtake you. Are you waiting for fakirlik that makes you forgetful; or affluence that makes you transgress; or illness that disables you; or old age that makes you senile; or sudden death; or Dajjāl and what an evil unseen creation that is to be; or the Final Hour, which will be terrible and most bitter?"(Tirmidhī)
578.commentary: Bu hadis passed in a previous chapter. See hadis 98. It identifies çeşitli circumstances of life that sık sık prevent a person from doing iyilikler. In essence, the hadis conveys the önem of utilising available time and opportunities for engaging in beneficial ameller. The wealthy are told to obey bütünāh (ﷻ) because poverty sık sık causes a person to beg and forget bütünāh (ﷻ). The poor are told to obey bütünāh (ﷻ) and not to desire wealth because wealth frequently leads a person to transgress the laws of Islām. The healthy are told to obey bütünāh (ﷻ) because if they are afflicted with illness they will not have the physical strength to engage in ibadet. The young are told to obey bütünāh (ﷻ) because old age weakens a person physically and mentally, making it difficult to ibadet bütünāh.

579.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Abundantly remember the destroyer of pleasures."In other words, death. (Tirmidhī)
579.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us to remember death frequently. Scholars say that one should do so by contemplating about it, discussing it and visualising it. This final form is the ultimate and çoğu useful in discouraging one from sinning. The faydalar of remembering death are birçok: it makes one prepare for death; it draws one away from the sevgi of this fleeting world; it encourages one to engage in good ameller; it leads one to repent from günah; and it prevents one from oppressing others and usurping their haklar.

580.text: When one third of the night had passed, Resûlullah (ﷺ) would stand up and say: 'O people! Remember Allāh. The rājifah (the first blowing of the Trumpet) has come and it will be followed by the rādifah (the second blowing of the Trumpet). Death has come with all that it comprises. Death has come with all that it comprises.' I sordu: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! I send abundant salutations upon you. How much of my time should I dedicate for you?' He cevap verdi: 'As much as you like.' I sordu: 'A quarter?' He cevap verdi: 'As much as you like, but if you do more, it will be better for you.' I sordu: 'A half?' He cevap verdi: 'As much as you like, but if you do more, it will be better for you.' I sordu: 'Two-thirds?' He cevap verdi: 'As much as you like, but if you do more, it will be better for you.' I sordu: 'Can I dedicate all my time in sending salutations upon you?' He dedi: 'If you do so, your worries will be removed and your günahlar forgiven.'"(Tirmidhī)
580.commentary: Bu hadis explains that Qiyāmah is close because the time of the blowing of the trumpet is close. It also explains two faziletler of sending salutations (durūd) upon the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ): a person is relieved of worries and his günahlar are forgiven. Relief from worries by reciting durūd is explained by a hadis that states that one who recites a single durūd is rewarded by bütünāh (ﷻ) with ten durūds. These ten durūds are in the form of bütünāh's (ﷻ) mercies and His pleasure and one who is blessed with these can asla be anxious, depressed or unhappy.

581.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"I used to prohibit you from visiting graves, but now visit them."(Müslüman) Another narration has:"So one who wishes to visit graves should do so because it reminds us of ahiret."
581.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) originally forbade the Muslims from visiting the graves of the deceased because of their closeness to the era of ignorance. He feared that their reverence of tombs and excessive lamentation over the deceased would lead them back towards haram practices. bununla birlikte, when their iman and inanç in bütünāh (ﷻ) became firm and unshakeable, this yasak was lifted. The hadis explains that the reason for the allowance to visit graves is that it serves as a beneficial reminder of death and the ahiret.

582.text: Whenever it was her turn with Resûlullah (ﷺ), he would go to al-Baqī' in the latter part of the night and say: 'Peace be upon you, O abode of the müminler! That which you were promised for tomorrow has come to you. If Allāh wills, we will join you. O Allāh, bağışla the dwellers of Baqī' al-Gharqad.'"(Müslüman)
582.commentary: Baqī' al-Gharqad is the famous graveyard in Madīnah. Gharqad is the name of a thorny tree which grew in the graveyard, bundan dolayı the graveyard was named after it. It contains the graves of ten thousand Ṣaḥābah, according to Imām Mālik (رحمه الله). From this hadis, we learn that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) regularly visited the graveyard and supplicated for the deceased.

583.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) taught them that when they went to the graveyards they should say:"Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the abode of müminler and Müslümans. If Allāh wills, we will join you. I ask Allāh for well-being for us and for you."(Müslüman)
583.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us the Sunnah du'ā' to be made for the deceased when one enters a graveyard. According to a narration of Ibn 'Abbās (رضي الله عنهما), a deceased person replies to the greeting of one who greets him, if they were acquainted with her biri other in their dünyevî lives. The hadis also bize öğretir ki the du'ā' of the living faydalar the dead.

584.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by some graves in Madīnah. He turned his face towards them and dedi:"Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the graves! May Allah (ﷻ) bağışla us and you. You preceded us and we will follow."(Tirmidhī)
584.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is advisable to face the grave of the deceased when greeting them. bazı âlimlere göre, this also applies when one is supplicating for the deceased, bununla birlikte according to other scholars, gibi Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله), it is advisable to face the Qiblah when supplicating. Mullā 'Alī Qārī (رحمه الله) stated that when visiting a grave, the bare minimum one should do is recite Sūrah Fātiḥah once and Sūrah Ikhlāṣ thrice. One should then pass the sevap of this to the deceased and supplicate for his or her bağışlanma.

585.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"None of you should desire death because if he is salih, it is possible that he will increase (in good deeds) and if he is a sinner, it is possible that he will repent."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) A narration of Müslüman from Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) states that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"None of you should desire death nor supplicate for it before it comes to him because when a person passes away, his deeds come to an end and the extended life of a mümin accrues good deeds in his favour."
585.commentary: From this hadis, we learn that it is not helal for a person to desire death due to financial difficulties, ill-health or personal problems because this bir işaretidir displeasure with the decree of bütünāh (ﷻ). One should instead be content with the decree of bütünāh (ﷻ) and exercise sabır. One should also not desire death because this closes the doors of tövbe. A Muslim should value and appreciate her moment of life so that he may engage in bazı form of good.

586.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"None of you should desire death because of a difficulty that has afflicted him. If he is constrained to do something, he should say: 'O Allāh, keep me alive as long as life is better for me and make me die if death is better for me.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
586.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki if a believer is overwhelmed with difficulties and feels constrained to desire death, he should instead supplicate to bütünāh (ﷻ) placing his güven in Him as the One who knows what is best. Scholars state that it is helal for a person to supplicate for death as a shahīd (martyr), as 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) used to supplicate: "O bütünāh, grant me martyrdom in Your yol and grant me death in the city of Your Messenger."

587.narrator: Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim (رضي الله عنه)
587.text: We went to visit Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt (رضي الله عنه) when he was ill and had been cauterized in seven places. He dedi: 'Our Sahâbe who went before us left without the world causing any decrease in them. We have acquired so much that we can find no place for it except the soil. If Resûlullah (ﷺ) had not yasakladı us from supplicating for death, I would have supplicated for it.' We went to visit him on another occasion when he was building a wall and he dedi: 'A Müslüman is rewarded for everything he spends except what he builds on this soil.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
587.commentary: Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt (رضي الله عنه) was one of the early Muslims who accepted Islām. He was severely tortured by the disbelievers. In this hadis, he expressed his desire to have passed away with the early Ṣaḥābah who did not accumulate wealth because the excessive wealth he acquired posed a trial for him. He refrained from supplicating for death because of the yasak. His ifade about building on soil indicates that excessive spending on buildings is sakındırılan, unless there is a genuine need.

588.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"The ḥalāl (lawful) is clear and the ḥarām (unlawful) is clear, but between the two there are doubtful things about which many people have no knowledge. Whoever abstains from things which are doubtful has protected his religion and his honour. Whoever gets involved in doubtful things is bound to be involved in the unlawful, just like a shepherd who grazes his sheep near a private sanctuary. He is bound to graze his flock there. Listen! Every king has a private sanctuary and the private sanctuary of Allah (ﷻ) is comprised of those things which He has made unlawful. Listen! There is a piece of flesh in the body, the nature of which is that when it is sound, the entire body will be sound and if it is unhealthy, the entire body will be unhealthy - it is the heart."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
588.commentary: Ḥalāl and ḥarām are clear in the sense that her intelligent person knows the difference between them. Ḥarām includes bütün forms of impermissible söz or ameller, and items gibi pork, urine, flowing blood, etc. Doubtful matters are those that have no clear sign of being either ḥalāl or ḥarām and are not clearly stated in the Qur'ān or Sunnah as such.
