The hadis encourages us to recognise ḥalāl and ḥarām and to abstain from the doubtful. tıpkı... gibi a shepherd fears grazing his sheep near the sanctuary of the king for korku of being punished for trespassing, we should avoid doubtful matters out of korku that they may lead us towards ḥarām. Bu hadis occupies a pivotal role in Islām. bazı scholars regard it as a third of Islām.

589.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) found a date on the road and dedi:"If I did not korku that it is a date of sadaka, I would have eaten it."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
589.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us the önem of exercising caution in matters of doubt. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) asla accepted zakāh or Nafl ṣadaqah for his personal use. It is helal for a person to utilise an object of little value if he finds it in a communal area and is convinced that its owner will not search for it.

590.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"İyilik is good character, while günah is that which creates doubt in your heart and you dislike that people become aware of it."(Müslüman)
590.commentary: The hadis defines salih amel and günah. It bize öğretir ki the best form of salih amel is to be embodied with admirable character. This encompasses, amongst other things, to deal with people with a pleasant countenance, to save others from harm, to be kind and helpful, to sevgi for others what one loves for oneself, to be just and to give preference to others over oneself. günah is defined as having two attributes. It creates doubts and uneasiness within a person that he is committing a günah, and it leads to a korku that one will be embarrassed if others get to know about it.

591.text: I came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he dedi: 'Have you come to ask about salih amel?' I cevap verdi: 'Yes.' He dedi: 'Ask your heart. İyilik is that with which the soul is at peace and the heart is at peace; and günah is that which creates doubt in the heart and causes hesitation in the chest, even if people give you a verdict, even if people give you a verdict.'"(Aḥmad, al-Dārimī)
591.commentary: In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained an easy yöntem of determining whether one should pursue an amel. One should introspect and contemplate in order to reach the truth, even if others say that the amel is helal. meselâ, if one is faced with the choice of doing business with a person whose income is primarily from ḥarām sources, one should avoid it due to the doubt that he combines his ḥalāl income with that which is ḥarām. bundan dolayı, a dinî verdict may bazen give the izin to proceed in a transaction, but if a person has doubts of its permissibility, taqwā and caution will demand that it be avoided.

592.narrator: Abū Sirwa'ah 'Uqbah ibn al-Ḥārith (رضي الله عنه)
592.text: He married a kız of Abū Ihāb ibn 'Azīz. A woman later geldi to him and şöyle dedi:"I breast-fed 'Uqbah and the woman he married."'Uqbah şöyle dedi:"I did not know that you breast-fed me nor did you tell me."So he gitti to Resûlullah (ﷺ) in Madīnah and sordu him about it. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"How can you remain together when that has been şöyle dedi?"So 'Uqbah (رضي الله عنه) separated from her and married another woman. (Bukhārī)
592.commentary: In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) instructed 'Uqbah ibn al-Ḥārith (رضي الله عنه) to separate from his wife because, having been suckled by the same woman, they were foster brother and sister. His instruction was because of caution and takvâ and is not regarded as binding in other benzer cases because a single woman's testimony does not serve as proof. Imām Aḥmad (رحمه الله) stated that the testimony of a single woman is sufficient to establish a foster relationship and he quotes Bu hadis as proof of his view.

593.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'den şunu öğrendim: "Seni şüphelendiren şeyi bırak, şüphelendirmeyene bak. Doğruluk kalbin huzurudur, yalancılık ise şüphedir." (Tirmizî)
593.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki we should abstain from matters that are doubtful because doubt genellikle develops because of bazı impermissibility or the other. The instruction to abstain is not farz, but based on taqwā and caution.

594.text: Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) had a köle boy who used to earn for him and Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) used to eat from his earnings. One day he brought something and Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) yedi from it. The boy sordu him: 'Biliyor musunuz what that was?' Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) sordu: 'What was that?' He cevap verdi: 'During the days of jāhilīyyah (ignorance) I used to work as an astrologer for a person despite me not having full expertise of astrology. I only deceived him. He met me today and verdi me what you adil yedi, in exchange for the work I did for him.' So Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) inserted his hand in his mouth and vomited out all that was in his stomach."(Bukhārī)
594.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the taqwā of Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه). He vomited bütün that he had consumed from his slave's income because his slave had not only engaged in the haram occupation of astrology, but also deceived his master into believing that he was an expert in the field.

595.text: 'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه) used to allocate an allowance of 4000 for the first grup of Muhājirūn and only 3500 for his oğul. He was told: 'He is also from the Muhājirūn, so why do you give him less?' He cevap verdi: 'His baba also emigrated with him.' He meant that he was not like those who emigrated on their own."(Bukhārī)
595.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the takvâ and caution of 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) in saygı of public funds. He allocated a lesser allowance for his son because the latter had emigrated with his parents at the age of eleven and bu nedenle did not bear the difficulty and challenges of emigrating that others bore.

596.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A person will not achieve the status of the salih until he abstains from that in which there is no harm so that he may be able to save himself from that in which there is harm."(Tirmidhī)
596.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to abstain from doubtful matters. It also bize öğretir ki we should avoid those things that are of no manevî or dünyevî fayda because life is far too valuable to be wasted in trivial pursuits.

597.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
597.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Allah (ﷻ) loves a person who is salih, independent and concealed."(Müslüman)
597.commentary: Bu hadis discusses three excellent qualities of a believer. Firstly, he fears bütünāh (ﷻ) by following His commands and abstaining from His prohibitions. Secondly, he is content with what he has. Thirdly, he secludes himself if there is korku of harm to his iman.

598.text: A man sordu:"Who is the best of people, O Messenger of Allāh?"He cevap verdi:"A mümin who wages cihat in the path of Allah (ﷻ) with his life and his mal."The man sordu:"Then who?"He cevap verdi:"A man who secludes himself in a valley where he worships his Sustainer."Another narration has,"who fears Allah (ﷻ) and saves people from his evil."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
598.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki the best of ameller is jihād for the pleasure of bütünāh (ﷻ). It also bize öğretir ki an era will dawn when a person will be better off secluding himself in a valley so that he can remain safe from the overwhelming günah that will be prevalent amongst people. We also learn that it is advisable for one to isolate oneself from others if he fears that he may harm others from a manevî perspective.

599.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A time will soon come when the best mal of a Müslüman will be some sheep which he will take to the mountain tops and the areas where rain falls, in order to escape and protect his religion from tribulations."(Bukhārī)
599.commentary: This hadis, like the previous one, explains that a time will come when günah will be so yaygın and prevalent that the only avenue of manevî safety will be for a person to take his sheep and flee to the mountains.

600.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Every Messenger sent by Allah (ﷻ) herded sheep."His Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"You as well?"He cevap verdi:"Yes. I used to herd sheep for the people of Makkah in exchange for a few qīrāṭ."(Bukhārī)
600.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki her Messenger, dâhil the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), was a shepherd. Scholars explain çeşitli faydalar of this: 1. It taught the Messengers to be humble and live off a modest salary. 2. It is an teşvik to earn ḥalāl sustenance even if it is little. 3. It develops sabır and forbearance within a person and this is greatly beneficial when one assumes leadership of men. 4. Sheep genellikle scatter and disperse into groups very readily and a shepherd is required to bring them together. This trains him to deal with people of varying temperaments and to unite them in purpose.

601.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One of the best livelihoods for people is that of a man who holds the reins of his horse in the path of Allah (ﷻ) and jumps onto its back. Whenever he hears the sound of battle or danger, he hastens towards it, seeking the opportunity of battle or death; or that of a person who tends to sheep at the top of one of these mountains or at the bottom of one of these valleys, establishing namaz, giving zekât and worshipping his Sustainer until death comes to him. He does not meddle in the affairs of people except in good."(Müslüman)
601.commentary: Bu hadis highlights a number of önem points: 1. One should be trained and prepared for jihād at bütün times. 2. One should resist the attacks of Shaiṭān and control one's base desires. 3. One should live amongst people and fulfil their haklar, bununla birlikte when it becomes extremely difficult to do so because of günah, one should adopt seclusion. 4. One should desire martyrdom. 5. One should help to protect the wealth and lives of other Muslims.

602.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allāh revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one will boast about himself over another and no one will commit injustice over another."(Müslüman)
602.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki our relations with fellow insanî beings should be based on sevgi, softness and iyilik rather than pride and arrogance. People should not regard themselves as superior to others and should not boast over their lineage, financial status or good qualities.

603.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"No sadaka ever decreases any mal; no person ever pardons (another) without Allah (ﷻ) increasing him in honour; and no person ever humbles himself for the sake of Allah (ﷻ) without Allah (ﷻ) elevating him."(Müslüman)
603.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki when a person gives in charity, bütünāh (ﷻ) places blessings in his remaining wealth that compensates for the apparent decrease. Further, bütünāh (ﷻ) will immensely increase his rewards in the ahiret. tevazu for the creation is praiseworthy when it is for bütünāh's (ﷻ) pleasure. bütünāh (ﷻ) will cause such a person to be honoured in the hearts of men and on the tongues of people, and his status will be elevated in the ahiret.

604.text: Anas (رضي الله عنه) passed by some children and greeted them, diyerek:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to do so."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
604.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) greeted children due to his tevazu and simplicity. Greeting children is an effective means of teaching them adab and saygı. The Ṣaḥābah meticulously followed the Sunnah of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ).

605.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to visit the Anṣār. He would greet their çocuklar, gently stroke their heads and supplicate for them."(Nasā'ī)
605.commentary: Greeting children is an effective means of teaching them adab and saygı. Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one should greet subordinates gibi employees and servants. This goes a long yol in eliminating one's sense of superiority and pride. It also bize öğretir ki the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) initiated the salām.

606.text: Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd anlatır: 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) was sordu:"What did Resûlullah (ﷺ) do in his house?"She cevap verdi:"He would serve his family members, but when it was time for namaz, he would go out to offer namaz."(Bukhārī)
606.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) served his family members by milking the goat, patching his clothes, mending his shoes, feeding fodder to their animals and cleaning the home. He would eat with his slave and would carry their goods from the marketplace. These bütün showed his exceptional tevazu and iyilik towards his family.

607.narrator: Abū Rifā'ah Tamīm ibn Usayd (رضي الله عنه)
607.text: I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) while he was delivering a sermon and dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! I am a traveller who has come to ask about his religion because I do not know what my religion is.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) turned towards me, stopped his sermon, and came up to me. A chair was brought and he sat on it, and began teaching me of that which Allah (ﷻ) had taught him. He then continued with his sermon until he completed it."(Müslüman)
607.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) stopped addressing the other Ṣaḥābah and focussed his attention to this Ṣaḥābī in order to teach him the basic essentials of Islām. This again illustrated his merhamet towards people. Scholars agree that if a person asks an essential question regarding īmān or a disbeliever wants to accept Islām, he should be given priority.

608.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) would eat food, he would lick his three fingers. He (the narrator) dedi that he (ﷺ) dedi:"When a morsel of your food falls down, remove the dirt from it and eat it. Do not leave it for Shaiṭān."He (ﷺ) ordered that the bowl be licked and dedi:"You do not know in which part of your food there is nimetler."(Müslüman)
608.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one should humble oneself before the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ). It also bize öğretir ki barakah is attained from consuming her portion of the food and not allowing any of it to go to waste. Not eating a fallen morsel regarding it as shameful bir işaretidir pride. Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) highlighted a number of Sunnah ameller from Bu hadis dâhil licking the fingers, eating with three fingers, picking up a fallen morsel, and licking the utensil.

609.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Every Messenger whom Allah (ﷻ) sent herded sheep."His Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"And you as well?"He cevap verdi:"Yes. I used to herd sheep in exchange for a few qīrāṭ for the people of Makkah."(Bukhārī)
609.commentary: The hadis is relevant to Bu bölüm because herding sheep bir işaretidir simplicity and tevazu. It also bize öğretir ki to earn a living by doing manual work is greatly honourable in the sight of bütünāh (ﷻ) as the Messengers of bütünāh (ﷻ) also did so.

610.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If I were invited for a meal in which a trotter or shoulder (of an animal) was served, I would accept the invitation; and if I were given a trotter or shoulder as a gift, I would accept it."(Bukhārī)
610.commentary: In Bu hadis the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) displayed his tevazu by saying that he would accept an invitation even if it was to a simple meal. Accepting an invitation from those who are poor inculcates tevazu in a person, bundan dolayı the believers are teşvik edilen to adopt this noble uygulama. The hadis also teaches us to accept gifts which are small because this creates joy in the heart of those who cannot afford to give more.

611.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) had a camel called al-'Aḍbā' and it could not be outrun in a race (or could rarely be outrun). A Bedouin came on his camel and outran it in a race. The Müslümans found this difficult to bear, and noticing this, Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi: 'It is the right of Allah (ﷻ) that nothing becomes elevated in this world without Him lowering it.'"(Bukhārī)
611.commentary: The hadis outlines the golden principle that nothing and nobody in dünya is invincible, bundan dolayı to be proud over one's accomplishments or qualities is inappropriate. The only being that enjoys the privilege of being mükemmel is bütünāh (ﷻ). It also bize öğretir ki the world and bütün that it contains is despised in the sight of bütünāh (ﷻ), bundan dolayı an intelligent person will not compete for it, or be proud on account of it.

612.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who has an atom'in weight of kibir in his heart will not enter Cennet."A person sordu:"And (what if) a man likes his clothes and shoes to be beautiful?"He (ﷺ) cevap verdi:"Allāh is beautiful and He loves beauty. Pride means to renounce truth and belittle people."(Müslüman)
612.commentary: In Bu hadis we are taught that bütünāh (ﷻ) dislikes pride, even if it is a little. One who has pride "will not enter cennet" demektir ki he will initially be punished and cleansed of his günah in the ahiret before entering cennet; or one whose pride led him to renounce īmān will forever be deprived of cennet. To boast over one's dressing, wealth, position or any other bounty of bütünāh (ﷻ) is expressly haram. bununla birlikte, such pride should not be confused with expressing and appreciating the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ). bütünāh (ﷻ) loves to see a person appreciating His bounties by utilising them in the doğru şekil.

613.text: A man ate his food with his left hand in the presence of Resûlullah (ﷺ), so he dedi to him:"Eat with your right hand."He cevap verdi:"I cannot."He (ﷺ) dedi:"Then you will not be able to."Only kibir had prevented him (from eating with his right hand). He dedi,"Consequently, he was never again able to raise it (his right hand) to his mouth."(Müslüman)
613.commentary: There was nothing yanlış with the man's hand. When advised with the truth, he proudly made an excuse to justify himself and thereby defied a emir of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), despite being extremely merciful and forgiving, cursed him. The result was that his hand was paralysed. The hadis bize öğretir ki one should asla justify his yanlış as this bir işaretidir pride. He should rather be humble and admit to his weakness.

614.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Size haber vereyim mi about the inhabitants of cehennem ateşi? All those who are miserly, harsh in temperament and arrogant."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
614.commentary: Bu hadis daha önceki bir bölümde zikredilmiştir. Bkz. hadis 252.

615.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Cennet and cehennem ateşi had a debate. Hell-fire dedi: 'Within me are the tyrants and the arrogant.' Cennet dedi: 'Within me are the poor and weak.' Allah (ﷻ) then resolved their dispute by diyerek: 'You, Cennet, are My rahmet; I show rahmet to whosoever I wish through you. And you, Hell-fire, are My azap; I punish whosoever I wish through you. And I will fill both of you.'"(Müslüman)
615.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 254. It advises us to adopt the simplicity and tevazu of the poor and downtrodden and to abstain from oppression, pride and arrogance. A point worthy of note is that bütünāh (ﷻ) mentioned His rahmet before His azap because His grace, iyilik and rahmet far supersede His anger, azap and wrath.

616.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"On the day of Kıyamet, Allah (ﷻ) will not look at a person who drags his lower garment out of kibir."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
616.commentary: "bütünāh (ﷻ) will not look at a person" demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) will not look at him with rahmet and saygı. Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is ḥarām (haram) to wear a garment below the ankles.

617.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There are three types of people whom Allah (ﷻ) will not speak to on the day of Kıyamet, nor purify them, nor look at them, and for them will be a painful azap: an old person who commits adultery, a ruler who lies and a poor person who is proud."(Müslüman)
617.commentary: "bütünāh (ﷻ) will not speak to them" demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) will not address them with sevgi and merhamet, but with anger. "bütünāh (ﷻ) will not purify them" demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) will not forgive their günahlar. her biri of the three transgressors mentioned in Bu hadis are sinful because they perpetrate a günah which is inappropriate, absolutely unnecessary and unjustifiable. Adultery is yanlış, no matter who commits it. bununla birlikte, an old man not only has years of experience and intelligence, but he does not have youthful desires, so his adultery is an indication of his extreme shamelessness. With reference to this chapter, pride and arrogance are evil qualities, bununla birlikte they become more despicable when associated with a poor person because he has nothing to boast about.

618.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) dedi: 'Honour is My lower garment and kibir is My upper garment, so I shall punish whoever tries to challenge Me regarding any of them.'"(Müslüman)
618.commentary: tıpkı... gibi a pair of clothing can only be worn by a single person at any one time, the qualities of pride and honour are exclusive to bütünāh (ﷻ), bundan dolayı it is not appropriate for any person to attempt to imitate bütünāh (ﷻ) in these qualities. Man should realise that he is by nature zayıf and bu nedenle has no doğru to assume any sense of honour or pride over others.

619.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A person was once walking in a beautiful set of clothes, proud of himself, his hair well groomed and arrogant in his step when Allah (ﷻ) suddenly caused the earth to swallow him. He will continue sinking into the earth until the day of Kıyamet."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
619.commentary: Bu hadis ya Benî İsrâil'den bir kişinin olayına atıfta bulunur ya da yatağın temiz olması için yıkanması gereken bir kıssaya işaret eder.

620.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A person who continues displaying his büyüklenme will be recorded among the tyrants, and he will then receive what they will receive (in azap)."(Tirmidhī)
620.commentary: Kişisel arzularına aldanarak kibir ve büyüklenme duygusuna kapılan ve bundan vazgeçmeyen kişi, bu günahı nedeniyle cezalandırılacaktır.

621.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) possessed the best character among people."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
621.commentary: bütün the Messengers of bütünāh taught their followers güzel ahlâk, bununla birlikte the example of güzel ahlâk taught by the Messenger of Islām, Muhammed (ﷺ), surpassed that taught by the other religions. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) himself said, "I was sent to mükemmel güzel ahlâk." (Baihaqī)

622.text: I did not touch any silk brocade or silk softer than the palm of Resûlullah (ﷺ). I did not smell any fragrance sweeter than the fragrance emitting from the body of Resûlullah (ﷺ). I served Resûlullah (ﷺ) for ten years, but he never dedi 'Uff' to me. If I did anything, he never sordu, 'Why did you do that?' and if I did not do anything, he never sordu, 'Why did you not do that?'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
622.commentary: Bu hadis expounds on the physical features and the character of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). The skin of his palms was extremely soft and his perspiration was more fragrant than that of musk. Qāḍi 'Iyāḍ (رحمه الله) stated that when the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would shake hands with someone, then the latter's hand would emit a sweet fragrance for the bütün day. That the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) asla rebuked Anas (رضي الله عنه) even once in ten years testifies to his exceptional forbearance and güzel ahlâk. He did not brood over what had passed, but accepted it as bütünāh's (ﷻ) decree. He did not taint his söz with complaints; rather, his foresight led him towards being positive and progressive. He teşvik edilen rather than criticised.

623.text: I gave Resûlullah (ﷺ) a wild donkey as a gift, but he returned it to me. When he saw the discontent on my face, he dedi: 'We are only returning it to you because we are in iḥrām.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
623.commentary: In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) taught that one should explain one's reason for refusing a gift so that the giver of the gift does not feel offended. It is helal to refuse a gift if one has a geçerli reason for doing so. It is not helal for a person in iḥrām to accept a live animal as a gift.

624.text: I sordu Resûlullah (ﷺ) about salih amel and günah. He dedi: 'İyilik is good character, and günah is that which creates doubt within you and you dislike that people become aware of it.'"(Müslüman)
624.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 590. It is relevant to Bu bölüm because it bize öğretir ki the best form of salih amel is to be embodied with admirable character.

625.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
625.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was neither vulgar nor obscene. He used to say: 'The best of you are those who are best in character.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
625.commentary: While the kelime "فحش" has been translated as "obscene", scholars state that it işaret eder a person who resolutely engages in shameful ameller.

626.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There will be nothing heavier in the scale of a mümin on the day of Kıyamet than good character. Allah (ﷻ) dislikes one who is vulgar and foul-mouthed."(Tirmidhī)
626.commentary: Scholars state that the mention of a believer in Bu hadis indicates that the ameller of a disbeliever will have no weight on the day of Qiyāmah because he lacks the qualifying attribute of īmān. başka bir deyişle, güzel ahlâk will only fayda a person when it is coupled with īmān. The Qur'ān confirms this: "And no weight will be attached to them on the day of Qiyāmah." (Sūrah al-Kahf, 105)

627.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was sordu about what was most instrumental in admitting insanlar into Cennet. He şöyle dedi:"The korku of Allāh and good character."He was sordu about what was most instrumental in leading insanlar into Hell-fire. He şöyle dedi:"The mouth and the genitals."(Tirmidhī)
627.commentary: Ibn Qayyim (رحمه الله) stated that the korku of bütünāh (ﷻ) has been mentioned alongside güzel ahlâk because the former rectifies a person's relationship with his Creator, while the latter rectifies his relationship with bütünāh's (ﷻ) creation. The mouth may lead a person to cehennem because of the birçok günahlar man commits with it gibi backbiting, slander, uttering sözler of küfür, lies, consuming ḥarām food, etc. The genitals also lead one to cehennem because of the günahlar of adultery and homosexuality.

628.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The müminler who are most perfect in faith are those who are best in character. And the best of you are those who are best to their wives."(Tirmidhī)
628.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 278. Being best in character to one's wife means to exercise sabır over her weaknesses and deficiencies, save her from harm, be kind to her, approach her with a cheerful countenance, and so forth.

629.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"By virtue of his good character, a mümin can attain the rank of a person who spends the night in ibadet and the day oruç."(Abū Dāwūd)
629.commentary: Fasting in the heat of the day and engaging in ibadet in the darkness of the night when others are asleep are her iki acts of great fazilet. The fact that one whose character is good attains their rank, is indicative of the tremendous fazilet bütünāh (ﷻ) has attached to güzel ahlâk. tıpkı... gibi fasting and nightly ibadet require dedication and exertion, one who is good to people, despite their varying temperaments, also exerts himself by suppressing his anger and being humble; bundan dolayı, güzel ahlâk has been equated with fasting and night ibadet. Being good to people includes showing merhamet and rahmet towards them, seeking bağışlanma for them, not being revengeful, etc.

630.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Cennet for a person who abstains from disputes, even though he may be in the right; and a house in the middle of Cennet for a person who abandons speaking lies even when he is joking; and a house at the highest point of Cennet for a person who has good character."(Abū Dāwūd)
630.commentary: güzel ahlâk is rewarded with the highest of stages in cennet because other good qualities gibi avoiding disputes and speaking the truth bütün stem from güzel ahlâk. To abandon or avoid a dispute when one is in the doğru, is a amel of great fazilet because it entails suppressing one's desire and anger. ayrıca, after pointing out the truth to an adversary who does not want to accept it, any further engagement is a waste of time. bununla birlikte, scholars state that this excludes such situations where silence will harm the din because it is incorrect to remain silent and complacent when any injunction or teaching of Islām is compromised. To not speak a lie is also an act of fazilet, bununla birlikte this excludes situations gibi war or to reconcile between people, when the speaking of a lie will be helal.

631.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The most beloved of you to me and those of you who will be seated closest to me on the day of Kıyamet will be those of you who have the best character. The most detested of you to me and those of you who will be furthest away from me on the day of Kıyamet will be those who talk excessively, who brag when talking, and who adopt an arrogant manner in speech in order to display their superiority."The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! We understand the meaning of those who talk excessively and who brag when talking, but who are those that adopt an arrogant manner in speech in order to display their superiority?"He cevap verdi:"They are those who are proud."(Tirmidhī)
631.commentary: While explaining the great fazilet of güzel ahlâk, the hadis also bize öğretir ki it is not advisable for a person to speak articulately and eloquently merely to show off his oratory skills or to impress his superiority upon others.

632.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to Ashajj 'Abd al-Qays:"You possess two qualities which Allah (ﷻ) loves: forbearance and composure."(Müslüman)
632.commentary: Ashajj 'Abd al-Qays arrived in Madīnah Munawwarah in a delegation to meet the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). While the rest of the delegation hastened to meet the Messenger (ﷺ), Ashajj remained behind. He tied their conveyances, performed ghusl, adorned a clean set of clothing and then presented himself to the Messenger (ﷺ). The Messenger (ﷺ) was greatly impressed by his intelligent şekil, and complimented him saying that he possessed forbearance and composure. It is helal to praise a person in his presence on şart that one is sure that he will not develop pride due to it. Praising a person's good qualities serves as teşvik for others to also inculcate them.

633.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) is gentle and loves yumuşaklık in all matters."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
633.commentary: Bu hadis demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) is forbearing and does not sevgi to punish His servants. He desires ease for them and does not overwhelm them with a burden that they cannot bear. It can also mean that bütünāh (ﷻ) loves to see the qualities of forbearance and rahmet in people. People who deal gently and calmly with one another find that their interactions are positive and harmonious because bütünāh (ﷻ) places barakah therein.

634.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) is gentle and loves yumuşaklık. He gives for yumuşaklık what He does not give for harshness or anything else."(Müslüman)
634.commentary: yumuşaklık in a person is superior in fazilet to his other good qualities, bundan dolayı bütünāh (ﷻ) rewards such a person with honour in dünya and the ahiret.

635.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When yumuşaklık is in anything, it adorns it, and when it is removed from anything, it spoils it."(Müslüman)
635.commentary: One who is gentle is respected amongst men and is loved by bütünāh (ﷻ), while one who is not gentle is despised in the sight of men and is mekruh by bütünāh (ﷻ).

636.text: A Bedouin urinated in the mescid. The insanlar rushed to him to hit him, but Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'Leave him and pour a bucket or a pail of su over his urine. You were gönderdi to make things easy and not to make things difficult.'"(Bukhārī)
636.commentary: The Bedouin was probably relieving himself before the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was able to say anything, because he was interrupted. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) exercised sabır and forbearance in addressing the matter and ordered that a bucket of water be poured over the urine to clean it. Bu hadis teaches us to be patient and gentle with people who are ignorant of din.

637.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Make things easy and not difficult. Give glad tidings and do not drive people away."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
637.commentary: The fact yanilām is a din that makes things easy rather than difficult is a theme that appears regularly in the Qur'ān. bütünāh (ﷻ) says: "bütünāh desires ease for you and He does not desire difficulty for you." (Sūrah al-Baqarah, 185). One should advise people in such a şekil that inspires them to practise. Kindly administered advice ssık sıks the heart to accept it, and encourages uygulama and ibadet. In contrast, when advice is given harshly, people flee from the person who gives it.

638.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"One who is deprived of yumuşaklık is deprived of all good."(Müslüman)
638.commentary: Bu hadis mentions the fazilet of yumuşaklık. One who is not gentle is deprived of birçok faydalar. This is beautifully encapsulated in an Arabic proverb: "yumuşaklık in matters is like musk in perfumes."

639.text: A man şöyle dedi to Resûlullah (ﷺ):"Advise me."He (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"Do not get angry."He repeated the request several times and Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"Do not get angry."(Bukhārī)
639.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 48. It cautions against getting angry. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) provided this advice to this particular Ṣaḥābī because he was probably one who was easily angered. He repeated the advice because he knew that there was nothing more beneficial for him than controlling his anger. Anger is dangerous and harmful because it causes one to become imbalanced and utter vulgarities, engage in detrimental ameller, develop malice and even utter sözler of küfür.

640.narrator: Abū Ya'lā Shaddād ibn Aus (رضي الله عنه)
640.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) prescribed goodness in every matter. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Each of you should sharpen your knife and be comforting to the animal that he is slaughtering."(Müslüman)
640.commentary: One should act decently and properly in bütün insanî interactions. Even in the field of battle or when taking the life of another insanî being as qiṣāṣ (retribution), one should not resort to torture or torment. Regarding animals, one should ensure that one does not harm or hurt the animal when slaughtering it. bundan dolayı, the knife should be sharp and the slaughter should be brisk, an animal should not be slaughtered in front of another, it should not be dragged to the place of slaughter because it may be injured, and it should not be skinned until it has become cold and bütün signs of life have ceased.

641.text: Whenever Resûlullah (ﷺ) was given a choice between two matters, he chose the easier of the two as long as it did not constitute a günah. If it was a günah, he was the furthest of people from it. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) never took revenge for himself in any matter. But if the sanctity of Allah (ﷻ) was violated, he took revenge for the sake of Allah (ﷻ)."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
641.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was compassionate to his Ummah, bundan dolayı he practised upon the easier option. meselâ, he did not desire the destruction of the people of Ṭā'if when he was given that option, hoping that they would reform and accept Islām. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) forgave people for the harm they caused him. This was a result of his sabır and forbearance in the face of hardship. bununla birlikte, in cases where the boundaries set by bütünāh (ﷻ) were violated, he would take the necessary steps in order to rectify the yanlış that had been perpetrated. The hadis teaches us two amelî dersler. Firstly, we should implement that which is easier, and not unnecessarily complicate matters. One should practise upon (rukhṣah) concessionary law unless it leads one to commit an error or günah. Secondly, one should pardon and forgive people. bununla birlikte, when the laws of bütünāh (ﷻ) are compromised, then one should stand firm upon the truth.

642.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Size haber vereyim mi of the person who is unlawful for cehennem ateşi - or the one for whom cehennem ateşi is unlawful? It is unlawful for every person who is close to people, soft, lenient and easy-going."(Tirmidhī)
642.commentary: One should be humble and soft-hearted when dealing with people. The Qur'ān mentions: "It is because of the rahmet of bütünāh that you (O Muḥammad ﷺ) are lenient with them. If you had been ill-tempered and hard-hearted, they would have bütün dispersed from you." (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 159)

643.text: She sordu Resûlullah (ﷺ):"Did you experience any day more severe than the day of Uḥud?"He cevap verdi:"I experienced many hardships from your people and the severest which I experienced from them was on the day of 'Aqabah (Ṭā'if) when I presented myself to Ibn 'Abd Yālīl ibn 'Abd Kulāl and he did not accept my message. I departed in great grief and only recovered when I reached Qarn al-Tha'ālib. Then I raised my head and saw a cloud shading me. I looked and saw Jibra'īl (عليه السلام) therein. He called to me and dedi: 'Allah (ﷻ) has heard what your people have dedi to you and how they cevapladı you. He (ﷻ) has sent the angel of the mountains to you so that you may command him to do whatever you like to these people.' The angel of the mountains then called me, greeted me and dedi: 'O Muḥammad! Allāh has heard what your people have dedi to you. I am the angel of the mountains and My Sustainer has sent me to you so that you may command me to do whatever you like. What would you like to do? If you so wish, I can crush them between the two mountains surrounding Makkah.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'No, I ümit that Allah (ﷻ) will produce from their progeny those who will ibadet Allah (ﷻ) alone, without ascribing any partners to Him.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
643.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was compassionate to bütün people, even his enemies. He forgave their weaknesses and pardoned their excesses. He did not avenge any harm that was meted out to him, but responded with sabır and restraint, thereby setting a superb example for those who invite to the truth. The battle of Uḥud was a difficult experience for the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) because he suffered a head injury causing him to bleed and lose his front teeth. His uncle, Ḥamzah (رضي الله عنه), and seventy other Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) were also martyred in the battle.

644.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) never struck anyone with his hand – not a woman nor a kul – except when he was waging cihat in the path of Allah (ﷻ). And never did he take revenge from anyone who harmed him. However, if any sacred law of Allah (ﷻ) was violated, he would take revenge for the sake of Allah (ﷻ)."(Müslüman)
644.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) patiently endured the harm inflicted upon him. meselâ, when he was requested to make du'ā' for the destruction of the enemy who fought against him in the battle of Uḥud, he instead supplicated for their bağışlanma. Those in authority are well-advised not to take revenge upon their subjects based on personal motives, but to daima strive to establish truth and adalet.

645.text: I was walking with Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he was wearing a Najrānī cloak which had thick edges. A Bedouin approached him and pulled his cloak violently. I looked at the shoulder of Resûlullah (ﷺ), and the edges of the cloak had left a mark due to the force with which he had pulled it. The man then dedi: 'O Muḥammad! Grant me some of the mal of Allah (ﷻ) which you have.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) turned towards him, smiled, and then ordered that he be given something."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
645.commentary: It was due to the Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) superior character that he smiled and gave a gift to the Bedouin who crudely confronted him. aslında, the narration of Baihaqī mentions that the Bedouin even abused him with the sözler, "Because that which you load for me is not yours nor your father's." The Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) response affirmed the Qur'ānic teaching: "Resist with that which is best." (Sūrah Fuṣṣilat, 34)

646.text: It is as if I can picture Resûlullah (ﷺ) relating the story of a Messenger whose people beat and wounded him. As he wiped the blood from his face, he dedi: 'O Allāh, bağışla my people as they do not know.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
646.commentary: Bu hadis tells of the sabır, forbearance, rahmet and bağışlanma that the Messengers (عليهم السلام) had for their nations. Instead of supplicating for bütünāh's (ﷻ) help against them, they supplicated for their guidance and bağışlanma. bazı scholars suggest that the Messenger referred to here was Nūḥ (عليه السلام), bununla birlikte others say that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was referring to himself, but did not mention his name due to tevazu.

647.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A strong person is not one who overpowers his opponent while wrestling. Rather, a strong person is one who controls himself when he is angry."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
647.commentary: gerçek strength is to discipline the soul, to restrain one's anger and to forgive when one has the power to punish.

648.text: A man dedi:"O Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), I have relatives with whom I maintain relations but they sever relations with me. I am good to them but they are evil to me. I am forbearing to them but they act ignorantly towards me."He (ﷺ) dedi:"If you are as you claim, then it is as if you are placing hot ash in their mouths. Allah (ﷻ) will remain your helper against them as long as you remain as you are."(Müslüman)
648.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 318. It is repeated here to point out that güzel ahlâk entails enduring the hardships inflicted upon oneself by others and forgiving those who do so.

649.narrator: Abū Mas'ūd 'Uqbah ibn 'Amr al-Badrī (رضي الله عنه)
649.text: A man came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'I am absent from the Sabah namaz because so-and-so person prolongs it for us.' I never saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) more angry when he was giving advice as he was on that day. He dedi: 'O people! Some of you are driving people away. Any of you who leads the people in namaz should shorten it because behind him are those who are old, young, and people who have needs to fulfil.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
649.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) rightly became angry because one of his Ṣaḥābah had inadvertently inconvenienced people by unduly lengthening the ṣalāh. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) mentioned three types of people who experience difficulty when the ṣalāh is long. The old cannot stand for long due to weakness, the young do not have the sabır, and those with needs lose concentration easily because their focus is elsewhere.

650.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) returned from a journey and I had hung a curtain over my porch which had some pictures on it. When Resûlullah (ﷺ) saw it, he tore it down and his face changed colour. He dedi: 'O 'Ā'ishah! Those who will be punished most severely on the day of Kıyamet will be those who attempt to create the like of Allāh'in (ﷻ) creation.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
650.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) here displayed his anger because he noticed a emir of bütünāh (ﷻ) being violated. Such an expression of anger for the sake of bütünāh (ﷻ) is meritorious. The hadis demektir ki one who creates animate images with the niyet of imitating bütünāh's (ﷻ) quality of being the Creator commits kufr (küfür) and will bu nedenle be punished çoğu severely in the ahiret.

651.text: The Quraysh were concerned about the Makhzūmī woman who had committed theft, and they dedi: 'Who will speak to Resûlullah (ﷺ) about her?' Others dedi: 'Who can be bold enough except for Usāmah ibn Zayd (رضي الله عنه), the beloved of Resûlullah (ﷺ)?' So Usāmah (رضي الله عنه) spoke to him and Resûlullah (ﷺ) sordu: 'Are you interceding with regard to one of the penal laws of Allah (ﷻ)?' He then stood up and addressed the people, diyerek: 'Those before you were destroyed because when a noble person among them committed theft, they left him alone, but when a weak person committed theft, they applied the penal law upon him. By Allāh, if Fāṭimah the daughter of Muḥammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
651.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained in his sermon that bazı of people of the past were not just in their judgments because they sought to evade the laws of bütünāh (ﷻ) by only subjecting the poor to azap and not the wealthy. By his ifade that "if Fāṭimah the daughter of Muḥammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand," the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) laid down an integral law of adalet and eşitlik: the poor should not be oppressed because of their weakness, neither should the wealthy be pardoned because of their power; bütün men are to be regarded as equal when implementing the law of bütünāh (ﷻ).

652.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) noticed some phlegm in the direction of the Qiblah. It displeased him to such an extent that it was noticeable on his face. He stood up and scraped it off with his hand. He then dedi:"When any of you stands up in namaz, he is conversing with his Sustainer, and his Sustainer is between him and the Qiblah. He should therefore not spit in the direction of the Qiblah, but rather to his left or beneath his feet."He then took hold of a corner of his cloak, spat into it, and folded it up. He then dedi:"Or he should do this."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
652.commentary: "His Sustainer is between him and the Qiblah" demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) is that Being towards whom one is focussed and whose pleasure one seeks while in ṣalāh. A muṣbütünī converses with bütünāh (ﷻ) while in ṣalāh, bundan dolayı it is as if bütünāh (ﷻ) is in front of him. For this reason, it is reprehensible to spit in the direction of the Qiblah. The order to spit to the left or under the feet applies when one is not in the masjid. In the masjid, one should only spit in his garment.

653.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Each one of you is a shepherd and each one of you is answerable for his flock. The leader is a shepherd and is answerable for his flock. The man is a shepherd over his family and is answerable for his flock. The woman is a shepherd over her husband'in house and is answerable for her flock. The kul is a shepherd in his master'in mal and is answerable for his flock. All of you are shepherds and each one of you is answerable for his flock."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
653.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 300. The kelime "shepherd" implies that one should protect, be güvenilir and see to the ahlâkî guidance of one's subordinates. bundan dolayı, those in any position of authority should fulfil their sorumluluklar because if they do not do so, they will be held accountable by bütünāh (ﷻ) on the day of Qiyāmah.

654.narrator: Abū Ya'lā Ma'qil ibn Yasār (رضي الله عنه)
654.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"No slave is made a shepherd over a flock by Allāh and then dies while deceiving his flock, except that Allah (ﷻ) makes Cennet yasakladı for him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). Another narration has:"If he did not protect them by giving good advice, he will not get the fragrance of Cennet."Another narration of Müslüman has:"Any leader who is appointed over the affairs of the Müslümans and then does not strive for their sake and does not advise them well, will not enter Cennet with them."
654.commentary: A leader sık sık has millions of followers and subjects whose affairs he has to oversee. If he does not deal with them amicably and justly, he will be regarded by them as an oppressor and will be punished in the ahiret as well. For this reason, leaders should strive to their utmost in fulfilling the haklar of their subjects and giving them the best advice regarding their dünyevî and dinî matters. "bütünāh (ﷻ) makes cennet prohibited for him," demektir ki such an oppressive leader will not enter cennet with the successful ones, or will be completely deprived of cennet if he assumed such oppression to be helal.

655.text: I heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek in this very house of mine:"Allah'ım! Whoever is appointed over the affairs of my Ummah and he inconveniences them, then You inconvenience him; and whoever is appointed over the affairs of my Ummah and he is kind to them, then You be kind to him."(Müslüman)
655.commentary: The fact that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), despite being a rahmet to mankind, made a du'ā' of this nature shows the great önem he placed upon governing the affairs of the Ummah with iyilik and integrity. Leaders who are unjust will face çeşitli forms of torment in dünya and the ahiret. Their azap will correspond to their ameller, according to the genel rule: Recompense is in accordance with the amel.

656.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The Banī Isrā'īl were ruled by the Messengers. Whenever a Messenger passed away, another would succeed him. There is no Messenger after me. There will be khulafā' after me and they will be many in number."The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! What do you command us to do?"He cevap verdi:"Fulfil the pledge of allegiance with the first and then the next. Then fulfil their rights and ask Allah (ﷻ) for that which is due to you. Allah (ﷻ) will question them about the authority which was given to them."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
656.commentary: Leaders should rule with adalet and integrity because they will be questioned regarding this on the day of Qiyāmah. Muhammed (ﷺ) was the final Messenger of bütünāh (ﷻ). Subjects should obey their leaders in helal matters, even if they are open sinners. bununla birlikte, if they emir towards günah, they should not be obeyed. It is not helal to rebel against a leader, unless he commits open kufr (küfür). The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) miraculously predicted events and they happened as he had said. Subjects should patiently supplicate to bütünāh (ﷺ) to guide their leaders and replace them with better ones, if they are oppressive.

657.text: He went to 'Ubaydullāh ibn Ziyād and dedi to him:"Ey oğlum! I heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek: 'The worst of rulers are those who are harsh upon their subjects.' So be careful that you are not from amongst them."(Müslüman)
657.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 192. The Ṣaḥābī, 'Ā'idh ibn 'Amr (رضي الله عنه), wisely counselled the leader of Iraq, 'Ubaydullāh ibn Ziyād, not to oppress his subjects and to be lenient with them. Scholars state that the Ummah will remain güçlü when it continues advising its leaders and when the leaders pay attention to such advice. ayrıca, advice needs to be given with merhamet, concern and in an appropriate şekil.

658.text: He dedi to Mu'āwiyah (رضي الله عنه):"I heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek: 'When Allah (ﷻ) appoints a person over the affairs of the Müslümans and he is blind to their needs, necessities and fakirlik, Allah (ﷻ) will be blind to his needs, necessities and fakirlik on the day of Kıyamet.'"Mu'āwiyah (رضي الله عنه) therefore appointed a person to see to the needs of the people. (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
658.commentary: Governors and leaders should enable their subjects to receive assistance from the state when they require it. Leaders who are neglectful in this regard will be dealt with in the same yol on the day of Qiyāmah when they will require bütünāh's (ﷻ) assistance.

659.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There are seven people to whom Allah (ﷻ) will provide shade beneath His shade on a day when there will be no shade except His shade: a just leader, a youth who grew up in the ibadet of Allah (ﷻ), a person whose heart is attached to the masājid, two people who love each other for the sake of Allah (ﷻ), meeting and parting ways only for the love of Allah (ﷻ), a man who says to a woman of nobility and beauty trying to seduce him, 'I korku Allāh', a person who gives in sadaka and conceals it so that even his left hand does not know what his right hand gives, a person who engages in the remembrance of Allah (ﷻ) in solitude, while shedding tears."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
659.commentary: Bu hadis daha önceki bir bölümde zikredilmiştir. Bkz. hadis 376.

660.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
660.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Those who were just will be with Allah (ﷻ) on pulpits of light. They are the ones who are just in their judgments, their families, and in what they were given authority over."(Müslüman)
660.commentary: Göre the scholars, "pulpits of light," can be interpreted literally, or it can mean that such people will enjoy an honourable status in the ahiret and they will be envied by the rest of creation.

661.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"The best of your rulers are those whom you love and who love you, whom you pray for and who pray for you. The worst of your rulers are those whom you dislike and who dislike you, whom you curse and who curse you."We sordu:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Should we not break our allegiance with them?"He cevap verdi:"No, as long as they establish namaz among you. No, as long as they establish namaz among you."(Müslüman)
661.commentary: Yöneticiler adalet ve dürüstlükle yönetmelidir çünkü yönettikleri kişiler hakkında sorguya çekileceklerdir. Zulümle yönetenler ağır bir cezaya çarptırılacaktır.

662.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"The inhabitants of Cennet are three: a leader who is just and inspired to do good, a compassionate person who is soft-hearted to all his relatives and Müslümans, and a chaste man who does not beg despite having dependents."(Müslüman)
662.commentary: Bu hadis cennete girecek üç grup insanı tartışır. Yöneticilere adil olmalarını, merhametli ve dürüst olmalarını tavsiye eder.

663.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A Müslüman must listen and obey in respect of what he likes and dislikes, unless he is emretti to commit a günah. If he is emretti to commit a günah, he should neither listen nor obey."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
663.commentary: It is Wājib (compulsory) for Muslim subjects to obey their leaders in matters which are agreeable to their temperament or not, except when they are commanded to commit günah. This is in accordance with the basic principle laid down in Islām: There can be no itaat to the creation when the Creator is disobeyed.

664.text: When we used to pledge allegiance to Resûlullah (ﷺ) to listen and obey, he would say to us: 'In as far as you are able to.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
664.commentary: Bu hadis iki açıdan değerlendirilebilir. Birincisi, Müslüman tebaa, adil olsun veya olmasın yöneticilerine itaat etmekle yükümlüdür. İkincisi, yöneticiler adaletsiz olduklarında sorumlu tutulacaklardır.

665.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"One who withdraws his hand from obedience will meet Allah (ﷻ) on the day of Kıyamet without any proof in his favour; and one who passes away without having pledged allegiance dies a death of jāhiliyyah (ignorance)."(Müslüman). Another narration has:"One who dies estranged from the Müslüman community dies a death of jāhiliyyah (ignorance)."
665.commentary: Once a person pledges allegiance to the Muslim leader, it is not helal for him to withdraw from it without a geçerli Islāmic reason. During the days of jāhiliyyah (ignorance), people lived a life without itaat to any leader because they considered itaat improper. Islām brought about an organised system of governance where allegiance to a leader was necessary. bundan dolayı, one who dies without allegiance to a Muslim leader is as if he prefers the errant system of jāhiliyyah.

666.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Listen and obey even if an Abyssinian slave whose head is like that of a raisin is appointed over you."(Bukhārī)
666.commentary: Müslüman bir yöneticiye itaat, ten rengi, kökeni veya fiziksel özellikleri ne olursa olsun zorunludur. Ancak yönetici açıkça küfre girerse itaat gerekmez.

667.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"It is compulsory upon you to listen and obey in your times of difficulty and ease, and with regard to what pleases or displeases you, and even if others are given preferential treatment over you."(Müslüman)
667.commentary: itaat to a Muslim leader is compulsory in bütün the circumstances specified in this hadis. It will not be helal to rebel against him because this will lead to greater harm than good, in the form of widespread bloodshed, disorder and infighting.

668.text: We were once with Resûlullah (ﷺ) on a journey and stopped at a place. Some of us began repairing our tents, some were competing in shooting arrows, and some were seeing to their animals, when the announcer of Resûlullah (ﷺ) announced that the namaz was ready to commence. So we gathered around Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he dedi: 'It was the responsibility of every Messenger who came before me to direct his Ummah towards that which he knew was good for them and to warn them against that which he knew was evil for them. The well-being of this Ummah has been associated with the first of its adherents, while the latter part of this Ummah will be afflicted by trials and matters which you dislike. Tribulations will follow one another, and each will seem worse than the one before it. A tribulation will come and a mümin will say: This will destroy me, and it will then be removed. Another tribulation will follow and the mümin will say: This is the one, this is the one! Whoever desires to be saved from cehennem ateşi and be admitted into Cennet should have his death come to him while he believes in Allah (ﷻ) and the Last Day, and he treats people as he would like them to treat him. And whoever pledges allegiance to a leader by giving him the grasp of his hand and the essence of his heart, should obey him as far as possible. If another person comes to usurp his leadership, then strike his neck.'"(Müslüman)
668.commentary: In Bu hadis the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) foretold of the time when the Ummah would be afflicted with endless tribulations, her biri worse than the one before it. istikrar upon īmān, following the truth and upholding good ahlâk are the factors which will safeguard a person during such difficult times. The hadis also bize öğretir ki those who attempt to revolt against a rightly appointed leader should be opposed by the genel subjects because unity of the Ummah is of paramount önem.

669.narrator: Abū Hunaydah Wā'il ibn Ḥujr (رضي الله عنه)
669.text: Salāmah ibn Yazīd al-Ju'fī sordu Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! What should we do if such rulers are given authority over us who demand their rights from us but deny us our rights?"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) turned away from him. He repeated the question and Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"Listen and obey because they are answerable for their responsibilities and you are answerable for your responsibilities."(Müslüman)
669.commentary: A deficiency on the part of the leader by not fulfilling the haklar of his subjects does not justify them responding to him with isyan and başkaldırı because a yanlış cannot be rectified by perpetrating another yanlış. her person will be held accountable for his own ameller and choices on the day of Qiyāmah. Leaders bu nedenle need to be just, and subjects need to be obedient to their leaders.

670.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"After I am gone, there will be preferential treatment and matters which you dislike."The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! What do you command us to do if we experience this?"He cevap verdi:"Fulfil the rights which you owe to others and ask Allah (ﷻ) for your rights."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
670.commentary: Subjects who live under an oppressive ruler should continue fulfilling their sorumluluklar gibi zakāh, going out in jihād, etc., and continue supplicating to bütünāh (ﷻ) to improve their şartlar.

671.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah (ﷻ), and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah (ﷻ). Whoever obeys the leader has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the leader has disobeyed me."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
671.commentary: itaat to the Muslim leader is synonymous to obeying bütünāh (ﷻ) and His Messenger (ﷺ), bundan dolayı it is farz upon Muslims to do so in helal matters.

672.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Whoever dislikes anything of his leader should exercise sabır, for whoever disobeys the leader by a hand-span, shall die the death of jāhiliyyah (ignorance)."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
672.commentary: While Bu hadis commands only sabır in the face of injustice, Muslim subjects should continue advising their leader towards salih amel. Unless he commits open kufr, one is not permitted to revolt against the leader because this shatters unity which in turn prevents the progress of Islām.

673.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Whoever dishonours the ruler, will be dishonoured by Allah (ﷻ)."(Tirmidhī)
673.commentary: Respecting Muslim leaders and scholars is necessary because any form of saygısızlık towards them will incite people towards disobeying their commands which will harm the genel order and organisation of the Muslims.

674.narrator: Ebû Saîd 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah (رضي الله عنه)
674.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'O 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura! Do not ask for leadership. If it is given to you without your asking for it, you will be helped in regard to it, and if it is given to you by your asking for it, you will be made responsible for it. If you take an oath and then realise something better than it, do that which is better and expiate your oath.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
674.commentary: her form of leadership is challenging and comes with difficulties, bundan dolayı one who relies upon his own skills and does not rely upon bütünāh's (ﷻ) assistance will not be successful in fulfilling its demands. One should only accept a position of leadership if he is requested to do so or if there is nobody capable of fulfilling its sorumluluklar effectively. In this case, he will be divinely assisted.

675.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'O Abū Dharr! I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself. Do not become a leader over even two individuals and do not take the responsibility of the mal of an orphan.'"(Müslüman)
675.commentary: Abū Dharr (رضي الله عنه) was one of those Ṣaḥābah who was ascetically minded. He did not care much for dünyevî matters, and even went to the extent of declaring it impermissible to gather wealth despite discharging zakāh upon it. Because he did not have experience regarding wealth and issues of leadership, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) commanded him not to place himself into a leadership position.

676.text: I sordu: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Why do you not appoint me as a governor?' He tapped my shoulder with his hand and dedi: 'O Abū Dharr! You are weak and it is a trust. On the day of Kıyamet, it will be a source of disgrace and remorse except for that person who assumes it dutifully and fulfils its responsibilities as required of him.'"(Müslüman)
676.commentary: Leadership is a güven and an important responsibility, bundan dolayı one who assumes this position should strive to his utmost to fulfil bütün its requirements. He should be knowledgeable regarding its görevler, and needs to be capable of fulfilling its sorumluluklar.

677.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"You will be desirous of leadership, but it will be a source of remorse on the day of Kıyamet."(Bukhārī)
677.commentary: One should not be desirous of leadership because of the tremendous responsibility it entails. It is not worth one's while to enjoy a az sayıda breaths of unjust power in dünya and then face intolerable agony in the ahiret.

678.text: Abū Sa'īd (رضي الله عنه) and Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) narrate that Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"Allah (ﷻ) did not send a Messenger nor appoint a khalīf without him having two advisors: one ordering him to do good and encouraging him towards it, and the other ordering him to do evil and encouraging him towards it. The one who is truly protected is the one whom Allah (ﷻ) protects."(Bukhārī)
678.commentary: A leader should choose such ministers and advisors who will advise him towards salih amel, güvenilirlik and adalet. He needs to follow the doğru Islāmic guidelines in his administration and policies so that he does not come under the influence of those who are corrupt and dishonest. bazı âlimlere göre, "two ministers" could also refer to angels who guide him towards good, and Shaiṭān who leads him towards evil.

679.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When Allah (ﷻ) desires good for a leader, He gives him a truthful minister who reminds him when he forgets, and helps him when he remembers; and when He desires the contrary for him, He gives him an evil minister who neither reminds him when he forgets nor helps him when he remembers."(Abū Dāwūd)
679.commentary: When a leader is surrounded by righteous advisors, it is a sign that bütünāh (ﷻ) is pleased with him and guides him along. On the contrary, evil advisors drive a leader and his people towards destruction. History is replete with examples of her iki types of advisors and the consequences of their counsel.

680.text: I visited Resûlullah (ﷺ) with two of my cousins. One of them dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Appoint us as governors over places which Allah (ﷻ) has granted you authority.' The other cousin also made a similar request. He (ﷺ) dedi: 'By Allāh, we will not appoint any person to such a post if he asks for it or desires it.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
680.commentary: Those who request for positions of leadership should not be appointed because their request işaret eder the fact that they are doing so for personal gain and acquisition of wealth. Such people will not serve the populace selflessly, rather their aim will be to usurp the haklar and wealth of people.

681.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by a man from the Anṣār who was advising his brother about modesty. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"Leave him, for modesty is part of īmān."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
681.commentary: The hayâ and utanç of a person bazen prevent him from seeking his haklar because he feels too shy to request for them. It was perhaps for this reason that the Anṣārī was cautioning his brother against excessive hayâ. He was prohibited from doing so by the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) as his hayâ was the stepping-stone to acquire the level desired by Islām. hayâ is an intrinsic quality that can be refined by embracing the teachings of Islām. bundan dolayı, the effort and struggle to achieve this makes it a part of īmān.

682.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Modesty brings nothing but good."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). A narration of Müslüman has:"Modesty is only goodness."
682.commentary: Since hayâ prevents a person from isyan, evil character, and a host of immodest ameller, it has been referred to as goodness. The desired hayâ is that which leads a person towards bütünāh's (ﷻ) itaat and the fulfilment of the haklar of others. Superficial hayâ which contravenes the teachings of Islām is not acceptable; aslında, such hayâ bir işaretidir weakness and cowardice.

683.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Īmān has more than seventy (or more than sixty) branches. The best of them is to bear şahit that there is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh and the least of them is to remove a harmful object from the path. And modesty is also a branch of īmān."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
683.commentary: This first portion of the hadis (şöyle ki, the testimony of iman) işaret eder the haklar of bütünāh (ﷻ), while the second portion (şöyle ki, removing a harmful object from the yol) işaret eder the haklar of insanî beings. başka bir deyişle, for the acquisition of mükemmel īmān, the haklar of bütünāh (ﷻ) and that of His creation need to be fulfilled. Even though hayâ is included as a branch of īmān, it has been specifically singled out here, because it leads a person to implement bütün the other branches. One who is modest fears being embarrassed in dünya and the ahiret, bundan dolayı he will fulfil yükümlülükler and abstain from prohibitions.

684.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was more modest than a virgin woman in her private room. When he saw something which he disliked, we realised it from his facial expression."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
684.commentary: "More modest than a virgin woman in her private room," işaret eder a virgin woman who is meeting her husband for the first time in solitude. Such a woman is an embodiment of utanç and hayâ, bundan dolayı the similarity with the lofty character of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). "When he saw something which he mekruh, we realised it from his facial expression," demektir ki when the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not naturally like something, he would not mention it due to his hayâ, bununla birlikte his facial expression would change. This does not refer to matters of din since the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would immediately caution those who acted contrary to ilâhî commandments.

685.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"From among the worst of people in the sight of Allah (ﷻ) on the day of Kıyamet will be a person who engages in conjugal relations with his wife and she with him, and he then exposes her secret."(Müslüman)
685.commentary: Bu hadis explains that bütün personal matters between a husband and wife relating to conjugal relations are a güven between them and should be kept secret. aslında, it is the doğru of the wife that her personal matters should not be exposed before others. Exposing such matters is a major günah in the sight of bütünāh (ﷻ) and is contrary to the nobility and honour of a respectable individual. It will be helal to mention such matters if there is a pressing need, gibi when seeking medical treatment or in a marital dispute before a judge.

686.text: When 'Umar'in (رضي الله عنه) kız, Ḥafṣah (رضي الله عنها), became a widow, 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi:"I met 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān (رضي الله عنه) and offered Ḥafṣah in marriage to him, diyerek: 'If you wish, I will marry you to Ḥafṣah bint 'Umar.' He cevap verdi: 'I will think about it.' I waited a few days and he then met me and şöyle dedi: 'I have decided not to marry at present.' I then met Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (رضي الله عنه) and şöyle dedi to him: 'If you wish, I will marry you to Ḥafṣah bint 'Umar.' Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) remained silent and verdi me no reply. I was more upset with him than I was with 'Uthmān. I waited a few days and Resûlullah (ﷺ) then proposed to her and I married her to him. Abū Bakr then met me and şöyle dedi: 'You were probably upset with me when you offered Ḥafṣah to me and I did not give you any reply.' I şöyle dedi: 'Yes.' He şöyle dedi: 'The only thing that prevented me from replying to your offer was that I bildi that Resûlullah (ﷺ) had mentioned her, and I did not want to disclose the secret of Resûlullah (ﷺ). If Resûlullah (ﷺ) had not married her, I would have certainly accepted her.'"(Bukhārī)
686.commentary: Ḥafṣah (رضي الله عنها) was married to Khunais ibn Ḥudhāfah (رضي الله عنه), who passed away in Madīnah Munawwarah due to a wound sustained during the Battle of Uḥud. The fact that 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) offered his daughter, Ḥafṣah (رضي الله عنها), in marriage to Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) and 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه) bize öğretir ki guardians may offer their daughters, sisters etc. in marriage to suitable husbands. In relation to the chapter, in this incident Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) did not respond to the request of 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) because he felt that the niyet of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) to marry Ḥafṣah (رضي الله عنها) was a private matter and was not to be exposed.

687.text: The wives of Resûlullah (ﷺ) were with him, when Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها) came walking, her gait not differing at all from that of Resûlullah (ﷺ). When he saw her, he welcomed her and dedi: 'Welcome, my daughter.' Then he seated her on his right or on his left. Then he whispered to her and she cried bitterly. When he saw her anguish, he whispered to her a second time and she laughed. I dedi to her: 'The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) singled you out from among his wives to whisper to you and then you cry!' When Resûlullah (ﷺ) stood up, I sordu her: 'What did Resûlullah (ﷺ) say to you?' She dedi: 'I am not going to reveal the secret of Resûlullah (ﷺ).' When Resûlullah (ﷺ) passed away, I dedi: 'I implore you by the right that I have over you, tell me what Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi to you.' She dedi: 'Now, yes. The first time he whispered to me, he told me that Jibrīl used to review the Kur'an with him once every year, and now he reviewed it with him twice. I sense that my time has drawn near, so korku Allāh and be patient, for I am a blessed predecessor for you. So I cried as you saw. When he saw my anguish, he whispered to me the second time and dedi: O Fāṭimah! Are you not pleased to be the leader of the women of the müminler, or the leader of the women of this Ummah? So I laughed as you saw.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
687.commentary: Bu hadis demonstrates the önem of keeping secrets. Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها) did not disclose what the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) told her until after his demise when it was no longer necessary to keep it secret.

688.text: Thābit anlatır from Anas (رضي الله عنه) who dedi:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) came up to me while I was playing with some children and greeted us. He then sent me on an errand, and I was therefore delayed in returning to my mother. When I returned, she sordu: 'What delayed you?' I cevap verdi: 'The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sent me on an errand.' She sordu: 'What errand was it?' I cevap verdi: 'It is a secret.' She dedi: 'Do not disclose the secret of Resûlullah (ﷺ) to anyone.' Anas (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'By Allāh, if I were to disclose it to anyone, I would have disclosed it to you, O Thābit.'"(Müslüman)
688.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the güvenilirlik and fazilet of Anas (رضي الله عنه). Even after the demise of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), he concealed the secret with which he was entrusted. The hadis also draws our attention to the wonderful upbringing that Anas (رضي الله عنه) received from his mother, Umm Sulaym (رضي الله عنها). She wisely realised that a secret should not be exposed and bundan dolayı advised him asla to expose the secret of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). Parents are well-advised to inculcate such noble habits within their children.

689.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There are three signs of a münafık: when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he is placed in a position of trust, he betrays his trust."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). The narration of Müslüman has:"Even if he fasts, offers namaz and claims that he is a Müslüman."
689.commentary: Bu hadis has been discussed in a previous chapter. See hadis 199. It mentions three qualities of a hypocrite. The fact that one who lies, breaks promises and abuses trusts has been likened to a hypocrite işaret eder the şiddet of these günahlar. The hadis is relevant to Bu bölüm because it bize öğretir ki breaking of promises is a quality of hypocrites, not believers.

690.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
690.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If anyone has four qualities, he is a pure münafık, and if he has one of them, then he has a quality of hypocrisy until he gives it up. When he is placed in a position of trust, he betrays his trust. When he speaks, he lies. When he makes a promise, he breaks it. When he disputes, he departs from the truth."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
690.commentary: One may question why the previous hadis mentions three qualities of a hypocrite and this one four. Scholars have answered this in çeşitli ways. One is that a hypocrite may have birçok qualities, and as circumstances demanded, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) mentioned bazı of them. According to Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله), such a believer merely resembles a hypocrite. bazı scholars suggest that the nifak referred to here relates to ameller and not inanç. According to 'bütünāmah Kashmīrī (رحمه الله), these are the signs of a hypocrite; bununla birlikte, possessing any of them does not necessarily make one a hypocrite.

691.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'When the mal of Bahrain comes, I will give you so much, so much and so much.' The mal from Bahrain did not come until after the demise of Resûlullah (ﷺ). When the mal of Bahrain came, Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) emretti that it be announced: 'Whoever has a promise from Resûlullah (ﷺ) or a debt, should come to us.' I came to him and dedi: 'The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) had promised me such-and-such.' So Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) filled both his hands with mal and gave it to me. When I counted it, it came to five hundred dirhams. He then dedi to me: 'Take twice as much again.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
691.commentary: Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) gave Jābir (رضي الله عنه) one-thousand-five-hundred dirhams in total. He was fully entitled to do so because he was the rightly appointed successor of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) narrates the hadis here in order to show the fazilet of Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) who duly fulfilled the vaad of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) after the latter's demise.

692.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
692.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'O 'Abdullāh! Do not be like so-and-so who used to engage in ibadet at night and then stopped doing so.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
692.commentary: The hadis stresses the önem of Tahajjud ṣalāh. Even though it is not compulsory, performing it is greatly meritorious. Based on this hadis, scholars state that one who commences any iyilik or ibadet should continue it with consistency and istikrar. Abandoning a good amel işaret eder indifference towards it, and indicates that the heart is disinclined to bütünāh's (ﷻ) remembrance.

693.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Safeguard yourselves from cehennem ateşi even if it is by giving half a date (in sadaka). And whoever cannot manage even this, then by diyerek a good word."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
693.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki charity is effective in saving one from the cehennem-fire. bu nedenle a believer should habitually give in charity. To stress the önem of this, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) teşvik edilen us to give even half a date in charity, if one possesses nothing else; it should asla be regarded as meagre or trivial. Further, if one does not even possess half a date, then he should express sözler of iyilik, as this is also a means of saving one from the cehennem-fire.

694.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A good word is sadaka."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). This is a portion of a hadis which was quoted previously.
694.commentary: Charity is not restricted to spending wealth in the yol of bütünāh (ﷻ). As a concept, charity is so vast that encouraging good, forbidding evil, smiling with people and speaking in a kind şekil enables one to receive the sevap of charity. This further indicates to the önem yanilām places upon noble character and adab.

695.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Do not regard any good deed to be insignificant even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face.'"(Müslüman)
