695.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) teşvik edilen his followers to deal with her biri other with an open heart and a smiling face. In this yol, Islām encourages the cultivation of mutual sevgi and unity. A cheerful countenance is a seemingly minor amel, bununla birlikte it is greatly valued by bütünāh (ﷻ) because it bir işaretidir the sevgi a person has in his heart for his Muslim brother.

696.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) konuştu, he would repeat his words three times so that they would be thoroughly anladı, and when he gitti to insanlar, he would greet them three times. (Bukhārī)
696.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) "repeating his sözler three times" işaret eder important matters or issues which he wished to stress, or if there was a large group of people; it does not mean that he repeated her sentence. Based on this hadis, scholars state that it is preferable to repeat a ifade thrice, if there is a need. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) "greeted three times" when there was a huge gathering of people. He would greet those in front of him, those on the doğru and then those on the left, so that bütün could hear him and reply.

697.text: The speech of Resûlullah (ﷺ) was so clear that it was anladı by all who heard it."(Abū Dāwūd)
697.commentary: The hadis demektir ki the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not utilise difficult and obscure sözler, as bazı do to make a show of their knowledge; rather, it was clear and easy for the yaygın person to understand his sözler. bazı scholars have said that it demektir ki her kelime which the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) uttered was distinct and separate from the next. The sözler were not joined together and spoken in haste. If the listener desired to count his sözler, it would have been easy to do so.

698.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me on the occasion of the Farewell Pilgrimage: 'Ask the people to be silent.' He then dedi: 'Do not become kuffār (disbelievers) after me by striking the necks of one another.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
698.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki when the Qur'ān is being recited or aḥādīth are being narrated, then people should remain silent. aslında, an announcement to this effect may be made in order to quieten the people. Scholars have further deduced from Bu hadis that it is necessary upon students and the genel masses to be quiet when they are addressed by the 'ulamā', as the 'ulamā' are the inheritors of the Messengers (عليهم السلام).

699.narrator: Abū Wā'il Shaqīq ibn Salāmah (رضي الله عنه)
699.text: Ibn Mas'ūd (رضي الله عنه) used to address us every Thursday. A man dedi to him: 'O Abū 'Abd al-Raḥmān! I wish that you would address us every day.' He cevap verdi: 'Listen! I do not want to do so because I korku that I may bore you. I am concerned about addressing you just as Resûlullah (ﷺ) was concerned about us, fearing that we would become bored.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
699.commentary: Bu hadis highlights the need for moderation in her amel. By nature, man becomes tired and bored, even with regard to things which are beloved to him. If a person is continuously advised, he will not fully focus upon the advice. At times, his heart will be disinclined to what is being said. bundan dolayı, one who is advising and teaching people should do so in accordance with their temperament and desire to learn.

700.narrator: Abū al-Yaqẓān 'Ammār ibn Yāsir (رضي الله عنهما)
700.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Performing lengthy namaz and delivering a short sermon is a sign of a person'in intelligence. So lengthen the namaz and shorten the sermon."(Müslüman)
700.commentary: The emir to "perform lengthy ṣalāh" is in relation to the sermon. It does not mean that the ṣalāh should daima be lengthened because in other aḥādīth, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) instructed those leading the ṣalāh not to lengthen it to such an extent that it inconveniences the ill and the elderly. One who lengthens the ṣalāh and shortens the sermon has been described as intelligent because one who does so knows that ṣalāh is the object, and the sermon is only a means of encouraging towards it. bundan dolayı, more attention should be given to that which is of greater önem.

701.narrator: Mu'āwiyah ibn al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī (رضي الله عنه)
701.text: While I was performing namaz with Resûlullah (ﷺ), a person in the congregation sneezed, so I dedi: 'May Allāh have rahmet on you.' The people began staring at me and I dedi: 'May your mothers be bereaved. Why are you looking at me?' They then began striking their hands on their thighs. When I realised that they wanted me to remain silent, I remained silent. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then completed the namaz. May my parents be his ransom. I have never seen a better teacher before or after him. By Allāh, he did not rebuke me, strike me, or verbally abuse me. He dedi: 'Any form of human dialogue is not correct in namaz. It is only for the glorification of Allāh, expressing His greatness, and the recitation of the Kur'an.' Or he dedi some similar words. I dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! I was until very recently in the era of jāhiliyyah, and Allah (ﷻ) has now brought İslâm to us, but there are some people among us who go to astrologers.' He dedi: 'Do not go to them.' I dedi: 'There are also people among us who believe in evil omens.' He dedi: 'That is something which they have in their hearts. They should never let it stop them from doing whatever has to be done.'"(Müslüman)
701.commentary: The approach and yöntem of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) when dealing with people was exceptional. Here a village-dweller who did not know the hükümler of Islām mistakenly spoke in ṣalāh. He was made aware of his mistake without his integrity being tarnished in any yol. The Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) affection and iyilik had such an impact upon him that he was prepared to sacrifice his parents for the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). bütün forms of söz are prohibited during ṣalāh. To visit astrologers with the aim of asking about matters of the unseen and the future is haram. Believing in evil omens was an erroneous âdet of the days of ignorance, bundan dolayı the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) prohibited it.

702.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) delivered a very profound and eloquent lecture to us which made our hearts tremble and our eyes shed tears."He related the hadis and it has been previously mentioned in full under the chapter on upholding the Sünnet.
702.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 157. It has been narrated in Bu bölüm to show that a lecture should not be so lengthy that its effect is lost. Rather, it should be concise, easy to comprehend and beneficial in content. The fact that the hearts of the Ṣaḥābah trembled and their eyes shed tears was a sign that they were greatly affected by the sözler of the Qur'ān and aḥādīth. This was a sign that īmān was firmly entrenched within their hearts.

703.text: I never saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) laughing to such an extent that the back of his mouth became visible. He used to merely smile."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
703.commentary: Bu hadis describes the laughter of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). After studying the çeşitli aḥādīth relating to this subject, scholars conclude that in çoğu cases, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would merely smile. Occasionally he would laugh to the extent that his teeth would be visible. In such cases he would place his hand over his mouth. This bize öğretir ki we should not engage in excessive laughter as this diminishes our honour and haysiyet. Further, too much of laughter indicates towards negligence.

704.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"When the namaz has commenced, do not go towards it running. Rather, go towards it walking, and you should be composed. Then perform whatever you get, and complete whatever you miss."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). Müslüman adds in a narration:"When one of you goes towards namaz, he is already in namaz."
704.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one should proceed early and walk with honour and haysiyet towards ṣalāh. Running to the masjid is contrary to the haysiyet and adab that ṣalāh demands. If there is a korku of missing ṣalāh, then one may walk briskly, bununla birlikte one should not run. Running causes difficulty in breathing, which in turn inconveniences others performing ṣalāh. Similarly, a person who runs to the masjid cannot concentrate in ṣalāh as he is trying to catch his breath. Another hikmet mentioned for this yasak is that a person going towards ṣalāh is considered to be in ṣalāh, bundan dolayı he should adhere to bütün its etiquettes.

705.text: He was returning with Resûlullah (ﷺ) on the day of 'Arafah when Resûlullah (ﷺ) heard a loud rebuke and the sound of a camel behind him. He pointed his whip towards them and dedi:"O people! Remain calm as it is not an act of devotion to proceed in haste."(Bukhārī and a portion of it by Müslüman)
705.commentary: To be present in 'Arafah is one of the main rükünler of Ḥajj. After completing their stay in 'Arafah, the Ḥujjāj normally hasten towards Muzdalifah after the setting of the sun on 9th Zul-Ḥijjah. In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) noticed bazı people beating their camels in order to urge them to move faster. He explained to them that hastening towards goodness is a noble amel, bununla birlikte to do so in such a yol that causes harm to others is not an act of takvâ. Such haste destroys the honour and haysiyet of a person. ibadet and proceeding towards places of ibadet should be done with calmness and composure because this enhances concentration and kulluk.

706.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who believes in Allāh and the Last Day should honour his guest. One who believes in Allāh and the Last Day should maintain ties of kinship. One who believes in Allāh and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
706.commentary: Bu hadis has been mentioned previously. See hadis 303. It emphasizes three important görevler of a believer: honouring guests, maintaining family ties, and guarding one's söz by either speaking good or remaining silent.

707.narrator: Abū Shurayḥ Khuwaylid ibn 'Amr al-Khuzā'ī (رضي الله عنه)
707.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"One who believes in Allah (ﷻ) and the Last Day should honour the right of his guest."The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"What is his right, O Messenger of Allāh?"He cevap verdi:"One day and one night. Hospitality is for three days, and anything in addition to that is sadaka for him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). A narration of Müslüman has:"It is not lawful for a Müslüman to stay with his brother for so long that he leads him to günah."The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! How can he lead him to günah?"He cevap verdi:"He continues staying with him while he has nothing to offer him in hospitality."
707.commentary: Bu demektir ki that on the first day, the host should take extra care in serving his guest, and for the next two days, he should feed his guest according to his normal routine. After three days, the guest has no doğru to stay longer; bununla birlikte, if the host allows him to stay, it will be an act of iyilik for which he will be greatly rewarded. The guest should, bununla birlikte, be considerate towards the host. He should not prolong his stay to the extent that the host is inconvenienced.

708.text: Abū Ibrāhīm, who is also known as Abū Muḥammad and Abū Mu'āwiyah 'Abdullāh ibn Abī Awfā (رضي الله عنهما), anlatır that Resûlullah (ﷺ) gave to Khadījah (رضي الله عنها) the glad tidings of a mansion of pearls in Cennet in which there will be no noise and no fatigue. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
708.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the tremendous fazilet of Khadījah (رضي الله عنها). She was the first wife of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and bore bütün his children except Ibrāhīm (رضي الله عنه). She was the first to accept his message, she spent bütün her wealth for the cause of Islām, and she consoled the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) when he had little support. As long as she lived, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not remarry. She passed away in the 10th year after prophethood.

709.text: He performed wuḍū' at his house and then went out. He dedi to himself:"I will stay close to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and remain with him today."He went to the mescid and sordu where Resûlullah (ﷺ) was. The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) dedi:"He went in that direction."He dedi:"So I followed him asking about him until he entered the well of Arīs. I sat down at the entrance waiting until Resûlullah (ﷺ) had relieved himself and performed wuḍū'. I then went up to him. He was sitting on the edge of the well with his legs exposed and were dangling into the well. I greeted him, and then sat at the entrance. I thought to myself: 'Today, I will be the guard of Resûlullah (ﷺ).' Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) came and knocked at the door. I sordu: 'Who is it?' He cevap verdi: 'Abū Bakr' I dedi: 'Please wait.' I went and dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), Abū Bakr is requesting permission to enter.' He dedi: 'Allow him in and give him glad tidings of Cennet.' I went back and dedi to Abū Bakr: 'You may enter, and Resûlullah (ﷺ) gives you glad tidings of Cennet.' Abū Bakr entered and sat down on the right of Resûlullah (ﷺ) on the edge of the well with his legs dangling over the edge as Resûlullah (ﷺ) had done, exposing his shanks. I then went back and sat down. I had left my brother performing ablution and intending to join me, and I thought to myself: 'If Allah (ﷻ) wills good for someone - referring to his brother - He will bring him.' At that moment, someone knocked at the door. I sordu: 'Who is it?' He dedi: ''Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.' I dedi: 'Please wait.' I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ), greeted him and dedi: ''Umar is requesting permission to enter.' He dedi: 'Allow him in and give him glad tidings of Cennet.' 'Umar entered, sat down on the left of Resûlullah (ﷺ) on the edge of the well with his legs dangling over the edge. I then went back and sat down. I thought to myself: 'If Allah (ﷻ) wills good for someone – referring to his brother – He will bring him.' At that moment someone knocked at the door. I sordu: 'Who is it?' He dedi: ''Uthmān ibn 'Affān.' I dedi: 'Please wait.' I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and haber verdi him. He dedi: 'Allow him in and give him glad tidings of Cennet together with a calamity that will afflict him.' I went back and dedi to him: 'You may enter, and Resûlullah (ﷺ) gives you the glad tidings of Cennet together with a calamity that will afflict you.' He entered and found no space to sit at the edge. So he went and sat on the other side facing them."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
709.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the fazilet of Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه), 'Umar (رضي الله عنه), and 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه), and shows that they are from the inhabitants of cennet. The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) were eager to be in the company of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and serve him. One should clearly state one's name when requesting for izin to enter any place. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) miraculously predicted the calamity that 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه) would face. Scholars mention that this calamity referred to the incident when people besieged his house and eventually martyred him.

710.text: We were sitting in a group with Resûlullah (ﷺ) together with Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) and 'Umar (رضي الله عنه). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then stood up and left us. After quite some time had passed and he still did not return, we began to korku that some harm had come to him. We stood up in alarm. I was the first to be alarmed and I went out in search of Resûlullah (ﷺ) until I reached an orchard of the Anṣār belonging to the Banū al-Najjār."I walked around the orchard to see if I could find an entrance, but I did not find any. But, there was a brook flowing into the orchard from a well on the outside. A brook is a small stream. I squeezed through and went inside to meet Resûlullah (ﷺ). He sordu: 'Is that Abū Hurayrah?' I cevap verdi: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allāh.' He sordu: 'What is the matter?' I cevap verdi: 'You were with us and then you got up and took a long time returning. We feared that something had happened to you in our absence and we became alarmed. I was the first to be alarmed and I came to this orchard, squeezing in like a fox. The people are waiting behind me.' He dedi: 'O Abū Hurayrah!' and he gave me his shoes. He dedi, 'Take these shoes of mine and give glad tidings of Cennet to whoever you meet behind this orchard who testifies with full conviction of heart that there is none worthy of ibadet except Allah (ﷻ).'"He then related the hadis in full. (Müslüman)
710.commentary: After Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) received this good news, he conveyed it to the first person he met, which was 'Umar (رضي الله عنه). 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) struck him on his chest and told him not to convey this to the people. When the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) heard of this, he asked 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) why he had prevented Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) from conveying the message. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) explained that people would rely on this good news and neglect the performance of iyilikler, with the result that they would be deprived of the higher stages of cennet. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) agreed with 'Umar's (رضي الله عنه) opinion. Bu hadis gives glad tidings for a gerçek believer who lives with īmān and passes away with īmān that he will enter cennet, either directly or after being punished in cehennem for his günahlar.

711.text: We were with 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنه) while he was on his deathbed. He cried for a long time with his face turned towards the wall. His son dedi to him: O my father! Did Resûlullah (ﷺ) not give you such and such glad tiding? Did Resûlullah (ﷺ) not give you such and such glad tiding?"He turned his face and dedi:"The best we prepared is the şehadet that there is none worthy of ibadet except Allah (ﷻ) and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh. I have passed through three stages in my life. I remember a time when there was no one with greater enmity for Resûlullah (ﷺ) than I, and I desired nothing more than to have power over him so that I could kill him. If I had died in that condition, I would have certainly been from the inhabitants of cehennem ateşi. When Allah (ﷻ) placed İslâm in my heart, I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'Extend your right hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.' He stretched out his right hand, but I then withdrew my hand. He (ﷺ) sordu: 'What is wrong, O 'Amr?' I cevap verdi: 'I would like to make a condition.' He (ﷺ) sordu: 'What condition would you like to make?' I cevap verdi: 'That I be forgiven.' He (ﷺ) dedi: 'O 'Amr! Do you not know that İslâm wipes out all the günahlar committed before it, and that emigration wipes out all the günahlar committed before it, and that Ḥaj wipes out all the günahlar committed before it?' There was no one who I loved more than Resûlullah (ﷺ) and no one was more honourable in my sight than him. I could not even look at him in the eye, due to the respect I had for him. If I were sordu to describe him, I would not be able to do so because I never looked at him in the eye. If I had passed away in that condition, I would have hoped to be among the inhabitants of Cennet. Then we were assigned the responsibility of certain matters and I do not know what my condition is regarding them. When I pass away, no wailing woman or fire should accompany me. When you bury me, ensure that you throw sand onto me gently. Then stand around my grave for as long as it takes to slaughter a camel and distribute its meat so that I may be comforted by your presence and I may know what answers to give to the angels of my Sustainer."(Müslüman)
711.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is desirable to encourage a person in the throes of death to be hopeful of bütünāh's (ﷻ) rahmet. Verses and aḥādīth of bütünāh's (ﷻ) rahmet and bağışlanma may be mentioned to him, and he may be reminded of his iyilikler. 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنه) mentioned three stages of his life: before he accepted Islām, after he accepted Islām, and his era of governorship. At the time of his demise, he was concerned about this third phase of his life, perhaps because he felt that he had been deficient in fulfilling his sorumluluklar. The hadis mentions the great fazilet of Islām, emigration and Ḥaj. Scholars have stated that these noble ameller obliterate günahlar pertaining to the haklar of bütünāh (ﷻ). As for günahlar pertaining to the haklar of fellow insanî beings, gibi trusts and loans, these will not be forgiven until they have been restored or bağışlanma has been sought from the wronged individual.

712.text: A hadis passed in the chapter on honouring the family of Resûlullah (ﷺ) in which Zayd ibn Arqam (رضي الله عنه) anlatır:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) stood up among us to deliver a sermon. He praised and glorified Allah (ﷻ), admonished and reminded us and dedi: 'Listen, O people! I am merely a mortal. A messenger of my Sustainer (i.e. the angel of death) will soon come to me and I will respond to his call. I am leaving two important things among you. The first is the Book of Allāh which contains guidance and illumination. So accept the Book of Allāh and hold on firmly to it.' He emphasised practising on the Book of Allāh and encouraged holding firmly onto it. He then dedi: And (the second is) my family. I order you to obey Allāh and to fulfil the rights of my family.'"(Müslüman) This hadis was quoted previously in full.
712.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 346. It has been mentioned in Bu bölüm in order to show that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) advised his Ṣaḥābah when he felt that his death was imminent. It is, similarly, Mustaḥab (advisable) for a Muslim to advise family and friends to practise upon Islām, at the time of death and before departing on a journey.

713.narrator: Abū Sulaymān Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith (رضي الله عنه)
713.text: We went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and we were a group of young men of similar age. We stayed in his company for 20 days. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was very merciful and soft-hearted. It therefore occurred to him that we were probably missing our families, and he sordu us about those of our family we had left. When we haber verdi him, he dedi: 'Return to your families, remain among them, teach them, and instruct them towards good. Perform such-and-such namaz at such-and-such time, and such-and-such namaz at such-and-such time. When it is time for namaz, one of you should call out the adhān and the eldest of you should lead the namaz as Imām.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman). Bukhārī adds in a narration of his:"Perform namaz as you saw me performing namaz."
713.commentary: The young men went to spend bazı time in the company of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) in order to learn the laws of Islām from him. This proves the compulsion of travelling for knowledge if there is no knowledgeable person in one's area. After acquiring knowledge, it is also necessary to impart it to those who are unlearned. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was extremely merciful and soft-hearted to those who sacrificed their time to acquire knowledge. He understood their mind-set, and when he felt that they were missing home, he sent them back. From this, we learn that it is Mustaḥab (advisable) for a teacher or superior to enquire regarding the well-being of his students or subordinates.

714.text: I sought permission from Resûlullah (ﷺ) to perform Umre, so he granted me permission and dedi: 'Ey kardeşim! Do not forget us in your supplications.' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'This phrase of Resûlullah (ﷺ) pleased me to such an extent that I would not exchange it for the entire world.'"Another narration has:"Ey kardeşim! Include us in your supplications."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
714.commentary: Bu hadis was discussed previously. See hadis 373. It has been mentioned in Bu bölüm to show that one should request for du'ā' from others, even if one is superior in knowledge and status. It also proves that it is beneficial to request the pious for du'ās. The hadis illustrates the tremendous tevazu of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). Despite his elevated status, he sought the du'ā' of his Ṣaḥābah. The fact that 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) sought izin before proceeding for an ibadet bize öğretir ki juniors should daima seek advice and izin from their seniors even when engaging in optional good ameller. The hadis işaret eder the fazilet and status of 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) and that he was from amongst those whose du'ās were readily accepted by bütünāh (ﷻ).

715.text: Abdullah bin Ömer (رضي الله عنهما), yolculuğa çıkacak bir kişiye şöyle derdi: "Yanıma gel de sana Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in vedalaşırken yaptığı gibi vedalaşayım..." (Tirmizî, Hâkim)
715.commentary: The du'ā' mentioned in Bu hadis is concise yet comprehensive. It combines the best needs of dünya and the ahiret. "Your din" means may bütünāh (ﷻ) protect your din and iman. "Your güven" means may bütünāh (ﷻ) protect your yükümlülükler of Sharī'ah, your family at home, and the haklar of fellow insanî beings on your journey. "Your final ameller" means may bütünāh (ﷻ) allow you to perform righteous ameller which will fayda you in the ahiret. din is mentioned first because people generally become lax in ṣalāh and other dinî injunctions during travel.

716.narrator: Abdullāh ibn Yazīd al-Khaṭmī (رضي الله عنه)
716.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) bir orduya veda etmek istediğinde şöyle derdi: "Allah'a, dininizi, emanetinizi ve amellerinizin sonunu emanet ediyorum." (Tirmizî)
716.commentary: It is advisable for a leader to send off his army with the du'ā' quoted in this hadis, impressing upon them the önem of the din for which they are going out to engage in battle.

717.text: A man came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! I intend going on a journey so give me provisions.' He dedi: 'May Allāh provide you with salih amel.' The man dedi: 'Give me more.' He dedi: 'May He bağışla your günahlar.' The man dedi: 'Give me more.' He dedi: 'May He make goodness easy for you wherever you are.'"(Tirmidhī)
717.commentary: It is Mustaḥab (advisable) for one proceeding on a journey to request du'ās from his brothers, and for them to supplicate on his behalf for goodness. Based on this hadis, it is also acceptable to ask a person for additional du'ās, and for the latter to comply in order to bring joy to the heart of the one requesting du'ās. From his approach, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) realised that the questioner wanted manevî provisions, bundan dolayı the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) supplicated for him. 'bütünāmah Ṭībī (رحمه الله) mentioned that it is possible that he requested physical provisions for the journey gibi food, bununla birlikte the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) wisely directed his focus to that which was of greater önem, şöyle ki salih amel and bütünāh-consciousness. The greatest provision that a believer can have is taqwā, which is to abstain from the isyan of bütünāh (ﷻ) and follow His commands. In the Qur'ān, bütünāh (ﷻ) has promised bağışlanma and His assistance for those who adopt taqwā. "May He make goodness easy for you wherever you are," is a comprehensive supplication of goodness for bütün dünyevî and dinî needs.

718.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to teach us to make istikhārah just as he would teach us a sūrah of the Kur'an. He would say: 'When any of you intends doing something, he should perform two rak'āts of optional namaz and then say: Allah'ım! I ask You for guidance through Your knowledge and I ask you for strength through Your power. I ask You of Your vast bounty. Surely, You have the power while I do not. You have knowledge while I do not. You have ultimate knowledge of the unseen. O Allāh, if You know that this matter is beneficial to my İslâm, my livelihood and the final outcome of my matters (or he dedi: my matter now or later) then ordain it for me, make it easy for me, and then bless me in it. And if You know that this matter is harmful to my İslâm, my livelihood and the final outcome of my matters (or he dedi: my matter now or later) then divert it from me and divert me from it, ordain good for me wherever it may be and make me pleased with it.' He dedi: 'He should then state whatever his need is.'"(Bukhārī)
718.commentary: Istikhārah literally means to ask for goodness and koruma from harm. Technically, it means to ask bütünāh (ﷻ) for goodness. Istikhārah may only be sought in helal matters and matters in which man does not know whether there is fayda or harm gibi nikāḥ (marriage), travel, business transactions, etc. Istikhārah cannot be performed for compulsory dinî görevler and prohibitions. Bu hadis teaches us the önem of seeking the guidance of bütünāh (ﷻ). We also learn that a believer should hand over bütün his matters to bütünāh (ﷻ), since He possesses bütün power and might. By istikhārah, one humbles himself before bütünāh (ﷻ), acknowledging his limited and imperfect anlayış. The fact that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would teach the Ṣaḥābah istikhārah tıpkı a sūrah of the Qur'ān shows the önem he accorded to it. After performing two rak'āts of ṣalāh and reciting the du'ā' stated in this hadis, a person should act according to that which seems beneficial to him. It is not a requirement that one should find ilâhî guidance in a dream.

719.text: Bayram günü olduğunda Resûlullah (ﷺ) farklı bir yoldan dönerdi. (Buhârî)
719.commentary: Başka bir deyişle, he would go by one route and return by another. Scholars have mentioned çeşitli reasons why the route should be changed: 1. The ibadet of bütünāh (ﷻ) will be performed in more places. 2. Two roads, instead of one, will testify in one's favour on the day of Qiyāmah. 3. The dhikr of bütünāh (ﷻ) will be more wide-spread. 4. The poor can be assisted on her iki routes. 5. There will be a greater show of the power and unity of the Muslims. 6. It bir vesilesidir taking a good omen. By changing one's route, it is hoped there will also be a change in one's life for the better. 7. It bir vesilesidir creating awe within the hypocrites and enemies of Islām. 8. It will be possible to visit the graveyards on her iki routes. 9. One may attain the blessings of her iki routes.

720.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to depart by al-Shajarah road and enter by the al-Mu'arras road. When he entered Makkah, he would enter by al-Thaniyya al-'Ulyā and depart by al-Thaniyya al-Suflā. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
720.commentary: The al-Shajarah road is a well-known place 6 miles out of Madīnah Munawwarah on the yol to Makkah Mukarramah. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would depart for Makkah Mukarramah on this road and proceed to Dhul Ḥulaifah where he would spend the night. When returning to Madīnah Munawwarah, he would again spend the night at Dhul Ḥulaifah and then enter from al-Mu'arras. Al-Thaniyya al-'Ulyā is the high mountain pass or trail. Al-Thaniyya al-Suflā is the low mountain pass or trail. Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) stated that it is Mustaḥab (advisable) to enter Makkah Mukarramah from the al-Thaniyya al-'Ulyā and leave from the al-Thaniyya al-Suflā due to this hadis. The hikmet for entering from al-Thaniyya al-'Ulyā is that when intending to visit a place of high status, gibi Makkah Mukarramah, one should enter from a high place.

721.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) liked doing things from the right – purifying himself, combing his hair, and wearing his shoes."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
721.commentary: It is Sunnah in wuḍū' to wash the doğru arm before the left, and the doğru foot before the left. Other limbs, like the ear, hands, cheeks, etc. should be washed simultaneously. The same hüküm applies for ghusl. In tayammum, sand should be passed over the doğru hand before the left. One should commence wearing shoes from the doğru. When one emerges from the masjid with his left foot, then he should place his left foot on his shoes. He should then emerge with the doğru foot, wear his doğru shoe and then wear his left shoe. This applies when the shoes are at the exit of the masjid.

722.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used his right hand for purification and eating yemek, and his ayrıldı hand when relieving himself and in things unclean."(Abū Dāwūd)
722.commentary: Bu hadis indicates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would utilise his doğru hand for bütün ameller of honour, while he would utilise the left for ameller which are regarded as unpleasant. "When relieving himself," işaret eder washing the private parts, holding the stones and removing the impurities.

723.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to the women when they were bathing his daughter, Zaynab (رضي الله عنها):"Begin with her right side and the parts which are washed in wuḍū'."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
723.commentary: The eldest daughter of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), Zaynab (رضي الله عنها), passed away in the 8th year of Hijrī at the age of 31. Umm 'Aṭiyyah (رضي الله عنها) was one of the women who used to bathe the deceased women in the time of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). When she was about to bathe Zaynab (رضي الله عنها), the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) gave her the guidelines mentioned in this hadis. Since a person normally commences with his doğru side in ghusl whilst he is alive, those who are giving ghusl to him after his death should do the same. The limbs of the body that are washed in wuḍū' possess nobility over the remaining limbs, bundan dolayı they should be washed first when performing ghusl for the deceased.

724.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you wears shoes, he should begin with the right foot and when he removes them, he should begin with the left foot so that the right is the first to be worn and the last to be removed."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
724.commentary: Wearing shoes bir vesilesidir honouring the feet. As the doğru foot has a superior status to the left, the doğru shoe should be worn first and removed last, so that it is covered for a longer period of time. Any such amel which is done to cleanse, purify or beautify should be commenced from the doğru.

725.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) would use his right hand for eating, drinking and wearing his clothes, and he would use his ayrıldı hand for other tasks."(Abū Dāwūd)
725.commentary: Bu hadis confirms that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) consistently used his doğru hand for honourable activities and his left hand for lesser or unpleasant tasks. Ḥafṣah (رضي الله عنها) was the daughter of 'Umar ibn Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه). She was first married to Khunais ibn Ḥudhāfah (رضي الله عنه). Her husband passed away in Badr, and the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) then married her. 60 aḥādīth have been narrated from her.

726.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When you wear your clothes and perform wuḍū', begin with your right."(Abū Dāwūd)
726.commentary: Bu hadis provides a genel principle for bütün ameller of honour and purity. Beginning from the doğru is a Sunnah that brings blessings and aligns one's ameller with the uygulama of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ).

727.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) arrived in Minā where he proceeded to the Jamarah (al-'Aqabah) and stoned it. He then went to his accommodation in Minā and sacrificed an animal. He then dedi to the barber:"Start shaving,"pointing to his right side and then his left. He then distributed it (the hair) among the people. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
727.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the 10th of Dhul-Ḥijjah when the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) returned to Mīnā after spending the night at Muzdalifah. On the 10th Dhul-Ḥijjah, a pilgrim has to perform four ameller: 1. Pelting of Jamarah al-'Aqabah 2. Sacrificing an animal 3. Ḥalq (shaving of the head) 4. Ṭawāf Ziyārah. According to Imām Shāfi'ī (رحمه الله), this sequence is Sunnah, while according to Imām Abū Ḥanīfah (رحمه الله) and Imām Mālik (رحمه الله), it is compulsory. Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) included Bu hadis in Bu bölüm to show the önem of beginning from the doğru in honourable ameller, because the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) had the doğru side of his head shaved before the left.

728.narrator: Ömer ibn Abī Salamah (رضي الله عنهما)
728.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Take the name of Allāh, eat with your right hand, and eat that which is closest to you.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
728.commentary: 'Umar ibn Abī Salamah (رضي الله عنه) was the son of Umm Salamah (رضي الله عنها), the wife of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) noticed his hands moving around the plate while eating, bundan dolayı he taught him three basic and important principles of eating: 1. One should recite 'bismillāh' before eating. To do so is Wājib, bazı âlimlere göre. The hikmet of doing so is that it attracts barakah and contentment, and prevents greed. 2. One should eat with the doğru hand. 3. One should eat the food yani closest to him. This applies when the food is of a single type e.g. gravy, rice, etc. bununla birlikte, if there are birkaç varieties of food in one plate, gibi fruits, then there is no harm in eating from bütün sides.

729.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you eats, he should take the name of Allah (ﷻ). If he forgets to take the name of Allah (ﷻ) at the beginning, he should say: 'In the name of Allāh at the beginning and at the end.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
729.commentary: Bu hadis, yemek, içmek gibi işlerin başında besmele çekmenin müstehap olduğunu ispat eder. Besmele bereket getirir ve şeytanı uzaklaştırır.

730.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"When a person enters his house and takes the name of Allah (ﷻ) both when he enters and when he eats, then Shaiṭān says to his cohorts: 'You have no place to spend the night, nor is there any food for you.' And when he enters and does not take the name of Allah (ﷻ) when he enters, Shaiṭān says: 'You have a place to spend the night.' If he does not take the name of Allah (ﷻ) when he eats, Shaiṭān says: 'You have a place to spend the night and you have food.'"(Müslüman)
730.commentary: Shaiṭān, the accursed, seeks to overpower man when man is unmindful. Bu hadis reminds us of the önem of remembering bütünāh (ﷻ) so that Shaiṭān and his cohorts do not have the opportunity of spreading mischief amongst us. When the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would enter his house, he would use the miswāk and then make salām to his family members, bundan dolayı it is advisable for believers to adopt this uygulama.

731.text: When we ate with Resûlullah (ﷺ), we would not place our hands (to eat) until he had first placed his hands. Once we ate with him, and a girl who seemed to be driven forward, joined us. She began to place her hand in the food, but Resûlullah (ﷺ) grasped her hand. Then a Bedouin, who also seemed to be driven forward, joined us. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) grasped his hand as well. He then dedi: 'Shaiṭān tries to make the food lawful for himself by not having the name of Allāh taken over it. He brought this girl to make it lawful for himself, so I grasped her hand. He then brought this Bedouin to make it lawful for himself, so I grasped his hand. By that Being in whose control is my life, his hand together with their two hands is in my hand.' He then took the name of Allah (ﷻ) and began eating."(Müslüman)
731.commentary: Scholars have interpreted Bu hadis literally; bundan dolayı it is our inanç that Shaiṭān physically joins a meal in which the name of bütünāh (ﷻ) is not taken. The Ṣaḥābah did not eat until the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) began to eat because of their saygı for him. This should also be the attitude of juniors in the presence of their seniors. It is necessary for elders, parents and teachers to teach their subordinates the Islāmic etiquettes of eating and drinking.

732.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was sitting with a man who was eating. He did not take the name of Allah (ﷻ) until only one morsel of his yemek remained. When he raised it to his mouth he şöyle dedi: 'In the name of Allah (ﷻ) at the beginning and at the end.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) laughed and şöyle dedi: 'Shaiṭān continued eating with him, but when he aldı the name of Allah (ﷻ), he vomited all that was in his stomach.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
732.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the önem and necessity of taking the name of bütünāh (ﷻ) when eating. bazı scholars literally explain Bu hadis to mean that Shaiṭān physically eats with a person who does not take the name of bütünāh (ﷻ) when eating. Others explain it figuratively in that the missed barakah is regained when the name of bütünāh (ﷻ) is taken. Omitting the name of bütünāh is an invitation for Shaiṭān to join in the meal resulting in the loss of barakah.

733.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was eating yemek with six of his Sahâbe, when a Bedouin geldi along and yedi it all up in two morsels. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'If he had taken the name of Allah (ﷻ), it would have been enough for all of you.'"(Tirmidhī)
733.commentary: The blessings of bütünāh (ﷻ) are found in that food upon which His name is taken. diğer yandan, blessings are removed when the name of bütünāh (ﷻ) is not taken.

734.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) would raise the table-cloth, he would say:"All praise be to Allāh, abundant praise which is pure, mübarek kıldı and not considered to be sufficient. O our Sustainer! We neither regard it (this yemek) as final, nor do we consider ourselves independent of it."(Bukhārī)
734.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki it is Mustaḥab (desirable) to praise bütünāh (ﷻ) after eating. In essence, the du'ā' demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) is independent, while bütün of creation is dependent upon Him. We are perpetually in need of His countless favours, and bütün the praises we offer to Him are grossly insufficient in adequately discharging His haklar. The food that we eat is a bounty from bütünāh (ﷻ) and we cannot survive without it, bundan dolayı, we are taught here to also express our helplessness. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) ate on the floor and not on a table. bütün food should be removed from the table-cloth before standing up to leave.

735.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who eats food and says, 'All praise be to Allah (ﷻ) who gave me this food and provided me with it without any power or might on my part,' will have his past günahlar forgiven."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
735.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the fazilet of praising bütünāh (ﷻ) after eating. One who does so acknowledges the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ) and is appreciative of His grace. The bağışlanma of past günahlar here işaret eder minor günahlar because major günahlar require tövbe.

736.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) never criticised food. If he liked it, he ate it, and if he disliked it, he left it aside."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
736.commentary: Bu hadis draws our attention to the noble character of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). If he did not like any type of food, he would abstain from consuming it. He (ﷺ) would not criticise it. Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) stated that this applied to Ḥalāl food. If the food was Ḥarām, he would disapprove of it. As the nature of her person is farklı, it is completely normal to like or dislike certain foods. bununla birlikte, one should asla criticise any type of Ḥalāl food, as it is a bounty of bütünāh (ﷻ). Criticising food bir çeşididir ingratitude and a sign of pride, extravagance and insensitivity.

737.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sordu his family for gravy. They cevap verdi:"We have nothing except vinegar."He sordu for it and began eating it, diyerek:"Vinegar is an excellent gravy. Vinegar is an excellent gravy."(Müslüman)
737.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) repeated the ifade, "Vinegar is an excellent gravy," to stress the fazilet of consuming a simple dish gibi vinegar. In another narration, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) is rivayet edilen to have stated, "Vinegar is the gravy of the Messengers." The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) also supplicated for blessings in it. From a purely medical perspective, doctors say that vinegar is beneficial. It removes bile and phlegm, assists in digestion, kills germs in the stomach, etc. The hadis illustrates the tevazu of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). He would consume whatever food was available and then praise bütünāh (ﷻ) for it.

738.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If any of you is invited to a meal, he should accept the invitation. If he is oruç, he should supplicate (for the host), and if he is not oruç, he should eat."(Müslüman)
738.commentary: When a person is invited for a meal, he should accept the invitation because this will please the host and cultivate sevgi between them. It was the Messenger of bütünāh's (ﷺ) noble uygulama to accept invitations. aslında, he even sounded a uyarı of being disobedient to bütünāh (ﷻ) and His Messenger (ﷺ) for those who reject an invitation. It is Mustaḥab (advisable) according to çoğu scholars to accept an invitation. It is Wājib to attend a walīmah, bazı âlimlere göre. This applies to such invitations which are based on ihlâs and sevgi, and which comply to the Sunnah. Invitations which are contrary to the Sunnah or which entail any sinful practices should not be accepted. If one is fasting, then he should supplicate for bağışlanma and blessings for the host. bazı scholars interpret it to mean that he should perform ṣalāh, so that the hosting family may derive blessings thereby.

739.text: A man invited Resûlullah (ﷺ) for a meal which he prepared for him and four other people. Another person followed them. When he reached the door, Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi: 'This person has followed us. If you wish, you may allow him to enter, and if not, he will go back.' The host dedi: 'No, I allow him to enter, O Messenger of Allāh.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
739.commentary: A narration of Muslim explains the above incident in greater detail. An Anṣārī Ṣaḥābī by the name of Abū Shu'aib (رضي الله عنه) noticed hunger on the face of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), so he said to his slave, who was a butcher, "Prepare food for five people as I would like to invite the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) with four others." Since the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not know whether his host would be pleased with the extra person joining them, he sought izin and made it clear that he had not brought him along. Bu hadis teaches us: 1. Whoever prepares food for a guest can either send it to him or invite him to his home. 2. When inviting someone, it is desirable to also invite bazı of his friends and companions. 3. It is not befitting for a believer to arrive at any place uninvited. 4. The host has the doğru to prevent an uninvited person from entering his home. 5. The guest does not have the doğru to invite or take others along with him to an invitation unless the host has explicitly given his izin. 6. The host should try to accommodate uninvited guests unless he fears bazı harm or loss. 7. It is acceptable for one who is invited to take along others with him if he is sure that the host would not mind.

740.narrator: Ömer ibn Abī Salāmah (رضي الله عنهما)
740.text: I was a young boy in the care of Resûlullah (ﷺ) and my hand used to go around in the whole plate (when eating). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi to me: 'Young boy, take the name of Allāh, eat with your right hand, and eat that which is closest to you.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
740.commentary: Bu hadis was discussed earlier. See hadis 728. It mentions three Sunnah ameller of eating. It shows the önem the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) attached to imparting the teachings of Islām to others. He did not regard it as below his haysiyet to teach Islām to a young boy. Whatever is taught to children generally remains with them throughout their lives. An Arabic proverb states, "Knowledge learnt in childhood is like engraving upon stone."

741.text: A man ate with Resûlullah (ﷺ) using his left hand. So he dedi to him:"Eat with your right hand."He cevap verdi:"I cannot."He dedi:"Then you will not be able to do so."Only kibir had prevented him! Consequently, he was never able to raise it (his right hand) to his mouth. (Müslüman)
741.commentary: There was nothing yanlış with the man's hand. When advised with the truth, he proudly made an excuse to justify himself and thereby defied a emir of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), despite being extremely merciful and forgiving, cursed him. The result was that his hand was paralysed. The hadis teaches us the following dersler: 1. A person should encourage good and forbid evil at bütün times, even whilst eating. 2. It was a miracle of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) that his du'ā' was accepted. 3. It is Sunnah to drink with the doğru hand. It is incorrect to hold the drinking utensil with the left hand, or to merely place a az sayıda fingers of the doğru hand on the cup. If the fingers of the doğru hand are soiled with food, then they should be licked before grasping the utensil. 4. One should asla justify his yanlış as this bir işaretidir pride. He should rather be humble and admit to his weakness.

742.text: We were afflicted by a year of drought during the khilāfah of ('Abdullāh) ibn Zubayr (رضي الله عنه) and we were given some dates. 'Abdullāh ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما) passed by us while we were eating and dedi: 'Do not eat two at the same time because Resûlullah (ﷺ) forbade eating two at the same time.' He then dedi: 'Unless a person asks his companion for permission.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
742.commentary: When in a group, eating two dates at the same time bir işaretidir greed and disregard for the haklar of others. bununla birlikte, if bütün the others give izin, then there is no harm in doing so. According to 'bütünāmah Suyūṭī (رحمه الله), this yasak only applies when there is poverty and hardship. If there is an abundance of provisions, then there is no yasak. The hüküm does not only apply to dates, but to other types of food and drinks as well.

743.text: The Sahâbe of Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! We eat but we are not satiated."He dedi:"Perhaps you are eating separately."They cevap verdi:"Yes."He dedi:"Gather together for your food, take the name of Allāh, and nimetler will be placed in your food."(Abū Dāwūd)
743.commentary: In another hadis narrated by 'Umar (رضي الله عنه), the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Eat together and do not eat separately, because there is blessings in a group." (Ibn Mājah) Jābir (رضي الله عنه) narrated that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "The çoğu beloved food in the sight of bütünāh is that in which there are birçok hands (eating together)." (Abū Ya'lā, Ṭabrānī) Eating in a group and taking the name of bütünāh (ﷻ) before and after eating are two factors which attract ilâhî blessings. ayrıca, bütünāh's (ﷻ) unique assistance is with a group, and eating collectively also creates mutual sevgi and unity. 'bütünāmah 'Ainī (رحمه الله) stated that it is Mustaḥab (advisable) to eat in a group and that barakah descends in proportion to the number of people in the group. Also, one who eats individually sık sık does so due to greed, and this is rectified if he eats with others.

744.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Blessings descend in the centre of the food, so eat from the sides and not from the centre."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
744.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki we should eat from the sides of a plate or bowl so that the blessings which descend in the centre remain until the end of the meal. This applies to solid foods gibi rice or liquid foods gibi gravy. Fruit is excluded from this hüküm. Imām Ghazālī (رحمه الله) stated that one should also not eat from the centre of bread, but from its sides. If the bread is less, then one should divide it up between people before eating.

745.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) had a bowl which was çağırdı al-Gharrā' and it was carried by four insanlar. When it was mid-morning and the Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) had offered the ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā, the bowl would be brought, filled with tharīd and they would sit around it. When they became many, Resûlullah (ﷺ) oturdu on his knees. A Bedouin sordu: 'What is this way of sitting?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) cevap verdi: 'Surely Allāh has yaptı me a noble kul, and He did not make me an arrogant person.' Then Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'Eat from its sides, and leave its top so that nimetler may be koydu in it.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
745.commentary: The bowl was named al-Gharrā' anlam distinguished or shining. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) sat on his knees to make more space for others around the bowl. This shows his tevazu and concern for his companions. When the Bedouin questioned this posture, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained that bütünāh (ﷻ) made him a noble and humble servant, not an arrogant tyrant. The instruction to eat from the sides and leave the centre reinforces the teaching of hadis 744 that blessings descend in the centre of the food.

746.narrator: Abū Juḥayfah Wahb ibn 'Abdillāh (رضي الله عنه)
746.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"I do not eat reclining."(Bukhārī)
746.commentary: Al-Khaṭṭābī (رحمه الله) said: "One who is 'reclining' in this context işaret eder one who is leaning against a mattress yani beneath him." He continues: "The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) meant that he did not sit on mattresses and pillows like a person who intends eating a lot of food; rather, he used to sit upright without leaning against anything. He used to eat only that amount of food that would suffice him." Other scholars are of the opinion that one who is "reclining" işaret eder a person who leans on his side when eating. bütünāh (ﷻ) knows best. bütün forms of reclining are prohibited since eating bir çeşididir ibadet and requires tevazu. If one is excused due to bazı medical reason, then there is no harm in sitting in any position which will be comfortable.

747.text: I saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) sitting with both his thighs upright and eating dates."(Müslüman)
747.commentary: This posture is further explained as a person sitting with his buttocks on the ground while his thighs are upright. çeşitli sitting postures of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) whilst eating have been narrated. bazı of these are: the above-mentioned position which is referred to as iḥtibā', sitting on her iki legs, placing the left leg flat down and keeping the doğru leg upright, and sitting cross-legged. Iḥtibā' was the posture generally adopted by the Messengers of bütünāh (ﷺ). It indicates that one will be eating that amount which is sufficient and that one will not be spending excessive time doing so. It also resembles the sitting posture of slaves and was an indication of the tevazu and simplicity of the Messenger (ﷺ).

748.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you has completed eating food, he should not wipe his fingers until he has licked them or had them licked."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
748.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us the desirability of licking one's fingers after eating. One may lick them himself or they may be licked by one who does not mind licking them gibi a spouse, slave-girl, child, etc. Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) has stated that to wash one's hands without licking them is prohibited. bunun sebebi is that the small particles of food on the fingers will be washed away whereas they may contain bütünāh's (ﷻ) special blessings. When the food is of a sticky nature or the smell of food remains on one's hands, then one should wash them as the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "The blessing of food is in washing the hands before and after meals." (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī) The middle finger should be licked first, then the index finger and lastly the thumb.

749.text: I saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) eating with three fingers, and when he finished, he licked them."(Müslüman)
749.commentary: It is commendable to eat with three fingers. The fourth and fifth finger should not be utilised unless one is eating foods which are difficult to eat with three fingers gibi gravy, etc. The fayda of eating with three fingers is that one's morsel will be smaller and this will aid in digestion. After eating, one should lick one's fingers. 'bütünāmah 'Ainī (رحمه الله) stated that the amel of licking the fingers bir işaretidir being appreciative of the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ) and that licking them repels pride. To regard licking of the fingers after meals as despicable is extremely dangerous because to despise any amel of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) is tantamount to kufr (küfür).

750.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) ordered that the fingers and the plate be licked, and he dedi:"You do not know in which portion of your food the nimetler lie."(Müslüman)
750.commentary: The reason for licking of the fingers and plate is in order to derive the dolu blessings of the food. Since one does not know where the blessings of the food are, he should not waste any portion of it. Another reason why the fingers and plate should be cleaned properly is that her biri food particle is a bounty from bütünāh (ﷻ) and discarding it is an act of ingratitude towards bütünāh, the Provider. If particles gibi rice are stuck to the pot, they should be removed and eaten. If this is difficult they should be placed outside so that animals, birds and insects may consume them.

751.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If a morsel of food of one of you falls, he should pick it up, remove any dirt that may be on it, and eat it. He should not leave it for Shaiṭān. He should not wipe his hand with a cloth until he has licked his fingers because he does not know in which portion of his food the nimetler lie."(Müslüman)
751.commentary: If a morsel of food falls to the ground while eating, one should pick it up and consume it. One should not regard this as reprehensible or blameworthy because the fallen morsel is from the same food that one is consuming. It is also possible that the blessings of the food lie in the fallen morsel. If one picks up a fallen morsel regarding it to be a Sunnah, he will be greatly rewarded. Scholars state that doing so bir işaretidir tevazu and appreciation for the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ). If there is bazı dirt on the fallen morsel, then one should clean it and then eat it if it is possible to do so. If not, then one should place it in such a place where animals, insects or birds may consume it.

752.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Shaiṭān is with each one of you in whatever he does, even when he is eating. If a morsel of food of any of you falls, he should pick it up, remove any dirt on it, and then eat it. He should not leave it for Shaiṭān. When he finishes, he should lick his fingers because he does not know in which portion of his food the nimetler lie."(Müslüman)
752.commentary: The hadis bize hatırlatır ki Shaiṭān persistently tries to lead man towards the isyan of bütünāh (ﷻ). If a person recites 'bismillāh' at the time of eating, then he is saved from the snares of Shaiṭān. bazı âlimlere göre, Shaiṭān literally eats the fallen morsel of food. According to others, this has a metaphorical anlam: not eating the fallen morsel and regarding it as shameful bir işaretidir pride, which is due to satanic influence.

753.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) used to eat food, he would lick his three fingers. He dedi:"If a morsel of food of any of you falls, he should pick it up, remove any dirt on it, and eat it. He should not leave it for Shaiṭān."He emretti us to lick the bowl and dedi:"You do not know in which portion of your food the nimetler lie."(Müslüman)
753.commentary: Bu hadis reinforces the key concept that one should humble oneself before the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ). It also bize öğretir ki barakah is attained from consuming her portion of the food and not allowing any of it to go to waste.

754.text: He sordu Jābir (رضي الله عنه) about performing wuḍū' due to eating something which had been cooked by fire. He şöyle dedi:"No. We would rarely have such yemek in the time of Resûlullah (ﷺ). When we did have such yemek, we did not have towels (to wipe our hands). We used our palms, forearms and feet and we would then offer namaz without performing wuḍū'."(Bukhārī)
754.commentary: bazı aḥādīth indicate that one should perform wuḍū' after eating food which is cooked by fire, bununla birlikte bütün the four Imāms of Fiqh agree that this law no longer applies. Those narrations which indicate that one should make wuḍū' have been regarded as abrogated or the literal anlam of wuḍū' is taken, şöyle ki one should wash his hands and mouth. Alternatively, it olarak kabul edilir Mustaḥab (desirable) to make wuḍū' after eating such food. The fact that the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) rarely ate food cooked by fire shows that they lived very simple lives.

755.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Food for two suffices for three, and food for three suffices for four."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
755.commentary: The hadis encourages eating in a group as this draws ilâhî blessings. Eating together creates generosity, unites hearts and encourages a person to give preference to others over himself. bazı scholars have explained Bu hadis to mean that a person should not eat to his fill, bununla birlikte he should eat to the extent of necessity and invite others to join in the meal. It could also mean that when eating together, the quantity of food will be adequate due to the blessings of the gathering.

756.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Food for one suffices for two, and food for two suffices for four, and food for four suffices for eight."(Müslüman)
756.commentary: Bu hadis does not contradict the preceding hadis because such differences may occur due to the varying nature of people and şartlar.

757.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to take three breaths while drinking. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
757.commentary: Başka bir deyişle, he used to take three breaths on the outside of the utensil. This demektir ki the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would not drink in one gulp. He would drink a little, move the utensil away from his mouth, breathe, then drink a second time, again move the utensil away from his mouth, breathe again, and then drink the remaining water. From a health perspective, this is more effective in quenching the thirst and allowing the stomach to digest the liquid.

758.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not drink in one gulp like a camel. Rather drink taking two or three breaths. Take the name of Allah (ﷻ) when you begin to drink and praise Allah (ﷻ) when you finish drinking."(Tirmidhī)
758.commentary: The hadis bize öğretir ki we should drink liquids in two or three sips and not bütün at once. It also bize öğretir ki a person should recite 'bismillāh' when he commences drinking and 'alḥamdulillāh' after drinking. Another du'ā' which the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) recited after drinking water was: "bütün praises are due to bütünāh who has granted us sweet, palatable water by His rahmet to drink, and He has not made it salty and bitter due to our günahlar." (Ḥilyat al-Awliyā')

759.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) forbade breathing into the utensil. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
759.commentary: Bu demektir ki that it is prohibited to breathe into the utensil itself. Man inhales oxygen and exhales carbon dioxide. The latter contains poisonous chemicals, bundan dolayı by breathing into a drinking vessel in order to cool it, allows harmful gases to enter the stomach. It is amazing that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) taught us such valuable prescriptions for the korunma of good health, which doctors only came to know of birçok centuries later. ayrıca, breathing or exhaling into food or drink may cause saliva to enter it causing inconvenience to oneself or others who may be sharing the utensil.

760.text: Milk which had been mixed with water was brought to Resûlullah (ﷺ). A Bedouin was sitting to his right and Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) to his left. He (ﷺ) drank some and then gave it to the Bedouin, diyerek:"The one to the right, and then the one to his right."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
760.commentary: The hadis bize öğretir ki when distributing anything, those on the doğru should be given preference to those on the left, even if the latter are higher in status than the former. For this reason, in this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) gave preference to the Bedouin over the greatest person after the Messengers, Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه). This also testifies to the hakkaniyet and adalet of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). Water is commonly added to milk in areas of hot climate as this is known to be beneficial for the health. It is also Sunnah to drink milk in which water is added, gibi yoghurt.

761.text: A drink was brought to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he drank from it. There was a young boy to his right and some elderly men to his left. He sordu the young boy:"Do you grant me permission to give it to them?"The young boy cevap verdi:"By Allāh, no! I will not give preference to anyone regarding my share from you."So Resûlullah (ﷺ) placed it in his hand. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
761.commentary: As mentioned in the previous hadis, those on the doğru should be given preference. bununla birlikte, if there is bazı fayda in commencing with those on the left, then one should seek izin from those on the doğru. Why did the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) not seek izin from the Bedouin in the previous hadis, whereas in Bu hadis he sought izin from the young boy? If the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) took izin from the uneducated Bedouin, he might have regarded it as an infringement of his haklar. In contrast, Ibn 'Abbās (رضي الله عنه) was a close family member and he would not feel offended by such a request. ayrıca, leaders of the Quraish, gibi Khālid ibn Walīd (رضي الله عنه), had recently accepted Islām and the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) wanted to win their hearts to the iman. Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) diğer yandan, was firm in iman and there was no need to win him over. One should be eager to acquire the blessings of the pious.

762.text: Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī (رضي الله عنه) anlatır,"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) forbade folding the mouths of waterskins inside out - namely folding back their mouths and drinking directly from them."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
762.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) prohibited drinking directly from such utensils which are closed, preventing one from seeing what is on the inside. One should instead pour out the liquid into another utensil, and then drink it. bunun sebebi is that there may be a harmful insect or substance therein. Another possible reason is that if a person drinks directly from a huge utensil, the liquid could gush out causing him to choke.

763.text: Abū Hurayra (رضي الله عنه) anlatır,"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) forbade drinking from the mouth of a waterskin."(Bukhārī and Müslüman)
763.commentary: Bu hadis reinforces the previous hüküm about not drinking directly from closed containers.

764.text: Umm Thābit Kabsha bint Thābit (رضي الله عنها), the sister of Ḥassān ibn Thābit (رضي الله عنه) anlatır,"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) came to us and drank from the mouth of a hanging water-skin. So I went to its mouth and cut it off."(Tirmidhī)
764.commentary: She cut it off in order to preserve the place which the mouth of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) had touched, to derive blessings from it and to protect it from being soiled. Bu hadis clarifies the permissibility of the amel, whereas the first two aḥādīth clarify that which is best and çoğu mükemmel. And bütünāh knows best. Bu hadis shows the permissibility of drinking directly from a closed utensil whereas the previous two indicate the impermissibility of doing so. Scholars have provided çeşitli explanations: 1. If there are no other utensils available, then it will be helal to drink from a closed utensil, as one is compelled to do so. 2. In the initial stages it was helal to do so. bununla birlikte, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) later abrogated the izin. 3. As Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) stated, to drink from it is Makrūh Tanzīhī (undesirable), but helal.

765.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) yasakladı blowing into a drink. So a man sordu:"What if I see blades of grass in the utensil?"He (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"Pour it out."The man şöyle dedi:"My thirst is not quenched in one breath."He (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"Then move the utensil away from your mouth."(Tirmidhī)
765.commentary: If a blade of grass or dirt falls into a drink, then one should not blow into it to get rid of it; rather, one should pour a portion of it out, or use a spoon to remove it. If a harmful or poisonous substance has fallen into it, then bütün of it should be poured out. When drinking any liquid, a person should drink slowly and in three breaths as this will cause satiation.

766.text: The Resûlullah (ﷺ) yasakladı breathing into a utensil or blowing into it. (Tirmidhī)
766.commentary: Islām emphasises the korunma of one's health by protecting oneself from bütün those factors which may cause harm to the body. Exhaling into a utensil causes injurious gasses from the body to enter the food causing harm to the body, bundan dolayı it is prohibited. When breathing into a utensil there is also the possibility that one's saliva may enter it resulting in inconvenience for oneself or others. Scholars have stated that one should not attempt to cool hot food items or drinks by blowing into them; one should instead wait until the food or drink cools by itself.

767.text: I gave Resûlullah (ﷺ) water from Zamzam and he drank it while standing."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
767.commentary: Scholars state that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) stood and drank Zamzam for the following reasons: 1. To clarify its permissibility. 2. One who stands and drinks is able to drink more, bundan dolayı, we are teşvik edilen to drink Zamzam in abundance. 3. There was a huge crowd making it impossible to sit. 4. There was a lot of mud making it difficult to sit.

768.text: 'Alī (رضي الله عنه) geldi to Bāb al-Raḥbah and içti while standing. He şöyle dedi: 'I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) doing as you gördü me doing.'"(Bukhārī)
768.commentary: To sit and drink is Sunnah, bununla birlikte one may stand and drink if sitting is a problem, meselâ, if there is a huge crowd of people, or if there is no place to sit, and so forth. Even though it is advisable to sit and drink, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) bazen stood and drank in order to teach people that if the necessity arises, one may stand and drink. It was compulsory for the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) to teach his followers certain ameller to show their permissibility, even though these were not the çoğu advisable to perform. meselâ, he once performed wuḍū' washing bütün the limbs only once and he once performed ṭawāf on a camel, whereas bütün the scholars are unanimous that to wash the limbs thrice in wuḍū' and to perform ṭawāf while walking is more superior. From çeşitli narrations we learn that his genel uygulama was to wash the limbs thrice, to perform ṭawāf while walking and to drink while sitting, bundan dolayı these should be regarded as best practices.

769.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) zamanında yürürken yedik ve ayakta içtik." (Tirmizî)
769.commentary: Bu hadis, yürürken yemek yemenin ve ayakta su içmenin caiz olduğunu gösterir. Bununla birlikte oturarak yemek ve içmek daha faziletlidir.

770.text: From his baba from his grandfather who şöyle dedi:"I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) drinking while standing and sitting."(Tirmidhī)
770.commentary: Bu hadis confirms that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did her iki ameller to demonstrate their permissibility, although sitting while drinking is preferred.

771.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) yasakladı people from drinking while standing. Qatādah says:"We sordu Anas: 'What about eating?' He cevap verdi: 'That is worse - or more reprehensible.'"(Müslüman). Another narration has that Resûlullah (ﷺ) warned against drinking while standing.
771.commentary: Bu hadis shows that drinking while standing is sakındırılan, and eating while standing is even more sakındırılan. The previous aḥādīth showing the permissibility demonstrate that it is allowed in cases of necessity, but sitting is the preferred uygulama.

772.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"None of you should drink while standing. Whoever forgets should vomit it out."(Müslüman)
772.commentary: Âlimler, kusmuğu geri çevirme emrinin farz değil, tavsiye edilen bir davranış olduğunu belirtmişlerdir.

773.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who provides people with a drink should be the last to drink."(Tirmidhī)
773.commentary: İnsanlara hizmet etme adabı, hizmet edenin önce yemeği veya içeceği başkalarına ikram etmesi, sonra kendisinin almasıdır.

774.text: It was time for namaz and those who lived nearby went to their houses, while the others remained behind. A bowl which was made of rock was brought to Resûlullah (ﷺ). It was so small that he could not even extend his palm in it, however, all present performed wuḍū' in it."People sordu (Anas رضي الله عنه):"How many were you?"He cevap verdi:"More than 80."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
774.commentary: From this hadis, we learn that it is helal to utilise utensils made of rock. The gushing of water from between the fingers of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and that so birçok Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) performed wuḍū' from a small quantity of water were miracles displayed by the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ).

775.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) geldi to us and we brought him some su in a bowl yaptı of copper. He then kıldı wuḍū'."(Bukhārī)
775.commentary: Bu hadis, bakır kapların kullanımının helal olduğunu ispat eder. Altın ve gümüş kaplar ise erkeklere haramdır.

776.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) gitti with one of his Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) to visit a man from the Anṣār. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi to him:"If you have some su from last night in a su-skin, bring it to us, otherwise we will go and drink directly from a su source."(Bukhārī)
776.commentary: While Bu hadis suggests that one may drink water from a river or pond by placing one's mouth directly into the water, a hadis in Ibn Mājah states that one should not drink in this şekil. Scholars have explained that to do so is mekruh, bununla birlikte when there is no alternative, there is no harm. The hadis indicates that drinking from a water-skin is helal. Water kept overnight in a water-skin stays cool in the hot summer months, bundan dolayı the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) requested for such water to drink.

777.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) yasakladı us from wearing silk and silk brocade, and drinking from gold and silver utensils."He dedi:"This is for them in this world and for you in ahiret."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
777.commentary: It is prohibited for men to wear silk clothing, except during times of war and as a treatment for certain illnesses. In contrast, women are permitted to wear silk. As for eating and drinking from gold and silver utensils, it is the unanimous view of bütün the scholars that her iki men and women are included in the yasak. Similarly, it is also not helal to use gold and silver objects for applying 'iṭr and antimony. The hadis explains that it is not appropriate for a believer to pursue and utilise those bounties which bütünāh (ﷻ) has kept for him as a sevap in the ahiret. It also bize öğretir ki a believer will be rewarded in the ahiret for abstaining from günah in dünya, whereas one who disobeys bütünāh (ﷻ) will be deprived of bounties in the ahiret unless he repents.

778.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who drinks from a silver utensil is filling his stomach with the fire of Hell."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). A narration of Müslüman has:"One who eats or drinks from a silver or gold utensil..."Another narration of Müslüman has:"One who drinks from a gold or silver utensil is filling his stomach with the fire of Hell."
778.commentary: The severe uyarı in Bu hadis işaret eder the absolute yasak (ḥurmah) of utilising gold and silver utensils. Jurists have stipulated this amel to be amongst the major günahlar because it constitutes wastage and extravagance. Further, utilising such utensils is amongst the traits of the polytheists and the arrogant ones.

779.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Wear white clothes because they are amongst the best clothing you have, and shroud your deceased in them."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
779.commentary: Ibn 'Abbās (رضي الله عنه) has also narrated that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "bütünāh (ﷻ) made cennet white, and bütünāh (ﷻ) loves white." (Musnad Bazzār, Majma' al-Zawā'id) Mullā 'Alī Qārī (رحمه الله) stated that white clothing işaret eder tevazu and hayâ, and it is a natural colour. According to scientists, white clothing is best for bütün seasons: in summer, white does not absorb heat, and in winter, white does not absorb cold. White clothing is also advised for those suffering from high blood pressure and allergies.

780.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Wear white garments because they are purest and excellent. And enshroud your deceased in them as well."(Nasā'ī)
780.commentary: White clothing is çoğu pure because even a small amount of dirt or impurity can be noticed on it compared to darker colours which conceal dirt. ayrıca, white clothing is simple and bu nedenle saves one from arrogance which easily develops when one wears coloured clothing. When a person passes away, he proceeds to the gathering of the angels; bundan dolayı, it is better for him to be dressed in white, as should be the case when one visits the pious and the masājid. Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) stated that the unanimous view of the scholars is that it is Mustaḥab (advisable) to shroud the deceased in white.

781.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was of average height. I saw him in a red robe and I never saw anything more beautiful than him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
781.commentary: A ḥullah (robe) işaret eder an outfit with the upper and lower garments her iki made of a single type of fabric. While Bu hadis states that the Messenger (ﷺ) wore a red robe, other aḥādīth state that it is prohibited for men to wear red clothing. We can reconcile these çeşitli aḥādīth by saying that clothing dyed with saffron is prohibited while other types of red clothing are mekruh. Ibn Qayyim (رحمه الله) has explained this apparent contradiction by stating that those narrations which mention that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) wore red or green clothing mean that they had red or green stripes. Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) similarly stated that the Yemeni cloaks of the time had coloured stripes.

782.narrator: Abū Juḥayfah Wahb ibn 'Abdillāh (رضي الله عنه)
782.text: I saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) in Makkah while he was at al-Abṭaḥ in a red leather tent. Bilāl (رضي الله عنه) came out with his wuḍū' water. Some were able to obtain only a few drops of it while others obtained more. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then came out wearing a red suit, and it is as if I can still see the whiteness of his calves. He performed ablution and Bilāl (رضي الله عنه) called out the adhān. I observed his mouth moving to and fro, as he was diyerek to the right and left: 'Come to namaz, come to success.' Then a spear was placed upright in the ground for him. He stepped forward and performed the namaz. A dog and a donkey walked passed in front of him without being prevented from doing so."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
782.commentary: Bu hadis points out that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) wore a red robe. It is helal to draw blessings from the personal effects of the pious, to utilise their left-over wuḍū' water and their left-over food and drink. The calves of a male are not part of the 'awrah (private parts), and bundan dolayı do not need to be concealed. It is best to call out the adhān while on a journey, although not essential. When the mu'adhdhin turns his face towards the doğru and left when saying 'Come to ṣalāh, come to success,' he should not turn his chest and feet away from the Qiblah. When performing ṣalāh in an open area, a sutrah (barrier) should be placed before the Imām.

783.narrator: Abū Rimthah Rifā'ah al-Taymī (رضي الله عنه)
783.text: I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) wearing two green garments."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
