783.commentary: As mentioned previously, this was a green striped garment, and not completely green in colour. A benzer narration of Ya'lā ibn Umayyah (رضي الله عنه) states that he saw the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) performing ṭawāf of the Ka'bah whilst wearing a green-striped upper garment, with the doğru side over the doğru shoulder. (Abū Dāwūd)

784.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest (of Makkah) wearing a black turban. (Müslüman)
784.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) çoğunlukla wore a white turban, bununla birlikte he wore a black turban when in jihād because black conceals signs of dust, etc. Also it served as an indication yanilām would not change tıpkı... gibi black does not change, in contrast to other colours. Islām has not restricted the wearing of a turban to that of any single colour, bununla birlikte if a certain colour becomes the distinguishing factor of a particular misguided group or din in an area, then one should abstain from wearing that colour so that one does not resemble them.

785.narrator: Ebû Saîd 'Amr ibn Ḥurayth (رضي الله عنه)
785.text: It is as if I can see Resûlullah (ﷺ) wearing a black turban with its two ends hanging between his shoulders."(Müslüman). Another narration has:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) delivered a sermon while wearing a black turban."
785.commentary: Göre a narration of Muslim, this sermon was delivered on the pulpit on the day of Jumu'ah. This proves that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) wore a black turban on occasions besides the conquest of Makkah. birçok aḥādīth encourage the wearing of a turban. meselâ, "The turban is a matter of honour for a believer." (Daylamī) "Wear the turban. It is a salient feature of Islām. It is the differentiating factor between the Muslims and disbelievers." (Daylamī)

786.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was enshrouded in three white garments of Saḥūlī cotton. None of these garments was a shirt or a turban."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
786.commentary: Saḥūlī cotton is attributed to the place of its origin, which is a place in Yemen. 'bütünāmah 'Ainī (رحمه الله) stated that during the era of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), garments from Yemen were popular among the Arabs. They were made from cotton and had red or green stripes. It is preferable for men to be enshrouded in three garments, and it is best that they are white, as the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) commanded. See hadis 779, 780.

787.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a shawl woven from black fibres and which had images of saddle-bags."(Müslüman)
787.commentary: Bu hadis, siyah yünlü elbise giymenin caiz olduğunu gösterir. Siyah elbise giymek sünnettir ve Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in uygulamasıyla sabittir.

788.text: I was with Resûlullah (ﷺ) one night on a journey and he sordu me: 'Do you have any water?' I cevap verdi: 'Yes.' He dismounted from his camel and walked until he disappeared into the darkness of the night. When he returned, I poured out some water from a utensil and he washed his face. He was wearing a woollen cloak and he could not get his forearms out of it, except by getting them out from beneath the cloak. He then washed his forearms and passed his wet hands over his head. I then bent down to remove his leather socks, but he dedi: 'Leave them because I wore them while in a state of wuḍū'.' He then passed his wet hands over them."(Bukhārī, Müslüman). Another narration has:"He was wearing a Syrian cloak which had narrow sleeves."Another narration has that this was on the expedition of Tabūk.
788.commentary: The expedition of Tabūk, in the 9th year Hijrī, was the final expedition in which the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) physically took part. In the era of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), woollen clothing was regarded as a very simple form of clothing because wool was very cheap and such clothing was thick and rough in texture. That the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) wore such clothing, proved his tevazu and simplicity. When relieving oneself in an open area, one should go as far as possible from the sight of others. It is helal to accept help from someone while making wuḍū', but it is better not to do so. It is helal to make masaḥ on leather socks instead of washing the feet, while adhering to the şartlar mentioned in the books of jurisprudence.

789.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in en çok sevdiği elbise gömlekti. (Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî)
789.commentary: A qamīṣ işaret eder a long, loose fitting shirt with sleeves, and which reaches below the knees and above the ankles. Although not very commonly worn during the era of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), the qamīṣ was still the çoğu beloved garment to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). It was also worn by other Messengers of bütünāh, as the Qur'ān mentions about the qamīṣ of Yūsuf (عليه السلام). 'bütünāmah 'Irāqī (رحمه الله) stated that it is more preferable to wear a qamīṣ and that the Messenger (ﷺ) was fond of it because it was more concealing for the body than other types of clothing. Mullā 'Alī Qārī (رحمه الله) stated that the qamīṣ is more concealing, lighter on the body and projects tevazu.

790.narrator: Asmā' bint Yazīd al-Anṣāriyyah (رضي الله عنها)
790.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in gömleğinin kolu bileğine kadar uzanırdı. (Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî)
790.commentary: Mullā 'Alī Qārī (رحمه الله), quoting 'bütünāmah Jazrī (رحمه الله), said that it is Sunnah to have the sleeves up to the wrist. bununla birlikte, in the case of a robe or cloak, the sleeves may reach the fingertips, but this is the maximum Sunnah length.

791.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"On the day of Kıyamet, Allāh will not look at a person who used to drag his garment out of kibir."Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) dedi:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! My loin cloth drags along unless I am extremely cautious in this regard."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi to him:"You are not among those who do it out of kibir."(Bukhārī, and a part thereof by Müslüman)
791.commentary: Allowing one's garments to hang below one's ankles is prohibited and severe warnings have been sounded for doing so. Allowing the garment to hang below the ankles is normally done because of pride as narrated in hadis 796. Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) has also quoted a narration of Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) who said, "Abstain from dragging your loin cloth, because dragging the loin cloth is due to pride." Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) also quoted the ifade of Ibn 'Arabī (رحمه الله) who said, "It is not helal for a man to allow his clothing to hang over his ankles and for him to claim, 'I do not do it out of pride.' This claim will not be accepted. Such dragging of his garment is a clear sign of his pride." (Fatḥ al-Bārī) Abū Bakr's (رضي الله عنه) loin cloth would bazen unintentionally hang below his ankles. The Messenger's (ﷺ) uyarı worried him, but the Messenger (ﷺ) consoled him saying that he was not doing it intentionally out of pride; it was a mistake for which he would not be deprived of bütünāh's (ﷻ) rahmet on the day of Qiyāmah. The Messenger (ﷺ) had the doğru to exclude whom he liked from any of the commands or warnings he issued. This does not allow any other person to claim that he is free of pride.

792.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"On the day of Kıyamet, Allah (ﷻ) will not look at a person who used to drag his loin cloth out of kibir."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
792.commentary: The phrase "out of pride" is referred to as an asıl clause (qaid wāqi'ī) and not a qualifying clause (qaid iḥtirāzī). This demektir ki pride is the reason why a person normally wears his garments below the ankles. meselâ, when bütünāh (ﷻ) has haram us from killing our children due to korku of poverty, it does not mean that if one does not korku poverty, it will be helal to kill one's children. The anlam of the verse is that killing of one's children is done due to korku of poverty. Similarly, dragging one's loin-cloth is because of pride. One who claims that he is free from pride, his claim itself is an indication that he possesses pride. Four reasons have been stated for this yasak: 1. Wastage and extravagance. 2. There is similarity to the dressing of women. The Messenger (ﷺ) cursed those men who wear clothing benzer to that of women. 3. A garment which hangs below the ankles can easily become impure. 4. People will regard the person as being proud. (Fatḥ al-Bārī)

793.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Whatever of the loin cloth is below the ankles shall be in cehennem ateşi."(Bukhārī)
793.commentary: Araplar arasında elbiseyi topuktan aşağı sarkıtmak büyüklük ve gurur işareti sayılırdı. İslâm bu âdeti kaldırmış ve elbiseyi kısaltmayı emretmiştir.

794.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There are three people that Allah (ﷻ) will not speak to, nor look at, nor purify on the day of Kıyamet, and they will have a painful azap."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) repeated this three times. Abū Dharr (رضي الله عنه) dedi:"They are ruined and destroyed. Who are they, O Messenger of Allāh?"He cevap verdi:"One who wears his garment below the ankles, one who boasts after doing favours for people, and one who sells his goods by taking false oaths."(Müslüman). Another narration has:"One who wears his loin cloth below the ankles."
794.commentary: "bütünāh (ﷻ) will not speak to them" on the day of Qiyāmah demektir ki bütünāh (ﷻ) will completely turn away from them, or that He will speak to them with anger and fury. He will not look at them demektir ki He will not look at them with the gaze of rahmet. He will not purify them demektir ki they will have to go through cehennem-fire to cleanse themselves of their günah before they can enter cennet. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) repeated the uyarı three times in order to draw the attention of the listeners to the şiddet of these ameller and so that they would remember his sözler. Four severe punishments are mentioned in Bu hadis for three groups of people. This indicates that these three günahlar are major and completely prohibited.

795.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allowing a garment to hang below the ankles applies to a loin cloth, qamīṣ, and turban. On the day of Kıyamet, Allah (ﷻ) will not look at a person who drags any garment out of kibir."(Abū Dāwūd, Nasā'ī)
795.commentary: Wearing a garment which covers the ankles is prohibited with regard to bütün such clothing which is worn from the top and hangs down. böylece, if the clothing is worn on the feet and covers the ankles gibi socks or leather socks then there is no harm. Also, the yasak applies when a person is walking and standing. If he is sitting or lying down and his ankles are covered, there is no harm. (Badh al-Majhūd)

796.narrator: Abū Jurayy Jābir ibn Sulaym (رضي الله عنه)
796.text: I gördü a person whom insanlar consulted, and they accepted his advice when he verdi it. I sordu: 'Who is this?' They cevap verdi: 'He is Resûlullah (ﷺ).' I şöyle dedi: 'On you be barış, O Messenger of Allāh,' twice. He şöyle dedi: 'Do not say,"On you be barış.""On you be barış"is the greeting of the dead. Instead, say: barış upon you.' I sordu: 'Are you the Messenger of Allāh?' He cevap verdi: 'I am the Messenger of that Allāh who, if any harm afflicts you and you supplicate to Him, He will remove it from you; if a year of famine afflicts you and you supplicate to Him, He will cause the ground to sprout with plants; and if you are in a desert or barren land and you lose your conveyance, and you supplicate to Him, He will return it to you.' I şöyle dedi: 'Advise me.' – He şöyle dedi: 'Never verbally abuse anyone.' – He şöyle dedi, 'Consequently, I never verbally abused a hür person, köle, a deve or a koyun.' – (He ﷺ şöyle dedi): 'Do not despise any act of goodness. And speaking to your kardeş with a smiling face is an act of goodness. Raise your loin cloth until the middle of your calves, but beware of lowering it below your ankles for that is because of kibir and Allah (ﷻ) does not like kibir. If a person is abusive towards you or criticises you for something which he knows about you, do not criticise him for that which you know about him. By doing so, the evil consequences thereof will be suffered by him.'"(Abū Dāwūd, At-Tirmidhī)
796.commentary: Bu hadis clearly states that lowering the garment below the ankles is because of pride. The best is to wear the loin-cloth until the middle of the calves because the objective is to conceal the private parts and this is achieved by doing so. During the days of ignorance, people would greet their deceased by mentioning their names before greeting, reciting poetry, etc. In Islām, her iki the living and the deceased are greeted with السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ, as the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would say while entering a cemetery. One should avoid vulgar and abusive language. One should not criticise others merely to ridicule them. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Whoever criticises his brother because of a günah will not pass away until he commits it himself." (Aḥmad)

797.text: Once while a person was offering namaz with his loin cloth below his ankles, Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi to him: 'Go and perform wuḍū'.' He gitti, kıldı wuḍū' and döndü. He (ﷺ) (again) şöyle dedi: 'Go and perform wuḍū'.' A person sordu: 'O Messenger of Allāh, why do you order him to perform wuḍū' and then remain silent?' He cevap verdi: 'He was offering his namaz with his loin cloth below his ankles, and Allah (ﷻ) does not accept the namaz of a person whose loin cloth is below his ankles.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
797.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) commanded him to repeat his wuḍū' in order to expiate the günah of him wearing his garment below his ankles. He was not commanded to repeat the ṣalāh because the ṣalāh was not nullified; bununla birlikte, he would have been deprived of the faydalar of ṣalāh gibi bağışlanma of günahlar, purification of the heart, ilâhî sevap in the ahiret, etc. It was also possible that his wuḍū' had been performed incorrectly on the first occasion, bundan dolayı he was told to repeat it.

798.text: My baba who was a Sahâbî of Abū al-Dardā' (رضي الله عنه) haber verdi me that there was a man in Damascus who was from among the Sahâbe of Resûlullah (ﷺ) and his name was Sahl ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah (رضي الله عنه). He led a solitary life and rarely mixed with insanlar. He would perform namaz in abundance and after completing his namaz, he would recite tasbīḥ and takbīr until he döndü ev. One day, we were sitting with Abū al-Dardā' (رضي الله عنه) when he passed by us. Abū al-Dardā' (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi to him: 'Tell us something that will benefit us and will not cause any harm to you.' He şöyle dedi: 'The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) gönderdi out a grup on an expedition and after some time it döndü. A man from this grup geldi and oturdu in the gathering in which Resûlullah (ﷺ) was seated. He then şöyle dedi to the person sitting next to him: 'If only you had seen us when we met the düşman face to face. A person picked up a spear, stabbed someone with it and şöyle dedi: Take this from me, I am a Ghifārī youth.' What do you have to say about his words?' He cevap verdi: 'I think that he destroyed his sevap.' Another person heard this and şöyle dedi: 'I do not see any harm in that.' They began arguing until Resûlullah (ﷺ) heard them and şöyle dedi: 'Glory be to Allāh! There is nothing wrong with being both rewarded and hamd etti at the same time.' I noticed that Abū al-Dardā' (رضي الله عنه) was delighted with this. He raised his head towards the man and sordu: 'Did you really hear this from Resûlullah (ﷺ)?' He cevap verdi: 'Yes.' He (Abū al-Dardā' رضي الله عنه) continued repeating this to him until I thought that he would end up on his knees..."(The hadis continues with further advice about the loin cloth and personal appearance) (Abū Dāwūd)
798.commentary: Bu hadis contains comprehensive advice from the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) dâhil: During times of war, a person can proclaim, "I am so-and-so," if his niyet is to instil korku in the hearts of the enemy, and not to boast. The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) showed tremendous enböyleceiasm for acquiring knowledge. Abū al-Dardā' (رضي الله عنه) was amongst the eminent Ṣaḥābah and çoğu knowledgeable, bununla birlikte he continued acquiring knowledge from other Ṣaḥābah who were lower than him in status and knowledge. A person should cleanse and beautify his body and clothing before meeting other Muslims. His external appearance should be a source of comfort for them and not one of annoyance and irritation. This is not a form of boasting but is an expression of appreciation for the bounties of bütünāh (ﷻ).

799.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The loin cloth of a Müslüman should be until the middle of his calves. There is no harm - or nothing wrong - if it is between the knees and the ankles. Anything below the ankles will be in cehennem ateşi. Allah (ﷻ) will not look at a person who drags his loin cloth (below his ankles)."(Abū Dāwūd)
799.commentary: Bu hadis, bir müminin elbisesini baldırının ortasına kadar kısaltmasının en iyisi olduğunu, topuğa kadar olanına izin verildiğini, topuktan aşağısının ise cehennemlik olduğunu açıklar.

800.text: I passed by Resûlullah (ﷺ) while my loin cloth was hanging down. He dedi: 'O 'Abdullāh! Raise your loin cloth.' So I raised it. He dedi: 'Raise it some more.' So I raised it some more, and I have been mindful of this ever since. Some people sordu: 'How high should the loin cloth be?' He dedi: 'Until the middle of the calves.'"(Müslüman)
800.commentary: On another occasion, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said to Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه), "Wear the loin-cloth as the angels do." When asked how the angels wear it, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Until the middle of the calves." (Majma' al-Zawā'id) Salamah ibn Akwa' (رضي الله عنه) stated that 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه) used to wear his loin cloth until the middle of his calves, and he would say, "This was how my Master (ﷺ) used to wear his loin cloth." (Shamā'il)

801.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"On the day of Kıyamet, Allāh will not look at anyone who drags his garment out of kibir."Umm Salāmah (رضي الله عنها) sordu:"What should the women do with the hem of their garments?"He cevap verdi:"They should let it hang down one hand span."She dedi:"Then their feet will be exposed."He dedi:"Then they should let it hang by one forearm'in length and not more."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
801.commentary: Elbiseyi topuktan yukarı kaldırma emri erkekler içindir. Kadınlar ise elbiselerini bir karış kadar indirmeye emredilmiştir, ancak bir zira'dan (yaklaşık 45 cm) fazla olmamalıdır.

802.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who abstains from elegant clothing out of tevazu before Allah (ﷻ) despite having the ability to do so, Allah (ﷻ) will summon him on the day of Kıyamet before all the creation to give him the choice of wearing whichever garments of īmān he desires."(Tirmidhī)
802.commentary: "Garments of īmān," refer to the clothing of cennet which will be granted to the believers. Bu hadis demektir ki whoever abandons wearing exquisite and elegant clothing because of the korku of bütünāh (ﷻ), deeming the attractions of dünya as valueless, or in order to attain high ranks in the ahiret, bütünāh (ﷻ) will sevap him greatly. bununla birlikte, his abandoning of fine clothing is subject to two şartlar: it should be done in tevazu and not to be called righteous; and one should be wealthy enough to afford such fine clothing. başka bir deyişle, it does not apply to a poor person. ayrıca to his sevap in cennet, bütünāh (ﷻ) will summon him before the bütün creation in order to honour him and acknowledge his distinction.

803.narrator: Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrates from his father from his grandfather that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ)
803.text: Allah (ﷻ), nimetinin eserini kulunun üzerinde görmeyi sever. (Tirmizî)
803.commentary: When bütünāh bestows a dünyevî bounty on a person, he should utilise it, but ensure that he does not indulge in wastage and extravagance. One should not utilise it with pride and show, but with the niyet of being grateful for the bounty granted by bütünāh. A boastful garment işaret eder any such garment which a person wears so that he may be the centre of attention. The best is for a person to wear average clothing - neither that which draws attention due to its üstünlük, nor that which draws attention due to its reprehensible nature.

804.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not wear silk, as one who wears it in this world shall not wear it in ahiret."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
804.commentary: Silk clothing will be worn by the inhabitants of cennet. A person who utilises something before its appointed time will be deprived of it when the time arrives. The hikmet for the yasak of men wearing gold and silk is that these are items of decoration and beauty, bundan dolayı they are appropriate for women and not men. The beauty of men lies in their character, bravery and masculinity.

805.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Silk is worn by a person who has no share."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) A narration of Bukhārī has:"who has no share in ahiret."
805.commentary: A person who wore silk in dünya and did not repent from it will be deprived of this bounty in cennet.

806.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who wears silk in this world will not wear it in ahiret."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
806.commentary: An elaboration of Bu hadis is the hadis of Abū Hurayrah in which he narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "One who wears silk in dünya will not wear it in the ahiret. One who drinks wine in dünya will not drink it in the ahiret. One who drinks from gold and silver utensils in dünya will not drink from them in the ahiret. This is the clothing, drink and utensils of the inhabitants of cennet." (Ḥākim)

807.text: I saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) take some silk and place it in his right hand and take some gold and place it in his left hand, and say: 'These two are yasakladı for the males of my Ummah.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
807.commentary: Hem ipek hem de altın erkek Müslümanlara haramdır. Kadınların her ikisini de kullanmasına izin verilmiştir.

808.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Silk clothing and gold are yasakladı for the males of my Ummah, but lawful for the females."(Tirmidhī)
808.commentary: Children are also haram from wearing silk clothing and gold. Since immature children are not responsible (mukallaf), the günah for wearing such items will be upon their parents and guardians. Gold in Bu hadis işaret eder only gold jewellery because gold utensils are prohibited for males as well as females.

809.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) yasakladı us to drink from altın and gümüş utensils, and to wear silk and silk brocade, or sit on them."(Bukhārī)
809.commentary: Islām does not encourage a life of extravagance, and because utilising utensils of gold and silver and sitting on silken fabrics and cushions indicates to a life of extravagance, these activities have been prohibited. tıpkı... gibi Islām emphasises a believer reforming his internal self, şöyle ki his heart and soul, it encourages the rectification of the external self which has an impact upon his character and behaviour.

810.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) permitted al-Zubayr and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Awf (رضي الله عنهما) to wear silk because of an itch they were suffering from."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
810.commentary: Bu hadisten, ihtiyaç durumunda cilt hastalığı gibi sebeplerle ipek giymenin caiz olduğunu öğreniyoruz.

811.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not ride on saddle cloths made of silk and leopard skins."(Abū Dāwūd)
811.commentary: İpek ve yün karışımı giysiler giymek helaldir çünkü sahâbîler ve tâbiîn de bu tür karışımları giymişlerdir. Asıl olan ipek oranının çoğunlukta olmamasıdır.

812.text: Abū al-Malīḥ anlatır from his father (رضي الله عنه) that Resûlullah (ﷺ) yasakladı using the skins of animals of prey. (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī) A narration of Imām Tirmidhī states:"He yasakladı sitting on skins of animals of prey."
812.commentary: This yasak işaret eder animal skins which have not been tanned; since they are impure, it is not helal to sit on them. Generally, even the tanning process does not render such animal skins pure because impure hair remains attached to the skin, bundan dolayı the yasak. bazı scholars state that the yasak is because the proud and affluent utilise the skins of animals of prey, bundan dolayı we are advised to avoid resemblance with them.

813.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) giydi a new elbise, he would name it – for example, sarık, long-shirt, rıda – and say:"O Allāh, all praise be to You. You have clothed me. I ask You for the good of it and the good for which it was yaptı. I seek refuge in You from the evil of it and the evil for which it was yaptı."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
813.commentary: To recite this du'ā' when wearing new clothing is Sunnah. By doing so, a person shows his gratitude and appreciation to bütünāh for His favours. "The good of it" işaret eder covering the private parts, koruma from heat and cold, and aiding in ibadet and itaat. "The evil of it" işaret eder it being haram, impure and not remaining usable for a long period. "The good for which it was made" demektir ki it should remain clean and be worn for necessity. "The evil for which it was made" işaret eder it being a means of günah, evil, pride and vanity.

814.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) would retire to his bed, he would lie down on his right and then say: 'Allah'ım! I submit myself to You; I have turned my face to You; I have entrusted all my affairs to You; I have placed my back (my entire body) in Your protection, in anticipation of Your sevap and due to korku of Your azap. There is no escape nor salvation from You except with You. I believe in the Book which You revealed and Your Messenger whom You sent.'"(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
814.commentary: This du'ā' and its açıklama were mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 80. Reciting it before sleeping is actually a renewal of one's inanç and pact with bütünāh. Sleeping on the doğru hand side of the body is beneficial from çeşitli perspectives. Ibn Ḥajar said that it aids a person in awakening without much difficulty. Mullā 'Alī Qārī stated that sleeping on the doğru reminds one of the grave because one will be buried in this position.

815.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Before going to bed, perform the wuḍū' as you would for namaz. Then lie down on your right side and say: '...' (he dedi the same words) and then dedi: 'Let these be the last words which you say (before falling asleep).'"(Bukhārī)
815.commentary: 'Ā'ishah narrates that wheasla the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) retired to bed, he would first perform wuḍū'. (Tirmidhī) Ibn Ḥajar stated that it is Sunnah to sleep with wuḍū'. bununla birlikte, there is no need to perform a new wuḍū' if the wuḍū' performed for the 'Ishā' ṣalāh is still geçerli. There are çeşitli faydalar and faziletler of sleeping with wuḍū': one's du'ās are readily accepted if one awakes in the dead of night; angels supplicate for him; a person receives the sevap of one who fasts and worships during the night; souls that are in a state of wuḍū' prostrate before the 'arsh of bütünāh; one is safe from Shaiṭān; and one experiences gerçek dreams.

816.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to perform 11 rak'āts at night. When it was dawn, he would perform 2 short rak'āts and then lie on his right side until the mu'adhdhin came and haber verdi him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
816.commentary: It was the usual uygulama of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) to perform 11 rak'āts of ṣalāh her night which consisted of 8 rak'āts of Tahajjud and 3 rak'āts of Witr. The 2 short rak'āts of ṣalāh refer to the two Sunnah rak'āts of Fajr. Compared to other ṣalāhs, they were very short because the Messenger (ﷺ) used to recite Sūrah Kāfirūn in the first rak'āt and Sūrah Ikhlāṣ in the second. Scholars state that it is desirable for those who spend the night in the ibadet of bütünāh to lie down for a short while after the Sunnah rak'āts of Fajr with the niyet of resting and gaining strength for further ibadetler.

817.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) gece yatağına çekildiğinde elini yanağının altına koyar ve şöyle derdi: "Allah'ım! İsminle ölür ve dirilirim." Uyandığında: "Bizi öldürdükten sonra dirilten Allah'a hamd olsun, dönüş O'nadır" derdi. (Buhârî)
817.commentary: One of the Sunnahs of sleeping is to initially place one's doğru hand under one's doğru cheek when lying down. Thereafter, if one needs to change his posture, it will be acceptable to do so as one will have fulfilled the Sunnah. In these du'ās, sleep has been likened to death because a sleeping person is like a dead person. He is not aware of his surroundings and is oblivious of even a thief entering his home. 'bütünāmah Ṭībī stated that the hikmet of comparing sleep to death is that the asıl purpose of life is to endeavour to attain the pleasure of bütünāh, obey Him, and to abstain from earning His anger and azap. When a person is asleep, these faydalar are temporarily removed, bundan dolayı one is like a dead person. When he then awakens, he should thank bütünāh for granting him this bounty and for removing the impediment of sleep.

818.narrator: Ya'īsh ibn Ṭikhfah al-Ghifārī (رضي الله عنه)
818.text: My baba şöyle dedi:"Once while I was yalan down on my stomach in the mescid, a man suddenly shook me with his foot and şöyle dedi: 'This manner of yalan down is despised by Allāh.' I looked up and it was Resûlullah (ﷺ)."(Abū Dāwūd)
818.commentary: Lying on one's stomach is mekruh by bütünāh because it is against the adab taught in Islām. The reason for the yasak of sleeping in this yol is explained in the hadis of Abū Dharr who narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) walked by him whilst he was lying on his stomach. The Messenger (ﷺ) tapped him with his blessed foot and said, "O Junaydib, this is the posture of the people of cehennem." (Ibn Mājah) Scholars mention four postures of sleeping: on one's back which is the posture of the Messengers who contemplate over the creation of bütünāh whilst relaxing; on one's doğru side which is the Sunnah yöntem of the Messenger; on one's left side which is generally the posture of the kings and wealthy; and on one's stomach which is the posture of Shaiṭān and the inmates of cehennem.

819.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who sits in a place without remembering Allah (ﷻ) therein, is subjected to a shortcoming from Allah (ﷻ), and one who lies down in a place without remembering Allah (ﷻ) therein, is subjected to a shortcoming from Allah (ﷻ)."(Abū Dāwūd)
819.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki when one sits in any place, one should remember bütünāh for a short while. One should at least recite the du'ā' which is mentioned in hadis 832, 833 and 834. A person should endeavour to remember bütünāh in bütün şartlar. bütünāh says, "They who remember bütünāh while standing, sitting and lying down, and they think about the creation of the heavens and earth. 'Our Sustainer, You have not created bütün this without a purpose. We glorify Your purity so save us from the azap of the Fire.'" (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 191) The fazilet of remembering bütünāh at the time of sleeping can be gauged from a narration of Abū Muray'ah al-'Ajalī in Fatḥ al-Bārī, which states that the bed of a person who retires to it in a state of wuḍū' and falls off to sleep while engaged in bütünāh's remembrance, becomes a masjid and he olarak kabul edilir one engaged in ṣalāh therein until he awakens.

820.text: He saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) lying on his back in the mescid with one leg over the other. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
820.commentary: Bu hadis shows the permissibility of lying in the şekil described, bununla birlikte, in another narration, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) prohibited it. Scholars state that the yasak applies when one is wearing a loin-cloth and there is a korku of the private parts being exposed. Where no such korku exists, there is no harm. It is helal to lie down in the masjid on şart that the masjid is not made into a hotel or permanent sleeping area. If one does lie down in the masjid, one should make an niyet for I'tikāf and perform bazı form of ibadet.

821.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) sabah namazını kılar, sonra güneş doğana kadar namaz kıldığı yerde bağdaş kurarak otururdu. (Buhârî, Müslim)
821.commentary: The time after the Fajr ṣalāh until Ishrāq (sunrise) is a very blessed time as a person's mind is fresh and attentive, bundan dolayı scholars state that it is Mustaḥab (desirable) to remain in the masjid to engage in dhikr, tilāwah, du'ā', etc. at this time. This was the genel uygulama of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah.

822.text: I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) sitting in the courtyard of the Ka'bah by drawing his legs against his belly with his hands like this,"and he demonstrated it with his hands. (Bukhārī)
822.commentary: This şekil of sitting is known as Iḥtibā' or Qurfuṣā'. It involves a person sitting on his buttocks with his knees raised, his thighs against his belly, and his hands around his shin bones.

823.text: I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) sitting by drawing his legs against his belly with his hands. When I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) sitting in such a humble position, I trembled out of korku."(Abū Dāwūd)
823.commentary: The posture described here is generally adopted by the poor and destitute, as well as those who are immersed in worries and korku. bundan dolayı, sitting in this şekil indicates one's humbleness and hayâ. That the Messenger (ﷺ), despite being the ruler of her iki the worlds, sat in this humble position, was an amazing sight and created korku in the heart of the Ṣaḥābī who saw him.

824.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by me while I was sitting like this: I koydu my ayrıldı hand behind my back and I was supporting myself on the fleshy part of my thumb. He şöyle dedi to me: 'Are you sitting like those who earned the anger of Allāh?'"(Abū Dāwūd)
824.commentary: Muslims have been haram from imitating the Jews and Christians in bütün forms of söz and ameller.

825.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"None of you should make a person get up from his seat and then take his place, but you should be accommodating and make place."If anyone stood up from his place to allow Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) to sit, he would not sit in it. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
825.commentary: It is haram to request a person to move from a place he has occupied first, so that another may sit in it, even if the latter is superior in knowledge and age. bununla birlikte, jurists have excluded from this yasak a person who teaches students in a özel section of the masjid. If it is occupied by someone else, he can be asked to move. Similarly, if a vendor in the marketplace has adopted a özel area, then he can ask another who has occupied it to move away. It is Mustaḥab (desirable) for a person to give place to his seniors provided that he is not coerced. Ibn 'Umar would not sit in a place where somebody had stood up for him due to his level of takvâ and abstinence, fearing that he should not be included in the yasak mentioned in this hadis.

826.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If any of you gets up from his place and then returns to it, he is more entitled to it."(Müslüman)
826.commentary: If a person is sitting in a particular place and he has to briefly go out for a need gibi wuḍū', then he is entitled to his place when he returns. If another person takes his place, he may be requested to move away. bununla birlikte, it is advisable that a person leaves behind bazı possession gibi a scarf so that others know that he intends returning. If he does not return for a long period of time, then he loses his doğru to that place. It is not helal for any person to permanently stipulate a place in the masjid for himself.

827.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in meclisine gittiğimizde, meclisin bittiği yere otururduk. (Ebû Dâvûd)
827.commentary: Bir kişi bir meclise geç gelirse ve insanlar oturmuşsa, meclisin boş bir yerine oturmalı, insanları yerlerinden kaldırmaya çalışmamalıdır.

828.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A person who performs ghusl on the day of Cuma, purifies himself to the best of his ability, applies oil or puts on any perfume he has in his house, then goes out and does not separate between two people, performs whatever namaz is prescribed for him, and is silent when the Imām speaks, then he is forgiven for günahlar committed from then until the next Cuma."(Bukhārī)
828.commentary: "Does not separate between two people," demektir ki if two people are sitting together as friends, then one should not intrude. Similarly, if two people are sitting in a row in the masjid and there is no space between them, then one should not squeeze and force his yol between them. Scholars state that the yasak of not moving between the rows applies when there are no gaps in front. If gaps have been left open in front, then it will be doğru to walk through the rows and proceed to the front because those sitting at the rear are at fault for not filling the spaces in front of them. bazı hadis scholars have stated that there is an indication in Bu hadis that a person should endeavour to arrive early for Jumu'ah so that such situations do not arise. It is Sunnah to perform ghusl on the day of Jumu'ah. It is advisable to cleanse oneself on the day of Jumu'ah by clipping nails, trimming the moustache, wearing clean clothes, etc. Applying 'iṭr on the day of Jumu'ah is Mustaḥab (advisable). It is Mustaḥab (advisable) to perform optional ṣalāh before the khuṭbah. It is compulsory to remain silent once the khuṭbah begins.

829.text: 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb anlatır from his father from his grandfather (رضي الله عنه) that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"It is not permissible for a person to separate two people without obtaining their permission."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī) A narration of Abū Dāwūd has:"He should not sit between two people without their permission."
829.commentary: If two people are sitting together then a third person should not intrude because their conversation may be regarding a private matter and an intrusion may spark ill feelings. Scholars state that if a person knows that two people are sitting because of their acquaintance or friendship with her biri other, then he should not intrude. If they are coincidentally sitting next to one another, then there is no harm if one sits with them after asking their izin. If one is not sure whether they are acquaintances or not, then caution demands that one should not intrude. If a person notices two people talking quietly, then he should not intrude. He should not even sit so close to them that he may be able to hear their söz.

830.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) cursed the person who sits in the centre of a circle. (Abū Dāwūd) Tirmidhī anlatır from Abū Mijlaz that a man sat in the centre of a circle, so Ḥudhayfah (رضي الله عنه) dedi,"One who sits in the centre of a circle is cursed on the tongue of Muhammed (ﷺ) - or Allah (ﷻ) has cursed him on the tongue of Muhammed (ﷺ)."(Tirmidhī)
830.commentary: çeşitli meanings have been suggested regarding sitting in the centre of a circle. bazı of these are: When people are sitting in a circle and a person sits in between bütün of them; when a person sits in the centre of a group of people to make them laugh; when a person jumps over people in a gathering causing them inconvenience, then sits in the centre and obstructs the view of bazı of them. The hadis may include bütün of the above scenarios, bundan dolayı a believer should abstain from such ameller. özetle, it is compulsory for a Muslim to abstain from inconveniencing others in any yol.

831.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"The best of assemblies is the one which is most spacious."(Abū Dāwūd)
831.commentary: Three meanings of Bu hadis have been suggested: If any gathering gibi a lecture or bazı helal function is taking place and birçok people will be attending, then it should be held at such a venue where there is adequate space, so that there is no difficulty and discomfort for people to sit; if people are sitting in a gathering and others arrive late, then the former should make space for the latter; a gathering which is constricted or in which there is little space bir sebebidir discomfort to those present and may lead to ill-feelings. diğer yandan, a spacious gathering provides comfort to those present allowing them to easily stand up and sit down.

832.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who sits in a gathering in which he speaks a lot of idle talk, will be forgiven for all that has transpired if he says before getting up from it, 'Glory be to You, O Allāh, and all praise be to You. I testify that there is none worthy of ibadet except You. I seek Your bağışlanma and I turn in repentance to You.'"(Tirmidhī)
832.commentary: Laghaṭ (idle talk) literally means söz in which there is noise, shouting and sözler whose anlam cannot be understood. In the context of the hadis, it işaret eder futile söz which will be of no fayda in the ahiret. bağışlanma here işaret eder minor günahlar because major günahlar as well as günahlar relating to the haklar of others will not be forgiven without sincere tövbe and restoring such usurped haklar.

833.text: Abū Barzah (رضي الله عنه) anlatır:"When Resûlullah (ﷺ) intended getting up from a gathering, the last thing he would say was, 'Glory be to You, O Allāh, and all praise be to You. I testify that there is none worthy of ibadet except You. I seek Your bağışlanma and I turn in repentance to You.'"A man sordu: 'O Messenger of Allāh, you are diyerek words which you did not say in the past?' He dedi: 'That is an expiation for what takes place in the gathering.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
833.commentary: Bu hadis encourages the recitation of this du'ā' at the end of gatherings. Even the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would recite this du'ā', seeking bağışlanma for any shortcomings in the gathering. It also shows that the Ṣaḥābah would observe the ameller of the Messenger (ﷺ) very closely and would enquire about any new practices they observed.

834.text: Rarely would Resûlullah (ﷺ) rise from a gathering without making the following supplication: 'O Allāh, grant us such korku of You that will be a barrier between us and Your disobedience, and such obedience of You that will convey us to Your Cennet, and such conviction that will make all the calamities of this world easy for us. Allah'ım! Enable us to benefit from our hearing, eyesight and strength for as long as You keep us alive and make these survive our death. Grant us revenge from those who oppress us and assist us against those who oppose us. Do not make us experience disaster in our religion. Do not make the world our main concern nor the limit of our knowledge. Do not grant authority over us to those who have no rahmet for us.'"(Tirmidhī)
834.commentary: This is a beautiful and comprehensive du'ā' which the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would make at the conclusion of a gathering. In it one seeks the goodness of her iki worlds. korku of bütünāh should be to the extent that it saves one from His isyan. The stronger a person's inanç and conviction is in bütünāh and the ahiret, the more insignificant the difficulties of this life will seem. Our senses are a güven from bütünāh and we should fayda from them by utilising them in the doğru avenues. One should hand over bütün matters pertaining to his enemies and oppressors to bütünāh. The worst trial that a person can experience is with regard to his din by committing günah and not doing good ameller.

835.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any group of people rise from a gathering wherein they did not engage in the remembrance of Allah (ﷻ), they rise as if they are rising from the carcass of a donkey and it will be a source of remorse for them."(Abū Dāwūd)
835.commentary: On the day of Qiyāmah, when people will see the reality of their futile söz and ameller, they will be utterly disgusted with them tıpkı... gibi people sitting around a dead donkey are disgusted. It also indicates that such people are foolish, since a donkey is proverbial for its foolishness. On the day of Qiyāmah, a person will see the rewards of those who engaged in the remembrance of bütünāh and will then express sorrow over her second of his life which he wasted.

836.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any group of people sit in a gathering without remembering Allah (ﷻ) therein and without sending salutations upon their Messenger, then they will suffer a shortcoming. If Allah (ﷻ) wills, He will punish them, and if He wills, He will bağışla them."(Tirmidhī)
836.commentary: Göre bazı scholars, it is compulsory to remember bütünāh and send salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ) in her gathering, since azap has been declared for those who do not do so.

837.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Whoever sits in any place without remembering Allah (ﷻ) therein, will suffer a shortcoming from Allah (ﷻ). Whoever lies down in a place without remembering Allah (ﷻ) therein, will suffer a shortcoming from Allah (ﷻ)."(Abū Dāwūd)
837.commentary: This and other benzer aḥādīth indicate that one should be aware of bütünāh at bütün times. If this state of mind is achieved, then our gatherings will be free of backbiting, accusations, slander and so forth, and we will be safe from enmity, nefret and animosity. Ideally, our gatherings need to resonate with the remembrance of bütünāh and His Messenger (ﷺ), the seeking of knowledge, enquiring about the state of Muslims so that we may supplicate on their behalf and assist them.

838.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"Nothing is left of prophethood except glad tidings."The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) sordu:"What are glad tidings?"He cevap verdi:"A true dream."(Bukhārī)
838.commentary: With the demise of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), ilâhî revelation providing knowledge of future events terminated; bununla birlikte, by means of dreams, bütünāh will continue granting gerçek knowledge of future events. When a believer sees a frightening dream, it is a sign for him to prepare for any difficulty which is to come his yol. It should be remembered that dreams are only a means of encouraging a person towards good or preventing him from evil. No hüküm of the Sharī'ah can be established or abrogated via dreams.

839.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When the time (of Kıyamet) draws near, the dream of a mümin will rarely be false. The dream of a mümin is a forty-sixth part of prophethood."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) Another narration states:"The most truthful of you in respect of your dreams is the most truthful of you in speech."
839.commentary: Göre the scholars, Bu hadis demektir ki bütünāh will grant solace and happiness to a believer by showing him certain realities at a time when people have become corrupt. Imām Khaṭṭābī stated that a gerçek dream is a forty-sixth part of prophethood because for six months prior to the commencement of ilâhî revelation, the Messenger (ﷺ) used to have gerçek dreams. Since the period of revelation stretched over a period of 23 years, six months are a forty-sixth portion of it. The heart and senses of a person who speaks the truth are enlightened and güçlü, bundan dolayı birçok intangible things are exposed to him and he generally sees the truth in his dreams.

840.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who sees me when he is asleep will see me while awake – or it is as if he had seen me while awake – Shaiṭān cannot take my form."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
840.commentary: bazı âlimler der ki one who saw the Messenger (ﷺ) in his sleep will be blessed with meeting the Messenger (ﷺ) in the ahiret. Ibn Baṭṭāl said that one who sees the Messenger (ﷺ) in his sleep will receive confirmation of the validity of this vision while he is awake; it does not refer to the ahiret because bütün Muslims will see him in the ahiret, irrespective of whether they had seen him in a dream or not. Ibn Ḥajar stated, "One who sees the Messenger (ﷺ) in a dream, will be honoured by a special meeting with the Messenger (ﷺ) after his demise. Beholding the Messenger (ﷺ) is a sign that he (ﷺ) will intercede on one's behalf." The Messenger (ﷺ) is the leader of guidance, whilst Shaiṭān is the leader of evil and misguidance. These are two opposing forces, bundan dolayı Shaiṭān cannot adopt the form of the Messenger (ﷺ). tıpkı... gibi the Messenger (ﷺ) was divinely protected from Shaiṭān's influence during his lifetime, he (ﷺ) has also been safeguarded against his mischief after his demise.

841.text: He heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"If any of you sees a dream which he likes, then it is from Allah (ﷻ), so he should praise Allah (ﷻ) for it and relate it – and in another narration – he should only relate it to those whom he loves. But if he sees something which he dislikes, then it is from Shaiṭān, so he should seek refuge from its evil and not relate it to anyone. It will not harm him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
841.commentary: When a person sees a good dream, he should attribute it to bütünāh and praise bütünāh. A good dream is a glad tiding for a believer because it will serve as a motivation for him to enhance his character and increase his ümit in bütünāh. The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "A dream remains suspended until it is interpreted. Once it is interpreted, it will manifest itself according to the yorum. bundan dolayı, do not narrate your dream except to a person you are fond of and who is intelligent." (Tirmidhī) Ibn Ḥajar stated that the Messenger (ﷺ) permitted one to narrate one's dreams only to those whom one loves because strangers and others may harbour jealousy. They may bu nedenle give an unpleasant yorum, and this may prove detrimental. In comparison, a scholar will provide a beneficial yorum and if he narrates it to those whom he loves it will be regarded as a good omen, and good omens are desirable. diğer yandan, when a person sees an evil dream, he should attribute it to Shaiṭān because such dreams are generally due to the latter's whisperings. One should seek refuge in bütünāh from such dreams and not mention them to anyone. This will protect a person from their evil effects.

842.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A good dream – and in another narration – a beautiful dream is from Allah (ﷻ), and a bad dream is from Shaiṭān. One who sees something which he dislikes should spit three times to his left and seek refuge from Shaiṭān. It will not harm him."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) Nafath means to blow lightly without emitting any saliva.
842.commentary: When seeing an evil dream, one is advised to spit to the left in order to drive away Shaiṭān as a rebuke and a form of ridicule. The left has been specified because it is associated with unpleasant and mekruh things. Ibn Ḥajar stated that the following etiquettes should be adhered to after seeing a bad dream: One should seek bütünāh's koruma by reciting a'ūdhu billāhi minash shaiṭānir rajīm; One should spit to the left side; One should refrain from discussing it with anyone; One should change the side in which one was sleeping; One should perform ṣalāh; One should recite Āyat al-Kursī.

843.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If any of you sees a dream which he dislikes, then he should spit three times to his left, seek refuge in Allah (ﷻ) from Shaiṭān three times, and turn over from the side on which he was lying down."(Müslüman)
843.commentary: In this hadis, the kelime falyabṣuq has been used. It işaret eder spitting with the emergence of saliva. In the previous hadis, the kelime falyunfuth was used. This işaret eder merely blowing without the emergence of any saliva. According to circumstances, a person may practise on her iki or any of the two. One should turn away from the side on which he was lying down believing that the evil of the dream will be averted in favour of good.

844.narrator: Abū al-Asqa' Wāthilah ibn al-Asqa (رضي الله عنه)
844.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The greatest of untruths is for a person to attribute his lineage to someone other than his father, to claim to have seen something in a dream which he did not see, or to attribute to Resûlullah (ﷺ) something which he did not say."(Bukhārī)
844.commentary: To attribute one's lineage to someone other than one's father is a major günah. It is the height of ingratitude and will ultimately lead to confusion in families and ancestries. To claim to have seen a dream which one did not see is a major günah. bunun sebebi is that dreams are a substitute for revelation which comes from bütünāh, bundan dolayı by narrating a yanlış dream, one attributes a lie to bütünāh. This is far worse than speaking a lie in normal circumstances because the latter involves only the creation, not the Creator. To attribute to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) something which he did not say is a reference to those who fabricate aḥādīth. This is also strongly prohibited because it allows falsehood to spread and it creates a blot upon the august personality of the Messenger (ﷺ). In another hadis, the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever intentionally lies against me should prepare his abode in cehennem." (Muslim)

845.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنهما)
845.text: A man sordu Resûlullah (ﷺ):"What type of deed in İslâm is best?"He cevap verdi:"Feeding people and offering salām to those you know and those you do not know."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
845.commentary: birçok Ṣaḥābah are rivayet edilen to have asked the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) which amel is best in Islām. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) gave farklı answers based on circumstances and occasions. ayrıca, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would take into consideration the person asking the question. If he had a particular deficiency or weakness within him, he would be given a related answer. Feeding has been mentioned alongside greeting because her iki ameller eliminate enmity and create sevgi and affection between people. Food may be given to Muslims, non-Muslims and even animals. By feeding others, one alleviates the burden of poverty and fulfils the needs of others. It creates sevgi, bonds hearts and işaret eder the generosity of the giver. A Muslim should daima endeavour to serve and assist others. A believer should make the salient features of Islām yaygın in society. Other greetings gibi hello, hi, good morning, good day, etc. can asla match the beauty of the Islāmic greeting.

846.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When Allah (ﷻ) created Ādam (عليه السلام), He dedi: 'Go and offer salām to those – a group of angels who were seated – and listen to their reply. That will be your greeting and the greeting of your progeny.' Ādam (عليه السلام) dedi: 'Peace be upon you.' They cevap verdi: 'Peace be upon you and the rahmet of Allāh.' They added, 'and the rahmet of Allāh.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
846.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki the Islāmic greeting of salām was initiated since the time of Ādam (عليه السلام) by bütünāh Himself, and that it was the greeting of bütün the previous ilâhî religions. It is advisable to answer to a greeting with more than what was uttered as mentioned in the Qur'ānic verse quoted above. The best is to offer the reply, "Wa 'alaykumus salām wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuhu."

847.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) emretti us to do seven things: to visit the ill, attend funerals, say yarḥamukallāh to the one who sneezes, assist the weak, assist the oppressed, make the greeting of salām common, and assist to fulfil the oath of a person who took an oath. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
847.commentary: Benzer bir hadis daha önceki bir bölümde zikredilmiştir. Bkz. hadis 239. İmam Nevevî bu konuyu Şerhu Müslim'de detaylıca açıklamıştır.

848.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"You will not enter Cennet unless you believe, and you do not believe unless you have love for each other. Should I not direct you towards that which, if you engage in, you will develop love for each other? Make the salām common among you."(Müslüman)
848.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 378. The perfection of īmān demands that there be mutual sevgi amongst believers. A person whose heart is filled with malice, jealousy, nefret and pride can asla have mükemmel īmān. Since sevgi is not a voluntary şart, one has to utilise those means which will create this quality within oneself. One such means is the greeting of salām. We are not merely ordered to say the salām, but to make it yaygın.

849.narrator: Abū Yūsuf 'Abdullāh ibn Salām (رضي الله عنه)
849.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"O people! Make the salām common among you, provide food, maintain ties of kinship, offer namaz while people are asleep, and you will enter Cennet with ease."(Tirmidhī)
849.commentary: 'Abdullāh ibn Salām stated, "When the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) entered Madīnah Munawwarah, people thronged to meet him. I was one of them. When I looked at the face of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), I knew that his face was not that of a liar. The first sözler I heard him say were, 'O people! Make the salām yaygın among you, provide food, maintain ties of kinship, offer ṣalāh while people are asleep, and you will enter cennet with ease.'" (Tirmidhī) The performance of these four ameller will cause a person to enter cennet amongst those who will enter it first. Providing food to people under normal circumstances is Sunnah, bununla birlikte during times of desperation, it becomes Farḍ (compulsory).

850.text: Al-Ṭufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b anlatır that he used to visit 'Abdullāh ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) and go with him to the market-place. He dedi:"When we went to the market-place, 'Abdullāh (رضي الله عنه) did not pass by anyone selling cheap quality goods or other commodities, a poor person, and anyone else without offering salām to them."Al-Ṭufayl dedi:"I visited 'Abdullāh ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) one day and he sordu me to go with him to the market-place. I dedi to him: 'What are you going to do in the market-place when you do not sell anything, nor ask about any goods, nor enquire about the price, nor sit in any of the assemblies of the market-place? We should just sit here and talk.' He dedi: 'O you with a belly' – Al-Ṭufayl had a large belly – 'we go only to offer salām to whoever we meet.'"(Mālik)
850.commentary: Market places are places of business and transactions, which make one negligent of bütünāh. Knowing this, Ibn 'Umar reminded people to remember bütünāh. A hadis states, "One who remembers bütünāh amongst those who are unmindful is like one who remains on the battlefield after bütün his companions have fled." (Bazzār and Ṭabrānī in Kabīr and Awsaṭ) It is helal to go to a gathering with no other objective but to offer the salām. This will apply when one is sure that one will not commit any günah. If there is a korku of günah, then one should not proceed. It is Mustaḥab (desirable) to offer the salām to her person one meets, even if this means making an abundance of salām. It is helal to refer to a person by mentioning a certain quality of his, provided that he does not object to it and the niyet is not to belittle or embarrass him. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) referred to bazı Ṣaḥābah in this yol gibi Abū Hurayrah, Safīnah, etc.

851.text: A man geldi to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and şöyle dedi: 'Assalāmu 'alaykum.' He cevap verdi to his greeting and the man oturdu down. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'Ten.' Then another man geldi and şöyle dedi: 'Assalāmu 'alaykum wa raḥmatullāh.' He cevap verdi to his greeting and the man oturdu down. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'Twenty.' Then another man geldi and şöyle dedi: 'Assalāmu 'alaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuhu.' He cevap verdi to his greeting and the man oturdu down. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'Thirty.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
851.commentary: The sözler "ten", "twenty" and "thirty" refer to the amount of rewards that her biri person obtained for offering the salām in the yol that he did. Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one is rewarded for offering salām according to the number of sözler he utters. It is advisable that one offers the salām in the şekil it was taught to us by the Messenger (ﷺ). It should not be abbreviated to phrases gibi 'salāms', and so forth.

852.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'This is Jibra'īl conveying the salām to you.' I cevap verdi: 'And upon him be peace and the rahmet and nimetler of Allāh.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
852.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the fazilet of 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها). From amongst bütün the noble wives, Jibra'īl (عليه السلام) only conveyed salām to Khadījah (رضي الله عنها) and 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها). It is compulsory to reply to the salām of a third person. When replying to the salām of a third person via an intermediary, one should should say 'alaihi' instead of 'alaikum'. When reading a letter, email, etc. it is compulsory to verbally reply to a salām. It is more virtuous to reply with additional sözler as 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) had done. It is helal for a strange man to send salām to a pious woman via her maḥram if no korku of evil exists between them. In this hadis, 'Ā'ishāh (رضي الله عنها) only replied to the salām of Jiba'īl (عليه السلام), bununla birlikte one may also offer salām to the person who conveys it.

853.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi something, he would repeat it thrice so that it could be anladı. When he gitti to any insanlar, he would greet them thrice. (Bukhārī) This applied when the gathering of insanlar was large.
853.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would greet thrice if the gathering was huge: once to those on the doğru, once to those on the left, and once to those in front of him. This was so that his blessed voice would reach everyone. If one person in the group had heard the salām and answered, it would have been sufficient, bununla birlikte, he wanted to please bütün those present. Scholars state that this was proof of his lofty character as he took into consideration the sentiments and feelings of people around him. Scholars state that it is reprehensible to only greet özel individuals in a gathering of people. The objective of salām is to create sevgi, bundan dolayı by only greeting bazı, one creates a dislike in the hearts of others. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would repeat himself thrice so that people who might not have understood his sözler the first time around could understand them. It was also possible that by means of repetition, doubts would be eliminated.

854.text: Al-Miqdād (رضي الله عنه), in a lengthy hadis of his, anlatır:"We used to take the Messenger of Allāh'in (ﷺ) share of milk to him. At night, he would come and offer salām in a tone that would not awaken those who were asleep, but could be heard by those who were awake. So, he came and offered salām as was his norm."(Müslüman)
854.commentary: An important adab of insanî interactions is taught to us in this hadis. If bazı people are awake whilst others are asleep, then one should greet in such a tone that will not awaken those who are asleep. bunun sebebi is that to make salām is Sunnah, but to cause harm and inconvenience to others is Ḥarām (prohibited). The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The gerçek believer is one from whom other believers are saved from his tongue and hands." (Bukhārī)

855.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) bir gün mescitten geçerken bir grup kadının oturduğunu gördü ve onlara selam verdi. (Câmi')
855.commentary: To suffice with salām by merely gesturing with the hand has been prohibited in other narrations, as this is the yol of the Jews and Christians. bundan dolayı, Imām Nawawī mentioned the second narration to indicate that when greeting females a gesture should be accompanied by a verbal söz. Scholars state that offering salām to strange women was a speciality of the Messenger (ﷺ) because he was sinless and protected from evil. With regard to the rest of the Ummah, it is not doğru for a man to offer salām or reply to the salām of a female and vice versa. In cases where there is absolutely no korku of evil, gibi a maḥram (whom one cannot marry) or an extremely old man or woman, then it will be helal to greet.

856.text: I came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'Upon you be peace, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He dedi: 'Do not say: 'Upon you be peace.' Upon you be peace is the greeting of the dead.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
856.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 796. During the days of ignorance, people would greet their deceased by mentioning their names before the greetings in their poetry, etc. In contrast, in Islām her iki the living and the deceased are greeted with Assalāmu 'alayka, as the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would say while entering a cemetery: Assalāmu 'alaykum dāra qawmin mu'minīn (Peace be upon you, O believing dwellers of the permanent abode).

857.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who is on a conveyance should offer salām to one who is walking, one who is walking should offer salām to one who is sitting, and a small group should offer salām to a larger group."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) A narration of Bukhārī states:"the young should offer salām to the old."
857.commentary: One who is on a conveyance should offer salām to the one who is walking so that the former does not develop a feeling of supremacy or pride due to his conveyance. This also applies to one who is walking in relation to one who is sitting. Another reason in the latter case, is that it would be difficult for one who is sitting to greet her person who walks by, bundan dolayı he is excused from initiating the greeting. A small group should offer salām to a larger group due to the fazilet of a larger group or because a single person or a small group may develop pride if a larger group greets first. The young should offer salām to the old because of the doğru a senior has over his junior. A junior has been commanded to honour and saygı his senior.

858.narrator: Ebû Ümâme Ṣudayy ibn 'Ajlān al-Bāhilī (رضي الله عنه)
858.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who is closest to Allah (ﷻ) is he who offers salām first."(Abū Dāwūd) Tirmidhī rivayet etti from Abū Umāmah (رضي الله عنه):"It was dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh, when two people meet, which of them should offer salām first?' He cevap verdi: 'The one who is closer to Allah (ﷻ).'"(Tirmidhī)
858.commentary: Scholars state that one who obeys bütünāh to a greater extent greets first because he remembers bütünāh first, and he is eager to please his Muslim brother and remind him to remember bütünāh.

859.text: In a hadis about a person who offered his namaz incorrectly that he came and offered namaz. He then went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and offered salām to him. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) returned the salām and dedi: 'Go back and offer your namaz as you have not offered your namaz.' The man went back and offered the namaz. He then went and offered salām to Resûlullah (ﷺ) until he did this three times."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
859.commentary: In this hadis, a village dweller performed his ṣalāh hastily, without composure in his rukū' and sajdah. The Messenger (ﷺ) told him to repeat his ṣalāh in order to teach him the önem of performing ṣalāh with kulluk and composure. her biri time the Ṣaḥābī completed his ṣalāh and came to the Messenger (ﷺ), he greeted. This shows that it is desirable to repeat the greeting of salām even if the period of separation is minimal.

860.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If any of you meets his brother, he should offer salām to him. If a tree, wall or rock comes between the two of them and he again meets him, he should offer salām to him."(Abū Dāwūd)
860.commentary: One should repeat the greeting of salām, even if only a short time has passed after the initial salām. This is because salām is a supplication and a pact of sevgi, bundan dolayı the more regularly it is done, the greater will be the faydalar and rewards.

861.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Ey oğlum! When you go to your family, offer salām. It will be a source of nimet for you and your family.'"(Tirmidhī)
861.commentary: Scholars have stated that if the name of bütünāh is taken before the commencement of any task, then it will be protected by bütünāh from the effects of Shaiṭān. bu nedenle, if the name of bütünāh is taken when entering the home, then Shaiṭān will not enter. ayrıca, salām is a supplication, and one's family members are çoğu deserving of one's supplications. Qaṭādah narrated that the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "When you enter your home, then greet with salām, and when you leave your home, then bid farewell to your family members with salām." (Shu'b al-Īmān) Imām Nawawī stated that if there is nobody present in one's home, then one should say, "Assalāmu 'alaynā wa 'alā 'ibādillāhiṣ ṣāliḥīn" (Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of bütünāh).

862.text: He passed by some children and offered salām to them, diyerek:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to do so."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
862.commentary: Offering salām to children has birçok faydalar. It inculcates tevazu. It teaches children the önem of offering salām. It also creates sevgi and affection in their hearts. bununla birlikte, scholars have mentioned that if a young boy is handsome in appearance and there is a korku of lust, then it is prohibited to offer salām to him.

863.text: There was a woman (and in another narration, an yaşlı kadın) who used to take beetroot and cook it in a pot together with some barley seeds which she would grind. When we döndü after completing the Cuma namaz, we would offer salām to her and she would present it to us."(Bukhārī)
863.commentary: Göre the unanimous view of the scholars, it is not helal for men to offer salām to strange young women. A man may only offer salām and return the salām of a very old woman if there is no korku of evil. The food consumed by the people of Ṣuffah pointed to their extreme poverty. It was the genel uygulama of the Ṣaḥābah to eat after the Jumu'ah ṣalāh.

864.narrator: Umm Hānī' Fākhitah bint Abī Ṭālib (رضي الله عنها)
864.text: I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) on the day of the conquest of Makkah while he was performing ghusl. Fāṭimah was screening him with a cloth and I offered the salām."She then rivayet etti the full hadis. (Müslüman)
864.commentary: Âlimler, bir erkeğin annesi, kız kardeşleri, halaları, teyzeleri gibi mahrem kadın akrabalarına ve yaşlı kadınlara selam vermesinin caiz olduğunu belirtmişlerdir.

865.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) bir grup kadının yanından geçti ve bize selam verdi. (Ebû Dâvûd)
865.commentary: As mentioned in the previous hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was permitted to greet females as he was protected from temptations and günah. bununla birlikte, for others besides him, it is not helal. It is only helal for men to greet extremely old women, when no korku of evil exists between them.

866.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not initiate the salām to the Jews and Christians, and if you meet one of them on the path, compel him to the narrowest section of it."(Müslüman)
866.commentary: The reason for not initiating salām to disbelievers is that salām is offered as a gesture of honour and saygı, and those who oppose bütünāh are not deserving of it. bazı scholars have also stated that by initiating the salām, sevgi is generated, and we have been prohibited from loving the enemies of bütünāh. bütünāh states, "You will not find any people who believe in bütünāh and the Final Day loving those who oppose bütünāh and His Messenger." (Sūrah Mujādalah, 22) The disbelievers should be compelled to the narrowest section of a crowded yol in order to show the grandeur of Islām. yani, they should not be honoured by creating a yol for them to walk. bununla birlikte, if there is no crowd, this rule will not apply. Also, when compelling them to the narrowest section, one should ensure that they are not physically harmed in any yol.

867.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If the people of the Book offer the salām to you, reply by diyerek: 'And upon you.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
867.commentary: Göre a narration of Bukhārī, "Wheasla the Jews used to greet the Messenger (ﷺ), they would say, 'Assāmu 'alaykum' which means, 'Death be upon you.'" The Messenger (ﷺ) used to merely answer them with the sözler "And upon you." 'Ā'ishah said, "Death be upon you, and may bütünāh curse you and may His anger be upon you." She asked, "Did you not hear what they said?" The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) replied, "Did you not hear what I said? I replied to them. My supplication against them will be accepted, whilst their supplication regarding me will not be accepted." Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one should reply to the greeting of a non-Muslim with the sözler, "وعليكم" or merely "عليكم" instead of "وعليكم السلام." bazı scholars have suggested that it is better to reply to a non-Muslim with the sözler 'هداك الله' anlam "May bütünāh guide you!"

868.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by a gathering consisting of Müslümans, polytheists, idol worshippers and Jews and Resûlullah (ﷺ) offered salām to them. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
868.commentary: If a Muslim passes by a mixed gathering, as stated in this hadis, then he should extend the greeting to bütün, with the niyet of offering salām to the Muslims only. This will apply even if the Muslims are in the minority. Other scholars are of the view that one should say the following salām in a mixed gathering: "Assalāmu 'alā manit taba'al hudā" (Peace be upon those who follow the guidance). Similarly, when writing a letter to a non-Muslim, one should write the above du'ā' instead of "السلام عليكم," in emulation of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) when he wrote his letter to Heraculius, the emperor of Rome.

869.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you goes to a gathering, he should offer salām, and when he intends to leave, he should offer salām. The first salām is not more important than the second."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
869.commentary: Selam vermek, karşılaşırken ve ayrılırken müstehaptır. Selam verildiğinde daha güzel bir şekilde veya aynı şekilde karşılık vermek vaciptir.

870.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One should seek permission to enter three times. If you are granted permission, then enter, or else, you should return."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
870.commentary: Bu hadis, bir kişinin içeri girmek için en fazla üç kere izin istemesi gerektiğini açıklar. Üçüncüden sonra izin verilmezse dönüp gitmelidir.

871.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Seeking permission to enter was prescribed on account of the eyes."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
871.commentary: A home is a private area. The inhabitants may bazen be engaged in a personal or confidential matter, which they would not want others to know about. ayrıca, women are generally engaged in household chores and they may not be dressed as they would normally in public. If a person enters without seeking izin, he will be intruding on their privacy and his gaze may fall on the womenfolk of the house, which could lead to temptations, be a source of dishonour for them, etc. To shut these avenues of evil, seeking izin has been regarded as compulsory in Islām. It was also for this reason that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would not stand directly in front of the doorway when he visited anybody's home. He would either stand to the doğru or left when requesting for izin to enter. We are well-advised to follow his noble example.

872.text: Rib'ī ibn Ḥirāsh anlatır:"A man from the Banū 'Āmir related to us that he sought permission to meet Resûlullah (ﷺ) when he was at home. The man sordu: 'May I enter?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi to his assistant: 'Go out to that person and teach him the etiquette of seeking permission. Tell him to say, 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?'' The man heard this and dedi: 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) granted him permission and he entered."(Abū Dāwūd)
872.commentary: The Sunnah şekil of entering the residence of another person is to first offer salām and then request for izin to enter. Parents, teachers and manevî mentors should teach those under their supervision and guidance these etiquettes and mannerisms. Bu hadis portrays a glimpse of the merhamet and sevgi of the Messenger (ﷺ). He did not reprimand nor taunt the person who made an error, but taught him in an affectionate şekil so that he would not repeat his mistake in the future.

873.text: I gitti to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and girdi without offering salām to him. He şöyle dedi to me: 'Return, and say, 'barış be upon you, may I enter?'"(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
873.commentary: If a person enters without the doğru adab, he should be advised to do so in a kind şekil.

874.text: In his famous hadis with regard to al-Isrā' that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"Jibra'īl took me to the lowest heaven and sordu for the door to be opened. It was dedi: 'Who is this?' He cevap verdi: 'Jibra'īl.' It was dedi: 'Who is with you?' He cevap verdi: 'Muḥammad.' He then went to the second, third, fourth and the remaining heavens, and at the entrance of every heaven it was dedi: 'Who is this?' and he would reply: 'Jibra'īl.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
874.commentary: İzin isteyen kişi, kim olduğunu açıkça belirtmelidir. "Ben" demek yeterli değildir, adını söylemelidir.

875.text: I went out one night and noticed Resûlullah (ﷺ) walking on his own. I began walking in the shadow of the moon, but he turned and saw me. He sordu: 'Who is this?' I cevap verdi: 'Abū Dharr.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
875.commentary: The Ṣaḥābah possessed tremendous sevgi for the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). When Abū Dharr saw the Messenger (ﷺ) walking alone, he realised that he desired privacy, bununla birlikte he also feared that bazı difficulty might afflict him. He bu nedenle began following the Messenger (ﷺ) quietly so that the Messenger (ﷺ) was not disturbed, but he could assist if the need arose. Abū Dharr identified himself by his agnomen and not his name, since he was generally known by his agnomen.

876.text: I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) while he was performing a ghusl and Fāṭimah was screening him. He sordu: 'Who is this?' I cevap verdi: 'I am Umm Hānī'."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
876.commentary: Bu hadis daha önceki bir bölümde zikredilmiştir. Bkz. hadis 864. Bu hadis ve önceki hadis, izin isteme adabını açıklar.

877.text: I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and knocked at the door. He sordu: 'Who is this?' I cevap verdi: 'It is I.' He dedi, 'I, I,' as if he disliked it."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
877.commentary: Resûlullah (ﷺ) bu ifadeyi onaylamadı çünkü net bir açıklama sağlamaz ve kişinin kimliğini belirsiz bırakır.

878.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) likes sneezing and dislikes yawning. When any of you sneezes and praises Allah (ﷻ), it is the duty of every Müslüman who hears him to say to him: 'Yarḥamukallāh (May Allāh have rahmet on you).' As for yawning, it is from Shaiṭān. If any of you yawns, he should try to suppress it as much as possible because when you yawn, Shaiṭān laughs at you."(Bukhārī)
878.commentary: Mullā 'Alī Qārī stated that bütünāh likes sneezing because by means of it the mind is cleared and the body is comforted and these assist in concentration, kulluk and itaat. Because of these beneficial effects on the çeşitli limbs of the body, one should praise bütünāh after sneezing. diğer yandan, yawning is due to heaviness and clouding of the senses which lead to negligence, laziness, and a lack of desire for ibadet. For this reason, Shaiṭān is pleased with yawning. 'bütünāmah Abū Ṣāliḥ Dimashqī stated that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) asla yawned. One should suppress a yawn by means of one's hand or by closing one's lips. One should avoid her such avenue by which Shaiṭān may gain ascendency over him.

879.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you sneezes, he should say: 'Al-ḥamdulillāh.' (All praise be to Allāh). His brother or companion should say to him: 'Yarḥamukallāh (May Allāh have rahmet on you).' Then (the one who sneezed) should say: 'Yahdīkumullāh wa yuṣliḥu bālakum.' (May Allāh guide you and put your affairs in order)."(Bukhārī)
