879.commentary: Göre the Ḥanafī scholars, replying to a sneeze is Wājib 'alal kifāyah. This demektir ki if a group of people heard a person saying 'Al-ḥamdulillāh' after sneezing, then at least one person should reply to him. If he does so, the rest of those present will be absolved of the farz; if not even one of them replies, then bütün will be sinners. bununla birlikte, her person should endeavour to reply to it because of the great sevap attached to it.

880.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"When any of you sneezes and praises Allah (ﷻ), then say to him: 'Yarḥamukallāh.' If he does not praise Allah (ﷻ), do not say 'Yarḥamukallāh' to him."(Müslüman)
880.commentary: The hadis demektir ki only if a person praises bütünāh after sneezing should he be answered. If a person does praise bütünāh, but his praise is not heard, then it will not be binding upon others to reply to him. In a gathering, if bazı did not hear him saying 'Al-ḥamdulillāh', but heard others replying to him, they should assume that he had praised bütünāh, and should then also say 'Yarḥamukallāh.

881.text: Two men sneezed in the presence of Resûlullah (ﷺ). He dedi: 'Yarḥamukallāh' to one and not the other. The one to whom he did not say, 'Yarḥamukallāh' dedi: 'So-and-so sneezed and you dedi, 'Yarḥamukallāh', but when I sneezed you did not say 'Yarḥamukallāh'?' He dedi: 'He praised Allah (ﷻ) and you did not.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
881.commentary: Aksırdıktan sonra "Elhamdülillah" diyen kişiye "Yerhamükellah" diye karşılık verilir. Aksırana karşılık vermek farz-ı kifayedir.

882.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) aksırdığında elini veya elbisesini ağzına koyar ve sesini kısardı. (Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî)
882.commentary: Bu hadis teaches an important adab which applies bilhassa when one is in a gathering: one should place one's hand or garment over his mouth in order to muffle the sahih when sneezing. çeşitli reasons have been given for this. One is that this bir işaretidir refinement and culture. Another is that when a person sneezes, mucus is emitted from the nose and mouth, causing inconvenience to others. A third reason is that the form of a person's face changes when sneezing. Fourthly, sneezing loudly may startle others. Abū Hurairah narrates that the Messenger (ﷺ) mekruh the sahih of sneezing aloud in the masjid. (Shu'b al-Īmān) As a genel rule, Islām emphasises the önem of respecting the feelings and sentiments of others.

883.text: The Jews used to make themselves sneeze in the presence of Resûlullah (ﷺ) in the ümit that he would say to them, 'Yarḥamukumullāh.' But he would say: 'Yahdīkumullāh wa yuṣliḥu bālakum' (May Allah (ﷻ) guide you and put your affairs in order)."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
883.commentary: The Jews were fully aware that the Messenger (ﷺ) was the gerçek Messenger of bütünāh, bununla birlikte their jealousy and pride led them to deny his prophethood. They thought that if he supplicated on their behalf, they would be successful and deserving of the Messenger's rahmet, bununla birlikte he supplicated for their guidance because only Muslims are worthy of bütünāh's rahmet. This bize öğretir ki in answer to a non-Muslim's sneeze, the above du'ā' should be recited.

884.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you yawns, he should place his hand over his mouth because Shaiṭān enters it."(Müslüman)
884.commentary: Şeytan her fırsatta insana zarar vermek ister. Bu hadis bize esnemeyi bastırmayı ve şeytanın vesvesesine karşı koymayı öğretir.

885.text: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb Qatādah şöyle dedi:"I sordu Anas (رضي الله عنه): 'Did the Sahâbe of the Messenger shake hands?' He cevap verdi: 'Yes.'"(Bukhārī)
885.commentary: Muṣāfaḥah is from the kelime ṣafḥah (palms) and işaret eder two people shaking hands in such a şekil that their palms touch her biri other. From this definition we learn that merely allowing the fingers to touch is incorrect. Ibn Baṭṭāl stated that shaking hands is a virtuous amel and nurtures sevgi between people. In the lengthy incident of Ka'b ibn Mālik, when his tövbe was accepted and he went to meet the Messenger (ﷺ), Ṭalḥah stood up and shook his hand. Ka'b said, "By bütünāh, I will asla forget this amel of Ṭalḥah." This shows how pleased and honoured he felt by Ṭalḥah's reaction and in his view, this was a superior form of bonding. Males may shake hands with other males as well as maḥram females (those females whom they cannot marry). It is haram to shake hands with beardless handsome lads when there is an element of desire, as well as with women who are not maḥrams. Similarly, women may not shake hands with men besides close family members for whom the rules of ḥijāb do not apply. Ibn Mas'ūd narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Shaking hands is the completion of the salām." (Tirmidhī) This shows that merely shaking hands is not sufficient; it should be preceded with salām.

886.text: When the insanlar of Yemen geldi, Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'The insanlar of Yemen have come to you. They were the first to perform muṣāfaḥah.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
886.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) affirmed good ameller and qualities that were prevalent before the advent of his prophethood, and he rejected evils. The uygulama of shaking hands was yaygın amongst the people of Yemen and the Messenger (ﷺ) approved of it when they came to meet him, bundan dolayı, it olarak kabul edilir Sunnah.

887.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"No two Müslümans meet and perform muṣāfaḥah with each other, without being forgiven before they part."(Abū Dāwūd)
887.commentary: Muṣāfaḥah has çeşitli faydalar. As mentioned in this hadis, it causes günahlar to be forgiven. From other aḥādīth we learn that muṣāfaḥah removes malice and disunity, and draws the rahmet of bütünāh. Ḥudhaifah narrated that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "When a believer meets another believer, offers salām to him, and then performs muṣāfaḥah, her iki of their günahlar fall off tıpkı... gibi the leaves of a tree fall off." (Ṭabrānī) Another narration states, "When two Muslims meet, perform muṣāfaḥah, praise bütünāh and seek bağışlanma for one another, their günahlar are forgiven." (Abū Dāwūd) An easy şekil of seeking bağışlanma is to say "يَغْفِرُ اللهُ لَنَا وَ لَكُمْ" (May bütünāh forgive us and you!) (Abū Dāwūd) bağışlanma here işaret eder minor günahlar related to the haklar of bütünāh because major günahlar and günahlar pertaining to the haklar of others require tawbah.

888.text: A man sordu:"O Messenger of Allāh, when one of us meets his kardeş or his dost, should he bow to him?"He cevap verdi:"No."The man sordu:"Should he embrace him and kiss him?"He cevap verdi:"No."The man sordu:"Should he take his hand and perform muṣāfaḥah?"He cevap verdi:"Yes."(Tirmidhī)
888.commentary: Bowing down while offering salām is contrary to the Sunnah. Sheikh Abū Manṣūr Māturīdī, the great Imām of aqīdah, stated that if any person kisses the ground before another or bows down before him, he will not become a disbeliever, but will have committed a major error. bununla birlikte, if a believer bows down before another person with the niyet of ibadet, he will have renounced his īmān. (Maṭālib al-Mu'minīn) While Bu hadis discourages embracing and kissing, from other aḥādīth we learn that these are helal. Sheikh Abū Manṣūr Māturīdī stated that if a person kisses or embraces others with evil intent and sexual feelings, then it will be reprehensible. bununla birlikte, if a person embraces or kisses due to friendship or saygı then it will be helal. Other scholars have stated that the yasak of embracing only applies when a person has no clothing on the upper section of his body. Imām Nawawī stated that if one kisses the hand of another for a dinî reason gibi to appreciate his knowledge, chastity, abstinence or takvâ, then it is not Makrūh, but desirable. If the underlying reason is to honour a person for his wealth or dünyevî status, it is Makrūh bazı âlimlere göre, and Ḥarām according to others. (Mirqāt) bazı scholars have stated that the yasak of embracing a brother or friend relates to frequent meeting. başka bir deyişle, it should only be done when necessary gibi when leaving on a journey or returning.

889.text: A Jew şöyle dedi to his Sahâbî: 'Let us go to this Messenger.' So they geldi to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and sordu him about the nine clear signs. He then rivayet etti the full incident and şöyle dedi: 'They then kissed his hands and feet and şöyle dedi: 'We testify that you are a Messenger.'"(Tirmidhī)
889.commentary: The nine clear commands which these Jews asked about were the nine commands of Mūsā (عليه السلام). They questioned the Messenger (ﷺ) in order to test his claim to prophethood. In another narration, the Messenger (ﷺ) mentioned these commands as follows: Do not associate any partners with bütünāh; do not steal; do not fornicate; do not kill any person unjustly; do not take an innocent person to the king to be killed; do not engage in magic; do not consume interest; do not slander a chaste woman; do not turn your backs from the battlefield when you are defeated. The Messenger (ﷺ) also mentioned one additional emir which applied specifically to the Jews: do not exceed the bounds regarding the Sabbath. Scholars state that kissing the feet of a pious person is helal, bununla birlikte one should not intentionally bow down when doing so. Kissing the hands or forehead of others is helal. Scholars have stated that it is Mustaḥab to kiss the hands of pious people and those scholars who are firm followers of the Sunnah. This is proven from the incident of Abū Lubābah as well as the incident of Ka'b ibn Mālik and his two companions who kissed the hands of the Messenger (ﷺ) when their tövbe was accepted.

890.text: An incident in which he şöyle dedi:"We gitti close to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and kissed his hand."(Abū Dāwūd)
890.commentary: Bu hadis is further proof that it is helal to kiss the hands of pious scholars out of saygı and admiration.

891.text: Zeyd bin Hârise (رضي الله عنه) Medine'ye geldiğinde Resûlullah (ﷺ) evimdeydi. Geldi ve kapıyı çaldı. Resûlullah (ﷺ) eteğini sürüyerek kalktı ve kapıya yürüdü. Onu kucakladı ve öptü. (Tirmizî)
891.commentary: Al-Mu'ānaqah is derived from the kelime 'unuq (neck). It işaret eder two people embracing her biri other by the neck. Bu hadis proves that embracing is helal when a person returns from a journey. The haste of the Messenger (ﷺ) in meeting Zayd was an illustration of the sevgi he had for him and served as a proof of the Ṣaḥābī's noble status.

892.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not belittle any good deed even if it means meeting your brother with a cheerful countenance."(Müslüman)
892.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 695. A cheerful countenance is an act of goodness because it gladdens the heart of a believer. 'Umar narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "When two Muslims meet and one offers salām to the other, the çoğu beloved in the sight of bütünāh is the one who shows a more happier countenance than his companion. When they shake hands, a hundred mercies descend upon them; ninety for the one who placed his hand forward first and ten for the one whose hands were shaken." (Bazzār, Ḥakīm Tirmidhī)

893.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) kissed al-Ḥasan ibn 'Alī (رضي الله عنهما). Al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis dedi:"I have ten children but I have never kissed any of them."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"One who does not show rahmet will not be shown rahmet."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
893.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 225. Kissing and being compassionate to one's children bir delilidir one's rahmet and affection. In contrast, a person who is not merciful and compassionate to others remains deprived of bütünāh's rahmet. A hadis states, "Have rahmet and rahmet will be shown to you; forgive others and you will be forgiven." (al-Jāmi' al-Ṣaghīr) çeşitli incidents in the lives of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah prove that they were compassionate to their children.

894.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) ordered us to visit the ill, attend funerals, say yarḥamukallāh to the one who sneezes, assist to fulfil the oath of a person who took an oath, assist the oppressed, accept the invitation of one who invites, and make the greeting of salām common."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
894.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 239. Imām Nawawī has repeated it here to show that the Messenger (ﷺ) commanded us to visit the ill and to attend funerals. Imām Nawawī stated that, according to bütün the scholars, visiting the ill is Sunnah, whether they are close family members, friends or strangers.

895.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A Müslüman has five rights over another Müslüman: to reply to the salām, visit the ill, attend funerals, accept an invitation, and say yarḥamukallāh to the one who sneezes."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
895.commentary: Scholars have stated that these ameller are Farḍ al-kifāyah. yani, if they are observed by bazı, then others will be absolved of the farz. Observing these important haklar of a believer creates sevgi and unity and strengthens the bonds of brotherhood. Scholars have mentioned çeşitli etiquettes when visiting an ill person: perform wuḍū' before visiting; visit him as soon as he falls ill; do not prolong the visit thereby causing inconvenience; make du'ā' for him in his presence; enquire from him about his health; sit at his head side; request for his du'ās; and encourage him towards sabır.

896.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"On the day of Kıyamet, Allah (ﷻ) will say: 'O Son of Ādam, I was ill but you did not visit me.' He will reply: 'Ey Rabbim, how could I visit You when You are the Sustainer of the worlds?' He will say: 'Do you not know that so-and-so kul of Mine had fallen ill, but you did not visit him? Did you not know that had you visited him, you would have found Me with him? O Son of Ādam, I sordu you for food but you did not feed me.' He will reply: 'Ey Rabbim, how could I feed You when You are the Sustainer of the worlds?' He will say: 'Do you not know that so-and-so kul of Mine sordu you for food but you did not feed him? Did you not know that had you fed him, you would have found that with Me? O Son of Ādam, I sordu you for a drink but you did not give Me.' He will reply: 'Ey Rabbim, how could I give You a drink when You are the Sustainer of the worlds?' He will say: 'So-and-so kul of Mine sordu you for a drink but you did not give him. Did you not know that had you given him a drink, you would have found that with Me?'"(Müslüman)
896.commentary: Bu hadis explains the honour an ill person enjoys in the sight of bütünāh. For this reason, scholars state that his supplication for or against others is readily accepted. bütünāh loves the three ameller specified in Bu hadis because they entail benefiting His creation.

897.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Visit the ill, feed the hungry, and free the captives."(Bukhārī)
897.commentary: While the phrase فكوا العاني has been translated as freeing the captives, it can also refer to assisting those in debt. Islām is a din which encourages mutual assistance and co-operation. bütünāh states, "Assist one another with takvâ and abstinence from günah, and do not help one another in günah and excesses." (Sūrah al-Mā'idah, 2) Visiting the ill in normal circumstances is Sunnah. As for taking care of an ill person, if nobody in the community does so, then bütün of them will be sinful, and if one of them assumes this responsibility then bütün will be absolved of it.

898.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When a Müslüman visits his Müslüman brother, he remains among the khurfah of Cennet until he returns."It was sordu:"O Messenger of Allāh, what is the khurfah of Cennet?"He cevap verdi:"The fruits of Cennet."(Müslüman)
898.commentary: Bu hadis mentions one of the faziletler of visiting the ill. bütünāh loves such an amel, bundan dolayı He rewards it with His rahmet in the form of fruits in cennet. From a purely sosyal and humanitarian angle, a visit to an ill person is a kind gesture. An ill person is normally distressed, and in pain and difficulty, bundan dolayı when family members and friends visit him, he is pleased and there is a change in his temperament. He sık sık even forgets his illness. bundan dolayı, one should visit wheasla possible.

899.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"No Müslüman visits a Müslüman in the morning without 70,000 angels sending salutations upon him until the evening; and if he visits him in the evening, 70,000 angels send salutations upon him until the morning. And he will be rewarded with the fruits of Cennet."(Tirmidhī)
899.commentary: The "angels sending salutations" demektir ki they seek bağışlanma on his behalf and make du'ā' of rahmet for him. Aḥādīth have specified çeşitli other faydalar of visiting the ill: one gains a special degree of closeness to bütünāh because it is mentioned in a hadis that bütünāh is with those who are ill; one is reminded of the ahiret; and one attains the du'ās of the ill.

900.text: A Jewish boy used to serve Resûlullah (ﷺ) and he fell ill. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went to visit him. He sat at his head side and dedi to him: 'Embrace İslâm.' The boy looked at his father who was with him. He dedi: 'Obey Abū al-Qāsim.' So the boy embraced İslâm. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) left diyerek: 'All praise be to Allāh who saved him from cehennem ateşi.'"(Bukhārī)
900.commentary: The name of the Jewish boy was 'Abd al-Quddūs. The Messenger (ﷺ) sat at his head side while visiting him, teaching us to do likewise, provided that it does not cause any inconvenience. It is helal to utilise the services of a disbeliever as well as a child on şart that the guardian grants izin. It is helal to visit a non-Muslim who is ill, with the aim of bringing him closer to Islām. One should utilise her available opportunity to invite others to Islām. The Messenger (ﷺ) was concerned about the welfare of her person and desired that he be saved from everlasting damnation in the ahiret.

901.text: If a person complained to Resûlullah (ﷺ) of some illness, or he had a wound or injury, Resûlullah (ﷺ) would say, doing this with his finger (and Sufyān ibn 'Uyaynah, the narrator, koydu his index finger on the ground, raised it and şöyle dedi):"In the name of Allāh, the soil of our earth mixed with the saliva of some of us by which our ill are cured by the permission of our Sustainer."(Bukhārī)
901.commentary: "The soil of our earth," âlimlerin çoğunluğuna göre, işaret eder any soil, bununla birlikte bazı are of the opinion that it işaret eder the sand of Madīnah Munawwarah as there are special blessings in it. The Messenger (ﷺ) placed his blessed saliva on his index finger which he then placed on the soil. With bazı of the soil stuck to his finger, he then rubbed it over the wound, whilst reciting the above du'ā'. It is helal to utilise the means of cure gibi medication, and also to request the people of knowledge and takvâ for du'ās, bununla birlikte one should have the conviction that ultimate cure is only from bütünāh.

902.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) hasta olan aile fertlerini ziyaret ederdi. Sağ elini onların üzerine koyar ve şöyle derdi: "Ey insanların Rabbi olan Allah'ım! Bu sıkıntıyı gider, şifa ver. Şifa veren sensin, Senin şifandan başka şifa yoktur, hiçbir hastalık bırakmayacak şekilde şifa ver." (Buhârî, Müslim)
902.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one is allowed to utilise medication, bununla birlikte one must be convinced that ultimate cure is in the control of bütünāh. By dâhil the phrase, "which leaves behind no illness," the Messenger (ﷺ) taught us to make a du'ā' for mükemmel health, and not to only seek a cure from one particular illness.

903.text: He dedi to Thābit (رحمه الله):"Shall I not recite for you a divine incantation which Resûlullah (ﷺ) used to recite?"He dedi:"Yes."He dedi:"O Allāh, Sustainer of mankind and the remover of discomfort. Provide cure, for You are the Healer, and there is no healer except You. Grant such cure which does not leave behind any illness."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
903.commentary: Imām Qurṭubī stated that ruqyā (incantations) are helal provided that the following three şartlar are fulfilled: they should be based on the sözler of bütünāh, His names or His attributes; they should be in the Arabic language or in a language whose anlam is understood; and one should have the conviction that such incantations do not have an effect by themselves, but are only effective due to the will of bütünāh. It is preferable that a person utilises the sözler found in the aḥādīth of the Messenger (ﷺ). ayrıca, one should ensure that no sözler of kufr (küfür) are utilised.

904.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
904.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) visited me (when I was ill) and dedi: 'O Allāh, cure Sa'd. O Allāh, cure Sa'd. O Allāh, cure Sa'd.'"(Müslüman)
904.commentary: It is desirable to make du'ā' when visiting the ill and to take the ill person's name when doing so. The Messenger (ﷺ) repeated the du'ā' thrice as an expression of tevazu. In another hadis, the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "bütünāh loves those who persist in du'ā'." (Shu'bul Īmān, Ḥākim Tirmidhī)

905.narrator: Abū 'Abdillāh 'Uthmān ibn Abī al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنه)
905.text: He complained to Resûlullah (ﷺ) of a pain which he was experiencing in his body. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi to him:"Place your hand on the portion of your body where you are experiencing pain and say, 'In the name of Allāh,' three times. Then say, 'I seek refuge in the power and might of Allāh from the evil of that which I experience and korku,' seven times."(Müslüman)
905.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki a person may himself perform ruqyā (incantations). 'bütünāmah Ṭabarī stated, "From these narrations we learn that requesting bütünāh for good health is more virtuous and beneficial for a person than desiring tribulations. For this reason the Messenger (ﷺ) used to make du'ā' for the ill that they be cured from their illness." Illness is a rahmet of bütünāh because it purifies one of günah, and for the pious and righteous, bütünāh elevates their stages in cennet through it.

906.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"He who visits an ill person whose time of death has not yet come and says seven times in his presence, 'I ask Allāh the great, the Lord of the grand Throne, to cure you,' Allāh will cure him from that illness."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
906.commentary: When bütün decisions are made by the owner of the grand Throne, it is only appropriate that one beseeches Him for assistance and cure. When du'ā' is made for the ill with ihlâs and earnestness, in the sözler taught to us by the Messenger (ﷺ), then there is great ümit of acceptance. bu nedenle, a person should supplicate with dolu conviction and humbleness. In a hadis al-Qudsī, bütünāh states, "I am according to the thoughts of My servant regarding Me." (Bukhārī) bundan dolayı, if a person supplicates with conviction that bütünāh will accept his du'ā', then it will be so.

907.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went to visit a Bedouin who was ill, and when he visited an ill person, he would say:"There is nothing to worry about. If Allah (ﷻ) wills, it is a purification of your günahlar."(Bukhārī)
907.commentary: When visiting an ill person, it is preferable to use such sözler which will comfort and console him. One should also inform him of the faydalar and rewards for exercising sabır during illness. Mullā 'Alī Qārī stated that the Messenger's (ﷺ) visit to a Bedouin was a amelî example of his tevazu. Based on this, scholars state that one should not only visit those who are of superior status in society, but also those who are downtrodden, poor and oppressed. bundan dolayı, it is greatly meritorious for a leader to visit his subjects, and for a learned person to visit those who are uneducated.

908.text: Jibrā'īl (عليه السلام) came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and sordu:"O Muḥammad, are you complaining (of any illness)?"He cevap verdi:"Yes."He dedi:"In the name of Allāh, I make an incantation for you from everything that may harm you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. May Allāh cure you. In the name of Allāh, I make an incantation for you."(Müslüman)
908.commentary: Visiting the ill is an established Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), Jibrā'īl (عليه السلام) and the Ṣaḥābah. It is helal to express one's pain as long as it is not done as a complaint against the decision of bütünāh. The Messenger (ﷺ) was insanî. He was inflicted with illness and the malice of others tıpkı other insanî beings, and he supplicated for cure and well-being.

909.narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah (ra)
909.text: Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī and Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنهما) both testify that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"One who says, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh, and Allāh is the greatest', his Sustainer affirms this by diyerek, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Me, and I am the greatest.' When he says: 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner', Allāh says, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Me. I am one and I have no partner.' When he says: 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. To Him belongs the kingdom and to Him is all praise', Allāh says, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Me. To me belongs the kingdom and to Me is all praise.' When he says: 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. There is no power and might except with Allāh', Allāh says, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Me. There is no power and might except with Me.'"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to say:"One who says this when he is ill and then passes away, cehennem ateşi will not consume him."(Tirmidhī)
909.commentary: There is great fazilet in reciting these sözler as they indicate to inanç in bütünāh, while affirming His unity and grandeur, praising Him for His bounties, and having güven in Him only.

910.text: Ali bin Ebû Tâlib (رضي الله عنه) Resûlullah (ﷺ)'in son hastalığında onu ziyaret ettikten sonra çıktı. İnsanlar ona: "Ey Ebû Hasan! Bu gece nasıl?" diye sordular. "Allah'ın afiyetiyle sabaha çıktık" dedi. (Buhârî)
910.commentary: It is desirable to enquire about an ill person's şart from his family members when it is difficult to visit him due to any reason gibi severe illness, a distant location, visitation regulations, etc. This will elevate his spirits when he is informed that others are concerned about his well-being. It will also console his family members. When asked about the şart of an ill person, it is preferable to answer with such sözler which serve as a good omen, even though there is very little ümit of life.

911.text: I heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) say, while he was leaning against me:"Allah'ım! Forgive me, have rahmet upon me, and unite me with the Highest Friend."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
911.commentary: الرَّفِيقِ الأَعْلَى (Highest Friend), according to birçok scholars, işaret eder the companionship with bütünāh, as one of the names of bütünāh is Al-Rafīq. According to others, it işaret eder the company of the Messengers, angels and pious, tıpkı... gibi Yūsuf (عليه السلام) supplicated, close to his demise, "Unite me with the pious." The hadis bize öğretir ki at the time of death, one should sever bütün connections with dünya, and focus towards bütünāh, having ümit in His bağışlanma and rahmet. As the Messenger (ﷺ) was sinless, his request for bağışlanma was to increase his status in the sight of bütünāh and to teach the Ummah to supplicate at the time of death.

912.text: I gördü Resûlullah (ﷺ) while he was in the throes of death and with him was a bowl of su. He would insert his hand in the bowl and wipe his face with the su. He would then say:"O Allāh, help me in the pains and pangs of death."(Tirmidhī)
912.commentary: The Messengers of bütünāh were insanî beings. They felt pain and suffered illness, tıpkı... gibi others do. Similarly, the Messenger (ﷺ) had an intense fever and sought to lessen the heat of his body by using water to rub his blessed face. The separation of the soul from the body is not void of difficulty. It is, bu nedenle, Mustaḥab to regularly supplicate for easiness at that time.

913.text: A woman from the Juhaynah tribe came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) while she was pregnant on account of adultery. She dedi:"Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! I am deserving of ḥadd (penal azap), so mete out the azap to me."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) summoned her guardian and dedi:"Be kind to her. Once she gives birth, bring her to me."He did so, and Resûlullah (ﷺ) then ordered that her clothes be drawn tightly around her. He then ordered that she be stoned, and then offered the (janāzah) namaz over her. (Müslüman)
913.commentary: Bu hadis has been mentioned previously. See hadis 22. Imām Nawawī has mentioned it here to teach people to be kind to those whose death is imminent. The family of the woman who had committed adultery would naturally feel embarrassed, but they were told not to be unkind to her, özellikle since she was remorseful over her günah. An ill person is in greater need of sympathy and assistance, bundan dolayı those nursing him should patiently bear any inconvenience. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) did not immediately institute azap upon the woman so that the innocent unborn child would not be harmed.

914.text: I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) while he had a fever. I touched him and dedi: 'You have a very high fever.' He dedi: 'Yes, my fever is equal to the fever of two of you.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
914.commentary: The pain and fever of the Messenger (ﷺ) was double that of others and served to raise his rank and increase his rewards in the ahiret. On one occasion, a person placed his hand on the Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "By bütünāh, I cannot bear to place my hand over you due to the intense heat of your body." The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Verily, our (i.e. the Messengers) tests are increased manifold tıpkı... gibi our rewards are increased manifold."

915.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
915.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) came to visit me on account of a severe fever which I was experiencing. I dedi: 'You can see the effects of my illness, and I am a wealthy person, but I have no heir except my daughter.'"He then related the remainder of the hadis. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
915.commentary: In this hadis, Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ explained the extent of his illness and the Messenger (ﷺ) did not object to him doing so, bundan dolayı affirming its permissibility. That the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) visited his Ṣaḥābah speaks volumes of the sevgi and iyilik he showed towards them.

916.narrator: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad narrates that 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها)
916.text: O the pain in my head!"So Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"On the contrary, the pain in my head!"He then rivayet etti the remainder of the hadis. (Bukhārī)
916.commentary: When 'Ā'ishah complained of pain in her head, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) mentioned that he too was suffering from intense pain. Based on this, scholars have stated çeşitli laws about expressing pain during times of illness: It is helal for an ill person to groan or sigh without complaining. It is prohibited to express displeasure with the decision of bütünāh by making statements gibi, "Was I the only person whom bütünāh chose for this illness?" or "Why did bütünāh afflict me with illness?" It is Makrūh (mekruh) for a person to groan due to impatience. It is helal to groan if it brings comfort from pain. If the aim of one's groaning is to express one's weakness and inability before bütünāh, it is Mustaḥab (advisable).

917.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One whose last words were Lā ilāha illallāhu (there is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh) will enter Cennet."(Abū Dāwūd, Ḥākim)
917.commentary: Bu hadis demektir ki if a person recites the kalimah (proclamation of iman) at the time of death, then it is a clear sign that he is a believer. He will promptly enter cennet with those who are successful, or after he is cleansed of his günahlar by being punished in cehennem.

918.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Encourage your dying to say Lā ilāha illallāh."(Müslüman)
918.commentary: Talqīn means to recite the kalimah, Lā ilāha illallāh, in the presence of the person who is in the throes of death so that he may hear it and repeat it. One should not force the ill person to recite the kalimah because it should not happen that due to intense pain and illness or the whisperings of Shaiṭān, he refuses to do so. ayrıca, once he has recited these sözler, then those around him should remain silent. If the ill person resumes any dünyevî discussions, then talqīn should be repeated. It is also advisable to recite Sūrah Yāgünah at this time. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Recite Sūrah Yāgünah upon those who are on the verge of death." (Abū Dāwūd)

919.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) visited Abū Salamah and his eyes were fixed. He (ﷺ) closed them diyerek: 'When the soul is taken, the sight follows it.' Some of his family members began wailing, so he dedi: 'Only supplicate for goodness for yourselves, for the angels say 'amen' to whatever you say.' He then dedi: 'O Allāh, bağışla Abū Salamah, elevate his rank among those who are guided, and appoint for him a successor among those he leaves behind. Forgive us and him, O Sustainer of the worlds. Expand his grave for him and illuminate it for him.'"(Müslüman)
919.commentary: When the soul of a person is taken out of his body, his eyes stare at it, bundan dolayı they remain open. Those who are present should close the eyes. At such a time of grief, du'ās are readily accepted, bundan dolayı one should be careful what one utters. Scholars state that when a person passes away, the learned should proceed to the home of the deceased, seek bağışlanma for him, and encourage his family members to be patient and to engage in good ameller. "Expand his grave for him and illuminate it for him," shows that a person enjoys bounties in the grave, and faydalar when the living supplicate on his behalf.

920.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When you are with an ill person or a deceased person, speak good words because the angels say 'amen' to whatever you say."She dedi:"When Abū Salamah passed away, I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh, Abū Salamah has passed away.' He dedi: 'Say: Allah'ım! Forgive me and him, and grant me a better replacement.' I dedi it, and Allāh thus granted me a better replacement, namely Muhammed (ﷺ)."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
920.commentary: When a person passes away, his family members should supplicate to bütünāh for a better replacement as bütünāh has power over everything. According to bazı narrations, Umm Salamah said, "I used to wonder whether I would ever find a better husband than Abū Salamah, bununla birlikte when I married the Messenger (ﷺ), I realised the effect of that supplication." One should utter good sözler in the presence of an ill person or a person who has just passed away. One should asla curse or supplicate against themselves at this time as the angels say 'āmīn,' (O bütünāh, accept!) to such supplications.

921.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"When a kul is afflicted with a calamity and then says, 'We belong to Allāh and to Him is our return. O Allāh, sevap me for my calamity and grant me a better replacement,' then Allah (ﷻ) rewards him for his calamity and grants him a better replacement."She dedi:"When Abū Salamah passed away and I dedi as Resûlullah (ﷺ) had emretti me, Allāh granted me a better replacement, namely Resûlullah (ﷺ)."(Müslüman)
921.commentary: The supplication, "We belong to bütünāh and to Him is our return," bize öğretir ki we are the possessions of bütünāh. He has exclusive haklar over us and can do with us as He pleases. tıpkı... gibi a slave has no doğru to question his master, we as slaves of bütünāh have no doğru to question Him why He takes one of His servants from this lowly world to a higher world, şöyle ki the ahiret. One who accepts this truth, will be able to exercise sabır over her calamity. The Messenger (ﷺ) would recite the du'ā' mentioned in Bu hadis even due to a thorn prick, a mosquito bite, the breaking of a shoe-lace and on the extinguishing of a lamp. He said, "Anything which causes harm to a believer is a calamity and a means of attaining sevap." (Musnad of 'Abd ibn Ḥumaid)

922.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When a kul'in child passes away, Allah (ﷻ) says to His angels: 'Have you taken the child of My kul?' They reply: 'Yes.' He then asks: 'Have you taken the fruit of his heart?' They reply: 'Yes.' He then asks: 'What did My kul say?' They reply: 'He praised You and dedi: To Allāh we belong and to Him is our return.' Allah (ﷻ) says: 'Build for My kul a house in Cennet and name it Bayt al-Ḥamd (the house of praise).'"(Tirmidhī)
922.commentary: Bu hadis encourages us to be patient at the time of a calamity and to be pleased with the decree of bütünāh. bütünāh işaret eder a person's child as the fruit of his heart in order to emphasise the sevgi a parent has for his child and the tremendous sabır he exercises upon the separation. When a person praises bütünāh and accepts that He has taken back a güven, bütünāh rewards him with a house in cennet. Because a person praised bütünāh, he is given a befitting recompense, şöyle ki a house in cennet with the same name.

923.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allah (ﷻ) says: 'When I take the life of My believing kul'in beloved in this world and he is hopeful of the sevap thereof, then I will grant him Cennet.'"(Bukhārī)
923.commentary: When a believer exercises sabır in the face of a calamity and is hopeful of a sevap from bütünāh, He grants him cennet in return.

924.text: One of the daughters of Resûlullah (ﷺ) sent a message to him calling him and informing him that her child – or son - was passing away. He dedi to the messenger:"Return to her and inform her that whatever Allāh takes is His, and whatever He gives is His. Everything has an appointed time with Him. So instruct her to remain patient and to be hopeful of a sevap."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
924.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned in a previous chapter. See hadis 29. Imām Nawawī has repeated it here to teach us that teşvik should be given to the family of one who is in the throes of death. Similarly, consoling a fellow insanî being on the death of a loved one is a fazilet. 'Amr ibn Hazm narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Wheasla a believer consoles his brother due to bazı calamity, bütünāh will clothe him with robes of honour on the day of Qiyāmah." (Ibn Mājah) "Whatever bütünāh takes is His, and whatever He gives is His," serves as an teşvik to be patient and to accept the decree of bütünāh. tıpkı... gibi a person does not become upset when a güven is returned to its owner, it is not appropriate for a person to complain and become angry when the life of his beloved is taken.

925.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went to visit Sa'd ibn 'Ubādah with 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Auf, Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and 'Abdullāh ibn Mas'ūd (رضي الله عنهم). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) wept. When the people saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) weeping, they also began to weep. He dedi:"Are you listening? Allāh does not punish for tears shed by the eyes nor for the sorrow of the heart, but He punishes or shows rahmet on account of this,"and he pointed to his tongue. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
925.commentary: Due to excessive grief, it is only natural for tears to flow from the eyes and for the heart to be sorrowful. This is perfectly acceptable in Islām. bununla birlikte, such crying is prohibited wherein a person utters sözler of impatience and ingratitude, or when a person beats his face and pulls his hair as was the uygulama during the days of ignorance. Similarly, it is incorrect for a person to scream while crying. Hiring people to mourn over the deceased or to praise him is also prohibited. If the deceased knew that his family members would do so and he did not prevent them, then he will also receive a share of the resulting günah.

926.text: The grandson of Resûlullah (ﷺ) was brought to him while he was in the throes of death. The eyes of Resûlullah (ﷺ) began flowing with tears. Sa'd sordu him:"What is this, O Messenger of Allāh?"He cevap verdi:"This is rahmet which Allah (ﷻ) has placed in the hearts of His kullar. Allah (ﷻ) is merciful to those of His kullar who are merciful to others."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
926.commentary: This incident referred to the son of Zaynab. Sa'd was surprised at the tears of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) as he was under the impression that any form of crying in such a situation was prohibited. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) explained that the mere flowing of tears is not prohibited, but an indication of the rahmet which bütünāh has placed in a person. Only such forms of crying which are accompanied by impermissible factors are prohibited.

927.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) visited his son Ibrāhīm (رضي الله عنه) while he was gasping for breath. The eyes of Resûlullah (ﷺ) began flowing with tears. 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Auf sordu him:"Even you (are crying), O Messenger of Allāh?"He cevap verdi:"O Ibn 'Auf, it is out of rahmet,"and more tears followed. He then dedi:"The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say nothing except that which pleases our Sustainer. O Ibrāhīm, we are certainly grieved at your separation."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
927.commentary: Ibrāhīm was the son of the Messenger (ﷺ) from his slave girl, Māriyā Qibṭiyyā. At the time of his demise, he was approximately 18 months. He passed away in the 10th year Hijrī. The Messenger (ﷺ) was saddened at his demise and began tearing. Scholars state that if tears do not flow on such an occasion, then this işaret eder a lack of sevgi and rahmet. başka bir deyişle, it is perfectly normal and helal to shed tears at the demise of a person, bununla birlikte one should not wail and scream. Similarly, one should accept the decision of bütünāh and be pleased with it.

928.text: Abū Rāfi' Aslam, the freed slave of Resûlullah (ﷺ), anlatır that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"One who performs ghusl for a deceased person and conceals whatever he sees, Allāh will bağışla him forty times."(Ḥākim)
928.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one who performs ghusl for the deceased should refrain from exposing any fault which he notices on the body. For this reason, scholars also state that it is Makrūh (reprehensible) for any person, even close family members, besides those who are appointed to perform ghusl, to be present when the deceased is being bathed. If one notices any good sign on the deceased's body, then he should mention it to others so that they may appreciate the goodness of the deceased person. Performing ghusl for the deceased has çok sayıda faydalar, the greatest of which is that one is reminded of one's own death.

929.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who is present at a funeral until the namaz for the deceased is performed will receive one qīrāṭ, and one who is present until he is buried will receive two qīrāṭs."It was sordu:"What is the meaning of two qīrāṭs?"He cevap verdi:"It is equivalent to two huge mountains."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
929.commentary: A qīrāṭ literally işaret eder a twelfth of a dīnār. Since this is a small amount, the Ṣaḥābah enquired what it meant. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) informed them that it referred to a huge amount and not what they had thought it to be. Assisting in the burial and associated matters of a deceased Muslim is a great fazilet.

930.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who attends the funeral of a Müslüman motivated by īmān and in expectation of sevap, and remains until the namaz is performed for him and his burial is complete, returns with two qīrāṭs. Each qīrāṭ is equivalent to Mount Uḥud. One who performs the namaz for the deceased and returns before he is buried returns with one qīrāṭ."(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
930.commentary: The great sevap mentioned in Bu hadis hinges upon the doğru niyet, şöyle ki the pleasure of bütünāh. bundan dolayı, if one attends funerals due to korku of public criticism and taunting, or as a mere âdet, one will not be entitled to the sevap.

931.text: We were yasakladı from following funerals, but not strictly."(Müslüman, Ibn Mājah, Al-Bayhaqī)
931.commentary: Bu demektir ki that the yasak was not as severe as that of other prohibitions. According to the vast majority of scholars, it is not helal for women to accompany funerals. The wisdoms of this yasak are birçok. Firstly, there is the possibility of intermingling with men. Secondly, women are by nature more emotional than men, and there is a great possibility of them indulging in prohibited ameller gibi wailing and lamenting. Thirdly, women attending funerals encourages exposure rather than seclusion. To prevent such evils from occurring, Islām has prohibited women from attending funerals. 'bütünāmah Subkī stated that according to the Ḥanafī, Ḥanbalī and âlimlerin çoğunluğu, it is Makrūh Taḥrīmī for women to attend funerals. According to Imām Shāfi'ī, it is Makrūh Tanzīhī.

932.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When a group of a hundred Müslümans perform namaz for a deceased Müslüman and all of them intercede for him, their intercession will be accepted."(Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
932.commentary: In the çeşitli aḥādīth relating to this topic, three farklı amounts have been mentioned: 100 people, 40 people and 3 rows of people. Scholars have stated that initially this fazilet was for a person whose janāzah was performed by 100 people. Thereafter, bütünāh enhanced His favour and reduced the amount to 40 and then further to a mere three rows. According to other scholars, a özel number is not the objective, rather the intent is to draw birçok people to the ṣalāh.

933.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"When a Müslüman passes away and forty people who do not ascribe partners with Allah (ﷻ) perform namaz for him, Allah (ﷻ) accepts their intercession for him."(Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
933.commentary: Cenaze namazına ne kadar çok kişi katılırsa, ölen kişi için sevap o kadar büyük olur. Kırk kişinin katıldığı cenaze namazında şefaat kabul edilir.

934.text: Marthad ibn 'Abdillāh al-Yazanī anlatır: When Mālik ibn Hubayrah (رضي الله عنه) performed namaz for a deceased person and considered the people in attendance to be few, he would divide them into three rows. He would then say: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"When three rows of people perform namaz for a deceased person, Allāh makes Cennet obligatory for him."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
934.commentary: Although nothing is binding upon bütünāh, He bazen promises a sevap due to His benevolence, and He daima fulfils whatever He promises.

935.narrator: Abū 'Abd al-Raḥmān 'Auf ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه)
935.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) performed namaz for a deceased person and I memorised a portion of his dua. He dedi:"O Allāh, bağışla him, be merciful to him, save him from azap, pardon him, host him with nobility, and expand his grave. Wash him with water, snow and hail. Cleanse him of günahlar as You cleanse a white garment of dirt. Grant him a better home in exchange for his home, a better family than his family, and a better wife than his wife. Admit him into Cennet, save him from the azap of the grave and the azap of cehennem ateşi."(The narrator dedi):"I wished that I could have been that deceased person."(Müslüman)
935.commentary: After the third takbīr, any supplication can be made in the Arabic language. It is best to recite those supplications which are narrated from the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), since they are çoğu comprehensive and beneficial for the deceased and the living. Supplication faydalar the deceased. The azap and rewards in the grave are a reality.

936.text: Abū Hurayrah, Abū Qatādah, and Abū Ibrāhīm al-Ashhalī narrate from his father who was a Sahâbî that Resûlullah (ﷺ) performed namaz for a deceased person and then supplicated:"O Allāh, bağışla our living and our dead, our young and our old, our males and our females, and our present and our absent. O Allāh, whoever You keep alive among us, keep him alive on İslâm, and whoever You give death to among us, give him death on īmān. O Allāh, do not deprive us of his sevap and do not put us into tribulation after him."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
936.commentary: This is the du'ā' which is çoğu famous and commonly recited by the genel Muslim Ummah during the Janāzah ṣalāh. It is extremely comprehensive requesting for the çoğu superior of bounties gibi living with Islām, dying with īmān and being saved from bütün tribulations.

937.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"When you perform namaz for a deceased person, supplicate for him with sincerity."(Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājāh, Bayhaqī)
937.commentary: Before the deceased is placed in the grave, the Janāzah ṣalāh is the last amel that will be done on his behalf, bundan dolayı one should supplicate with ihlâs. It should not be done merely as a âdet or ritual. It should be noted that there is no du'ā' after the salām of the Janāzah ṣalāh.

938.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) supplicated in his dua for a deceased person:"O Allāh, You are his Sustainer, You created him, You guided him to İslâm, You took his soul, and You know best his actions in private and public. We have come to You as intercessors on his behalf, so bağışla him."(Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
938.commentary: Bu, üçüncü tekbirden sonra okunabilecek başka bir duadır. Cenaze namazında dua etmek sünnettir.

939.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) led us in namaz for a deceased Müslüman and I heard him say:"O Allāh, so-and-so person is in Your security and under Your protection, so save him from the trials of the grave and the azap of cehennem ateşi. You are the Being who fulfils promises and is worthy of praise. O Allāh, bağışla him and be merciful to him. Surely, You are All-Forgiving, Most Merciful."(Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah)
939.commentary: bağışlanma obliterates günahlar, while rahmet draws goodness, bundan dolayı by declaring that bütünāh is bütün-Forgiving and çoğu Merciful, we request safety from cehennem-fire and entry into cennet. This is the ultimate success. May bütünāh grant it to us through His grace!

940.text: 'Abdullāh ibn Abī Aufā (رضي الله عنه): It is related that he dedi the takbīr (Allāhu Akbar) four times when performing namaz for his deceased daughter. After the fourth takbīr he remained standing for as long as he stood between two takbīrs, seeking bağışlanma for her and supplicating. He then dedi:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to do so."Another narration has:"He dedi the takbīr for the fourth time and then remained silent until I thought that he would say the fifth takbīr. He then made salām to his right and left. When he turned around, we sordu him: 'What is this?' He cevap verdi: 'I will not make you do more than what I saw Resûlullah (ﷺ) doing.' (or 'This is what Resûlullah (ﷺ) did.')"(Ḥākim, Ibn Mājah, Bayhaqī)
940.commentary: Göre bütün the scholars, there are four takbīrs in Janāzah ṣalāh. Even though more than four have been narrated from the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) recited only four towards the end of his life. This shows that the narrations in which more than four are mentioned were abrogated.

941.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Hasten with carrying the deceased. If he was a salih person, you are advancing him towards good, and if he was other than that, you will be removing an evil from your shoulders."A narration of Müslüman has:"You will be presenting him for something good."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
941.commentary: A sinful person is far from bütünāh's rahmet, bundan dolayı there is no fayda in being with him. This bize öğretir ki we should daima stay away from evil company. Imām Nawawī stated that it is Mustaḥab to hasten when carrying the deceased. bununla birlikte, one should not run or proceed so quickly that it causes the bier to shake excessively or so that it causes difficulty to those who are following it.

942.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"Once the deceased is placed and men carry it on their shoulders, if it was a salih person, it says, 'Take me forward,' and if it was not a salih person, it says to its family: 'Destruction to me! Where are you taking me?' All creation except man hear its voice. If he were to hear it, he would fall unconscious."(Bukhārī)
942.commentary: The speaking of the corpse or the soul is one of the hidden realities which the Messenger (ﷺ) informed us of. It bize öğretir ki the deceased has a sense of perception. We believe in these realities without any doubt or misgiving. Only men should carry the deceased, even if the deceased is a female. This is because men are stronger. Also, it is possible that a portion of the body of one who is carrying it may become exposed and this is inappropriate for women.

943.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The soul of a mümin is left suspended because of his debts until they are paid on his behalf."(Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, Bayhaqī)
943.commentary: Göre 'bütünāmah 'Irāqī, "the soul of a believer is left suspended," demektir ki its result is left pending and no decision of success or destruction is passed until it is seen whether his debts are settled or not. This önemini gösterir quickly settling the debts of the deceased. After the burial expenses, debts should be given first priority. Bu hadis işaret eder the genel golden principle of Islāmic finance, şöyle ki moderation in spending. Overspending and extravagance generally lead to debts which in turn bring disgrace, worry and frustration, bundan dolayı a Muslim should live within his means. The Messenger (ﷺ) expressed severe warnings regarding debts and their non-payment when one has the means to do so. The Messenger (ﷺ) said that one who incurs a debt and has no niyet of repaying it, will pay for it with his iyilikler on the day of Qiyāmah. In another hadis, the Messenger (ﷺ) said that a person who takes a loan with the niyet of not paying it back, and passes away, will rise as a thief in the presence of bütünāh on the day of Qiyāmah. Even the noble death of martyrdom does not absolve one of his debts. The Messenger (ﷺ) would not perform the Janāzah ṣalāh of a person who passed away with debts.

944.text: Ṭalḥah ibn al-Barā' (رضي الله عنه) fell ill and Resûlullah (ﷺ) came to visit him. He dedi:"I think the time of Ṭalḥah'in demise is near, so you should inform me of it and hasten with it because it is not appropriate for the corpse of a Müslüman to be held back among his family people."(Abū Dāwūd)
944.commentary: Bu hadiste, cenaze işlemlerinde acele etmemiz emredilmiştir. Kişi öldükten sonra cenazesi geciktirilmeden defnedilmelidir.

945.text: We attended a funeral in Baqī' al-Gharqad. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) came to us and sat down, so we sat down around him. He was holding a stick and he lowered his head and began prodding the ground with the stick. He then dedi:"Every one of you has his place in cehennem ateşi and in Cennet written for him."The Sahâbe sordu:"O Messenger of Allāh, should we not then rely on what has been written for us?"He cevap verdi:"Perform good deeds because every person is inspired to do the deeds for which he was created."He then related the entire hadis. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
945.commentary: There is great fayda in giving advice to others at a grave because the heart of a person is more receptive when he is in the vicinity of the deceased. Bu hadis touches upon a delicate aspect of predestination. The Ṣaḥābah here asked whether they should abandon the effort of engaging in iyilikler when bütünāh already has knowledge of one's end result. The Messenger (ﷺ) explained that it is incorrect to abstain from righteous ameller by relying on the knowledge of bütünāh. Instead, man is obligated to do good because bütünāh has granted him the ability to do so and He has made it compulsory upon him to do good. A person will be held accountable for his ameller which are voluntary and not based on the knowledge of bütünāh.

946.narrator: Abū 'Amr – and according to some, Abū 'Abdillāh, and according to others, Abū Laylā – 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān (رضي الله عنه)
946.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) completed burying the body of the deceased, he would stand at the grave and say:"Seek bağışlanma for your brother and ask for steadfastness for him because he is presently being questioned."(Abū Dāwūd)
946.commentary: Ölen kişi, Münker ve Nekir'in sorularını doğru cevaplarsa, kabri genişletilir ve aydınlatılır. Kötü cevap verenler ise azap görür.

947.text: When you have buried me, stand around my grave for as long as it takes to slaughter a camel and distribute its meat, so that I may be comforted by you and know what reply to give to the messengers of my Sustainer."(Müslüman, Aḥmad) The entire hadis was cited previously.
947.commentary: 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ requested them to stand around his grave because it is insanî nature that when one is in familiar company, he is comforted and it is easier for him to speak and answer questions, as opposed to when he is alone or in the company of strangers. Īṣāl al-thawāb means to perform a virtuous amel and then to request bütünāh to grant the sevap of it to any person who may be alive or deceased. It is not only helal but Mustaḥab. Recitation of the Qur'ān bir vesilesidir attracting ilâhî rahmet, and faydalar the deceased. It is Mustaḥab (advisable) to recite bazı portion of the Qur'ān at his grave, and if the bütün Qur'ān is recited, it will be good.

948.text: A man dedi to Resûlullah (ﷺ):"My mother passed away suddenly and I think that if she had the opportunity of speaking, she would have given sadaka. Will she be rewarded if I give sadaka on her behalf?"He cevap verdi:"Yes."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
948.commentary: Scholars state that if a person performs any optional iyilik, then he can convey the rewards of it to the deceased by saying, "O bütünāh, whatever sevap has been granted on account of this amel, convey it to so-and-so person." Examples of ameller whose sevap could be conveyed to others are feeding and clothing someone, performing optional ṣalāh, observing optional fasts, performing an optional Ḥaj or 'Umrah, reciting the Qur'ān, making dhikr, building a masjid or madrasah, and printing Islāmic literature and distributing it.

949.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When a man passes away, his deeds come to an end except for three: continuous sadaka, knowledge which benefits and a salih child who supplicates for him."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
949.commentary: "A continuous charity" may include such ameller as building a masjid or madrasah, digging a well or borehole and providing water for people, distributing Qur'āns, etc. "Knowledge which faydalar" işaret eder knowledge which one imparts to others. As long as the recipient practises upon it and imparts it, the dispenser will continue to reap the rewards. A "righteous child" işaret eder a believer. Scholars state that by qualifying child with the kelime righteous, the child is teşvik edilen to become pious, in which case his her amel will be a source of sevap for his parents. bununla birlikte, even if the child is not pious, his supplication for his parents will fayda them. bazı scholars have stated that this serves as an teşvik to parents to ensure that they guide their children towards salih amel, so that they can gain maximum fayda when they are çoğu in need of it.

950.text: A funeral passed by and the people praised him. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"It is compulsory."Then another passed by and the people spoke evil of him. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"It is compulsory."'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه) sordu:"What is compulsory?"He cevap verdi:"You people praised him, so Cennet is compulsory for him, and you spoke evil of this person, so cehennem ateşi is compulsory for him. You are the witnesses of Allāh on earth."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
950.commentary: Imām Nawawī stated that the scholars have provided two possible meanings for this hadis. bazı state that the praises and reproaches mentioned here refer to those uttered by the people of fazilet and takvâ because their statements will be according to the deceased's ameller. Other scholars say that the hadis is genel. başka bir deyişle, if a Muslim passes away, bütünāh inspires bütün or birçok of the people to praise him and this is a sign that he is amongst the inhabitants of cennet, irrespective whether his ameller necessitate it or not. If his ameller do not necessitate him entering cennet, azap is not binding on him, but his result is subject to the decision of bütünāh. When bütünāh inspires the people to praise him, we can assume that bütünāh has wished bağışlanma for him.

951.text: Abū al-Aswad anlatır:"I came to Madīnah and sat in the company of 'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه). A funeral passed by and people praised the deceased. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'It is compulsory.' Then another funeral passed by and people praised the deceased. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'It is compulsory.' Then a third funeral passed by and people spoke evil of the deceased. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'It is compulsory.' I sordu: 'What is compulsory, O Amīr al-Müminīn?' He cevap verdi: 'I dedi as Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi: 'When four people testify to the goodness of a deceased Müslüman, Allāh admits him into Cennet.' We sordu: 'What about three?' He dedi: 'Even three.' We sordu: 'What about two?' He dedi: 'Even two.' We did not ask him about one.'"(Bukhārī)
951.commentary: The kelime "Muslim" shows that the fazilet mentioned here applies only to a believer. If a disbeliever is praised for his good ameller, noble character, etc. he will not be entered into cennet because he lacks the qualifying quality of īmān. The praise and honour which is lauded on a disbeliever is the dünyevî sevap granted to him by bütünāh for whatever good he has done in dünya. bununla birlikte, he will asla enter cennet because of his küfür (kufr). Bu hadis relates to the opinions of the people of īmān and taqwā. The opinions of evildoers and sinners are not taken into consideration, since their praise or criticism is generally for ulterior motives. The hadis teaches us to praise the deceased. Ibn 'Umar narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Mention the noble ameller of your deceased and abstain from mentioning their evil qualities." (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)

952.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A Müslüman whose three children pass away before reaching puberty, Allāh will admit him into Cennet by virtue of His rahmet for them."(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
952.commentary: The hadis demektir ki if a person's three children pass away, and he bears the loss patiently and has ümit of receiving sevap from bütünāh, then bütünāh will enter him into cennet.

953.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A Müslüman whose three children pass away, cehennem ateşi will not touch him except in fulfilment of the oath."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Tirmidhī)
953.commentary: The oath yani referred to in Bu hadis işaret eder the Qur'ānic verse wherein bütünāh states that her person will have to pass through the cehennem-fire. her person has to pass over the Ṣirāṭ which is a bridge spanning over cehennem and that leads a person into cennet. The believers will cross over the bridge in accordance with their ameller. bazı will cross over as fast as lightning due to their takvâ, while others will pass over more slowly. The disbelievers and sinful Muslims will fall headlong into cehennem, bununla birlikte by intercession, the sinful believers will eventually be removed. In this hadis, we learn that if a person patiently bears the difficulty of losing three children, he will pass over this bridge comfortably without the flames burning him in any yol.

954.text: A woman came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"O Messenger of Allāh, the men are benefiting from your discourses, so assign a day for us in which we can come to you and you can teach us some of that which Allāh has taught you."He dedi:"Gather on such-and-such day."So they gathered and Resûlullah (ﷺ) went to them and taught them some of that which Allāh had taught him. He then dedi:"If any of you women loses three of her children, they will be a barrier for her from cehennem ateşi."A woman sordu:"And two?"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"Even two."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
954.commentary: The lap of the mother is the first madrasah of a child. bundan dolayı, Muslim women should yearn to acquire sahih Islāmic knowledge which they can practise upon and impart to their children. Scholars should allocate time to teach them about such matters of önem. bununla birlikte, such gatherings should comply with the rules of ḥijāb and should be free of fitnah (evil). The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) stipulated a day and time for the womenfolk so that they would yearn for it because knowledge yani acquired by effort is more beneficial than that which is attained without effort and desire.

955.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to his Sahâbe when they reached al-Ḥijr, the houses of the Thamūd:"Do not enter the area where these people were punished, without crying. If you are unable to cry, then do not enter for korku that what afflicted them may afflict you."Another narration has: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) passed by al-Ḥijr, he dedi:"Do not enter the houses of those who wronged themselves, without crying for korku that what afflicted them may afflict you."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then covered his head and quickened his pace until he crossed the valley. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
955.commentary: Al-Ḥijr is the name of the place where the tribe of Thamūd resided. It is situated between Shām and Madīnah Munawwarah. The Messenger, Ṣāliḥ (عليه السلام), was sent to them. The incident referred to in Bu hadis took place when the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was proceeding to Shām for the Battle of Tabūk. If a person happens to pass by an area where people were punished due to their wrongdoings, then he should contemplate and ponder over the power of bütünāh and the need to obey His commands. One should not pass by negligently nor view such places as holiday destinations or places of sight-seeing. One should hasten and pass the area quickly, seeking bütünāh's koruma and bağışlanma. Other examples of such places of azap are 'Wādī Muḥaṣṣar' in Makkah Mukarramah where the People of the Elephant were destroyed, the museum in Egypt where the mummy of Fir'awn is kept and the Dead Sea which is where the people of Lūṭ (عليه السلام) were destroyed.

956.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) Tebûk seferine Perşembe günü çıktı ve Perşembe günü yola çıkmayı severdi. (Buhârî)
956.commentary: Tabūk is an area between Madīnah Munawwarah and Damascus. It is approximately 465 miles from Madīnah Munawwarah. The Battle of Tabūk took place in 9th year of Hijrī. This was the final battle in which the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) participated. Scholars have given çeşitli possible reasons why Thursday is specified for commencing a journey: On Mondays and Thursdays, one's book of ameller is presented in the court of bütünāh, bundan dolayı the Messenger of bütünāh wished that the noble act of jihād should commence on a Thursday. In Arabic, an army is referred to as khamīs, and Thursday is called Yaum al-Khamīs. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) used to begin his journeys on this day, in order to take a good omen that his army will be victorious against the enemy. It is advisable to depart on a journey on a Thursday, bununla birlikte this does not mean that it is incorrect to commence a journey on any other day.

957.narrator: Ṣakhr ibn Wadā'ah al-Ghāmidī (رضي الله عنه)
957.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"O Allāh, bless my Ummah in the early part of the day."When he sent out an expedition or army, he would send them out in the first part of the day. Ṣakhr was a trader and used to send out his goods in the early part of the day. As a result, he became wealthy and possessed much mal. (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah)
957.commentary: Due to the supplication of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), the time of early morning contains great blessings. It is bu nedenle best to start trading and working immediately after sunrise. The early morning is also beneficial because a person is fresh and vibrant at that time and can easily expend more energy which will be a cause of progress and blessings.

958.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If people only knew what I know about travelling alone, no traveller will travel alone at night."(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
958.commentary: Scholars state that there are dünyevî and dinî harms in travelling alone. The dinî harm is that a person will be deprived of performing ṣalāh in jamā'ah (congregation). The dünyevî harm is that if any accident or difficulty befalls him, there will be nobody to assist. This was more so in the days of the past when people used to travel on camels, horses or on foot, and they had to traverse through deserts and jungles. There was also the korku of animals, thieves, etc. For these reasons, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) prohibited a person from travelling alone. bununla birlikte, Imām Bukhārī has dedicated a chapter to this entitled 'The chapter of a man travelling alone,' in his Ṣaḥīḥ showing that it is helal. Such a scenario will occur when a person has to suddenly travel alone, or act as a spy in times of war gibi when the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) sent Zubayr to spy during the Battle of the Trench.

959.text: 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb anlatır from his father who anlatır from his grandfather (رضي الله عنه) that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"One rider is Shaiṭān. Two riders are two Shaiṭāns. Three is a group."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
959.commentary: As far as possible, at least three people should travel together on a journey. If there are only two and one of them has to leave to fulfil bazı need, then the remaining person may easily become perplexed and influenced by Shaiṭān. Similarly, if a person is alone and passes away, there will be none to bath him, shroud him and bury him. There will be no one to take his goods back to his heirs and inform them about what had transpired. There will be none to help him to carry his possessions. bu nedenle, if there are at least three people, they can assist one another and take turns to guard their possessions. Importantly, they can perform ṣalāh in jamā'ah. Another yorum of Bu hadis is that one or two people can easily fall into the plots and deceit of Shaiṭān, but when in a group, the assistance of bütünāh will be with them. Sa'īd ibn Muṣayyab narrated, "Shaiṭān attacks one or two. If there are three, he will not attack them."

960.narrator: Ebû Saîd and Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنهما)
960.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When three people set out on a journey, they should appoint one of them as their leader."(Abū Dāwūd, Bayhaqī)
960.commentary: 'bütünāmah Ṭībī stated that the emir to appoint a leader is so that if during the journey, any such matter occurs which could lead to a dispute, then they can refer to the leader and practise in accordance with what he says. 'bütünāmah Zabīdī stated that such a person should be appointed as a leader who possesses noble character, is soft-natured and has the quality of giving preference to others over himself. Shaikh 'Abdul Haq Muḥaddith Dehlawī stated that the leader should not only possess noble character and a soft nature, but he should also be intelligent, experienced, have a desire to do good and give preference to others over himself.

961.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The best number of companions is four, the best expedition is 400, the best army is 4000, and 12,000 will never be defeated because of small numbers."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
961.commentary: If there are only three people together on a journey, two of them will engage in obtaining food or guarding their possessions while the third person will be left alone. If there are at least four people, then two of them can engage in one duty whilst the other two can engage in another duty. The number of 12,000 olarak kabul edilir a large number and if they are defeated, it will not be due to a lack of numbers. It will be due to bazı other weakness gibi pride, arrogance, etc.

962.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When you travel in grasslands, then give the camel its share of the land. When you travel in barren lands, then travel quickly so that you reach your destination before it tires. When you camp at night, avoid the paths because those are the paths of animals and the places of refuge for other creatures."(Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
962.commentary: In the days of the past, and even today in birçok rural areas, camels, horses, donkeys and mules are used to travel from one place to another. In this hadis, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) provides bazı guidelines for those who travel in this şekil. The first is that a person should provide sufficient fodder for his animals. He should allow them to graze when the opportunity allows for it. If not, one should try to tam the journey as quickly as possible, so that one can reach one's destination where the animals can feed. The second guideline is that if a person has to stop over at night to rest, he should divert from the main road since other creatures may utilise these paths at night and may pose a danger to his safety.

963.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) was on a journey and camped over at night, he would lie down on his right side. If he camped just before dawn, he would place his arm upright and put his head on his palm."(Müslüman)
963.commentary: Âlimler, yolculukta binitin üzerinde uyumamak için kolunu dik tuttuğunu, böylece derin uykuya dalmaktan korunduğunu belirtmişlerdir.

964.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"You should travel at night because the earth is folded at night."(Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
964.commentary: The hadis demektir ki it is easier to travel by night than by day because one feels energetic and fresh due to the coolness of the night. Secondly, a person does not notice birçok landmarks at night and he will bu nedenle think that he has travelled very little whereas this is not the case. It is also possible that the earth gerçekte is folded up at night as is mentioned in a narration of Kanz al-'Ummāl. The hadis does not mean that one should not travel during the day since other aḥādīth encourage one to commence his journey in the beginning portion of the day. It demektir ki a person should not confine himself to only travelling by day, but should also travel at night.

965.text: When the insanlar used to stop over at a place, they would disperse into the passes and valleys. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi to them:"This dispersing of yours into passes and valleys is from Shaiṭān."Thereafter, whenever they would stop over at a place, they would remain close together. (Abū Dāwūd, Bayhaqī)
965.commentary: Yolculukta sahâbîler birbirine ne kadar yakın olursa, yardımlaşmaları o kadar kolay olur. Dağınık olmak tehlikelere yol açabilir.

966.text: Sahl ibn 'Amr (or according to some, Sahl ibn al-Rabī' ibn 'Amr al-Anṣārī), popularly known as Ibn al-Ḥanẓaliyyah, who was from among those present for the Bay'ah al-Riḍwān, anlatır:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by a camel whose back was sticking to its stomach and dedi: 'Fear Allāh with regard to these dumb animals. Ride them in good condition and eat them in good condition.'"(Abū Dāwūd)
966.commentary: Animals are the creation of bütünāh and have a soul like man. They can perceive pain and starvation like insanî beings, but they cannot express their feelings in sözler, bundan dolayı a Muslim should ensure that he is merciful to them. It is incorrect to deprive them of food and to overwork them. On the day of Qiyāmah, a person will be questioned regarding his treatment of animals. When animals have been given haklar in Islām, servants and workers should to a greater extent not be overburdened with work which is beyond their capabilities and strength. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Do not burden them with that which will overcome them. If you do give them work which overpowers them, then assist them." (Bukhārī) "Eat them in good şart," demektir ki one should eat the flesh of healthy and fit animals and not that of ill or lean animals as this will contribute towards good health. It could also mean that one should slaughter animals in a humane şekil by ensuring that the knife is sharp and that the animal is not harmed in any yol while slaughtering.

967.narrator: Abū Ja'far 'Abdullāh ibn Ja'far (رضي الله عنهما)
967.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) made me ride behind him one day and he confided to me something which I will never relate to anyone. When Resûlullah (ﷺ) cevapladı the call of nature, the place he liked best for concealing himself was a wall or a date orchard."(Müslüman)
967.commentary: The secret matter which the Messenger (ﷺ) confided to the Ṣaḥābī was obviously regarding a personal issue. It was not a matter relating to the laws of Islām because this was not helal to conceal. When one is in an area where one has to answer the call of nature in the open, one should ensure that one's private parts are concealed from the view of others. The speaking and tearing of the camel was a miracle of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). It is helal for two people to sit on a conveyance if it has sufficient strength to bear their weight. One should encourage others to be compassionate to the creation of bütünāh. The Messenger (ﷺ) was a rahmet to the bütün creation.

968.text: Bir yerde konakladığımızda, yüklerimizi indirmeden nafile namaz kılmazdık. (Müslim)
968.commentary: Yolculukta konaklama yerine varıldığında, yükler indirilmeden önce nafile namaz kılınmazdı. Önce konaklama düzenlenir, sonra namaz kılınırdı.

969.text: While we were on a journey, a man riding his animal came to us and began looking to his right and left. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'One who has a spare animal should give it to the one who does not. One who has extra provisions should give to the one who does not.' He (ﷺ) continued mentioning various types of mal until we began to think that none of us has any right to anything extra."(Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
969.commentary: The rider was in dire straits and began looking around to see whether he could get assistance. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) noticed his poverty and teşvik edilen the Ṣaḥābah to assist him. Bu hadis in essence is teaching the beautiful humanitarian teachings of Islām. It encourages iyilik and generosity and discourages greed and selfishness.

970.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) intended to go out for an expedition and he şöyle dedi:"O assembly of Muhājirīn and Anṣār! Among your brothers are insanlar who have no possessions and no aile. Each of you should therefore attach two or three of them to himself."Therefore, those of us who had conveyances would take equal turns with them in riding them. Jābir (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi:"I also attached two or three of them to myself and I had a turn to ride my deve adil as they had turns to ride it."(Abū Dāwūd)
970.commentary: During the initial stages of Islām, the Muslims were forced to leave behind their wealth and families in Makkah Mukarramah and migrate to Madīnah Munawwarah. The Messenger (ﷺ), bu nedenle teşvik edilen the people of Madīnah to assist the Muhājirīn of Makkah. As Bu hadis mentions, the Anṣār complied to such an extent that they gave preference to their Muslim brothers over themselves. They sacrificed bütün that they had for their brothers and assisted them wherever they could.

971.text: Yolculuk sırasında Resûlullah (ﷺ) arkaya geçer, zayıfları cesaretlendirir, onlara dua eder ve bineğine alırdı. (Ebû Dâvûd)
971.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was a mükemmel example of tevazu. During journeys, he would move to the rear of the army so that he could assist the zayıf and helpless.
