The Messengers were insanî beings and also experienced death. bununla birlikte, they are blessed with a special life in their graves after death which resembles the life of this earthly abode. Their souls as well as their bodies are korunan in their graves. bütünāh says regarding the martyrs: "asla regard those slain in the yol of bütünāh as dead. Rather, they are alive in the presence of their Sustainer and provided with sustenance." (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 169). The scholars explain that if the martyrs, who are of a lower status than the Messengers, are alive in their graves, then the Messengers should enjoy the same privilege and honour to a greater extent.

1403.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A miser is one in whose presence my name is mentioned and he does not send salutations upon me."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1403.commentary: A miser is a person who does not grant another his due haklar. Abandoning ṣalawāt upon the Messenger (ﷺ) bir işaretidir miserliness and a proof of one's baseness because sending ṣalawāt does not require much effort. ayrıca, such a person deprives himself of great sevap and disobeys the Wājib emir of bütünāh as mentioned in the Qur'ān. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) deserves that ṣalawāt be sent upon him as he is the cause of our success in dünya and the ahiret.

1404.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating in his namaz without glorifying Allāh or sending salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'This person is hasty.' He then çağırdı for him and şöyle dedi to him – or to someone else – 'When any of you performs namaz, he should commence with praising his Sustainer and glorifying Him. He should then send salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and he may thereafter supplicate for whatever he desires.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Nasā'ī)
1404.commentary: Scholars have stated that a person should commence his du'ā' by praising bütünāh and then sending salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ). He should then request whatever he desires from bütünāh. At the end of his du'ā' he should again send salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and praise bütünāh. It is hoped that because the praise of bütünāh and salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ) are accepted forms of ibadet, whatever is requested between them will also be accepted by bütünāh. 'Umar mentioned, "Du'ās remain suspended between the heavens and the earth. They do not proceed towards the heavens as long as ṣalawāt upon the Messenger (ﷺ) have not been recited." (Tirmidhī)

1405.narrator: Abū Muḥammad Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah (رضي الله عنه)
1405.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) came out to us and we dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh, we know how to offer salām to you, but how should we send salutations upon you?' He cevap verdi: 'Say:"O Allāh, send salutations upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You sent salutations upon the family of Ibrāhīm. You are worthy of praise, majestic. O Allāh, grant nimetler upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You granted nimetler upon the family of Ibrāhīm. You are worthy of praise, majestic."' (Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1405.commentary: This ṣalawāt is considered to be the çoğu virtuous form of ṣalawāt, since the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) taught it to the Ṣaḥābah when they requested him. The Ṣaḥābah knew how to offer salām to the Messenger (ﷺ) because this was the salām they normally recited in ṣalāh in tashahhud: "Al-salāmu 'alayka ayyuha'l-nabiyyu wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuhu." Why do we ask bütünāh to send salutations upon the Messenger (ﷺ) when we have been commanded in the Qur'ān to send salutations ourselves? çeşitli answers have been given for this: 1. We have been taught to do so by the Messenger (ﷺ) himself when he was asked by the Ṣaḥābah. 2. Man is sinful and the Messenger (ﷺ) is sinless, bundan dolayı we can asla praise him as he deserves to be praised. For this reason, we refer the matter to bütünāh so that our supplication can increase in value and purity and be presented in this şekil. 3. We reinforce our inanç in tawḥīd. Despite our sevgi for the Messenger (ﷺ), we acknowledge that he is also in need of bütünāh's special rahmet, bundan dolayı we request bütünāh to send salutations and rahmet upon him. "The family of Muḥammad" may refer to the close family members of the Messenger (ﷺ) gibi his wives, children, the Banū Hāshim and Banū 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib, etc. Alternatively, it can refer to her person who obeys the Messenger (ﷺ).

1406.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) came to us while we were in the assembly of Sa'd ibn 'Ubādah (رضي الله عنه). Bashīr ibn Sa'd dedi to him: 'O Messenger of Allāh, Allāh has ordered us to send salutations upon you. How should we send salutations upon you?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) remained silent for so long that we wished that he had not sordu him the question. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then dedi: 'Say,"O Allāh, send salutations upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You sent salutations upon the family of Ibrāhīm. Grant nimetler to Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You granted nimetler upon the family of Ibrāhīm. You are worthy of praise, majestic."And the salām is as you know.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1406.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) remained silent anticipating revelation to descend. The Ṣaḥābah wished that he had not asked the question because they feared that it may have been inappropriate and because of their merhamet and sevgi for the Messenger (ﷺ).

1407.text: The Sahâbe sordu: 'O Messenger of Allāh, how should we send salutations upon you?' He cevap verdi: 'Say,"O Allāh, send salutations upon Muḥammad, his wives and his progeny as You sent salutations upon the family of Ibrāhīm. Grant nimetler to Muḥammad, his wives and his progeny as You granted nimetler upon the family of Ibrāhīm. You are worthy of praise, majestic."' (Bukhārī, Müslüman, Nasā'ī, Abū Dāwūd)
1407.commentary: "Zürriyet" kelimesi bu hadiste geçmektedir ve diğer rivayetlerde geçmez. Kişinin nesebi genellikle babası yoluyla devam eder.

1408.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"There are two phrases which are light on the tongue, weighty in the scale, and most beloved to the Merciful (Allāh): 'Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him. Glory be to Allāh, the Majestic.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah)
1408.commentary: This was the last hadis narrated by Imām Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ. It mentions a dhikr which is easy to recite but is extremely weighty in sevap. It is "light on the tongue" demektir ki it contains only those letters of the Arabic alphabet which are light and easy to pronounce. It does not contain letters of shiddah (أجد قطبكت) and isti'lā (خص ضغط قظ) which require greater effort. ayrıca, the phrases are concise. They will be "weighty in the scale" of ameller on the day of Qiyāmah due to the blessings of the name of bütünāh and the anlam of tawḥīd contained in them. Scholars state that despite these sözler being abstract, bütünāh will give them a form on the day of Qiyāmah so that they can be weighed. That these sözler are çoğu beloved to bütünāh implies that one who recites them will also become beloved to Him. bütünāh's name al-Raḥmān (the Merciful) has been used in Bu hadis to show the vastness of bütünāh's rahmet because He grants great rewards for small acts of goodness gibi recitation of the dhikr mentioned here. By reciting سُبْحَانَ الله, one testifies that bütünāh is pure from bütün such qualities which are not befitting of His grand status. The kelime بِحَمْدِه is an acknowledgement of His perfection in her saygı. سُبْحَانَ اللهِ العَظِيم is also an acknowledgement of ones inability to appropriately praise and glorify Him. سُبْحَانَ الله is repeated in emphasis because there have daima been more people who have attributed yanlış qualities to Him compared to those who contested His qualities of perfection.

1409.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"I prefer diyerek, 'Glory be to Allāh, praise be to Allāh, there is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh, and Allāh is the greatest,' to everything upon which the sun rises."(Müslüman, Tirmidhī)
1409.commentary: Bu hadis and the previous one encourage us to glorify and praise bütünāh, and proclaim His oneness and greatness. This is the crux of tawḥīd - the çoğu important inanç in life. Scholars have stated that bütün the beautiful names of bütünāh are encompassed in these four phrases. سُبْحَانَ الله encompasses those names of bütünāh which indicate towards His purity gibi al-Salām, al-Quddūs, etc. الحَمْدُ لله encompasses those names which indicate towards the rahmet, beauty, knowledge, and power of bütünāh gibi al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, al-Karīm, al-'Alīm, al-Samī', al-Baṣīr, al-Qadīr, etc. لَا إِلهَ إِلاَّ الله encompasses those names which indicate to the oneness of bütünāh gibi al-Wāḥid, al-Aḥad, etc. اللهُ أَكْبَرُ encompasses those names which indicate to the loftiness and grandeur of bütünāh gibi al-'Alī, al-Kabīr, al-A'lā and al-Muta'āl. These sözler are far superior to the bütün world because they are amongst the ameller of the ahiret, referred to as bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt (noble ameller which will remain forever). Their rewards will asla terminate whereas everything in dünya will perish and be destroyed.

1410.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who says, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. His is the sovereignty and all praise is due to Him. He has power over everything,' a hundred times a day receives the sevap equivalent to freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds are recorded in his favour, a hundred günahlar are wiped out and he is protected from Shaiṭān for that day until the evening. No one will come with anything better than what he has brought except a person who did more than him."And he dedi:"One who says, 'Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him,' a hundred times a day, his günahlar are removed even if they are like the foam of the ocean."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1410.commentary: One may recite these sözler in any order, bununla birlikte it is best to follow the order mentioned in the aḥādīth. These sözler are generally the çoğu virtuous to recite, bununla birlikte, du'ās which have been taught for özel occasions are more virtuous at those times. "He is one," demektir ki bütünāh is unique in His qualities and attributes. "His is the sovereignty," demektir ki bütün power and dominion is solely in His control. "bütün praise is due to Him," since He is the possessor of bütün perfection. "He has power over everything," is a reminder for man that he is completely dependent upon bütünāh. Imām Nawawī mentioned that a person will be granted the sevap mentioned in Bu hadis whether he recites these sözler a hundred times in one or separate gatherings. bununla birlikte, it is best to recite them in one gathering.

1411.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who recites, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. His is the sovereignty and all praise is due to Him. He has power over everything,' ten times is one who frees four slaves from the progeny of Ismā'īl."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1411.commentary: The progeny of Ismā'īl has been specifically mentioned because they were the ancestors of the Messenger (ﷺ). çeşitli other aḥādīth have mentioned the faziletler of these or benzer sözler. meselâ, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "One who recites the sözler in the marketplace will receive a million rewards, a million of his günahlar will be forgiven and a house will be built for him in cennet." (Tirmidhī)

1412.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Should I not tell you of the words which are most beloved to Allāh? Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him.'"(Müslüman)
1412.commentary: bütünāh loves that His servant praises Him and proclaims His purity from inappropriate attributes. bundan dolayı, the fazilet and rewards of these phrases are birçok as stated in çeşitli aḥādīth. A az sayıda of these are mentioned below: 1. "One who says, 'سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ', a date palm is planted for him in cennet." (Bazzār) 2. "One who recites 'سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ' one hundred times a day, his günahlar will be forgiven, even if they are equal to the foam of the ocean." (Muslim, Tirmidhī) 3. "One who is too zayıf to engage in ibadet at night, too miserly to spend wealth and too cowardly to fight the enemy, should recite in abundance, 'سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ', since this is more beloved to bütünāh than a mountain of gold which one spends in the yol of bütünāh." (Ṭabrānī)

1413.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Purity is half of faith. (The phrase) al-Ḥamdulillāh fills the scale. (The phrases) Subḥānallūh and al-Ḥamdulillāh fill (or the sevap fills) all the space between the heavens and the earth."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Dārimī)
1413.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 25. سُبْحَانَ الله is an bütün-encompassing phrase which demektir ki bütünāh is pure from bütün deficiencies, weaknesses and faults. This purity can be categorised in the following şekil: 1. His being is free from bütün deficiencies. He has no partner. He is free from being confined to a particular place. He was not created. He does not possess a body and He has no spouse and offspring. 2. His qualities are free from bütün deficiencies. He is free from ignorance, weakness and His qualities can asla change. 3. His ameller are free from bütün deficiencies. He does according to His hikmet, which man, due to his deficient anlayış, can asla fully comprehend. 4. His names are free from bütün deficiencies. He possesses beautiful names and her name reflects a quality within Him, as opposed to man, who may have a name which does not befit his qualities. 5. His laws are free from bütün deficiencies. The rules and statutes of bütünāh are free from error, injustice, ignorance, irrationality and prejudice. الحَمْدُ لله is also an bütün-encompassing phrase which demektir ki bütünāh is mükemmel in her yol. This perfection can be categorised in the following şekil: 1. He is mükemmel and unique in His Being. There asla was and asla can be anyone benzer to Him. 2. He is mükemmel in His qualities. His qualities of knowledge, power, rahmet and bağışlanma are mükemmel and matchless. 3. He is mükemmel in His ameller. His ameller of creating, sustaining, honouring and disgracing are exclusive and unparalleled. 4. He is mükemmel in His names. His names are çoğu beautiful and her name of His describes one of His beautiful qualities. 5. He is mükemmel in His laws. her law which He prescribed for man is the best and çoğu superior. No better system of living exists other than that commanded by Him and His her law is completely suited to man's nature and temperament.

1414.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
1414.text: A Bedouin came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"Teach me some words which I could say."He dedi:"Say, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. Allāh is the greatest. Abundant praise be to Allāh. Glory be to Allāh, the Sustainer of the worlds. There is no power and might except with Allāh, the Almighty, the All-Wise.'"The man dedi:"These words are for my Sustainer. What about for me?"He dedi:"Say, 'O Allāh, bağışla me, be merciful to me, guide me, and provide me with sustenance.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1414.commentary: The essence of this du'ā' is as follows, "O bütünāh, forgive me for bütün past günahlar, be merciful to me so that I can abstain from bütün future günahlar, guide me to bütün righteous ameller, and grant me Ḥalāl and pure sustenance." It is an extremely comprehensive du'ā' because it combines one's needs of dünya and the ahiret. The greatest needs of a person regarding his manevî life are bağışlanma, the rahmet of bütünāh and guidance which will lead him to attain the pleasure of bütünāh. His greatest need in dünya is sustenance which gives life to his physical body. The du'ā' incorporates bütün of these aspects. The Messenger (ﷺ) teşvik edilen the Ummah to regularly make du'ā' using these two magnificent names of bütünāh. In a narration, Mu'ādh ibn Jabal narrates that the Messenger (ﷺ) heard a man uttering these two names. He remarked, "Your du'ā' has been accepted, bu nedenle ask whatever you desire." (Tirmidhī)

1415.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) used to complete his namaz, he would seek bağışlanma three times and say: 'O Allāh, You are peace and all peace is from You. You are most blessed, O possessor of might and honour!'"Al-Auzā'ī, one of the narrators of this hadis, was sordu:"How should one seek bağışlanma?"He cevap verdi:"Say, 'I seek bağışlanma from Allāh. I seek bağışlanma from Allāh.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1415.commentary: The fact that the Messenger (ﷺ) sought bağışlanma thrice after her ṣalāh bize öğretir ki no matter how mükemmel one's ibadet may be, it can asla fulfil the haklar due to bütünāh. When the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), who was çoğu mükemmel in carrying out ibadetler, sought bağışlanma after an ibadet, then his followers should do so bütün the more. "O bütünāh, You are peace," can have one of two meanings: 1. "O bütünāh, You are pure from any form of change as well as her deficiency, weakness and flaw." 2. "O bütünāh, You are the being who grants peace." başka bir deyişle, peace and security is in bütünāh's power. By pleasing Him, man will find peace in his life, family, home and society. "bütün peace is from You" can have one of two meanings: 1. "We desire that You rid us of bütün weaknesses, flaws and faults." 2. "We desire peace and security from You." ذَا الجَلالِ indicates towards bütünāh's qualities of Jalāl (grandeur and might), whilst وَالإِكْرَام işaret eder His qualities of Jamāl (beauty and perfection.) Perfection is in possessing her iki these types of qualities, böylece tam perfection is only for bütünāh.

1416.text: 'Abdullāh ibn al-Zubayr anlatır that he (Resûlullah (ﷺ)) used to say after every namaz when he had made the salām,"There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. His is the sovereignty and all praise is due to Him. He has power over everything. There is no power and no might except with Allāh. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. We ibadet Him only. All nimetler, excellence and beautiful praises belong to Him alone. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. We are totally devoted in ibadet to Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it."Ibn al-Zubayr dedi:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to say these words after every obligatory namaz."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
1416.commentary: Göre the Ḥanafī scholars, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) would generally recite a short du'ā' after those Farḍ ṣalāhs which were followed by Sunnah ṣalāhs. After performing the Sunnah ṣalāhs, he would recite the longer du'ās. bunun sebebi is that the Sunnah ṣalāhs are a completion of the Farā'iḍ. As for those Farḍ ṣalāhs which are not followed by Sunnah ṣalāhs, gibi Fajr and 'Aṣr, one may recite the longer du'ās immediately after the Farḍ. This has been mentioned in authoritative books of Ḥanafī Fiqh gibi Shāmī, Fatāwā 'Ālamgirī, Hindiyyah, Tartarkhāniyyah, etc. "The influence of any person who has it is of no avail against You," demektir ki wealth, status or dünyevî power cannot assist a person in bütünāh's court. Only His rahmet and one's iyilikler will be of fayda at that time. This is affirmed by the verse, "...the day when neither wealth nor sons will be of any fayda. Except for him who comes to bütünāh with a sahih heart." (Sūrah al-Shu'arā', 88-89)

1417.text: He used to say after every namaz when he had made the salām,"There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. His is the sovereignty and all praise is due to Him. He has power over everything. There is no power and no might except with Allāh. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. We ibadet Him only. All nimetler, excellence and beautiful praises belong to Him alone. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. We are totally devoted in ibadet to Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it."Ibn al-Zubayr dedi:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to say these words after every obligatory namaz."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
1417.commentary: Ibn al-Zubayr said: "The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) used to say these sözler after her farz ṣalāh."

1418.text: The poor Muhājirūn came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"The wealthy have appropriated high ranks and eternal bounties."He sordu:"How is that?"They dedi:"They perform namaz as we perform namaz and they fast as we fast. They have extra mal with which they perform Ḥaj, Umre, wage cihat and give in sadaka."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"Should I not teach you something by which you can reach those who went ahead of you and outshine those who will come after you, and none will be better than you except one who does the same as you do?"They cevap verdi:"Please do, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!"He dedi:"You should glorify Allāh (i.e. say Subḥānallāh), praise Allāh (i.e. say Alḥamdulillāh) and express the greatness of Allāh (i.e. say Allāhu Akbar) thirty-three times after every namaz."Müslüman adds in his narration: These poor Muhājirūn then returned to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"Our wealthy brothers heard of what we were doing and they did the same."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"That is the bounty of Allāh which He gives to whoever He wills."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1418.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 573. According to Abū Ṣāliḥ, the narrator of the hadis from Abū Hurayrah, her biri of these three phrases should be recited in succession thirty-three times. bununla birlikte, the majority of the scholars are of the opinion that her biri one should be recited thirty-three times individually, before commencing with the next. In dinî matters, one should emulate those who possess greater fazilet so that one may progress spiritually, while in dünyevî matters, one should look towards those who possess less, so that one may increase in gratitude. One should adhere to the quantities in saygı of the adhkār mentioned in the aḥādīth because of the special hidden hikmet which is contained within them.

1419.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who says subḥanallāh thirty three times, Alḥamdulillāh thirty three times, and Allāhu Akbar thirty three times after every namaz, and then brings it to a total of 100 by diyerek, 'There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. His is the sovereignty and all praise is due to Him. He has power over everything,' will have his günahlar forgiven even if they are like the foam of the ocean."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
1419.commentary: Maulāna Rūmī explained that, when we recite Subḥānallāh (declaring the purity of bütünāh), it is as if bütünāh is saying to us, "I am pure and unblemished and I do not become pure by your proclamation. bununla birlikte, by the blessings of subḥanallāh, I will purify those who recite it (from faults, weaknesses and günahlar)." Similarly, by reciting Alḥamdulillāh, bütünāh will create such qualities within us that will make us praiseworthy, and by reciting bütünāhu Akbar, bütünāh will make us respectable and honourable in the opinion of others. böylece, these sözler are actually a three-in-one cleansing agent of the heart. It is to be noted that the bağışlanma of günahlar referred to in Bu hadis işaret eder minor günahlar and not major günahlar as the latter require istighfār and tawbah.

1420.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who says – or does – the mu'aqibāt after every obligatory namaz will never be unsuccessful: tasbīḥ thirty three times, taḥmīd thirty three times, and takbīr thirty four times."(Müslüman, Dārimī, Bayhaqī)
1420.commentary: There are slight differences between the çeşitli tasbīḥāt which are to be recited after the Farḍ ṣalāhs. bunun sebebi was that the Messenger (ﷺ) advised her biri person according to his manevî requirements. We may recite any one of them, or bazı âlimlere göre, rotate between bütün of them so that we may practise on bütün these aḥādīth. According to Ibn Ḥajar, the narration of reciting takbīr 34 times is preferred over bütün other narrations. According to Mujaddid Alf Thānī, these adhkār after ṣalāh are recited in order to compensate for the deficiencies in the ṣalāh and to acknowledge one's weakness and imperfection. bütünāhu Akbar is recited once more than the tasbīḥ and taḥmīd in order to emphasise bütünāh's greatness and grandeur.

1421.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
1421.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to seek refuge in Allāh after every namaz with these words:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from cowardice and cimrilik. I seek refuge in You from being döndü to an age of infirmity. I seek refuge in You from the tribulation of this world. I seek refuge in You from the tribulation of the grave."(Bukhārī, Nasā'ī, Tirmidhī)
1421.commentary: This was the du'ā' which the Messenger (ﷺ) used to recite after ṣalāh, bununla birlikte bazı scholars are of the view that it was recited in the last rak'āt before the salām. The narrator of this hadis, Sa'd, used to teach this du'ā' to his children. "Miserliness" işaret eder not fulfilling one's compulsory financial yükümlülükler. According to the Arabs, it işaret eder withholding one's excess items from a beggar. The "age of infirmity" işaret eder old age when the memory becomes zayıf, the limbs become fragile and one is benzer to a little child. The "tribulation of dünya" işaret eder becoming so engrossed in the matters of the world that one forgets bütünāh, abstains from His ibadet and begins following one's desires. bazı âlimler der ki it işaret eder such wealth or poverty which diverts one from bütünāh. The "tribulation of the grave" işaret eder the çeşitli punishments of the grave which will be meted out to people for their evil ameller. bazı âlimler der ki it işaret eder questioning by the angels in the grave.

1422.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) held his hand and şöyle dedi:"O Mu'ādh, by Allāh, I love you."He then şöyle dedi:"O Mu'ādh, I advise you not to omit diyerek after every namaz, 'O Allāh, help me remember You, be şükreden to You, and ibadet You in an excellent manner.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Nasā'ī, Aḥmad)
1422.commentary: bütünāh's remembrance here işaret eder the tilāwah of the Qur'ān as well as other forms of dhikr. By this, one emerges from heedlessness towards the closeness of bütünāh. We ask bütünāh to assist us in being grateful to Him because bütünāh's bounties upon His servants are countless. Such bounties may be outward or inward, dünyevî or eternal. her biri bounty conceals millions of other bounties. bütünāh states, "If you attempt to count bütünāh's bounty, you will not be able to do so." (Sūrah al-Naḥl, 18). We ask bütünāh for assistance in worshipping Him in an excellent şekil. This entails fulfilling bütün ibadetler with their required etiquettes, concentration, kulluk and ihlâs. bazı scholars are of the opinion that this işaret eder the stage of iḥsān where a person worships bütünāh as though he is seeing Him. The three requests in Bu hadis are linked because the dhikr of bütünāh leads a person to being grateful to Him, which in turn leads to him worshipping bütünāh in the best possible şekil. The hadis highlights the great status of Mu'ādh in the sight of the Messenger (ﷺ). A person should inform those whom he loves regarding his sevgi for them. A lover daima endeavours to teach his beloved that which is beneficial.

1423.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you sits for the tashahhud (the final sitting posture in namaz), he should seek refuge in Allāh from four things, by diyerek: 'O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the azap of Hell-fire, from the azap of the grave, from the tribulation of the living and the dead, and from the evil tribulation of Dajjāl.'"(Müslüman)
1423.commentary: "The azap of cehennem-fire" has been mentioned first to show that the asıl object of life is to save oneself from the cehennem-fire and that one who succeeds in this is truly fortunate. "The azap of the grave" is a reality. Since it is the first stage of the ahiret, it is a good reflection of how one will fare in the subsequent stages. It is for this reason that when 'Uthmān used to stand at a grave, he used to cry so much that his beard would become wet with tears. Someone asked him why he wept more at the mention of the grave than he did at the mention of cennet and cehennem. He replied, "I have heard from the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) that the grave is the first stage towards the ahiret. One who is saved from azap in it, will have ease in the subsequent stages, and one who is not saved from azap in it, will have a harsher experience in the subsequent stages. I have also heard that no scene is more terrifying than that of the grave." (Ibn Mājah). "The tribulation of the living" işaret eder bütün the tests which cause harm to one's physical or manevî self. The tribulation of the dead işaret eder tests which begin when one is about to leave dünya, when Shaiṭān makes his final and çoğu dangerous attack upon man's īmān. It also includes bütün the stages in the grave, the plains of Qiyāmah and the life of the ahiret. "The evil tribulation of Dajjāl" is mentioned because it is from amongst the greatest of tribulations man will face in life. The Messenger (ﷺ) taught this du'ā' to his Ummah for their fayda, and not for his fayda because he was guaranteed koruma from bütün evils.

1424.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) performed his namaz, the last thing that he would say between the tashahhud and the salām was:"O Allāh, bağışla me my future and past günahlar, my private and public günahlar, my extravagance, and for all that You have more knowledge about than me. You alone can cause one to advance and You alone can cause one to retrogress. There is none worthy of ibadet besides You."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī, Tirmidhī)
1424.commentary: The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) sought bağışlanma due to his humbleness and in order to teach his Ummah to do likewise since none can fulfil the haklar of bütünāh's grandeur.

1425.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to frequently say in his rukū' and sajdah: 'Glory be to You, O Allāh, our Sustainer, and praise be to You. O Allāh, bağışla me.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
1425.commentary: In çeşitli aḥādīth, we are commanded to supplicate in rukū' and sajdah. Supplication is of two types: praising bütünāh and mentioning His grandeur, and requesting for one's needs from bütünāh. bazı Ḥanafī scholars are of the opinion that one should not supplicate for one's needs in rukū' and sajdah, while others state that in the Farḍ ṣalāhs, one should suffice on the tasbīḥāt only, but in Nafl ṣalāhs, these other du'ās should be recited. According to the Ḥanafī scholars, these other du'ās should be recited in Nafl ṣalāhs, özellikle the Tahajjud ṣalāh, as we have been commanded not to lengthen the Farḍ ṣalāh, keeping the old, sick and zayıf in mind. Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar has stated that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) used to recite the du'ā' mentioned in Bu hadis out of ṣalāh as well.

1426.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi: in his rukū' and sajdah: 'Allāh is exceptionally pure and majestic. He is the Sustainer of the angels and of the spirit.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1426.commentary: The names Subbūḥ and Quddūs mean that bütünāh is free from bütün weaknesses and attributes which are contrary to His lofty position. One mentions these two names of bütünāh to emphasise that one's rukū' and sajdah are only for that being who is mükemmel in her saygı. الرُّوح (spirit), bazı âlimlere göre işaret eder Jibrā'īl, whilst others assert that it işaret eder a special angel by that name.

1427.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When in rukū', express the majesty of the Sustainer. When in sajdah, exert yourself in supplication as it is highly likely that your supplication will be accepted."(Müslüman)
1427.commentary: In sajdah, one expresses his submissiveness and humbleness before bütünāh and this pleases bütünāh tremendously. Du'ās are bu nedenle readily accepted in this posture of ṣalāh. Generally, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) used to recite 'سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الأَعْلَى' in sajdah, bununla birlikte at times, he would recite other du'ās and other forms of tasbīḥ. According to the Ḥanafī scholars, these other du'ās should be recited in Nafl ṣalāhs, özellikle the Tahajjud ṣalāh.

1428.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The closest a person is to his Sustainer is when he is in sajdah, so engage in abundant supplication."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1428.commentary: Closeness here does not refer to physical proximity because bütünāh is free of space. It işaret eder acceptance and honour. başka bir deyişle, the best time when du'ās are accepted is in sajdah because a person places the çoğu honourable portion of his body – his face – on the ground, expressing his kölelik and tevazu. When bütünāh then raises the status of those who humble themselves before Him, a person should engage in supplication in this posture. bununla birlikte, supplications should be in the Arabic language and should be done in the Nafl ṣalāhs. Bu hadis serves as proof for those who say that sajdah is superior in fazilet to standing in ṣalāh.

1429.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi: in his sajdah:"O Allāh, bağışla me all my günahlar: minor and major, first and last, open and secret."(Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
1429.commentary: One should request bütünāh for bağışlanma from bütün günahlar because this is a requirement to gain immediate entry into cennet. Since a person is closest to bütünāh in sajdah, he should beg for bağışlanma at such a time. A proud person justifies his ameller, whereas a lover is daima repentant and anxious whether his ameller are in conformance to the pleasure of his beloved. Minor günahlar are mentioned before major günahlar because people generally overlook them. Also, when minor günahlar become a alışkanlık, they eventually lead to major günahlar. bununla birlikte, if one abstains from minor günahlar, then it will become much easier to abstain from major günahlar.

1430.text: I could not find Resûlullah (ﷺ) one night and reached out to touch him. He was in rukū' – or sajdah – and dedi: 'Glory be to You and praise be to You. There is none worthy of ibadet besides You.'"Another narration has:"My hand touched the inside part of his feet and he was in sajdah. They were upright and he was diyerek: 'O Allāh, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure, and Your pardon from Your azap. I seek refuge in You from You. I am unable to fully praise You. You are as You praised Yourself.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1430.commentary: Bu hadis in bütün probability işaret eder the 15th night of Sha'bān. The du'ā' is one of progression. Firstly, the Messenger (ﷺ) sought refuge in the ameller of bütünāh, then from the qualities (anger) of bütünāh, and finally from the Being of bütünāh. According to 'bütünāmah Khaṭṭābī, the du'ā', "I am unable to fully praise You. You are as You praised Yourself," işaret eder man's weakness and inabilities because no matter how much he tries, he will not be able to praise bütünāh in conformity to His status. The fact that 'Ā'isha's hand touched the foot of the Messenger (ﷺ) proves the Ḥanafī view that if a woman touches a man, his wuḍū' is not nullified. It is Sunnah for the feet to be upright during sajdah and for the toes to face the Qiblah.

1431.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
1431.text: We were with Resûlullah (ﷺ) when he dedi: 'Are any of you able to earn 1000 rewards every day?' One of those who were seated sordu: 'How can a person earn 1000 rewards?' He cevap verdi: 'Glorifying Allāh 100 hundred times results in 1000 rewards being recorded for him and 1000 günahlar erased.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1431.commentary: bütünāh grants a minimum increase of tenfold, as explained in this hadis. bununla birlikte, He can increase the sevap to 700 times and even more if He so chooses. We are truly fortunate to receive such great rewards for such minimal effort.

1432.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Every morning, sadaka is due on behalf of every joint of your body. Every tasbīḥ (Subḥānallāh - glorification of Allāh) is sadaka; every taḥmīd (Alḥamdulillāh - praise of Allāh) is sadaka; every tahlīl (lā ilāhā illallāh - proclamation of the oneness of Allāh) is sadaka; every takbīr (Allāhu akbar - expression of the greatness of Allāh) is sadaka; commanding good is sadaka; and forbidding evil is sadaka. However, two rak'āts of namaz at mid-morning (Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā) suffices for all of this."(Müslüman)
1432.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 118. It is repeated here to show the fazilet of taḥmīd, tasbīḥ, tahlīl and takbīr. Two rak'āts of Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā are equal in sevap to the charity due for the 360 joints of the body because ṣalāh is such an ibadet in which bütün the limbs are utilised.

1433.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) left her one morning to perform the Sabah namaz while she was in her place of namaz. He returned after mid-morning and she was still sitting. He dedi:"You are still in the same position from the time I left you?"She cevap verdi:"Yes."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi:"After I left you, I recited four phrases three times. If they were to be weighed against all that you had recited today, they would equal them: 'Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him equal to the number of His creation. Glory be to Allāh equal to His pleasure. Glory be to Allāh equal to the weight of His Throne. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His words.'"Another narration has:"'Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His creation. Glory be to Allāh equal to His pleasure. Glory be to Allāh equal to the weight of His Throne. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His words.'"A narration of Tirmidhī has:"Should I not teach you some words which you should say? 'Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His creation. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His creation. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His creation. Glory be to Allāh equal to His pleasure. Glory be to Allāh equal to His pleasure. Glory be to Allāh equal to His pleasure. Glory be to Allāh equal to the weight of His Throne. Glory be to Allāh equal to the weight of His Throne. Glory be to Allāh equal to the weight of His Throne. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His words. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His words. Glory be to Allāh equal to the number of His words.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1433.commentary: "His sözler" can refer to the Qur'ān, bütünāh's knowledge or His uncreated quality of söz which is free from the qualities of insanî söz. The hadis bize öğretir ki when making dhikr, quality is of greater value than quantity. bundan dolayı, the content of the dhikr should be excellent and it should be recited with ihlâs. Mullā 'Alī Qārī has written that the dhikr mentioned in Bu hadis is more rewarding since one concentrates on bütünāh's attributes which are mentioned therein and one meditates over them. Other scholars consider this dhikr to be superior because in it one expresses one's helplessness in saygı of counting the praises and favours of bütünāh and this is the best form of teslimiyet to Him. A person should stipulate a portion of his home specifically for the ibadet of bütünāh. bütünāh grants great rewards for minimal acts of kulluk.

1434.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The similitude of one who remembers his Sustainer and one who does not remember Him is that of the living and the dead."(Bukhārī) Müslüman rivayet etti it as follows:"The similitude of the house in which Allāh is remembered and the house in which Allāh is not remembered is that of the living and the dead."(Müslüman)
1434.commentary: The similarity of one who makes dhikr to a living person, and one who does not do so to a dead person can be in any of the following ways: 1. One who engages in dhikr utilises his external limbs in the itaat of bütünāh and fills his heart with bütünāh's recognition. Through this he becomes a means of fayda and guidance for others and is like a living person. In contrast, a person who does not engage in dhikr, neither faydalar himself nor others. aslında, he is worse than a dead person, because he is an enemy to himself and misguides others as well. 2. One who engages in dhikr is spiritually alive, whilst one who does not is spiritually dead. The more dhikr one engages in, the easier it becomes for him to abstain from günah and to perform righteous ameller. In contrast, one who does not engage in dhikr is spiritually dead, and it becomes extremely difficult for him to abstain from günah and to perform righteous ameller. Ḥakīm Tirmidhī stated: "Dhikr moistens the heart and ssık sıks it. A heart devoid of dhikr becomes dry and hard, due to the excessive heat of lust and base desires. bütün parts of the body likewise become stiff and abstain from teslimiyet to bütünāh. If you try to bend them, they break like a dry piece of wood which can only be used as firewood." 3. Bu hadis işaret eder the eternal life of those who engage in dhikr. They will enjoy a special life after death, benzer to the martyrs. 4. The contrast is in saygı of gain and loss. A person who harasses one who engages in dhikr is like one who harasses a living being, bundan dolayı he will suffer for this harassment. In contrast, one who ill-treats the unmindful, ill-treats a dead body, which cannot defend itself.

1435.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allāh says: 'I treat My kul according to his thoughts about Me and I am with him when he remembers Me. When he remembers Me by himself, I remember him by Myself. When he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1435.commentary: A person should daima be teşvik edilen by the fact that bütünāh's rahmet overpowers His anger. To lose ümit in the rahmet of bütünāh is kufr (küfür), tıpkı... gibi not fearing Him at bütün is also kufr. A gerçek believer is one who has ümit in the rahmet of bütünāh, but at the same time fears azap for his günahlar. "I am with him when he remembers Me," demektir ki when a person remembers bütünāh verbally or in his heart, bütünāh protects him from Shaiṭān and his cronies and grants him the ilâhî ability to do good.

1436.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The mufarridūn have surpassed others."The Sahâbe sordu:"Who are the mufarridūn, O Messenger of Allāh?"He cevap verdi:"The men and women who remember Allāh abundantly."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1436.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) mentioned these sözler while returning from Makkah to Madīnah at Mount Hamdān. The mufarridūn are those who engage in abundant dhikr of bütünāh, gaining lofty ranks in the ahiret, being granted a bond with bütünāh in dünya, and achieving a good şart of the heart.

1437.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ)'i şöyle derken işittim:"The best zikir is, 'there is no deity worthy of ibadet besides Allāh.'"(Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah)
1437.commentary: This dhikr is çoğu superior because it is the proclamation of the kalimah which is the foundation of Islām. When a person utters 'lā ilāha', he negates bütün yanlış deities, and when he utters 'illallāh', he affirms one sovereign being who deserves to be worshipped. The Messenger (ﷺ) also said, "Continue renewing your īmān by reciting lāilāha illallāh in abundance." (Aḥmad, Ḥākim)

1438.text: A man dedi:"O Messenger of Allāh, the laws of İslâm are too many for me. Tell me something which I can adhere to."He dedi:"Keep your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allāh."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah, Bayhaqī)
1438.commentary: The Ṣaḥābī meant that to attain perfection in her emir of Islām is difficult. He wanted the Messenger (ﷺ) to recommend something easy which would draw great rewards. "Keep your tongue moist" işaret eder excessive dhikr, since moistness of the tongue işaret eder the mouth moving, whilst dryness işaret eder keeping silent. Abū al-Dardā' said that those who keep their tongues moist with dhikr of bütünāh will enter cennet smiling.

1439.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who says, 'Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him,' has a date-palm tree planted for him in Cennet."(Tirmidhī)
1439.commentary: cennet oluşur orchards and gardens, and other areas which are completely barren. The more a person remembers bütünāh, the more trees will be planted for him in cennet. These trees will asla die, nor will they ever shed their leaves. The trunk of her biri tree will be of gold or green emerald and its branches will be of red gold. Its fruit will be the size of huge drums, and they will be sweeter than honey, softer than cream and will have no seeds or pits on which one may choke.

1440.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"I met Ibrāhīm on the night of my ascension (Mi'rāj). He dedi to me: 'O Muḥammad, convey my greetings of peace to your Ummah and inform them that Cennet has good soil and sweet water. It is barren and its plants are,"Glory be to Allāh. All praise be to Allāh. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. Allāh is the greatest."'"(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1440.commentary: We have been told that "cennet has good soil and sweet water" as an teşvik to make it our eternal abode. Because trees grow well where the sand is fertile and water is in abundance, we are teşvik edilen to recite the specified dhikr and have as birçok trees planted as we can in cennet. Scholars have stated that whoever hears or reads Bu hadis should reply to the salām of Ibrāhīm by saying, "wa 'alayhi al-salām wa raḥmat bütünāh wa barakātuh."

1441.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Size haber vereyim mi of the best and purest of your actions in the sight of your Master, that will enable you to reach the highest levels, that are better for you than spending gold and silver, and that are better for you than meeting your enemy, striking their necks and their striking your necks?"The Sahâbe dedi:"Indeed."He dedi:"The zikir of Allāh."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1441.commentary: In this hadis, the dhikr of bütünāh is stated to be the çoğu virtuous of ameller, whereas we know ṣalāh, fasting, etc. are more superior. Scholars have provided çeşitli explanations: 1. The objective of ibadet is the remembrance of bütünāh and dhikr is the means of acquiring this objective. 2. Dhikr here işaret eder the dhikr of the heart. 3. Dhikr purifies the heart which creates ihlâs and gives life to ibadet. 4. Bu hadis işaret eder genel şartlar and circumstances. bununla birlikte, at özel times of necessity, charity, jihād, etc. are the çoğu virtuous of ameller.

1442.narrator: Sa'd bin Ebû Vakkās (رضي الله عنه)
1442.text: He and Resûlullah (ﷺ) visited a woman and she had some date pits – or pebbles – in front of her with which she was glorifying Allāh. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi to her:"Should I inform you of something that is easier for you – or better?"He then şöyle dedi:"Glory be to Allāh equal to all that He created in the heavens. Glory be to Allāh equal to all that He created on earth. Glory be to Allāh equal to all that is between the two. Glory be to Allāh equal to all that He created. Allāh is the greatest, equal to that number. All praise be to Allāh, equal to that number. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh, equal to that number. There is no power and might except with Allāh, equal to that number."(Tirmidhī, Abū Dāwūd, Ḥākim)
1442.commentary: The woman referred to here was either Ṣafiyyah or Juwayriyyah, the honourable spouses of the Messenger (ﷺ). Mullā 'Alī Qārī stated that the dhikr mentioned in Bu hadis is more rewarding since one concentrates on bütünāh's attributes and meditates over them. Other scholars consider this dhikr to be superior because in it one expresses one's helplessness in saygı of counting the praises and favours of bütünāh and this is the best form of teslimiyet to Him. Scholars have stated that Bu hadis proves the permissibility of using a tasbīḥ for counting dhikr because the Messenger (ﷺ) saw pebbles and date seeds being used for counting dhikr, but did not object to it.

1443.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me:"Should I not show you one of the treasures of Cennet?"I cevap verdi:"Indeed, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!"He dedi:"There is no power and might except with Allāh."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1443.commentary: This dhikr is called a treasure of cennet for one of the following reasons: 1. It is extremely valuable and will draw birçok faydalar, özellikle in cennet. 2. In cennet it will change into a treasure. 3. By these sözler, one negates any ability and strength from his own self and attributes bütün ability and strength to bütünāh. He bu nedenle attaches himself to the everlasting mercies of bütünāh which will protect him from günah and help him towards good ameller. "Lā ḥawla 'an ma'ṣiyat bütünāh illā bi'iṣmat bütünāh" demektir ki there is no ability to abstain from disobeying bütünāh and sinning, except by the koruma of bütünāh. "Wa lā quwwata 'alā ṭā'at bütünāh illā bi'awn bütünāh" demektir ki there is no strength to obey bütünāh, except with the help of bütünāh.

1444.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to engage in the remembrance of Allāh at all times."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1444.commentary: This işaret eder the remembrance of bütünāh in the heart and not on the tongue because there are occasions when it is prohibited to verbally make dhikr, gibi when relieving oneself or engaging in intercourse. başka bir deyişle, he was daima conscious of bütünāh in whatever he did. This is referred to as the level of iḥsān which is the perfection of one's Islām. The fayda of regular dhikr can be gauged from the following narration. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "The inhabitants of cennet will not feel remorse or grief over anything of dünya except those moments which passed by in which they did not make the dhikr of bütünāh." (Ṭabrānī in Kabīr)

1445.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When one of you comes to his wife and says: 'In the name of Allāh. O Allāh, protects us from Shaiṭān and protect what You provide us from Shaiṭān,' and a child is destined to them, Shaiṭān will not harm it."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah)
1445.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki one should not forget bütünāh even at the time when one is about to fulfil one's desires with one's spouse. This indicates that at other times one should remember bütünāh bütün the more. Harm refers only to küfür, bundan dolayı by reciting this du'ā', the child will be granted death upon īmān. Others say it işaret eder witchcraft, bundan dolayı the child will be saved from difficulties and calamities. bazı say no harm will be caused to the child's beliefs and din. It is inappropriate to recite this du'ā' at the time of intercourse. It should be recited before engaging in intercourse.

1446.narrator: Ḥudhayfah and Abū Dharr (رضي الله عنهما)
1446.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) retired to his bed, he şöyle dedi: 'O Allāh, in Your name do I live and die.' When he uyandı up, he şöyle dedi: 'All praise be to Allāh who verdi us life after giving us death, and to Him is the rising.'"(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1446.commentary: "O bütünāh, in Your name do I live and die," can be rephrased as, "O bütünāh, by making dhikr of Your name, I will live and with it I will die." This indicates that the object of life is to gain the closeness of bütünāh by worshipping Him at bütün times. Sleep is known as the sister of death because when a person sleeps, his soul is temporarily removed from his body and he resembles a dead person. For this reason, we are commanded to show gratitude to bütünāh for returning our souls to our bodies so that we can have one more day to prepare for the life of the ahiret. "And to Him is the rising" bize öğretir ki although we have one more day of life, we should asla forget that a time will come upon us when we will not awaken from our sleep and we will return to bütünāh. It is Mustaḥab to recite these du'ās at the time of sleeping and awakening so that one commences one's day and night with the remembrance of bütünāh and ponders over the life of the ahiret.

1447.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Allāh has angels that travel the paths seeking out the people of zikir. When they find people engaged in the remembrance of Allāh, they call out to one another: 'Come to fulfil your needs.' They then surround them with their wings until they reach the lowest heaven. Their Sustainer – who knows best – asks them: 'What are My kullar diyerek?' They reply: 'They are glorifying You, proclaiming Your greatness, praising You, and exalting You.' He asks: 'Have they seen Me?' They reply: 'No, by Allāh, they have not seen You.' He asks: 'What if they were to see Me?' They reply: 'If they were to see You, they would ibadet You more intensely, exalt You more intensely, and glorify You more abundantly.' He asks: 'What are they asking for?' They reply: 'They are asking You for Cennet.' He asks: 'Have they seen it?' They reply: 'No, by Allāh, they have not seen it.' He asks: 'What if they were to see it?' They reply: 'If they were to see it, they would desire it more intensely, seek it more passionately, and yearn for it more strongly.' He asks: 'What are they seeking refuge from?' They reply: 'They are seeking refuge from cehennem ateşi.' He asks: 'Have they seen it?' They reply: 'No, by Allāh, they have not seen it.' He asks: 'What if they were to see it?' They reply: 'If they were to see it, they would flee from it more intensely and korku it more fervently.' He says: 'I make you a şahit that I have forgiven them.' One of the angels says: 'Among them is so-and-so who is not part of them. He merely came there to fulfil some need.' Allāh replies: 'They are such companions that even the one sitting with them is not deprived.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Nasā'ī)
1447.commentary: Bu hadis highlights the fazilet of dhikr, those who engage in dhikr, and the gatherings of dhikr. Scholars state that bütünāh specifically questions the angels regarding the group engaged in dhikr to remind them of their ifade "Will You place in the earth such creation who will cause corruption therein and spill blood (of one another), whereas we make Your tasbīḥ (proclaim your purity) along with Your ḥamd (praises) and glorify You." It is as if they are being told, "Look at the dhikr which is emanating from insanî beings despite their carnal desires and the whisperings of Shaiṭān working against them." This also indicates that the dhikr done by humans is far superior and nobler than that of the angels because: 1. Man has birçok sorumluluklar and görevler apart from ibadet, bundan dolayı his engaging in dhikr requires effort and discipline. 2. A host of obstacles and distractions gibi the desire to günah, inclination towards the world, Shaiṭān and carnal desires serve as deterrents from ibadet. 3. Man has not seen the unseen gibi bütünāh, cennet and cehennem, as opposed to the angels who have seen the unseen. It is bütünāh's grace that those who merely sit in the company of people engaged in the dhikr of bütünāh are not deprived of blessings. This also teaches us the value of good company.

1448.narrator: Ebû Hüreyre and Abū Sa'īd (رضي الله عنهما)
1448.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"No people gather to engage in the remembrance of Allāh without the angels surrounding them, rahmet engulfing them, tranquillity descending upon them, and Allāh mentioning them to those (close angels) who are with Him."(Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1448.commentary: A hadis of benzer wording was mentioned previously regarding those who engage in tilāwah of the Qur'ān. See hadis 1023. It indicates the fazilet of dhikr as well as the status of those engaged in dhikr in the sight of bütünāh. The "angels surrounding them" is in order to honour them and allow angelic qualities to be transferred to them. bütünāh's "rahmet engulfing them" ssık sıks their hearts and enables them to enjoy ibadetler. "Tranquillity descending upon them" işaret eder a şart in which the heart becomes tranquil and it then disinclines from fulfilment of prohibited desires. "bütünāh mentioning them to those (close angels) who are with Him" is in order to honour them in front of the angels who objected when man was created.

1449.narrator: Abū Wāqid al-Ḥārith ibn 'Awf (رضي الله عنه)
1449.text: While Resûlullah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mescid with some people, three people arrived. Two of them came towards Resûlullah (ﷺ) and the other left. The two stood before Resûlullah (ﷺ). One of them saw a place in the gathering and sat down, while the other person sat down behind them. The third person turned and left. When Resûlullah (ﷺ) had completed, he dedi: 'Should I not tell you about these three people?' One of them sought refuge in Allāh so Allāh granted him refuge. The second person felt shy so Allāh was shy towards him. The third person turned away so Allāh turned away from him.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
1449.commentary: The hadis explains the great fazilet of participating in the gatherings of knowledge and dhikr. The first person loved to listen to the advice of the Messenger (ﷺ), so bütünāh granted him bunun faydası. The second person did not push his yol into the gathering due to shyness, so bütünāh forgave him. The third person turned away from knowledge, so bütünāh deprived him of the sevap. One should seek to advance and progress in Islāmic matters. One may head to the front of a gathering in order to fill an empty space provided that it does not inconvenience others. Turning away from the gatherings of knowledge without any reason deprives one of bütünāh's rahmet and rewards.

1450.text: Mu'āwiyah (رضي الله عنه) went towards a circle of people in the mescid and sordu them: 'Why are you seated here?' They cevap verdi: 'We sat down to engage in the remembrance of Allāh.' He sordu: 'By Allāh, have you gathered here solely for this purpose?' They cevap verdi: 'We have gathered solely for this purpose.' He dedi: 'Listen, I did not request you to take an oath in Allāh because of any suspicion of you. No person who had a similar position to mine in respect of Resûlullah (ﷺ) has related less aḥādīth than I have. Once, Resûlullah (ﷺ) went towards a circle of his Sahâbe and sordu them: 'Why are you seated here?' They cevap verdi: 'We sat down to engage in the remembrance of Allāh, to praise Him for guiding us with İslâm.' He sordu: 'By Allāh, have you assembled here solely for this purpose?' They cevap verdi: 'By Allāh, we have gathered solely for this purpose.' He dedi: 'Listen, I did not request you to take an oath in Allāh because of any suspicion of you, but because Jibrā'īl came to me and haber verdi me that Allāh is boasting about you to the angels.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1450.commentary: The reason the Messenger (ﷺ) asked them to take an oath was out of caution because it was possible that something else besides the dhikr of bütünāh caused Him to speak highly of them. Mu'āwiyah had a close family link to the Messenger (ﷺ) because his sister, Umm Ḥabībah was one of his (ﷺ) blessed spouses. He further stated that he narrated very az sayıda aḥādīth due to his cautious approach in this field. By him mentioning these aspects, he sought to highlight to his audience his special concern for them in narrating this hadis. bütünāh was boasting about them because they engaged in His remembrance despite their carnal desires, Shaiṭān's whisperings, and their dünyevî commitments. Angels are free of bütün these hindrances, bundan dolayı their dhikr and ibadet cannot match the sacrifice of man.

1451.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"None will bring anything on the day of Kıyamet better than one who says in the morning and in the evening 100 times, 'Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him,' except a person who says the same or more."(Müslüman)
1451.commentary: These sözler of praise are very meritorious and birçok rewards have been recorded in the aḥādīth for reciting them. Scholars state that this dhikr negates bütün qualities contrary to the grandeur of bütünāh, and affirms bütün qualities of perfection in saygı of His lofty Being. The hikmet of reciting these sözler morning and evening is that one engages in righteous ameller at the beginning and end of the day and this will serve as an expiator of günahlar for that day. Because the shifts of the angels change and the books of ameller are taken up at these times, it is hoped that by engaging in dhikr, one's record will commence and end with righteous ameller.

1452.text: A man came to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi:"O Messenger of Allāh, how severely I was stung by a scorpion last night."He dedi:"If you had dedi, 'I seek refuge with the perfect words of Allāh from the evil of what He has created,' it would not have harmed you."(Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1452.commentary: The hadis bize öğretir ki a person should seek bütünāh's koruma from bütün evils and that bütünāh protects those who seek His koruma. "From the evil that He created" is genel and includes koruma from bütün the creation which can harm a person. It also includes koruma from following one's desires.

1453.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi: in the morning:"O Allāh, by You we start the morning and by You we start the evening. By You we live and by You we die, and to You is the rising."In the evening he would say:"O Allāh, by You we start the evening. By You we live and by You we die, and to You is the rising."(Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah, Aḥmad)
1453.commentary: One of the outstanding features of Islām is that we are taught du'ās for her activity of the day. bunun sebebi is that a gerçek believer wishes to live his bütün life in accordance with ilâhî guidance and there is bu nedenle a need for him to continuously beseech bütünāh for ilâhî ability and istikrar. The approach of dawn after the darkness of the night is a great bounty of bütünāh because if the morning does not come, the bütün system of the world will be thrown into chaos. Similarly, the coming of the night is a great bounty because it allows man to remove his tiredness of the day.

1454.text: Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi:"O Messenger of Allāh, teach me some words which I could say in the morning and evening."He cevap verdi:"Say: 'O Allāh, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the visible, Sustainer and Master of everything. I testify that there is none worthy of ibadet besides You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, from the evil of Shaiṭān and his prompting me to polytheism.'"He (ﷺ) şöyle dedi:"Say these words in the morning, in the evening, and when you go to sleep."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1454.commentary: The request to be protected from günahlar is mentioned before the request for itaat because günah results in the anger and wrath of bütünāh, whereas the ability to do good is only by the rahmet and iyilik of bütünāh. bundan dolayı, the causes for the wrath of bütünāh need to be removed before his rahmet can be attained. Sufis have mentioned this dhikr to be very effective for the purposes of submitting to bütünāh, self-reformation, abstaining from günah, doing iyilikler, and attaining safety from pride.

1455.text: In the evening, Resûlullah (ﷺ) used to say: 'We are spending the evening and the entire universe is spending the evening for Allāh, while all praise is due to Allāh. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner.' The narrator dedi: 'I think he dedi within this: 'To Him belongs all kingdom and all praise. He has power over everything. Ey Rabbim, I ask You for the good of this night and the good that follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil that follows it. Ey Rabbim, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evil of old age. Ey Rabbim, I seek refuge in You from azap in the Fire and azap in the grave.' And when it became morning, he would also say the same: 'We are spending the morning and the entire universe is spending the morning for Allāh.'"(Müslüman)
1455.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) sought refuge from laziness because it prevents a person from fulfilling his görevler. He sought refuge from the evil of old age because it can lead to senility, weakness and dependence on others. He sought refuge from azap in the Fire and the grave because they are the ultimate consequences of günah. These comprehensive du'ās teach us to seek koruma from bütün forms of evil and to ask for bütün forms of good.

1456.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Recite Qul huwallāhu aḥad (Sûre al-Ikhlāṣ), and the Mu'awwadhatayn (Sûre al-Falaq and Sûre al-Nās) in the morning and evening three times. They will be sufficient for you from everything.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1456.commentary: Reciting Sūrah al-Ikhlāṣ her morning and evening is a proclamation of tawḥīd and a koruma of a believer's īmān and beliefs. Similarly, reciting the Mu'awwadhatayn protects one from harm and günahlar. Sūrah al-Ikhlāṣ which extols bütünāh's Oneness and exclusivity is recited before the Mu'awwadhatayn in which one seeks koruma, because praise of bütünāh should precede du'ā'. By reciting these Sūrahs one will be protected from evil gibi black magic, jealousy and sicknesses. The Messenger (ﷺ) used to recite these Sūrahs when going to sleep and then rub his hands over his bütün body. (Bukhārī)

1457.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any kul says in the morning of every day and the evening of every night, 'In the name of Allāh with whose name nothing in the earth and the heavens can cause harm. He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing,' three times then nothing will harm him."(Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, Ḥākim)
1457.commentary: In this hadis, one seeks koruma with the name of bütünāh from her evil animal, jin, insanî or inanimate object. bütünāh alone is the controller of the universe, bundan dolayı a believer should place his total iman in Him alone. 'Abbān, a narrator of this hadis, was afflicted with kısmi paralysis. He was once narrating it to others and a person was staring at him. 'Abbān realised that the man was doubting why he had become paralysed when he was a narrator of this hadis. He explained that the hadis was doğru and that he had once forgotten to recite this du'ā' due to being angry over a certain matter and on that day he was afflicted with paralysis. (Tirmidhī)

1458.narrator: Hudhayfah and Abū Dharr (رضي الله عنهما)
1458.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) retired to his bed, he dedi: 'In Your name, O Allāh, I live and die.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1458.commentary: Bu dua ölümü hatırlatır ve bu nedenle kişiyi iyi işler yapmaya teşvik etmelidir. Ölümü sıkça hatırlamak kalbi yumuşatır.

1459.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to him and Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها):"When you retire to your bed – or when you lie down on your bed – say Allāhu akbar thirty-three times, Subḥānallāh thirty-three times, and al-Ḥamdulillāh thirty-three times."Another narration has:"Say Allāhu akbar thirty four times."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
1459.commentary: Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger (ﷺ), would do bütün her household chores herself and this caused her substantial difficulty. Her husband, 'Alī, suggested that she request her father for a servant to assist her. Her father, instead, taught her this supplication and she immediately expressed her pleasure with bütünāh and His Messenger (ﷺ). Scholars say that one who recites this supplication before sleeping will not tire from his work during the day. 'Alī stated that he asla omitted this prescription of the Messenger (ﷺ) his bütün life, even during the battle of Ṣiffīn. According to Mujaddid Alf Thānī, the above three phrases incorporate istighfār (by reciting 'Subḥānallāh'), gratitude (by reciting 'Alḥamdulillāh'), and deficiencies that have occurred in istighfār and gratitude are also acknowledged (by reciting bütünāhu Akbar).

1460.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When any of you retires to his bed, he should dust his bed with the inside of his loin cloth because he does not know what might be on it. He should then say: 'In Your name, My Sustainer, I place my side (on the bed) and through Your name I raise it up. If You take away my soul, have rahmet upon it. If You release it, protect it like You protect Your salih kullar.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1460.commentary: Going to sleep and awakening with the remembrance of bütünāh is meritorious because one begins and terminates the amel of sleeping in a blessed şekil. The righteous explain through experience that one who sleeps with bütünāh's dhikr is protected from Shaiṭān. ayrıca, the negligence that affects one due to sleep and dreams is countered when one falls asleep taking bütünāh's name because one then remains conscious of bütünāh while sleeping. By means of this du'ā', one surrenders completely to bütünāh and accepts that He is in total control of everything. Blowing into ones hands after reciting verses of the Qur'ān is in order to derive its celestial blessings. As with other forms of ibadet, we are teşvik edilen to combine a verbal dhikr with a physical amel. Wiping over the bed is to remove any dangerous insect or object that may be there.

1461.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) retired to his bed, he would blow into his hands, recite the Muawwadhatayn (Sûre al-Falaq and Sûre al-Nās) and wipe them over his body."Another narration states:"When Resûlullah (ﷺ) retired to his bed every night, he would put his palms together, blow into them, and recite in them Qul huwallāhu aḥad, Qul a'ūdhu bi rabbil falaq and Qul a'ūdhu bi rabbin nās. He would then wipe his hands over as much of his body as he could. He would begin with his head and face, and then the front of his body. He would do this three times."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Ibn Mājah)
1461.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) used to recite these Sūrahs when going to sleep and then rub his hands over his bütün body. The linguists state that "nafth" (blowing) is a gentle blowing without saliva.

1462.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me,"When you go to bed perform wuḍū' as you would for namaz. Then lie down on your right side and say: 'Allah'ım! I submit myself to You; I have entrusted all my affairs to You; I have placed my back (my entire body) in Your protection, in anticipation of Your sevap and due to korku of Your azap. There is no escape nor salvation from You except with You. I believe in the Book which You revealed and the Messenger whom You sent.' If you pass away, you will pass away with īmān. Let these words be your last words (before falling asleep)."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
1462.commentary: Bu hadis teaches us three Sunnah ameller before sleeping: 1. To perform wuḍū'. 2. To lie down on one's doğru hand side. 3. To engage in dhikr of bütünāh. Scholars mention that sleeping on the doğru hand side prevents one from falling into a deep sleep which will prevent him from awakening for Tahajjud and Fajr ṣalāh.

1463.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) retired to his bed, he dedi: 'All praise is due to Allāh who granted us food and drink, and who gave us sufficient and provided us with shelter. There are so many people who do not have sufficient and who have no shelter.'"(Müslüman)
1463.commentary: Scholars have given three explanations for the phrase, "there are so birçok people who do not have sufficient and who have no shelter." 1. It işaret eder the birçok people who are in enemy custody or living under oppressive şartlar. 2. It işaret eder the birçok polytheists, disbelievers, agnostics and others who do not know bütünāh or recognise His bounties. bütünāh does not assist them because He only assists those who believe in Him and appreciate His bounties. 3. It işaret eder those who have no one to save them from difficulties because bütünāh has destined destruction for them. The purpose of the supplication is to make a believer appreciate the birçok dünyevî and manevî bounties of bütünāh upon him and to make him realise how fortunate he is compared to those who do not enjoy such bounties.

1464.text: When Resûlullah (ﷺ) wanted to sleep, he would place his right hand under his cheek and then say: 'Allah'ım! Save me from Your azap on the day when You resurrect Your kullar.'"(Tirmidhī, Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah) Abū Dāwūd rivayet etti it from Ḥafṣā. It states that he used to say it three times.
1464.commentary: Through this supplication a believer declares his tevazu before His Creator and it reminds him that he should asla be negligent of or underestimate bütünāh's azap. While such a du'ā' can be made during the day, a believer is teşvik edilen to do so at night before sleeping as a form of tövbe from his günahlar because it is possible that he may asla wake up from his sleep.

1465.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Supplication is ibadet."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1465.commentary: Du'ā' has been referred to as ibadet in Bu hadis for the following reasons: 1. To supplicate is the emir of bütünāh, bundan dolayı fulfilling this emir is an ibadet. 2. The aim of ibadet is to express one's tevazu and need before bütünāh, and to acknowledge that He is the Creator and is bütün-Powerful, bütün-Knowing, çoğu Gracious and Independent. This acknowledgement is found to the greatest extent in du'ā'. Qaḍī 'Iyāḍ stated, "Du'ā' is asıl ibadet and is worthy of being called ibadet since a person turns his dolu attention to bütünāh and turns away from bütün those besides Him." 3. Du'ā' has been referred to as ibadet in emphasis. This is benzer to the hadis in which the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Ḥaj is 'Arafah." bu nedenle, it would mean that du'ā' is an extremely important ibadet. One cannot supplicate to anyone else besides bütünāh, as du'ā' is an ibadet and ibadet cannot be done for any being besides bütünāh.

1466.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) kapsamlı duaları tercih eder, diğerlerini bırakırdı. (Ebû Dâvûd)
1466.commentary: "Comprehensive supplications," bazı âlimlere göre refer to supplications which encompass goodness in this life and the ahiret. Others state that it işaret eder using sözler which are concise, but whose anlam is comprehensive. Scholars state that supplications in congregation should be bütün-encompassing and concise so that people are not inconvenienced by the length. Also, we have been commanded to make comprehensive and concise supplications since her person does not have the ability to fulfil the etiquettes of lengthy du'ās in terms of the required saygı and reverence.

1467.text: The most frequent supplication of Resûlullah (ﷺ) was, 'O Allāh, grant us goodness in this world, goodness in ahiret, and save us from the azap of cehennem ateşi.'"The narration of Müslüman adds:"When Anas (رضي الله عنه) intended making a supplication, he would do so with any words, but he would always include these words."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1467.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) recited this du'ā' in abundance because it is extremely comprehensive and includes the goodness of her iki worlds. It is also mentioned in the Qur'ān. "Goodness in dünya" işaret eder her form of goodness and safety from her form of evil. Scholars have stated that these include knowledge, anlayış of the book of bütünāh, Ḥalāl wealth, ability to do ibadetler, a pious spouse, pious children, well-being, the company of the pious and righteous, good health, praises of the creation and help against one's enemies. "Goodness in the ahiret" işaret eder bütün forms of goodness in the ahiret gibi safety from korku on the plains of Qiyāmah, koruma from a difficult reckoning, attaining cennet and its pleasures, and the enjoyment of beholding bütünāh. Safety from the azap of the cehennem-fire işaret eder being granted bağışlanma and being entered into cennet without azap. Ḥasan Baṣrī stated that it means, "O bütünāh, save us from desires and günahlar which will lead to the azap of the Fire."

1468.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, I ask You for guidance, salih amel, abstinence and self-sufficiency."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1468.commentary: "Guidance" işaret eder the ability to remain steadfast on the doğru yol. The önem of asking for guidance can be gauged from the fact that we have been commanded to ask for it from bütünāh in her rak'āt of ṣalāh in the verse of Sūrah Fātiḥah, "Guide us on the straight yol." "salih amel" işaret eder fulfilling bütün the commands of bütünāh and refraining from bütün prohibitions. "Abstinence" işaret eder restraint from günah and evil. Despite it being included in salih amel, it is repeated to highlight its önem, since the carnal desires of man continuously invite him towards evil. "Self-sufficiency" işaret eder a person not having to request for his needs from creation. It işaret eder contentment in the heart which is gerçek wealth, as the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Wealth is not having an abundance of provisions, but is independence of heart." (Bukhārī) The sequence of the du'ā' is significant. Guidance is requested first because it is the crucial ingredient of success. Thereafter, the ability to do good and abstain from evil is requested so that one's dinî life can be perfected. At the end, one requests for his needs of dünya.

1469.text: When a person embraced İslâm, Resûlullah (ﷺ) would teach him namaz and then instruct him to supplicate with the words: 'O Allāh, bağışla me, be merciful to me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide me with sustenance.'"Another narration of his has that Ṭāriq heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) when a man came to him and dedi:"O Messenger of Allāh, what should I say when I ask my Sustainer?"He cevap verdi:"Say, 'O Allāh, bağışla me, be merciful to me, grant me well-being, and provide me with sustenance.' These words will combine for you the good of this world and ahiret."(Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1469.commentary: We are taught to request for bağışlanma from bütünāh because bütün insanî beings commit günahlar and none besides bütünāh can forgive them. "Well-being" ('āfiyah) işaret eder safety from trials and günahlar in din, as well as safety from major illnesses and tribulations of dünya. One should request bütünāh for sustenance because one cannot ibadet bütünāh with tam kulluk unless his dünyevî needs are met. Ṣalāh constitutes the core of Islām.

1470.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنه)
1470.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"O Allāh who turns the hearts. Turn our hearts to Your obedience."(Müslüman)
1470.commentary: Since bütünāh is the being who changes the state of our hearts, we implore Him to enable us to remain in a state of itaat, and abstain from günah. A supplication benzer to this is found in the Qur'ān, "O our Sustainer, do not cause our hearts to stray after You have guided us. Grant us Your rahmet for verily You are the Great Giver. (Āl 'Imrān, 8)

1471.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Seek refuge in Allāh from the severity of calamity, the approach of misfortune, an evil destiny, and the delight of enemies (due to our misfortune)."(Bukhārī, Müslüman) Another narration has:"Sufyān (a narrator of this hadis) dedi: 'I may have added one.'"
1471.commentary: Göre Ibn 'Umar, "the şiddet of calamity" is when a person has insufficient wealth and birçok dependents. bazı scholars have said that it işaret eder difficulties at the time of death. Others state that it işaret eder such şartlar which a person is unable to bear or eradicate. "The coming of misfortune", according to Ibn Ḥajar işaret eder destruction or the causes of destruction. bazı âlimler der ki it işaret eder an evil end. "An evil destiny" includes an evil death or any evil outcome in relation to one's body, wealth or family members. Man is zayıf and requires bütünāh's assistance at her moment of life.

1472.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, rectify for me my religion in which lies the protection for all my affairs. Rectify for me my world in which lies my livelihood.
