Rectify for me my Hereafter in which is my final abode. Make this life for me a source of increase in every good and make death for me a source of relief from every evil."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1472.commentary: The phrase "rectify for me my din in which lies the koruma for bütün my affairs," can be rephrased as, "grant me the ability to fulfil bütün my dinî görevler in a çoğu mükemmel and beautiful şekil and in this is my success and koruma from the evil of Shaiṭān, cehennem-fire and the anger of bütünāh." The phrase "rectify for me my world in which lies my livelihood," is a request for sufficient Ḥalāl sustenance which will assist a person to engage further in the itaat of bütünāh. The phrase "rectify for me my ahiret in which is my final abode," işaret eder ameller of ibadet, ihlâs and a righteous ending, because without these, one's life of the ahiret will be in jeopardy. The phrase "make this life for me a source of increase in her good," indicates that a Muslim should continuously increase his knowledge and gain perfection in his ameller. özetle, in this du'ā' a person asks bütünāh to enable him to engage in ameller which please Him and to protect him from ameller which displease Him. The scholars have included this du'ā' in the jawāmi' al-kalim (comprehensive söz) of the Messenger (ﷺ), since a person beseeches bütünāh for success in dünya and the ahiret.

1473.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: to me: 'Say,"O Allāh, guide me and keep me upright."'"Another narration has:"O Allāh, I ask You for guidance and uprightness."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
1473.commentary: A person requires her iki guidance and the strength to remain steadfast upon the straight yol. başka bir deyişle, he should not commit any excesses or deficiencies in his ameller. Imām Ghazālī stated, "tıpkı... gibi it will be difficult on the day of Qiyāmah to walk on the bridge of ṣirāṭ, it is likewise difficult to walk on the straight yol in dünya. One who walks firmly on this yol in dünya, will be able to cross the bridge of ṣirāṭ on the day of Qiyāmah."

1474.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from inability, laziness, cowardice, senility, and cimrilik. I seek refuge in You from the azap of the grave and I seek refuge in You from the tribulation of the living and the dead."Another narration has:"From the burden of debts and the oppression of people."(Müslüman, Nasā'ī, Ibn Mājah)
1474.commentary: "Inability" işaret eder failure in doing righteous ameller. bazı scholars have stated that it işaret eder abandoning or procrastinating in those ameller which are compulsory. "Laziness," according to Imām Nawawī, işaret eder the inability to induce oneself to carry out righteous ameller and to have little desire to do them despite them being possible to accomplish. "Cowardice" işaret eder korku of others and a zayıf heart. Due to cowardice, one is deprived of the ability to engage in jihād, assist the oppressed, defend his family, etc. "Senility" işaret eder such old age wherein a person is unable to understand simple, perceivable and logical matters. "Miserliness" işaret eder not fulfilling the Wājib haklar which one is required to fulfil, gibi zakāt, Ṣadaqat al-Fiṭr, qurbāni, spending on one's family members (wife and children) as well as other dependants who have no other source of income (zayıf or disabled parents, sisters, divorced daughters, etc.). Miserliness is detestable because it arises from excessive sevgi for wealth. The "azap of the grave" should be a hakiki concern for her Muslim. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "The grave is a garden of the gardens of cennet or a pit of the pits of the cehennem-fire." (Tirmidhī) In another narration, the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The grave is the first stage of the ahiret. If one's şart therein is good, then the subsequent stages will be even better. If one's şart therein is evil, then the subsequent stages will be worse." (Tirmidhī) "The tribulation of the living" işaret eder bütün such tribulations which cause harm to one's physical or manevî self. The tribulation of the dead işaret eder tribulations which begin when one is about to leave dünya. At this time, Shaiṭān makes his final and çoğu dangerous attack. It also includes bütün the stages in the grave, the plains of Qiyāmah and the life of the ahiret. "Oppression of people" can either refer to a person being oppressed by others or oppressing others due to his excessive sevgi for power and fame.

1475.text: He dedi to Resûlullah (ﷺ):"Teach me a supplication which I could make in my namaz."He dedi:"Say, 'O Allāh, I have wronged myself greatly and none forgives günahlar except You, so bağışla me by pardon from Your side. Be merciful to me. You are All-Forgiving, All-Merciful.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad) A narration has,"And in my house."It is rivayet etti as"much wronged"and"greatly wronged,"so it is appropriate that they should be joined by diyerek:"much and greatly."
1475.commentary: In bazı narrations of this hadis, it is mentioned that this supplication should be recited at the end of ṣalāh, bu nedenle, one should recite it after tashahhud and durūd in the final sitting. It may also be recited at other times. "I have wronged myself greatly" is an acknowledgement of one's evil ameller and not fulfilling bütünāh's commands as they ought to be fulfilled. This du'ā' is very comprehensive because a request for bağışlanma is a request for safety from cehennem-fire, while a request for rahmet is a request for entry into cennet. One who gains her iki of these is truly successful.

1476.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to make this supplication:"O Allāh, bağışla me for my mistakes, my ignorance, my extravagance in my affairs, and all that You know better than me. O Allāh, bağışla me for what I did in seriousness, in jest, mistakenly and deliberately. All these are part of me. O Allāh, bağışla me for my future and past actions, my private and public actions, all that You know better than me. You alone can cause one to advance and You alone can cause one to retrogress, and You have power over everything."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1476.commentary: As the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was totally sinless, he did not commit any of the günahlar which he supplicated bağışlanma from. His niyet in making these supplications was to teach his followers to do the same. ayrıca, the Messenger's (ﷺ) continuous progression in spirituality led him to consider his past ameller as unacceptable to bütünāh. It was also possible that he regarded the omission of khilāf al-awlā (the best and mükemmel) as a günah. By the phrase "and bütün that You know better than me," a person seeks bağışlanma from those of his günahlar which he is unaware of. "You alone can cause one to advance and You alone can cause one to retrogress" demektir ki bütünāh grants cennet to whom He wishes by granting them the ability to do good, and He sends to the cehennem-fire whom He wishes by not assisting them to do good.

1477.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi: in his supplication:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the evil which I have committed and the evil which I did not commit."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah)
1477.commentary: Engaging in evil and günah causes a black spot to form on the heart and by continuously sinning, the bütün heart is blackened. Seeking bağışlanma cleanses the heart. In this supplication, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) reminded the Ummah to continuously seek bağışlanma from past and future günahlar. bazı âlimlere göre, it may also mean that a person should daima be concerned whether his good ameller are accepted by bütünāh or not. He should not be boastful and proud.

1478.text: One of the supplications of Resûlullah (ﷺ) was: 'O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the removal of Your bounty, the changing of Your gift of well-being, the swiftness of Your azap, and from every form of Your anger.'"(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd, Ḥākim)
1478.commentary: Bounties here refer to dinî bounties as well as dünyevî bounties which are beneficial for the ahiret. ayrıca to supplicating for korunma of bounties, one should also utilise such bounties correctly, as this helps to protect them. The bounties granted to the disbelievers and sinners which distance them further from bütünāh, are not really bounties, but istidrāj (respite). We are taught to request for safety from her iki the removal and changing of bütünāh's bounties because the former entails a tam elimination, while the latter entails a replacement. Examples of the latter are good health being replaced with ill-health and wealth being replaced with debts. We are reminded to seek koruma from bütünāh's sudden azap because it denies one the opportunity of repenting.

1479.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from inability, laziness, cowardice, cimrilik, senility and the azap of the grave. O Allāh, grant the korku of Allāh to my soul and purify it. You are the best of those who can purify it. You are its protector and master. O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that is of no benefit, from a heart that is not fearful, from a soul that is not content, and from a supplication that is not cevapladı."(Müslüman, Nasā'ī, Aḥmad)
1479.commentary: In this du'ā' we are taught to request for bütünāh-consciousness and purification from bütün evil qualities like küfür, nifak, pride, jealousy, insincerity and miserliness. "Knowledge yani of no fayda" can refer to any of the following: 1. Knowledge which is haram to acquire gibi magic, astrology, etc. 2. Knowledge which does not lead to practise. 3. Knowledge which does not reform one's internal attributes. "A heart yani not fearful" işaret eder a hardened heart which is not affected by the dhikr of bütünāh and the recitation of the Qur'ān. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "The person who is the çoğu distant from bütünāh is the one with a hardened heart." (Tirmidhī) "A soul yani not content" işaret eder a soul which is daima desirous of eating and fulfilling its sexual desires. Such a soul is the worst enemy of man. ayrıca to du'ā', one should physically and psychologically strive to prevent laziness, cowardice, miserliness and other harmful qualities from gaining dominance over a person. A believer should endeavour to attain beneficial knowledge and abstain from that which is detrimental.

1480.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, I have submitted myself to You, I have believed in You, in You I have put my trust, to You I have turned, through Your help I dispute and to You have I presented my case. Forgive me my future and past günahlar and my private and public günahlar. You alone can cause one to advance and You alone can cause one to retrogress. There is none worthy of ibadet besides You."Some narrators added:"There is no power and might except with Allāh."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1480.commentary: This comprehensive du'ā' teaches tam teslimiyet to bütünāh and tevekkül on Him alone. "I have submitted myself to You" means tam surrender to bütünāh's commands. "Through Your help I dispute" demektir ki one argues against opponents using the proofs and evidences that bütünāh has provided. "To You have I presented my case" demektir ki one refers bütün disputes and judgments to bütünāh's law as revealed in the Qur'ān and Sunnah.

1481.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to supplicate with these words:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the tribulation of cehennem ateşi, the azap of cehennem ateşi, and from the evil of mal and fakirlik."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Bukhārī)
1481.commentary: The tribulation of the cehennem-fire may refer to tribulations which lead one to the cehennem-fire, or the reproach of the custodians of the cehennem-fire. Wealth in itself is not evil, bununla birlikte it becomes evil when it is not used correctly or when evil qualities develop as a result of it. Similarly, poverty is not evil in itself. Through this du'ā' we seek bütünāh's koruma from the evils that can arise due to poverty gibi impatience, seeking doubtful and Ḥarām wealth, and becoming displeased with bütünāh's decisions.

1482.text: Ziyād ibn 'Ilāqah anlatır from his uncle, Quṭbah ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه) who dedi:"The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to say: 'O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from evil character, deeds and opinions.'"(Tirmidhī)
1482.commentary: Evil character işaret eder evil quality traits gibi stinginess, jealousy, nefret, anger, excessive lust, pride, arrogance, show, etc. Evil ameller refer to outward evil ameller gibi indulging in adultery, intoxicants, gambling, stealing, murder, etc. Evil desires refer to desires which are contrary to Islām gibi incorrect beliefs, innovations, incorrect niyetler, destructive notions, etc.

1483.text: I şöyle dedi, 'O Messenger of Allāh, teach me a dua.' He şöyle dedi: 'Say, O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my ears, the evil of my eyes, the evil of my tongue, the evil of my heart, and the evil of my semen.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1483.commentary: The eyes, ears, tongue, heart and semen are valuable bounties from bütünāh. If utilised correctly, one attains great fayda in dünya and the ahiret. bununla birlikte, if they are utilised incorrectly, they can lead one to the depths of cehennem. The evil of my eyes işaret eder staring at strange women, viewing pornography, looking with desire at the possessions of others, etc. The evil of my tongue işaret eder backbiting, slander, lies, futile discussions, etc. The evil of my heart işaret eder fantasizing, thinking evil of others, engaging the heart in bütün matters other than bütünāh, etc. The evil of my semen işaret eder utilising one's private parts in the yanlış avenues gibi fornication, adultery, etc.

1484.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from white leprosy, insanity, leprosy, and all other evil illnesses."(Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1484.commentary: Although illness bir vesilesidir sevap for those who exercise sabır, Islām desires that we ask bütünāh for 'āfiyah (well-being) because of our inability and weakness to accept illness. bununla birlikte, when one is afflicted with illness, one should endeavour to accept bütünāh's decision, exercise sabır and thereby gain the birçok promised rewards.

1485.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from hunger because it is an evil companion. I seek refuge in You from treachery because it is an evil internal quality."(Abū Dāwūd, Nasā'ī, Ibn Mājah)
1485.commentary: Hunger here işaret eder such a severe state of hunger that completely overpowers a person's internal and external şart, causing him to become restless and disturbing his ibadetler. It does not apply to kısmi hunger which is beneficial for the body and spirituality. Treachery işaret eder not fulfilling the amānah (güven) of bütünāh or His creation. The Arabic kelime used here is البطانة which literally işaret eder the inside section of one's clothing. It is an apt description because such clothing is hidden from view tıpkı... gibi a treacherous individual hides his treachery.

1486.text: A köle who had a contract to earn his freedom geldi to him and şöyle dedi:"I am unable to pay the price for my freedom. Please help me."'Alī (رضي الله عنه) şöyle dedi:"Should I not teach you some words which Resûlullah (ﷺ) öğretti me? Even if you had debts equal to a dağ, Allāh will pay them off on your behalf. Say, 'O Allāh, grant me sufficient of what You have yaptı lawful so that I have no need for what You have yaptı unlawful, and make me independent of all apart from You by Your bounty.'"(Tirmidhī, Ḥākim)
1486.commentary: The slave asked 'Alī for money to pay his debts, but 'Alī taught him a du'ā' instead. Scholars state that 'Alī did not perhaps have any money to assist him and mekruh sending him away empty-handed. It is also possible that 'Alī was trying to focus the man's attention towards bütünāh so that he would, in the future, ask from his Creator and not from the creation.

1487.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) öğretti his baba, Ḥuṣayn, two sentences which he used when supplicating:"O Allāh, inspire me towards hidayet, and protect me from the evil of my self."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1487.commentary: Guidance here either işaret eder being guided to the straight yol or istikrar on the straight yol. The evil of my self işaret eder one's nafs (carnal desires) because it is the focal point of bütün evil. Scholars have stated that this supplication is amongst the jawāmi' al-kalim (concise sözler with deep anlam) of the Messenger (ﷺ) because when a person is rightly guided, he is saved from her type of misguidance, and when his carnal self is rectified, he is saved from günahlar.

1488.narrator: Abū al-Faḍl al-'Abbās ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib (رضي الله عنه)
1488.text: I şöyle dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh, teach me something which I could ask from Allāh.' He cevap verdi: 'Ask Allāh for well-being.' I stayed away a few days and then I gitti back to him and şöyle dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh, teach me something which I could ask from Allāh.' He cevap verdi: 'O 'Abbās, O uncle of the Messenger of Allāh, ask Allāh for well-being in this world and in ahiret.'"(Tirmidhī)
1488.commentary: This du'ā' is extremely comprehensive because it includes a request for her type of goodness, and koruma from her type of evil. 'Āfiyah (well-being) in dünya işaret eder safety from sicknesses, trials and difficulties, while 'āfiyah in the ahiret işaret eder bağışlanma of günahlar and safety from azap. The fact that the Messenger (ﷺ) repeated the du'ā' when he was questioned a second time shows that it is amongst the best of du'ās. Another narration states that one should ask bütünāh for 'āfiyah because there is no greater bounty after īmān than 'āfiyah.

1489.text: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab anlatır: I sordu Umm Salamah (رضي الله عنها):"O Mother of the Believers! What was the most frequent supplication of Resûlullah (ﷺ) when he was with you?"She cevap verdi:"His most frequent supplication was, 'O Turner of hearts! Keep my heart steadfast on Your religion.'"(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1489.commentary: The phrase "O Turner of hearts" bize öğretir ki bütünāh is the one who can grant her iki guidance and misguidance. In this du'ā' there is an indication that one's end result is decisive, bundan dolayı one should be concerned that he is blessed with death upon īmān. In the narration of Tirmidhī, the following is added: "Once Umm Salamah asked the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) why he recited this supplication so sık sık. He remarked, 'O Umm Salamah, there is no person except that his heart is between the two fingers of Raḥmān. He keeps straight those whose hearts He wishes to and misguides those who He wishes to.'" Thereafter the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) recited the verse: "O our Sustainer, do not cause our hearts to stray after You have guided us. Grant us Your rahmet for verily You are the Great Giver." (Sūrah Āl-'Imrān, 8)

1490.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One of the supplications of Dāwūd (عليه السلام) was, 'O Allāh, I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and actions that will bring me to Your love. O Allāh, make Your love more beloved to me than my own self, my family, and cold water.'"(Tirmidhī)
1490.commentary: The sevgi of those who sevgi You işaret eder sevgi for the Messengers, the Ṣaḥābah, the scholars and pious. Loving them bir işaretidir īmān and a means of attaining lofty stages in the ahiret because the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "A man will be with those whom he loves." her person loves himself more than others. In this supplication, we request bütünāh to make us sevgi Him more than our own selves because in this yol one will daima give preference to the commands of bütünāh over one's own desires. The reference to cold water is an indication that tıpkı... gibi a person has natural desire for cold water on a hot day, we request bütünāh to grant us such natural sevgi for Him which will permeate her portion of our bodies.

1491.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Say the words, 'O the possessor of might and honour' in abundance."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1491.commentary: ذا الجلال indicates towards bütünāh's qualities of Jalāl (grandeur and might), whilst الإكرام işaret eder His qualities of Jamāl (beauty and perfection), bundan dolayı tam perfection belongs exclusively to bütünāh. Mu'ādh ibn Jabal narrates that the Messenger (ﷺ) once heard a man uttering these sözler and he (ﷺ) remarked, "Your du'ā' has been accepted, bu nedenle ask whatever you desire." (Tirmidhī)

1492.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) yaptı many supplications and we could not remember any of them. We şöyle dedi: 'O Messenger of Allāh, you yaptı many supplications and we do not remember any of them.' He şöyle dedi: 'Should I not direct you to that which combines all of them? Say, O Allāh, I ask You for all the good which Your Messenger Muhammed (ﷺ) sordu for, and I seek refuge in You from all the evil from which Your Messenger Muhammed (ﷺ) sought refuge. You are the only Being whose help is sought and supplications reach You alone. There is no might and power except with Allāh.'"(Tirmidhī)
1492.commentary: Bu hadis is indicative of the vast rahmet of bütünāh upon His servants as well as the easiness of Islāmic teachings because those who are unable to memorise the birçok supplications of the Messenger (ﷺ) can suffice on this brief supplication. It encapsulates bütün the supplications made in the 23 year life span of the Messenger (ﷺ). It also includes the request for her good in dünya and the ahiret and koruma from her evil in dünya and the ahiret.

1493.text: One of the supplications of Resûlullah (ﷺ) was this:"O Allāh, I ask You for that which will make Your rahmet obligatory, that which will make Your bağışlanma obligatory, safety from every günah, benefit of every act of goodness, the success of attaining Cennet, and salvation from cehennem ateşi."(Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, Ḥākim)
1493.commentary: That which will make Your rahmet farz işaret eder righteous ameller and characteristics which will draw ilâhî rahmet. That which will make Your bağışlanma farz işaret eder acts of itaat to bütünāh which will draw bütünāh's bağışlanma. Safety from her günah means the elimination of günah and evil traits from a person's character. The acquisition of cennet and salvation from the cehennem-fire is the asıl objective of life as bütünāh states, "The one who is kept far from the Fire and entered into cennet, then he is undoubtedly successful." (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 185)

1494.text: He heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"No Müslüman kul supplicates for his brother in his absence without an angel diyerek: 'And for you is the same.'"(Müslüman)
1494.commentary: When a person supplicates for others, he also faydalar from his supplication because he receives the supplication of the angels. This fazilet will be attained if one supplicates on behalf of one Muslim, a group of Muslims or bütün the Muslims as a tüm.

1495.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi:"The supplication of a Müslüman for his brother in his absence is cevapladı. Close to his head is an appointed angel. Whenever he supplicates for goodness for his brother, this appointed angel says: 'Āmīn! And for you is the same.'"(Müslüman, Ibn Mājah)
1495.commentary: Scholars of hadis state that Bu hadis is an açıklama of the previous hadis. The reason for such a supplication being accepted is because the highest level of ihlâs is found therein and the more ihlâs found in an amel, the quicker it is accepted in the court of bütünāh. Based on this, scholars state that if a person quietly supplicates in his heart for his brother in his presence, then he too will be included in the above hadis, since ihlâs is prevalent. When a person supplicates on behalf of another, then the appointed angel requests bütünāh to accept that supplication on behalf of the person for whom the supplication was made. Thereafter the angel supplicates on behalf of the one who made the supplication that bütünāh should grant him a benzer bounty. For this reason, it has been narrated from bazı of the pious predecessors that wheasla they required anything, they would supplicate that their need be granted to others. In this yol, their supplication would be accepted and they would then receive the supplication of the angels on their behalf.

1496.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who has an act of iyilik done for him and he says to the person who did it: 'May Allāh sevap you well', he has praised him to the highest degree."(Tirmidhī)
1496.commentary: In another narration we are taught to recompense a benefactor in kind. If this is not possible, then one should supplicate for him until one feels that he has recompensed him. (Abū Dāwūd) An act of iyilik may include physical bounties gibi food, clothing, safety from harm or manevî bounties gibi Islāmic knowledge, recognition of bütünāh, etc. The phrase "May bütünāh sevap you well" implies that one is unable to repay his benefactor, bundan dolayı he requests bütünāh to grant him a better recompense in dünya and the ahiret. This is an excellent supplication because bütünāh will grant in return what no insanî ever can. Supplicating is more superior than granting assistance or a tangible gift because a sincere du'ā' is irreplaceable in value. It should be remembered that the doğru and tam du'ā' is جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْراً and not just جَزَاكَ الله.

1497.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not curse yourselves. Do not curse your children. Do not curse your possessions. It should not be that you coincide with a time wherein requests that are sordu from Allāh are accepted."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd)
1497.commentary: In another hadis, Umm Salmah narrates that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Do not supplicate against yourselves except for goodness, since the angels say āmīn to whatever you say." (Muslim, Abū Dāwūd) Generally, it is bütünāh's system that, through His rahmet, He accepts good supplications quickly and delays in accepting evil supplications. The following verse of the Qur'ān indicates to this: "If bütünāh rushes evil to people as they want good to rush their yol, their term (of azap) would have expired for them." (Sūrah Yūnus, 11) Mujāhid states that this demektir ki at times a person in a fit of anger, curses his children, wealth and possessions, but it is bütünāh's grace that He does not accept this supplication quickly. (Bukhārī) Despite this, there are certain special times when supplications and curses are readily accepted, bundan dolayı we are well advised to control our tongues.

1498.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The closest a slave is to his Sustainer is when he is in sajdah so engage in abundant supplication."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1498.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 1428. 'bütünāmah Shāmī stated two şartlar for the validity of abundant supplications in sajdah: it should be in Nafl ṣalāh and not Farḍ ṣalāh; and it should be in the Arabic language.

1499.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Each of your supplications will be accepted as long as you are not impatient, by diyerek: 'I supplicated to my Sustainer but He did not accept it.'"A narration of Müslüman has:"A slave'in supplication will continue to be accepted as long as he does not supplicate for something sinful, for the severing of ties of kinship, and as long as he is not impatient."The Sahâbe sordu:"O Messenger of Allāh, what is impatience?"He cevap verdi:"He says, 'I supplicated and I supplicated but I did not see any acceptance.' So he holds back and gives up supplicating."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
1499.commentary: Bu hadis mentions bazı şartlar for the acceptance of supplications. A person should think positively that his du'ā' has been accepted. At times, bütünāh delays the effects of du'ās because one then supplicates with greater ihlâs which bütünāh loves, or bütünāh wants to increase a person spiritually. By being impatient at such a time, one loses ümit in the rahmet of bütünāh and fails to realise that du'ā' is an ibadet, for which he will be handsomely rewarded. bütünāh may bazen delay the effects of du'ā' for a prolonged period. meselâ, the time period between Zakariyyā's supplication for a son and the glad tidings of the same was forty years. Similarly, Mūsā's and Hārūn's supplication against Fir'awn came to fruition after forty years.

1500.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was sordu:"Which dua is most likely to be accepted?"He cevap verdi:"The dua that is yaptı in the latter part of the night and after the obligatory namazs."(Tirmidhī)
1500.commentary: Supplications made in the latter part of the night are readily accepted by bütünāh because they are indicative of a person's ihlâs and concentration at a time when others are asleep. It is also a time when bütünāh's special mercies descend.

1501.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"No Müslüman on earth supplicates to Allāh, without Allāh granting his request or averting a similar harm from him provided that he does not supplicate for something sinful or for the severing of ties of kinship."A man sordu:"In that case, we will supplicate in abundance."He dedi:"Allāh will grant even more."(Tirmidhī) Ḥākim rivayet etti it on the authority of Abū Sa'īd and added:"Or He stores a similar sevap for him."
1501.commentary: Bu hadis explains that bütünāh's acceptance of du'ās is manifested in çeşitli ways. Scholars have listed bazı of these as follows: 1. A person's request is granted immediately or after bazı time, if there is greater fayda for him in a delay. 2. Instead of the request being granted, a calamity, evil, sickness or difficulty is averted. 3. The sevap of the du'ā' is stored for him in the ahiret. When a believer will see the great rewards stored for him in the ahiret, he will ümit that none of his supplications were accepted in dünya. 4. bütünāh does not grant that which was requested, but something better.

1502.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle derdi: at the time of difficulty:"There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh, the Great, the Forbearing. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh, the Lord of the mighty Throne. There is none worthy of ibadet besides Allāh, the Lord of the heavens, the Lord of the earth, and the Lord of the noble Throne."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1502.commentary: This supplication bize öğretir ki the cure and solution for her problem lies in turning wholeheartedly to bütünāh. One who acknowledges that bütünāh is the Creator, Sustainer and Controller of such huge creations as the earth, heavens and the mighty throne will have no difficulty in accepting that He can solve her problem. Imām Nawawī stated that it was the alışkanlık of the pious predecessors to recite this du'ā' at the time of calamities and problems. Why does this supplication mention nothing about removing difficulties? Scholars have provided two answers for this: 1. These are the opening sözler of the supplication. After reciting these sözler, one should supplicate for the removal of one's problems, as understood from a narration in Adab al-Mufrad. 2. It is bütünāh's system that He grants people their heart's desires when they engage in His remembrance and cannot find time to supplicate to Him.

1503.narrator: Abū Muḥammad 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (رضي الله عنه)
1503.text: The people of al-Ṣuffah were poor people. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi on one occasion:"Whoever has food sufficient for two, should take three people; whoever has food sufficient for four, should take five or six people,"or words to this effect. Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) took three people and Resûlullah (ﷺ) took ten. Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) ate supper with Resûlullah (ﷺ) and remained with him until he had performed the Yatsı namaz. He then returned to his house after as much of the night had passed as Allāh willed. His wife sordu him:"What kept you from your guests?"She cevap verdi:"They were offered food but they refused to eat until you come."Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) dedi:"O foolish boy!"and rebuked and scolded him. He dedi (to the guests):"Eat without any welcome,"and added,"By Allāh, I will never eat it."He ('Abd al-Raḥmān, the narrator) dedi:"By Allāh, with every morsel of food we took, several times more of it appeared from beneath until they were all satiated. The food was now more than what it had been at the beginning."Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) looked at it and dedi to his wife:"O sister of the Banū Firās! What is this?"She cevap verdi:"By the delight of my eye, there is now three times more than what it had been before we began eating."So Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) ate from it and (Abū Bakr'in wife) sent some of it to Resûlullah (ﷺ), and related that he ate from it. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1503.commentary: Bu hadis demonstrates the miracles (karāmāt) granted to the awliyā' (friends of bütünāh). The food miraculously increased as they ate from it. Abū Bakr's initial anger at his son was because the guests had not been served promptly, but when he saw the miracle, he realized this was from bütünāh's blessings. According to the Ahlus Sunnah wal Jamā'ah, the miracles of the awliyā' are a reality. The under-mentioned verses and birçok aḥādīth establish the correctness of this inanç. There are five types of ameller which are contrary to normal practices: 1. Irhāṣ - Supernatural ameller of a Messenger of bütünāh before proclaiming prophethood. 2. Mu'jizah - Supernatural ameller of a Messenger. It is called as such because man is normally 'ājiz (unable) to do something benzer. 3. Karāmat - Supernatural ameller of pious individuals who follow a Messenger. 4. Ma'ūnat - Supernatural ameller done by a believer. 5. Mahānat/Ihānat - Supernatural ameller done by one who falsely claims prophethood. Such claims are unsuccessful and daima have the opposite effect.

1504.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Among the nations before you, there were people who were divinely inspired. If there had been such a person among my followers, he would have been 'Umar."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1504.commentary: The people who were divinely inspired işaret eder those who are granted ilâhî knowledge which is unknown to others. bazı âlimler der ki it işaret eder those from whose tongue the truth emerges without them even intending it. The Qur'ān mentions that the mother of Mūsā and Maryam (the mother of 'Īsā) were divinely inspired. 'Umar was also granted this bounty. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Undoubtedly, bütünāh placed the truth on the tongue and heart of 'Umar." (Tirmidhī)

1505.text: The people of Kufah complained about Sa'd, that is Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (رضي الله عنه), to 'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه). So 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) removed him from his post and appointed 'Ammār (رضي الله عنه) in his place. They complained that he (Sa'd) did not perform namaz properly. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) questioned him diyerek: 'O Abū Isḥāq! These people claim that you do not perform namaz properly.' He cevap verdi: 'By Allāh, I used to lead them in namaz just as Resûlullah (ﷺ), without any deficiency. I performed the Yatsı namaz by lengthening the first two rak'āts and shortening the last two rak'āts.' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'That is exactly what I had expected of you, O Abū Isḥāq!' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) sent a man – or some men – with him to Kūfah to inquire from the people about Sa'd (رضي الله عنه). They went to every mescid and enquired about him and all praised him. At the mescid of Banū 'Abs, a man by the name of Usāmah ibn Qatādah, who had the title of Abū Sa'dah, stood up and dedi: 'Now that you have sordu us, (know that) Sa'd does not go out on military expeditions, he does not distribute equally, and he does not show justice when passing judgement.' Sa'd (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'I will supplicate for three things: Allah'ım! If this kul of Yours is a liar and has merely stood up for show and popularity, then grant him a long life, prolong his fakirlik, and expose him to tribulations.' Thereafter, whenever he was questioned, he would say: 'I am an old man who has been afflicted and is suffering from the supplication of Sa'd.' 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, the narrator from Jābir ibn Samurah (رضي الله عنه), dedi: 'I saw him later on. His eyebrows were hanging over his eyes due to old age. He would approach young girls on the roads and wink at them.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1505.commentary: Bu hadis illustrates the fazilet of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqāṣ (رضي الله عنه). He was one of the 'Asharah al-Mubashsharah (the ten people who were given glad tidings of cennet in one hadis). He was also mustajāb al-da'wāt (one whose supplications were readily accepted). Once the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) supplicated for him, "O bütünāh, accept the supplications of Sa'd when he supplicates to you." (Tirmidhī, Ibn Ḥibbān, Ḥākim)

1506.text: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr anlatır:"Arwā bint Aus took her dispute with Sa'īd ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl (رضي الله عنه) to Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam. She claimed that he (Sa'īd ibn Zayd (رضي الله عنه)) had usurped some of her land. Sa'īd dedi: Would I usurp some of her land after what I heard from Resûlullah (ﷺ)?' Marwān sordu: 'What did you hear from Resûlullah (ﷺ)?' He cevap verdi: 'I heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek: One who oppressively takes a hand-span of land, will be necklaced with seven earths.' Marwān dedi to him: 'I cannot ask you for further evidence after this.' Sa'īd (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'O Allāh, if she is a liar, make her blind and cause her to die on her land.' 'Urwah dedi: 'She did not die before becoming blind, and while she was walking on her land, she fell into a pit and died.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1506.commentary: Hadisi duyduktan sonra, karar Saîd (رضي الله عنه) lehine verildi. Bununla birlikte, diğer rivayetler farklı yorumlar da içermektedir.

1507.text: At Uḥud, my baba çağırdı me at night and şöyle dedi: 'I think that I will be from among the first of the Sahâbe of Resûlullah (ﷺ) to be killed. Apart from Resûlullah (ﷺ), I will not be leaving behind anyone more beloved to me than you. I have some debts which you should repay, and treat your sisters well.' The next morning, he was the first to be killed. I buried him together with another person in a grave. Subsequently, I was unhappy to leave him with someone else so I removed his body after six months. Apart from his ear, his body was exactly as it had been on the day when I first buried him. I then koydu him in a separate grave."(Bukhārī)
1507.commentary: Abdullah (رضي الله عنه)'ın kerametleri bu hadiste açıkça görülmektedir. Vücudu çürümedi ve annesi onu bu haliyle 80 yıl sonra bile teşhis edebildi.

1508.text: Two Sahâbe of Resûlullah (ﷺ) once ayrıldı his company on a dark night with something like two bright lamps in front of them. When they parted ways, each of them had one of his own until he reached his aile. (Bukhārī) Some narrations of Bukhārī have that the two Sahâbe were Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr (رضي الله عنه) and 'Abbād ibn Bishr (رضي الله عنه).
1508.commentary: This was a miracle of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and a karāmat of these Ṣaḥābah. The physical light which manifested before them was drawn from the celestial light of prophethood which they had experienced in the manevî gatherings of the Messenger (ﷺ).

1509.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sent out a military regiment of ten people and appointed 'Āṣim ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī (رضي الله عنه) as their leader. They proceeded until they reached al-Had'ah which is between 'Usfān and Makkah. This was bildirdi to a branch of the Hudhayl tribe called the Banū Liḥyān. About a hundred men who were all archers set out after them and began to track them. When 'Āṣim and his companions perceived their approach, they took cover at a particular spot. The archers surrounded them and dedi: 'Surrender and hand over yourselves. You have our promise and reassurance that we will not kill anyone of you.' 'Āṣim ibn Thābit (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'O people! I have no faith in the guarantee of a kâfir. Allah'ım! Inform Your Messenger about us.' So they shot arrows at them and killed 'Āṣim."(Bukhārī) [The hadis continues to describe how Khubayb (رضي الله عنه) was captured, sold to the Quraysh, and martyred. Before his execution, he performed two rak'āts of namaz, establishing the Sünnet of praying before martyrdom. Allāh sent a swarm of bees like a cloud to protect 'Āṣim'in body from the disbelievers who wanted to mutilate it.]
1509.commentary: Bu hadis işaret eder the following karāmāt of the Ṣaḥābah: 1. The martyrdom of 'Āṣim (رضي الله عنه) was immediately conveyed to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). 2. Khubayb (رضي الله عنه) ate fruit out of season. 3. 'Āṣim's (رضي الله عنه) body was protected from the disbelievers by bees. 4. The curse of Khubayb (رضي الله عنه) upon his killers was accepted. Apart from those who accepted Islām, the rest were bütün killed within one year of his supplication.

1510.text: Ömer (رضي الله عنه)'i bir şey hakkında "Şöyle olduğunu zannediyorum" derken her duyduğumda, dediği gibi çıkardı. (Buhârî)
1510.commentary: Through the blessings of the company of the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ), 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) was frequently blessed with the honour of bütünāh revealing commands in conformity with the thoughts he expressed to the Messenger (ﷺ). These are referred to as 'Muwāfaqāt 'Umar'. Shāh Waliyullāh Muḥaddith Dehlawī has recorded twenty-four such cases in Izālat al-Khifā. bazı of them are as follows: 1. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said, "O Messenger of bütünāh! Assume the Maqām Ibrāhīm as a place of ṣalāh. bütünāh then sent down the verse, "Take the Maqām of Ibrāhīm as a place of ṣalāh." (Sūrah al-Baqarah, 125) 2. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said, "O Messenger of bütünāh! emir your pure wives to remain veiled as her type of person comes to your home. bütünāh then revealed the verses of ḥijāb." 3. Regarding the prisoners of Badr, it was the opinion of 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) that they should bütün be killed. Subsequently, the following verses were revealed: "It is not for a Messenger that he takes prisoners until he has thoroughly overcome (the enemy) in the land. You desire the things of dünya while bütünāh desires the ahiret. bütünāh is Mighty, the Wise." (Sūrah al-Anfāl, 67)

1511.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who believes in Allāh and the Last Day should speak good words or remain silent."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
1511.commentary: Bu hadis clearly indicates that one should not speak unless the sözler he utters are good, şöyle ki söz which is clearly beneficial. If there is any doubt about it being beneficial, one should not speak. When a person believes in bütünāh, he knows that bütünāh is bütün-Hearing and bütün-Knowing, and when he believes in the Last Day he knows that he will have to account to bütünāh for his her kelime and amel. For these reasons, he will only speak after pondering whether his sözler will be beneficial for his dinî or dünya hayatı. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) also said, "One who keeps silent is saved." (Tirmidhī) Scholars have stated, "If speaking is silver, then keeping silent is gold." Imām Mālik stated that Luqmān, the wise, was asked, "How did you achieve such a high rank?" He replied, "By means of three ameller: speaking the truth, fulfilling trusts and abstaining from futile söz." (Iḥyā')

1512.text: I sordu: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Who is the best Müslüman?' He cevap verdi: 'One from whose tongue and hand other Müslümans are safe.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1512.commentary: The hadis does not mean that it is helal to harm non-Muslims. It mentions the kelime "Muslim" merely because a Muslim generally deals more with other Muslims. gerçekte, a gerçek Muslim ensures that he does not cause harm to even animals and his natural surroundings. The tongue and hand have been mentioned because the harm caused by these is more than that of other limbs. Backbiting, slandering, yanlış accusations, lies, cursing and utilising vulgar language bütün come within the scope of the harms of the tongue. Physical abuse, murder, writing offensive sözler and messages are bazı of the evils of the hand. The tongue has been mentioned before the hand because the harm caused by the tongue is greater and more yaygın. For this reason, the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said to Ḥassān (رضي الله عنه), "Utter poems disparaging the polytheists, since this is heavier on them than a rain of arrows." (Muslim) A poet stated, "The wounds of the spear can heal, but the wounds of the tongue asla heal."

1513.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who gives me the guarantee that he will safeguard what is between his jaws and what is between his thighs, I will guarantee him Cennet."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1513.commentary: The hadis bize öğretir ki protecting the tongue and private parts from engaging in the prohibited bir vesilesidir entry into cennet and safety from cehennem. On the contrary, incorrect usage of these two organs will cause a person to enter cehennem. "What is between his jaws" işaret eder beneficial söz as well as consuming Ḥalāl sustenance. "What is between his thighs" işaret eder protecting one's chastity and abstaining from adultery, fornication, masturbation, homosexuality and lesbianism.

1514.text: He heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"A kul utters a word without pondering over its seriousness and in so doing slips into cehennem ateşi to a depth that is greater than the distance between the east and the west."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Bayhaqī, Ḥākim)
1514.commentary: It is necessary for a believer to daima control his tongue. He should not allow it to speak freely. sık sık, a single kelime uttered mockingly at an aspect of Islām is sufficient to land a person in cehennem without him even realising it. A person should bu nedenle ponder before uttering anything. This may prove difficult initially, but with practise, one will easily be able to think before speaking.

1515.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A kul utters a word that pleases Allāh and he does not even realise it, due to which Allāh elevates his ranks. A kul utters a word that angers Allāh and he does not even realise it, due to which he falls into Hell."(Bukhārī, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
1515.commentary: At times, a person utters such sözler of goodness that reform others or cause them to abandon a life of günah and oppression. The result of this is that he will be greatly rewarded in the ahiret. diğer yandan, a person bazen utters such evil sözler which disunite people or lead to günah and misguidance. The result of this is that he will be greatly punished in the ahiret.

1516.narrator: Abū 'Abd al-Raḥmān Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī (رضي الله عنه)
1516.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A person utters a word that pleases Allāh without him realising its full implication, due to which Allāh records His pleasure for him until the day he meets Allāh. A person utters a word that angers Allāh without him realising its full implication, due to which Allāh records His wrath against him until the day he meets Allāh."(Mālik, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1516.commentary: Göre Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, Bu hadis işaret eder söz before an oppressive ruler which is either meant to please or caution him. If his sözler encourage the evil which the ruler intends doing, it will distance him from bütünāh and earn His anger. diğer yandan, if he convinces the ruler not to fulfil his prohibited desires and to abstain from günah, it will elevate his rank in the sight of bütünāh.

1517.text: I dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Tell me something which I could hold on to.' He cevap verdi: 'Say: My Sustainer is Allāh', then remain steadfast.' I dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! What is the thing which you korku most for me?' He held his tongue and dedi: 'This.'"(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah, Dārimī)
1517.commentary: Bu hadis is an açıklama of the Qur'ānic verse, "Verily those who say, 'Our Sustainer is bütünāh' and are then steadfast, angels shall surely descend to them, 'Neither have any korku nor grief, and rejoice about the cennet that you have been promised.'" (Sūrah Hā Mīm Sajdah, 30) istikrar (istiqāmah) means to remain firm on bütün the commandments of Islām and abstain from bütün the prohibitions. Scholars state that it is a concise kelime, but it encompasses bütün the laws of the iman. The tongue is the çoğu dangerous of bodily organs because it moves very easily and asla tires. ayrıca, birçok evils arise from the tongue and if it is left unrestricted, it causes great damage to oneself and others.

1518.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Do not talk much without remembering Allāh because much talk without the remembrance of Allāh causes hard-heartedness. Those furthest away from Allāh are those who are hard-hearted."(Tirmidhī)
1518.commentary: Excessive dünyevî söz causes the heart to become hard. As a result, a person cannot derive dersler from events occurring around him. The dhikr of bütünāh counters the effects of dünyevî söz, bundan dolayı one should continuously engage in it.

1519.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One whom Allāh protects from the evil that is between his jaws and the evil that is between his thighs will enter Cennet."(Tirmidhī, Ḥākim)
1519.commentary: Dil ve cinsel organ cehenneme giren insanların başlıca sebebi olduğu için, bu iki organı kontrol altında tutmak gerekir.

1520.text: I sordu: 'O Messenger of Allāh, how can salvation be attained?' He cevap verdi: 'Restrain your tongue, let your house be spacious for you, and cry over your günahlar.'"(Tirmidhī)
1520.commentary: The prescription provided in Bu hadis is extremely relevant to the times we are living in. One who practises upon it will be saved from the birçok evils and temptations that are prevalent. Firstly, a person should carefully choose his sözler when speaking. Secondly, he should avoid unnecessary mixing with people, and rather remain in his home. Thirdly, he should cry over his günahlar because this will cause iyilikler to be recorded in place of his evil ameller.

1521.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When the son of Ādam starts the day, all his body parts submit themselves to his tongue, diyerek: 'Fear Allāh with regard to us because our existence is dependent on you. If you are straight, we will be straight, and if you deviate, we will deviate.'"(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1521.commentary: The heart controls the ameller of the body, while the tongue translates whatever emanates from the heart. When a person speaks sözler of salih amel, he is granted saygı and honour in dünya and the ahiret. This serves as a means of comfort for the remaining limbs of the body. On the contrary, if a person speaks sözler of evil, he is disgraced and embarrassed in dünya and bütün his limbs will suffer azap in the ahiret. The Arabs appropriately combine the önem of these two limbs by the expression, "A man is according to his two small limbs: his tongue and his heart."

1522.text: I sordu: 'O Messenger of Allāh, tell me of an action that will admit me into Cennet and keep me far from cehennem ateşi.' He cevap verdi: 'You have sordu about a very serious matter, but it is very easy for the person for whom Allāh makes it easy: that you ibadet Allāh without ascribing any partners to Him, establish the namaz, give the zekât, fast in Ramaḍān and perform Hac to the House.' He then sordu: 'Should I not direct you to the doors of good? Fasting is a shield, sadaka extinguishes günahlar as water extinguishes fire, and the namaz performed by a person in the dark of the night.' He then recited, 'Their sides part from their beds, they make dua to their Sustainer in korku and ümit, and they spend from what We have provided for them. No soul knows what pleasures are hidden for him as a sevap for the deeds he carries out.' (Sûre al-Sajdah, 16-17) He then sordu: 'Size haber vereyim mi of the head of the matter, its pillar, and its peak?' I cevap verdi: 'Indeed, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He dedi: 'The head of the matter is İslâm, its pillar is namaz, and its peak is cihat.' He then sordu: 'Size haber vereyim mi of the basis of all this?' I cevap verdi: 'Indeed, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!' He took hold of his tongue and dedi: 'Restrain this.' I sordu: 'O Messenger of Allāh, will we be taken to task for what we speak?' He cevap verdi: 'May your mother be bereaved. People will be cast into cehennem ateşi on their faces solely because of the harvest of their tongues.'"(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1522.commentary: Bu hadis önemine işaret eder the fundamental teachings of Islām. It concludes by pointing out the great harm which can be caused by the tongue, şöyle ki entry into cehennem. The Messenger (ﷺ) stated that "it is very easy for the person for whom bütünāh makes it easy," in order to explain that while salvation is an important matter it is easy to attain when one is granted the ilâhî ability to do so. "May your mother be bereaved" is not a supplication for death, but an expression used by the Arabs to convey önem or to warn about a serious matter.

1523.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sordu:"Biliyor musunuz what backbiting is?"The Sahâbe (رضي الله عنهم) cevap verdi:"Allāh and His Messenger (ﷺ) know best."He dedi:"Speaking about your brother in a manner which he dislikes."He was sordu:"What if my brother is as I say?"He cevap verdi:"If what you say is found in him, you have certainly engaged in backbiting about him, and if what you say is not found in him, you have slandered him."(Müslüman, Bayhaqī)
1523.commentary: Backbiting işaret eder speaking ill of any person in his absence or about anything related to him, gibi his children, vehicle, house, etc. Backbiting may be verbal, by means of hand signs, eye-signs, writing or mimicking any of his ameller. If one feels that the person will be displeased if he gets to know about it, then it is backbiting, even if it is gerçek. If it is not gerçek, then it is referred to as buhtān (slander), which is also prohibited.

1524.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu: in his sermon on the day of sacrifice at Minā during the Farewell Hac:"Your blood, your property and your honour are sacred like the sanctity of this day, in this month, in this city. Listen! Have I conveyed it to you?"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1524.commentary: tıpkı... gibi Makkah Mukarramah, Dhul Ḥijjah and the day of 'Īd are honoured and sanctified, so too are the lives, wealth and honour of Muslims. aslında, the honour and saygı of a believer is even more sanctified. Once Ibn 'Umar looked towards the Ka'bah and said, "How great you are and how great is your sanctity! bununla birlikte the sanctity of a believer is greater than you in the sight of bütünāh." (Ibn Kathīr) bütünāh prohibited murder and physical violence so that the lives of Muslims are protected. He prohibited robbery and misappropriation so that the properties of Muslims are protected. He prohibited backbiting, slander and vulgar language so that the honour of Muslims is protected.

1525.text: I şöyle dedi to Resûlullah (ﷺ): 'Such-and-such in respect of Ṣafiyyah is sufficient for you.' Some narrators state that she referred to her being short. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) şöyle dedi: 'You have yaptı such a statement that if it were to be mixed with the su of the ocean, it would pollute it.' 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) şöyle dedi: 'I rivayet etti something about a person to Resûlullah (ﷺ), so he şöyle dedi: I would never relate something about a person even if I was given such-and-such in recompense.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
1525.commentary: The sözler "pollute it" mean that it is polluted in such a yol that its taste or smell changes because of the terrible odour and stench of the pollutant. This is one of the çoğu eloquent forms of reproach against backbiting. bütünāh says: "He does not speak of his own desires. Whatever he says is revelation revealed to him." (Sūrah al-Najm, 3-4) When a single undesirable ifade has such disastrous effects on the largest of bütünāh's creations in dünya, şöyle ki the ocean, then one can imagine the effects of continuous backbiting and slandering? Imām Nawawī specifically quoted the verse at the end to indicate the şiddet of backbiting and that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) was not speaking of his own accord, but in accordance with ilâhî revelation.

1526.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"When I was taken up to the heavens (during Mi'rāj), I passed by some people who had fingernails of copper, with which they were scratching their faces and chests. I sordu: 'Who are these people, O Jibrā'īl?' He cevap verdi: 'These are the people who consumed the flesh of people and attacked their honour.'"(Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1526.commentary: Backbiting is benzer to eating the raw flesh of one's dead brother - an amel which olarak kabul edilir çoğu contemptible. tıpkı... gibi cannibals are despised and hated, so too is a person who backbites. bazı âlimlere göre, the literal anlam of the hadis applies, şöyle ki that one who backbites, fills his belly with flesh of his Muslim brother. This is desteklenen by the following incident. A man came to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of bütünāh! Two women are fasting. They are on the verge of death due to excessive thirst." The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) turned away. He returned in the afternoon and repeated what he had said. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "Call them." When they came a container was placed before them, and they were commanded to vomit. The first one vomited blood, pus and flesh until half the container was filled. Then the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) commanded the second woman to do the same. She also vomited pus, blood, fresh meat, etc. until the tüm container was dolu. Then the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "These two abstained from that which bütünāh had permitted for them, and broke their fast on that which bütünāh had prohibited them from. They sat together, eating the flesh of people." (Aḥmad)

1527.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The blood, honour and property of every Müslüman is sacred for another Müslüman."(Müslüman, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
1527.commentary: The kelime "Muslim" has been used here to indicate that a gerçek Muslim would asla cause harm to others as the literal anlam of a "Muslim" is one who gives security and safety to others. When a Muslim gives safety to others, how can it ever be possible for him to cause harm to the lives, honour and properties of fellow insanî beings?

1528.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"On the day of Kıyamet, Allāh will protect from cehennem ateşi the face of one who defends the honour of his brother."(Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1528.commentary: If a believer is spoken ill of in any gathering, then it is the duty of another believer to defend him, since bütün believers are brothers. ayrıca, as Bu hadis explains, defending a Muslim in dünya bir sebebidir salvation from the cehennem-fire in the ahiret. The Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) said, "A Muslim who does not assist another Muslim in a place where his honour is torn apart and he is being dishonoured, then bütünāh will not come to his assistance in that place where he will sevgi assistance. A Muslim who assists another Muslim in a place where his honour is torn apart and he is being dishonoured, then bütünāh will come to his assistance in that place where he will sevgi assistance." (Abū Dāwūd) The face has been mentioned because it is generally the point of pain and embarrassment.

1529.text: In his lengthy and well-known hadis quoted previously in the chapter on ümit that Resûlullah (ﷺ) stood up to perform the namaz and sordu:"Where is Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum?"Another cevap verdi:"That man is a münafık. He does not love Allāh and His Messenger."On hearing this, Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"Do you not see that he testifies that there is none worthy of ibadet except Allāh and he says it for the pleasure of Allāh? One who testifies that there is none worthy of ibadet except Allāh, desiring thereby the pleasure of Allāh, then Allāh makes it unlawful for him to enter cehennem ateşi."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Nasā'ī)
1529.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 417. That the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) immediately prohibited the person from backbiting shows that the amel is prohibited. One may prohibit another from backbiting by either reprimanding him or by refuting what he says.

1530.text: In his lengthy hadis regarding the story of his repentance which was quoted previously in the chapter on repentance:"While Resûlullah (ﷺ) was sitting with the people at Tabūk, he sordu: 'What happened to Ka'b ibn Mālik?' A person from the Banū Salimah dedi: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! His cloak and self-conceit have kept him back.' Mu'ādh ibn Jabal (رضي الله عنه) dedi: 'What an evil thing to say! By Allāh, O Messenger of Allāh, we know nothing but good about him.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) remained silent."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1530.commentary: That the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) remained silent, proves that Mu'ādh's (رضي الله عنه) amel of defending his Muslim brother was meritorious.

1531.text: A man requested permission to meet Resûlullah (ﷺ), so he (ﷺ) dedi:"Give him permission. He is an evil person of the tribe."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad) Bukhārī used it to prove the permissibility of speaking ill of the people of corruption and people of doubt.
1531.commentary: People are sık sık misled by the outward appearance of others causing harm to their dünyevî and dinî lives. It is bu nedenle necessary to inform people of their harm tıpkı... gibi the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) informed those around him about the evil of others.

1532.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"I do not think that so-and-so and so-and-so know anything of our religion."(Bukhārī) Al-Layth ibn Sa'd, one of the narrators of this hadis, dedi:"These two people were hypocrites."
1532.commentary: Münafıkları ifşa etmek caizdir ki diğer insanlar onların tuzağına düşmesin. Ancak gizli kusurları ifşa etmek caiz değildir.

1533.text: I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and dedi: 'Abū al-Jahm and Mu'āwiyah have both proposed marriage to me.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'Mu'āwiyah is poor and has no mal, and Abū al-Jahm does not remove his stick from his shoulder.'"(Müslüman, Aḥmad) Another narration of Müslüman has:"Abū al-Jahm beats women,"which is an explanation of the narration,"he does not remove his stick from his shoulder."It is also dedi to mean that he travels a lot.
1533.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki if one is aware of bazı weakness in a potential spouse, he should inform the opposite party of this. This is not prohibited provided that one's niyet is to give good advice and not to disgrace or disunite people. From other narrations we learn that the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) married Fāṭimah bint Qays (رضي الله عنها) to Usāmah ibn Zayd (رضي الله عنه). She later said, "We had such sevgi between us that I was envied." (Muslim)

1534.text: We went out on a journey with Resûlullah (ﷺ) during which the people experienced considerable hardship. 'Abdullāh ibn Ubayy dedi: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allāh so that they become disunited.' He also dedi: 'If we return to Madīnah, the powerful ones will expel those who are weak.' I went to Resûlullah (ﷺ) and haber verdi him of this. He summoned 'Abdullāh ibn Ubayy but he took a passionate oath that he did not say it. They (the hypocrites) dedi: 'Zayd lied to Resûlullah (ﷺ).' Their accusation hurt me greatly until Allāh revealed verses confirming my doğruluk: 'When the hypocrites come to you...' (Sûre al-Munāfiqūn, 1) The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then called them to seek bağışlanma for them but they arrogantly turned away."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1534.commentary: This incident took place during the Battle of Banū Muṣṭaliq in Sha'bān around 5 Hijrī. 'Abdullāh ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, referred to the Muslims as poor and said that if they are not given wealth, they would disperse. bütünāh answered him by stating, "To bütünāh belongs the treasures of the heavens and the earth but the hypocrites do not understand." (Sūrah Munāfiqūn, 7) 'Abdullāh also referred to himself as honourable and the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) and his Ṣaḥābah as disgraced and lowly. His aim was to stoke the flames of nefret so that the residents of Madīnah Munawwarah would expel the Muslims emigrants. bütünāh answered this by stating, "bütün honour belongs to bütünāh, His Messenger and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know." (Sūrah Munāfiqūn, 8) Zayd ibn Arqam (رضي الله عنه) was a young boy at the time. He proceeded to inform the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) about what he had heard. That the Messenger (ﷺ) heard his sözler and acted, bize öğretir ki to inform others about the plots and plans of the hypocrites is helal.

1535.text: Hind, the wife of Abū Sufyān, dedi to Resûlullah (ﷺ): 'Abū Sufyān is a miserly man. He does not give me sufficient for myself and my children unless I take some of it from him without his knowledge.' He (ﷺ) dedi: 'You may take a reasonable amount for yourself and your children.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1535.commentary: From this hadis, the jurists have extracted the following laws: 1. It is compulsory for a husband to provide food, clothing and shelter for his wife and children. 2. It is helal to speak to a strange woman due to necessity. 3. It is helal to mention the evil quality of a person whilst asking a hukukî hüküm (fatwā) regarding him. 4. If a husband does not provide for the basic expenses of his wife and family, she may take from his wealth to the extent of necessity. 5. A woman may emerge from her home due to necessity.

1536.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"A slanderer will not enter Cennet."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Aḥmad)
1536.commentary: The scholars unanimously agree that slander and carrying tales with the niyet of causing trouble amongst people is prohibited. If a person does so, regarding the amel as helal, he will become a disbeliever and will be deprived of cennet. If a person does not regard it as helal, but engages in it due to his weakness, he will not enter cennet with those who enter it first, but will have to enter cehennem-fire to cleanse himself from this evil amel. bununla birlikte, if one repents from the günah, he will be forgiven.

1537.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by two graves and dedi:"They are being punished at present but they are not being punished for something major (in their opinion). But it is major (in günah). One of them was a slanderer, and the other was not careful of urine drops when relieving himself."(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd, Bayhaqī) Scholars have stated,"They are not being punished for something major"means that it was not a major günah according to them. It is also dedi that it means that it was difficult for them to avoid it.
1537.commentary: Negligence regarding urine drops is a serious matter because the çoğu important ibadet is ṣalāh and the key to ṣalāh is tahārah (purity). It is bu nedenle compulsory for a person to purify himself properly after relieving himself. One should ensure to the best of his ability that the last az sayıda drops of urine in the bladder have been expelled. This can be done by leaning towards the left side, exerting pressure on the private part, walking a az sayıda brisk steps, etc. Similarly, carrying tales is a serious günah because it generates anger and nefret between individuals, families and societies, ayrıca to the azap one will experience for it in the grave.

1538.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Should I not tell you what slander is? It is tale-bearing bandied about among people."(Müslüman)
1538.commentary: Ḥammād ibn Salamah (رضي الله عنه) said: A man sold a slave and said to the buyer, "The only fault he has is that he carries tales." The buyer thought it to be inconsequential and purchased the slave. After bazı time had passed, the slave said to his master's wife, "Your husband does not sevgi you and he wants to remarry. Take a knife and cut off bazı strands of hair from his nape whilst he is asleep. I will make a charm with it and his sevgi will then only be for you." He then went to the husband and said, "Your wife has a lover and she wants to kill you. Pretend to be asleep and you will see for yourself." The man pretended to be asleep that night. His wife brought a knife, and the husband, thinking that she wanted to kill him, stood up and killed her. The wife's family were upset and killed the husband. This resulted in great bloodshed between her iki families. (Iḥyā')

1539.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"None of my Sahâbe should convey to me anything evil about someone else because I like to come out to you with a clean heart."(Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
1539.commentary: Bu hadis, başkalarının kusurlarını örtmemizi öğretir çünkü insanî varlıklar hata yapmaya eğilimlidir ve merhamet edene merhamet edilir.

1540.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"You will find people to be like mines. The best of them in jāhiliyyah are the best in İslâm provided they understand İslâm. You will find that the best of people for this issue (of leadership) are those who dislike it the most. You will find that the worst of people are the two-faced who go to some people with one face, and to other people with another face."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1540.commentary: Bu hadis bize öğretir ki, like mines, her person has been granted abilities and strengths and when a person learns and practises upon the laws of Islām, he shines out and becomes an asset to humanity. We also learn that people who do not desire leadership, fulfil its sorumluluklar best. People of intelligence and iman know that leadership is a difficult matter because of the complexity of administering adalet, preventing oppression, being accountable to bütünāh regarding the haklar of others, etc. This realisation leads them to assuming positions of leadership with adalet and diligence. A two-faced individual is tantamount to a hypocrite because his internal and external do not reconcile. Scholars, bununla birlikte, state that to reconcile between individuals in this yol is commendable and an act of great sevap.

1541.text: Muḥammad ibn Zayd anlatır that some people dedi to his grandfather, 'Abdullāh ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه):"When we go to our leaders, we speak contrary to that which we say when we are not with them."He dedi:"During the era of Resûlullah (ﷺ), we considered this as hypocrisy."(Bukhārī)
1541.commentary: The hadis in essence bize öğretir ki it is incorrect to flatter one's leaders in their presence and to speak ill of them in their absence. This bir işaretidir cowardice and nifak because a gerçek Muslim will clearly proclaim what he feels. If the leader is engaged in evil, he will prohibit him from it in person and in public. He will not withhold the truth, hoping to acquire temporary and fleeting dünyevî faydalar.

1542.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Truthfulness leads to salih amel and salih amel leads to Cennet. A person habitually speaks the truth until he is recorded as a very truthful person in the sight of Allāh. Falsehood leads to evil and evil leads to cehennem ateşi. A person habitually speaks lies until he is recorded as a grave liar in the sight of Allāh."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1542.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 54. It is desteklenen by another hadis which states: "A person continues lying and aspires to speak lies, and a black dot is continuously formed in his heart until his tüm heart becomes black. He is then written amongst the liars in the sight of bütünāh." (Muwaṭṭā') Being truthful indicates towards bravery in the face of reality, while dishonesty indicates towards cowardice, doubt and insecurity.

1543.narrator: Abdullah bin Amr bin el-Âs (رضي الله عنه)
1543.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"If anyone has four qualities, he is a pure münafık, and if he has one of them, he has one quality of hypocrisy until he leaves it: when he is trusted he betrays, when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he acts treacherously, and when he argues he behaves improperly."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1543.commentary: Bu hadis, Ebû Hüreyre (رضي الله عنه)'nin benzer hadisiyle birlikte daha önce açıklanmıştır. Bkz. hadis 1522.

1544.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who anlatır a dream which he did not have will be made to tie a knot between two barley seeds (on the day of Kıyamet) and he will not be able to do so. One who listens to the conversation of people who do not want him to, will have molten copper poured in his ears on the day of Kıyamet. One who makes an image will be punished and compelled to breathe a soul into it, but he will not be able to do so."(Bukhārī)
1544.commentary: Bu hadis mentions severe warnings for narrating yanlış dreams, eavesdropping and creating images. A dream is a portion of revelation, so one who narrates a yanlış dream fabricates and attributes a lie to bütünāh while deceiving people. Eavesdropping is a serious günah and the azap will match the crime. Creating images is an attempt to imitate bütünāh, the Creator.

1545.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"The worst lie is for a person to claim to have seen something which he did not see."(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1545.commentary: Bu, uyanıkken veya rüyada bir şey gördüğünü iddia etmeyi de kapsar. Yalan rüya anlatmak da büyük günahlardandır.

1546.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) often sordu his Sahâbe: 'Did any of you see a dream?' One morning, Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi to us: 'At night two men came to me and dedi to me: Come with us.' So I went with them. We came upon a person who was lying down and another was standing over him with a heavy rock in his hand. He dropped the rock forcefully onto his head and crushed it. The rock then rolled away and he went and retrieved it. By the time he returned, this man'in head was normal as it had been. So he struck him again as he had done the first time. I sordu them: 'Glory be to Allāh! Who are these two?' They cevap verdi: 'Continue, continue!' We continued until we came upon a man lying on his back and another man was standing over him with an iron hook. He went to one side of his face and cut his mouth until the nape. He also cut from his nostril to the nape and from his eye to the nape. He then went to the other side and did the same... [The Prophet described many scenes of azap in ahiret, then the angels explained:] The first person you came upon whose head was being crushed with a rock, was a person who had memorised the Kur'an, but then abandoned it, and slept through the compulsory namaz. The person whose mouth, nostril and eye was being cut until his nape, was one who would leave his home in the morning and tell lies which spread widely. As for the naked men and women who were in an oven like structure, they were adulterers and adulteresses. As for the man whom you came upon swimming in the river and was made to swallow a stone, he used to consume interest (usury). As for the man with a repulsive appearance who was kindling a fire and running around it, he is Mālik, the guard of Hell. The tall man in the bahçe was Ibrāhīm, and the children who were around him, were those infants who passed away on fiṭrah (natural disposition).' The narration of al-Barqanī has, 'born in the natural state.' One of the Sahâbe sordu: 'Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! What about the children of the polytheists?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) cevap verdi: 'The children of the polytheists as well.'"(Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1546.commentary: Bu hadis mentions severe warnings for neglecting the Qur'ān, abandoning the five daily ṣalāhs, speaking lies, carrying tales, engaging in adultery and consuming interest. The person who neglected reciting and practising upon the Qur'ān will be severely punished because, after being blessed with the çoğu honourable of bounties, he abandoned it. The adulterers and adulteresses will be punished naked because they exposed their private parts before others. The consumer of interest will swim in blood because he was like a parasite who devoured the blood of people in distress.

1547.text: Umm Kulthūm (رضي الله عنها) who heard Resûlullah (ﷺ) diyerek:"The person who strives to reconcile between people by causing good or diyerek good is not a liar."Müslüman adds in a narration:"Umm Kulthūm dedi: 'I did not hear him (the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ) granting concession in regard to what people say except in three cases: namely, war, reconciling between people, and the words of a husband to his wife and a wife to her husband."(Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1547.commentary: Although lying is essentially prohibited, it is permitted in certain situations with şartlar. If any praiseworthy objective can be achieved without lying, then it is haram to lie. If it can only be achieved by lying, then lying will be helal. If the achievement of that objective is lawful, lying will be lawful. If that objective is farz, lying will be farz. The best approach is to utilise tawriyā - sözler which are not lies in relation to him, but may appear to be lies on the face of it.

1548.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"It is sufficient for a person to be considered a liar if he anlatır whatever he hears."(Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd, Ḥākim)
1548.commentary: Bu hadis highlights a critical principle of insanî relations: as long as a person has not investigated and established the truth of any matter, he should not narrate it to others. Practising upon this will prevent birçok quarrels and misunderstandings in society. One who conveys unverified matters olarak kabul edilir a liar.

1549.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"One who relates something from me while he deems it to be a lie is one of the liars."(Müslüman)
1549.commentary: One who fabricates hadis is a liar as well as one who narrates it to others, bundan dolayı a person should be extra careful when narrating aḥādīth and attributing sözler to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ). It is the unanimous opinion of the scholars that consciously attributing something yanlış to the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) is prohibited.

1550.text: A woman dedi: 'I have a co-wife. Is there any günah on me if I give her the impression that I am receiving more than what my husband gives me?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dedi: 'One who gives the impression of having received something which he did not receive is like a person who wears two false garments.'"(Bukhārī, Müslüman, Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1550.commentary: A woman who deceives her co-wife by giving the impression that she is the recipient of extra sevgi and affection from her husband is a liar. Such behaviour only creates ill-feelings between partners, bundan dolayı the Messenger of bütünāh (ﷺ) prohibited this. "One who wears two yanlış garments" işaret eder a person who deceives people by adopting the ways of ascetics, scholars or affluent people while not possessing such attributes.

1551.narrator: Abū Bakrah Nufay' ibn al-Ḥārith (رضي الله عنه)
1551.text: Resûlullah (ﷺ) şöyle buyurdu:"Size haber vereyim mi of the most serious of major günahlar?"We cevap verdi:"Indeed, Ey Allah'ın Resûlü!"He dedi:"Ascribing partners with Allāh and disobeying parents."The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) had been lying down, but suddenly sat up and dedi:"And giving false şehadet."He continued repeating this until we hoped that he would remain silent. (Bukhārī, Müslüman)
1551.commentary: Bu hadis was mentioned previously. See hadis 336. It is repeated here to highlight the şiddet of giving yanlış testimony. It is a major günah because the harms of it are not confined to a single individual, but sık sık have broad implications in society. The fact that it has been mentioned in the same breath as ascribing partners to bütünāh and isyan to parents illustrates its evil.

1552.narrator: Abu Zayd Thabit ibn Dahhak al-Ansari (ra)
1552.text: Abū Zayd Thābit ibn Ḍaḥḥāk al-Anṣārī (رضي الله عنه), one of those who were present during the Bay'at al-Riḍwān, anlatır that Resûlullah (ﷺ) dedi:"One who consciously takes a false oath that he will adopt a religion other than İslâm, it will be as he dedi.
